biovolt-0c8e.name: BioVolt
biovolt-0c8e.tagline: Trustworthy telemetry for living power cells

description.title: Software
description.body:
BioVolt is designed as a reusable, collaborative experiment platform rather than a one-off hardware prototype.

It uses a common telemetry format, modular backend, simulator, database, and dashboard so researchers and developers can:

- Connect different microbial-cell and sensor designs
- Reuse the same data-processing pipeline
- Add new biomass, OD680, carbon-fixation, or optimization models
- Test ideas through simulation before hardware is available
- Compare experiments using consistent data structures
- Extend the platform without redesigning the entire system

The goal is to make bioelectrochemical research more accessible, reproducible, and collaborative by allowing new hardware, algorithms, and datasets to plug into the same open system.

description.title: Hardware
description.body:
The software is the measurement and visualization layer around the physical BioVolt hardware:

```text
BioVolt cell + sensors
        ↓
ESP32 firmware
        ↓ USB serial / COM5
ESP32 serial bridge
        ↓ WebSocket
Backend
        ↓
Dashboard
```

- The hardware produces the real signal: electrodes generate BPV voltage/current, ADS1115 reads BPV and BPW34, BH1750/GY-302 reads light, and DS18B20 reads temperature.
- The ESP32 firmware reads those sensors and sends raw values plus health status.
- The serial bridge transports the ESP32 frames to the backend.
- The backend validates data, applies calibration, calculates current, power, energy, OD680, biomass, and carbon fixation, then stores and broadcasts the results.
- The frontend displays live values and graphs.

The simulator is only a pre-hardware substitute. Its PWM-like spikes and load-sag model help test the dashboard before or between hardware runs; they are not evidence that the real cell is producing spikes.

For the hardware track, the remaining validation is physical:

- Verify wiring and sensor health.
- Connect and measure the real electrical load.
- Calibrate voltage/current against the multimeter.
- Capture proper BPW34 dark and blank references for OD680.
- Compare sustained ESP32 readings against the dashboard.
- Run the system for an extended period to check noise, drift, and connection stability.

A software load setting changes calculations; it cannot physically reduce the ESP32 circuit voltage. The real voltage drops only when the load is connected to the hardware circuit.

description.title: Software
description.body: HepatoGuard is a software-based health project because it solves a real problem of spotting early liver cancer risk by using data processing and gene mapping. HepatoGuard takes data from biopsies looks at the important molecular details and creates a molecular progression score with a clear report. It blends programming, bioinformatics data analysis and an easy interface to turn genetic data into useful research results. As members, in our first hackathon we want to show our tech skills, creativity, teamwork and eagerness to learn by building a working prototype that can help future health research and clinical decisions.

description.title: Best Beginner
description.body:
HepatoGuard is our first hackathon project, so we wanted to take on something ambitious while still learning by building. We combined concepts we’re excited about, like AI, bioinformatics, and healthcare, and turned them into a practical prototype rather than trying to solve everything at once.

We started with the frontend and user experience, then began exploring real liver datasets and building the backend pipeline step by step. Along the way, we’ve had to learn about gene-expression data, dataset challenges, machine learning, explainability, and responsible medical AI.

For us, HepatoGuard is not about pretending we have built a finished medical product. It’s about learning how to turn a difficult real-world problem into a working AI prototype, while being honest about what still needs validation.

description.title: Software

Here is a short, concise description you can use directly for your hackathon submission:

---

### Why CyberShield AI Fits into the **Open Track**

> **CyberShield AI qualifies for the Open Track because it breaks the boundaries of traditional software categories by converging low-level network systems, autonomous cyber-deception, on-premise AI, and DevOps automation into a single unified platform.**
>
> Rather than fitting into a single vertical like a standalone AI wrapper or standard web app, CyberShield AI solves a systemic, industry-wide crisis through cross-disciplinary innovation:
>
> 1. **Cross-Domain Fusion**: Seamlessly connects raw TCP network socket emulation, cryptographic forensic logging (SHA-256), offline local Vector RAG (ChromaDB), and live WebSocket command-center visualizations.
> 2. **A Paradigm Shift in Defense**: Moves beyond reactive firewalls and noisy log scanners to introduce active deception—safely trapping live attackers in synthetic sandboxes with zero false positives.
> 3. **End-to-End Autonomous Remediation**: Bridges defensive security directly with software engineering by using Gemini AI to write vulnerability fixes and submit 1-click GitHub Pull Requests for human review.
> 4. **Universal Impact**: Applicable across critical infrastructure, FinTech, cloud providers, and small businesses alike, making it a foundational, open-ended technological solution.

description.title: Best Beginner
description.body: HydraNexus is a good beginner project because, despite us picking an extremely complex real-life problem, we made the solution to it somewhat beginner-friendly by dividing it into approachable parts. Our MVP is mostly made up of Python, Pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, NetworkX, FastAPI, and React because we did not rely on heavy non-free software or used labeled big data sets. Instead, we implemented controlled simulations that produce telemetry data and allow us to test various solutions and their outcomes in different scenarios. Then, we tie all of these minor parts, such as anomalous detection and cause analysis, topology-based localization, impact assessment, What-If analysis, and decision-making, into a single cohesive product. In this way, our first hackathon project serves as a perfect example of how someone with little to no prior experience can address an otherwise complicated real-world issue without jumping into overcomplicated or black-box solutions right away.

description.title: Hardware
description.body:
SYNAPSE is a hardware–software integrated system. It uses physical EEG hardware to capture neural signals from the user, processes those signals in real time, and converts the detected intent into actions.

The hardware layer includes:

🧠 EEG electrodes + BioAmp — captures brain activity
🔌 Arduino UNO — acquires and transmits the EEG signal
💻 Computer/— performs signal processing and ML inference
🤖 ESP8266 — can extend the same intent system to physical machines/robots

The key point is that SYNAPSE cannot function as intended from software alone—the physical EEG acquisition hardware is what creates the input signal that drives the entire system.

SYNAPSE bridges human neural signals and physical computing hardware, creating a real-time hardware–AI interface for hands-free control.

noticeiq-8e0c.name: NoticeIQ
noticeiq-8e0c.tagline: Catch It. Act on It. Never Miss It.

description.title: Software
description.body: NoticeIQ solves a genuine, universal student problem: information overload from disorganized channels leading to missed deadlines. Our solution combines two complete, working systems: a secure Digital Campus ID with QR-based verification, and an AI pipeline (dual-provider: Groq for text, Gemini for images/PDFs) that converts messy notices into structured tasks with automatically scheduled, multi-stage reminders delivered via real push notifications — confirmed working even with the app fully closed. The entire system is built on production-grade security (Row Level Security on every database table) and deployed as an installable PWA.

description.title: Best Beginner
description.body: This was our first time building a full production-style pipeline: AI extraction, real-time database security (Row Level Security), and — the hardest part — genuine OS-level push notifications that work even when the app is closed, which most beginner (and even experienced) teams don't attempt. We hit real, unglamorous bugs along the way — a silent authentication failure, a date-parsing edge case, a task-deletion bug — and learned to properly diagnose root causes with real evidence (database queries, raw API responses) instead of guessing. We also learned when NOT to build something: we deliberately avoided native mobile app development and a WhatsApp integration once we recognized the live-demo risk outweighed the benefit, choosing a PWA instead.

description.title: Best Girl Team
description.body: Our team built NoticeIQ end-to-end — from architecture decisions to live debugging under time pressure. We made real engineering trade-offs together: pivoting from our original FastAPI + OCR plan to a leaner single-stack architecture once we realized it would be more reliable, and systematically diagnosing genuinely hard bugs (like OneSignal's authentication header format, and a subtle date-parsing bug) rather than giving up or working around them. We divided work across backend, frontend, and pitch/testing roles, and iterated together based on real mentor and judge feedback — reprioritizing our lead feature (Campus ID) mid-hackathon based on direct guidance we received and acted on quickly.

description.title: Software
description.body:
The Open Track is designed for projects that push boundaries, defy conventional software categories, and introduce fundamentally new ways to interact with technology. CLICKit is not a standard web dashboard or a wrapper around an API; it is a profound reimagining of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) at the operating system level.

We are submitting to the Open Track because CLICKit proves that the future of AI isn't in chat interfaces—it's in ambient, context-aware companions that inhabit our existing digital environments.

By unifying system-level CoreGraphics event hooking, multi-monitor coordinate mapping, and low-latency multimodal reasoning (vision + voice), CLICKit bridges the gap between what the user sees, what the user says, and how the computer responds. It breaks out of the browser and into the OS, serving as a blueprint for the next generation of frictionless, spatially-aware computing. This level of architectural complexity and unconstrained innovation perfectly aligns with the spirit of the Open Track.

autoflow-ai-e65b.name: AutoFlow AI
autoflow-ai-e65b.tagline: AI That Turns Intent Into Outcomes.

description.title: Software
description.body:
## How AutoFlow AI Fits the Open Track

AutoFlow AI is a general-purpose agentic execution platform designed to turn natural-language intent into complete, reliable workflows.

Unlike solutions built for a single domain, AutoFlow can be applied across a wide range of use cases — from research and data processing to software development, productivity, business operations, and multi-step digital tasks.

A user simply describes **what they want to accomplish**, while AutoFlow handles the complexity behind the scenes:

- **Intent Understanding** — interprets the user's goal, constraints, and requirements.
- **Intelligent Planning** — breaks complex goals into structured, executable steps.
- **Agent & Model Orchestration** — dynamically selects the appropriate agents and AI models for each task.
- **Tool Execution** — connects workflows with APIs, applications, browsers, and other tools.
- **Governance** — applies permissions, policies, budgets, and human approval where required.
- **Verification** — checks whether actions actually produced the expected results.
- **Recovery** — detects failures and can retry, recover, or re-plan instead of simply stopping.
- **Observability** — makes the execution process visible and traceable to the user.

This makes AutoFlow a flexible foundation for building many kinds of AI-powered workflows without requiring users to manually design every step, select agents, or understand the underlying orchestration.

The **Open track** is a natural fit because AutoFlow is not solving just one narrow problem — it introduces a general framework for moving from **human intent to verified execution** across different domains.

> **AutoFlow AI — Where Intent Becomes Execution.**

description.title: Hardware
description.body: Our project strongly fits the Hardware Track because the system uses a combination of physical sensors to collect real-world environmental data and feed it into our security and monitoring pipeline. We have integrated **MQ-3, MQ-5, MQ-9, MQ-135, DHT22, and HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensors** to detect parameters such as gas concentration, air quality, temperature, humidity, and distance. These sensors provide continuously changing physical-world inputs, which can be processed as additional entropy and contextual parameters for our encryption model. By combining sensor-generated data with timestamp signatures, hashing, quantization, and human-generated randomness, our system creates a hardware-assisted security architecture rather than relying purely on software. This makes the project applicable to **IoT devices, industrial monitoring, smart systems, and secure edge devices**, where both real-time sensing and secure data transmission are essential.

opsgenome-5751.tagline: AI Agents. Real-Time Fixes. Zero Downtime.

description.title: Software
description.body:
**OpsGenome** fits the **Open Source Software (OSS) Track** because it democratizes advanced SRE and self-healing infrastructure without vendor lock-in, proprietary cloud dependencies, or data privacy compromises:

1. **100% Local-First & Air-Gapped (Zero Vendor Lock-in):** Unlike closed SaaS observability platforms (like Datadog or proprietary AI tools), OpsGenome requires **zero external API keys or cloud subscriptions**. It runs completely on local developer machines using an offline SQLite memory engine (`global.db`), POSIX Unix domain sockets, and local heuristics or air-gapped Ollama models.
2. **Modular & Extensible Plugin Architecture:** It features an open, pluggable parser and specialist registry. Any open-source developer can easily add new technology stacks (e.g. Go, Rust, Helm, Pulumi) by simply inheriting from standard base classes (`BaseSpecialistAgent`, `BaseErrorParser`).
3. **Open Standards & Non-Proprietary Tooling:** It leverages universal open-source standards—transparent Zsh/Bash hooks, standard Unified Diff patches, the official Kubernetes API client, and Kahn’s Algorithm DAGs—rather than black-box proprietary automation.
4. **Community Democratization of Operational Knowledge:** It transforms individual terminal troubleshooting into transparent, reusable, and verifiable open runbooks, enabling open-source teams and solo developers to achieve enterprise-grade incident recovery and prevent recurring outages for free.

description.title: Software
description.body:
**CoEvolve Sandbox** fits strongly within the Open Innovation track by addressing an emerging challenge at the intersection of Generative AI, autonomous software development, and cybersecurity. As AI coding agents become increasingly capable of writing and modifying software, ensuring that their outputs remain secure is a continuously evolving problem. Our project proposes an innovative, self-improving security framework that allows coding agents to learn from verified failures without retraining their underlying models.

The system creates a continuous attacker–developer co-evolution loop: an Attacker LLM generates adversarial coding tasks, a Developer LLM attempts to solve them, and a Hybrid Judge validates vulnerabilities using both static analysis (SAST) and dynamic exploit replay (DAST). Confirmed failures are transformed into natural-language security rules and incorporated into the developer agent's system prompt. This creates a non-parametric alignment mechanism where defensive capabilities evolve while model weights remain frozen.

The project demonstrates innovation through adaptive Elo-based difficulty, hardened Docker isolation, regression guarding, Git-backed prompt evolution, and portable security rules. It already supports multiple LLM providers, three programming languages, 29 SAST rules, and 19 vulnerable applications for DAST validation.

Therefore, CoEvolve is not simply another cybersecurity scanner; it is an **adaptive innovation platform for continuously improving the security of autonomous AI coding systems**, with potential to evolve alongside new models, attack techniques, and software environments.

sentinelxai-c763.name: SentinelX-AI
sentinelxai-c763.tagline: Don't Just Detect Threats, Resolve Them

description.title: Software
description.body:
# Track Submission: Open Innovation / Open Track

### Project Title
**SentinelX — Autonomous Local-First DevSecOps with Dual-Agent Self-Healing Architecture**

---

### Track Fit & Overview
In the **Open Track**, innovation is judged by tackling systemic industry bottlenecks with novel engineering, unconstrained by narrow problem statements. SentinelX re-engineers modern application security by eliminating the trade-off between **privacy, operational cost, and autonomous remediation**. 

Most modern security platforms (like GitHub Copilot Autofix, Snyk, or Veracode) treat code analysis as a cloud-dependent service. This forces companies with proprietary codebases, healthcare data, or defense contracts to leak IP to third-party APIs while paying steep SaaS premiums. Furthermore, existing tools remain passive: they produce raw alerts, inundating developers with false positives, while leaving the remediation burden entirely manual.

SentinelX introduces an entirely autonomous, closed-loop DevSecOps system running **100% locally on commodity consumer hardware**. By pairing a static analysis-driven **AI Red Team** (for discovery and noise filtering) with a verified **AI Blue Team** (for syntax-validated in-place self-healing and Pull Request automation), SentinelX transforms security from a reactive bottleneck into an invisible, self-contained development partner.

---

### Core Innovation & Uniqueness
1. **Zero-Data-Exfiltration DevSecOps:**
   SentinelX executes both discovery and remediation fully air-gapped using local small language models (`qwen2.5-coder:7b` via Ollama) and local CLI static scanners. No line of source code, secret key, or repository metadata ever touches an external server.

2. **Dual-Agent Closed Loop (Red vs. Blue):**
   * **The Red Team:** Gathers scanner signals (Semgrep, Gitleaks, Trivy) and uses contextual AI reasoning to drop false positives (e.g., test tokens or mock database strings). It models modern attack surfaces (SQLi, Command Injection, Insecure Deserialization, XSS, and simulated IDOR/CSRF) into persistent telemetry streams.
   * **The Blue Team:** Takes verified exploits, writes contextual patches, validates structural syntax using local language runtimes (`ast.parse` and `node --check`), writes a safe `.bak` disk backup, and autonomously pushes a branch and GitHub Pull Request with AI-generated developer notes.

3. **Deterministic Safety Architecture:**
   AI agents should never write broken code into production. SentinelX implements a multi-tier fallback mechanism:
   * **Parser Verification:** Hallucinated syntax is blocked at the AST level before writing to disk.
   * **Rule-Based Fail-Safes:** If local hardware encounters memory limits or Ollama timeouts, deterministic rule-based engines (`RULE_BASED_FALLBACK_ENGAGED`) guarantee successful patch delivery.
   * **CLI Portability:** Missing host binaries seamlessly hand off to heuristic regex engines (`HEURISTIC_FALLBACK_ENGAGED`).

---

### Technical Architecture
* **AI & Remediation Engine:** FastAPI (Python 3.11+), Ollama (`qwen2.5-coder:7b`), AST compiler tools, and Server-Sent Events (SSE) telemetry pipelines.
* **Scanning & Detection:** Semgrep rulesets, Gitleaks entropy scanners, Trivy vulnerability databases, and internal heuristic regex fallback engines.
* **Authentication & Integrations:** Node.js / Express microservice handling granular GitHub OAuth token workflows and Octokit PR creation.
* **Frontend & Operations Console:** Next.js / React interactive dashboard visualizing live Red Team attack telemetry, vulnerability triage graphs, real-time code diffing, and automated PR deployment statuses.

---

### Impact & Scalability
* **Cost Disruption:** Zero recurring API token costs. Startups and enterprise teams can run continuous security audits on standard developer laptops or self-hosted CI/CD runners at zero marginal cost.
* **Velocity Multiplier:** Reduces vulnerability triage and patching cycle time from an industry average of **15–20 days to under 30 seconds**.
* **Ecosystem Agnostic:** Expandable across languages (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Rust) by simply registering language-specific syntax validation checkers into the Blue Team pipeline.

---

### Future Roadmap
* **CI/CD Action Runner:** Package SentinelX as a self-hosted GitHub Action / GitLab Runner container for air-gapped enterprise pipelines.
* **Multi-File Context Graphing:** Extend the Blue Team's AST analyzer to resolve cross-file import dependencies when patching distributed vulnerabilities.
* **Dynamic Ephemeral Sandboxing:** Spin up isolated Docker containers to dynamically verify exploit payloads before and after Blue Team patch application.

hackproof-c712.name: HACKPROOF
hackproof-c712.tagline: GitHub shows the code, HackProof proves the story.

description.title: Software
description.body:
HackProof addresses a critical problem in hackathons: how do judges know that a submitted project was actually built by the team during the event? Instead of relying solely on the final repository, HackProof creates an evidence-backed provenance trail by analyzing GPG/SSH commit identities, Git tracking and concealment signals, commit timestamps and chronology, and GitHub activity through webhooks and repository data. These independent signals are correlated into a single integrity report, helping judges identify inconsistencies such as unsigned or unregistered commits, suspicious timestamp patterns, hidden tracking states, or activity that doesn't align with the claimed development timeline.

HackProof doesn't ask judges to blindly trust the code- it gives them evidence to make that judgment.

description.title: Software
description.body:
1. Real-World Problem + Autonomous Solution: Negotia AI addresses the real-world challenge of slow and repetitive contract negotiation by using autonomous AI agents to negotiate between Buyer and Seller.
2. Cross-Domain Innovation: The platform is not limited to one industry; it can be adapted for SaaS, healthcare, finance, procurement, manufacturing, logistics, and enterprise contracts.
3. Multi-Agent Collaboration: Separate Buyer and Seller agents represent different objectives, constraints, and negotiation strategies, creating a genuine multi-agent environment.
4. Goal-Oriented Decision Making: Each agent works toward its party's goals while respecting hard and soft constraints, rather than simply generating text.
5. Autonomous Negotiation: Agents independently analyze clauses, propose changes, evaluate counteroffers, make concessions, and continue negotiations across multiple rounds.
6. Intelligent Conflict Resolution: Arbiter-3 evaluates conflicting requirements and trade-offs to determine whether a compromise is acceptable.
7. Bounded Agentic Behavior: The Negotiation Controller limits rounds and time while monitoring progress, preventing agents from negotiating indefinitely.
8. Deadlock Detection: When both parties have incompatible hard constraints, Negotia does not force an agreement. It identifies the conflict and intelligently terminates the negotiation.
9. State & Memory: Negotiation checkpoints preserve agreed clauses, unresolved issues, offers, concessions, and constraints, allowing negotiations to resume without starting from scratch.
10. Explainable AI Decisions: Every major outcome—agreement, concession, or deadlock—can be supported by a clear decision rationale and negotiation history.
11. Scalable Open Architecture: Components such as document validation, contract ingestion, negotiation strategies, arbitration, and reporting can be extended or replaced for different use cases.
12. Beyond a Traditional AI Chatbot: Unlike a simple LLM-based contract analyzer, Negotia demonstrates autonomy, planning, multi-agent interaction, state management, decision-making, feedback loops, and controlled termination.

Strong one-line positioning:

“Negotia AI brings Open Innovation to contract negotiation through Agentic AI—enabling autonomous, explainable, bounded negotiations that know when to compromise, when to agree, and when to stop.”

description.title: Software
description.body:
Here is the exact, high-conviction breakdown of why **ThermalGuard** is the ideal candidate and winning fit for the **Open Track (Open Innovation Track)**:

---

# 🏆 Why the Open Track Best Fits ThermalGuard

The **Open Track** is designed for projects that **defy narrow categories** and tackle massive, open-ended global challenges using creative cross-disciplinary engineering. 

ThermalGuard is the quintessential Open Track project for four distinct reasons:

---

### 1. It Fuses Four Major Tech Domains Into One Unified System
Most track-specific projects stay inside a comfortable silo (e.g., only Web3, only FinTech, or a simple chatbot). ThermalGuard breaks these boundaries by uniting:
* **SpaceTech / Remote Sensing:** Direct orbital ingestion from NASA FIRMS satellites (MODIS & VIIRS).
* **Applied Machine Learning:** Python-based XGBoost pipeline estimating Fire Radiative Power (FRP) and spread probability.
* **Geospatial & Spatial Mathematics:** DBSCAN clustering to aggregate scattered thermal pixels into unified fire perimeters, plus Haversine 25km emergency proximity calculations.
* **Civic Tech & Disaster Management:** Actionable ground-level dispatch targeting Fire (`101`), Police (`112`), and Trauma Hospitals (`108`).

Because it spans Aerospace, AI, Climate Tech, and Public Safety, no single restrictive track can capture its full scope—**it belongs in the Open Track**.

---

### 2. It Rejects "AI Wrapper" Tropes in Favor of Real Systems Engineering
In many open hackathon tracks, judges are overwhelmed by dozens of superficial ChatGPT wrappers with static UIs. 
ThermalGuard stands apart as **deep, practical systems engineering**:
* **Real Automated Testing:** 11/11 automated unit and integration test suites verifying data contracts, API coalescing, and ML model constraints.
* **Production Database Persistence:** Full local SQLite engine running in high-concurrency `WAL` mode to maintain audit trails and watch areas.
* **Optimized DevOps:** Solved Linux C-extension compilation bottlenecks on Render with automated binary wheel deployment.

---

### 3. The "Zero-Hallucination" Standard in Critical Systems
Open innovation awards solutions that are **safe and viable for real-world deployment**.
* In disaster response, hallucinated or simulated data can lead to tragic false dispatches.
* ThermalGuard incorporates strict **data provenance**: if satellite telemetry drops, it never invents synthetic coordinates; it serves authenticated, timestamped cached snapshots with explicit operator alerts.
* This level of operational maturity is rare in hackathon prototypes and immediately resonates with Open Track judges.

---

### 4. Unmatched Humanitarian & Planetary Impact
The Open Track often rewards projects with the **highest ceiling of real-world impact**:
* **Climate Crisis:** Wildfires and agricultural stubble burns emit gigatons of carbon, decimate ecosystems, and trigger severe health and air pollution crises.
* **The Last-Mile Solution:** ThermalGuard does not just visualize the crisis—it provides the missing link between NASA orbiters and local emergency responders on the ground.

---

# 📝 Ready-to-Use Submission Blurb (For Forms & Pitch Decks)

> **Why Open Track?**  
> *"ThermalGuard fits the Open Track because it represents open, boundary-defying innovation at the intersection of SpaceTech, Climate Resilience, and Civic Emergency Response. Rather than building a conventional web app or a generic LLM wrapper, we engineered an end-to-end disaster intelligence system that bridges NASA orbital satellites, DBSCAN spatial clustering, Python XGBoost ML, and ground-level 25km emergency dispatch infrastructure. With zero-hallucination data integrity, full SQLite persistence, and 11 automated test suites, ThermalGuard represents the highest standard of open-domain engineering built to solve an urgent planetary crisis."*

description.title: Best Beginner
description.body:
# 🎯 1. Why Apply for the Beginner Track? (Accurate Reasons)

In hackathons, the **Beginner Track** is not just for trivial "hello world" apps; it is meant for **teams exploring new, complex engineering domains for the first time** and demonstrating an extraordinary learning curve.

Here are the precise, authentic reasons to state:

### A. First Time Building with Remote Sensing & Geospatial Tech
* **The Reality:** Our team had **zero prior background in satellite remote-sensing, GIS (Geographic Information Systems), or orbital data ingestion**.
* **What We Learned From Scratch:**
  * How to query and parse live orbital telemetry from **NASA FIRMS satellites (MODIS & VIIRS)**.
  * How to implement spatial clustering algorithms (**DBSCAN**) to mathematically aggregate scattered heat pixels into cohesive firefronts.
  * How to integrate interactive multi-basemap engines (**Google Maps JS API, OpenStreetMap, Three.js**).

### B. Overcoming Multi-Language & Multi-Tier Architecture Challenges
* Building a beginner project typically means a single-file script or a simple frontend template. Instead, our team stepped outside our comfort zone to connect:
  * **Frontend:** React 19 interactive geospatial dashboard.
  * **Backend & Persistence:** Node.js server with SQLite write-ahead logging (`WAL`) and automated caching.
  * **Machine Learning:** A separate Python pipeline running **XGBoost** for fire radiative power and spread risk estimation.
  * **DevOps & Cloud:** Solving real-world production deployment hurdles on **Render** (resolving Linux C-compilation bottlenecks with binary wheels) and **GitHub Pages**.

### C. Competitive Edge in the Beginner Track
* Beginner track judges look for **ambition, learning speed, and execution**.
* While most beginner projects are mock e-commerce sites or basic chatbot wrappers, **ThermalGuard is an end-to-end, working full-stack system with 11 automated test suites, zero-hallucination data integrity, and live cloud deployment**. This makes it an exceptionally strong contender for top honors in the beginner category.

---

# 🌍 2. Why ThermalGuard is an Impactful Project

Judges and evaluators care deeply about **real-world relevance**. Here is why ThermalGuard carries profound real-world impact:

### A. Solves the Critical "Last-Mile" Emergency Gap
* **The Problem:** Satellites detect fires 24/7, but the data sits in scientific portals that rural fire departments and local police cannot access or interpret.
* **The Impact:** ThermalGuard doesn't just show a dot—it calculates the **nearest Fire Stations (`101`)**, **Police (`112`)**, and **Hospitals (`108`) within 25 km** and auto-generates a one-click **Emergency Dispatch Dossier**. It bridges the gap between orbit and the ground.

### B. Climate & Environmental Protection
* **Wildfires & Stubble Burning:** Uncontrolled fires release gigatons of $CO_2$, destroy biodiversity, and cause catastrophic seasonal air pollution (especially across agricultural belts in North India and global forest regions).
* **Early Intervention:** Extinguishing a fire within the first 30–60 minutes requires a fraction of the water, personnel, and cost compared to fighting an out-of-control crown wildfire. ThermalGuard provides that early-warning window.

### C. Life-Safety Through "Zero-Hallucination" Design
* In emergency tech, bad data costs lives.
* Many modern AI projects blindly generate synthetic data when an API fails. ThermalGuard enforces strict **data provenance**: if NASA APIs experience downtime, it serves authenticated, timestamped cached snapshots with clear warnings, never fabricating false fire coordinates.

> **Why Beginner Track?**  
> *"Our team consists of first-time builders in geospatial engineering and satellite remote-sensing. Entering this hackathon, we had never worked with orbital telemetry or spatial clustering algorithms. Over the course of the event, we pushed through a steep learning curve—integrating NASA FIRMS satellite data, implementing DBSCAN clustering, building a Python XGBoost ML pipeline, and architecting an authenticated Node.js/SQLite backend with full test coverage and live cloud deployment."*
>
> **What is the Impact?**  
> *"ThermalGuard addresses the deadly latency between when a wildfire ignites and when emergency crews respond. By converting raw NASA satellite heat readings into clustered firefronts and instantly mapping the nearest emergency stations (Fire, Police, Trauma) within 25 km with ready-to-use dispatch dossiers, ThermalGuard slashes response times from hours to minutes—protecting lives, ecosystems, and rural communities."*

description.title: Best Girl Team
description.body:
As a team of three women engineers, we deliberately chose to tackle one of India’s most notoriously male-dominated, overlooked, and unsafe sectors: the informal construction and daily-wage labour market.

Here is why our background and perspective make LabourLink uniquely aligned with this track:

1. Designing with Empathy for Vulnerable Female Daily-Wage Workers
The Hidden Reality of Women at Labour Chowks: Women comprise over 30% of India’s informal daily-wage workforce (helpers, brick-carriers, painters, cleaners, and agricultural laborers).
Safety & Harassment on Roadside Curbs: While male workers face physical hardship standing at chowks, women face severe safety hazards, catcalling, and exploitation while waiting on roadside curbs before dawn.
Wage Inequality: Women informal laborers are routinely paid 20% to 35% less than their male counterparts for the exact same hours of heavy manual labor.
Our Impact: By digitizing the chowk through an AI voice assistant accessible from home, female laborers no longer have to endure unsafe street corners or predatory middlemen. The transparent, published daily wage system ensures pay parity and dignity for women workers.
2. Reimagining "Laxmi": An Empathetic, Trust-First Voice Interface
Traditional software systems are built with text-heavy forms, bureaucratic jargon, and cold interfaces.
We intentionally engineered our Conversational Voice AI persona—Laxmi—to speak with patience, warmth, and high emotional resonance in regional languages (Hindi, Bengali, English).
For a marginalized or first-time smartphone user, speaking to a reassuring female voice dispatcher lowers intimidation, establishes trust, and provides an approachable entry point into the digital economy.
3. Women Engineers Tackling Deep Tech & Hardcore Systems
Often, women-led projects are pigeonholed into conventional lifestyle or health domains. We wanted to shatter that stereotype by tackling complex, low-latency deep-tech engineering:
Writing custom low-level in-memory PCM-to-WAV binary header synthesis in Dart to enable real-time streaming audio playback on Android devices.
Architecting a bidirectional bridge uniting modern WebSockets, telephony telecom carriers (Exotel/Twilio), and cloud databases (Supabase/PostgreSQL).
Building production-ready cross-platform experiences on Flutter and Node.js.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Sui's SDK moved out from under us. Partway through the build we discovered @mysten/dapp-kit had just been superseded by a new architecture (dapp-kit-core plus a gRPC client) — most tutorials online still reference the old one. We ended up reading the installed package's own TypeScript definitions directly rather than trust outdated examples.

A real bug in our first contract draft. An early version of the escrow module had @0xS as a placeholder address — S isn't a valid hex digit, so it failed to even compile. sui move test caught it immediately, a good reminder to run the actual compiler early.

Environment setup ate real time. Getting the Sui CLI running meant discovering Windows PowerShell isn't a Unix shell, setting up WSL, and learning that a Windows username and a WSL username aren't the same thing — small things, but each cost a debugging round before we could start building.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Campus marketplace groups — Facebook, Telegram, WhatsApp — run entirely on trust. A buyer sends payment first and just hopes the seller ships; there's no recourse if they don't, and no way to verify a stranger's reputation.

Vault fixes this with an escrow smart contract on Sui. The buyer's payment locks on-chain the moment they pay. The seller ships, the buyer confirms receipt, and only then does the money move — or, if the buyer goes silent past a deadline, the seller can claim the funds directly, so they're never left holding an unpaid item either. zkLogin means a buyer can do all of this signing in with a Google account, no wallet experience required, and sponsored transactions mean they never need to hold SUI just to pay gas.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body:
Vault builds directly on the track's own idea list: campus payments and escrow, combined into one product. A buyer locks a stablecoin payment into a Move contract at purchase; the seller ships; funds release the moment the buyer confirms — or automatically to the seller if the buyer goes silent past a deadline, so both sides are protected without a middleman holding the money.

It also uses both Sui features the brief calls out directly: zkLogin lets a buyer sign in with a Google account instead of managing a seed phrase, and sponsored transactions mean that buyer never needs to hold SUI just to pay gas. Programmable Transaction Blocks tie the lock-and-release logic together as a single atomic on-chain action.

tiba-f440.name: Tiba
tiba-f440.tagline: Software pays people. Policy holds the line.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
The first working version took 45 seconds per payment — too slow for a stage demo. The two checks were running one after the other instead of at the same time; fixing that was the first win.
Response times on the router varied about tenfold depending on which node answered. We now send each check to two models at once and take the first valid answer.
One model kept "thinking out loud" before answering and ran out of space before giving us anything usable, so we dropped it.
Another returned oddly padded answers when we asked for strict JSON, so we validate every answer ourselves instead of trusting the format.
The router doesn't accept images, so evidence is text only for this submission.
Our deployment shipped with no styling for a while because a build plugin was missing. Nobody had looked at a rendered page — only at status codes. Lesson learned.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
When software needs to pay a person, a human still has to approve every transfer. That works at ten payments a day and breaks at ten thousand, and nobody gets paid at 2am or on a weekend. Meanwhile the person waiting is a freelancer or contractor who did the work, and the person on the hook if the software pays the wrong claim is the operator who switched it on.

Tiba lets software pay a person without a human approving each transfer, and keeps that safe with limits set once in advance. When an agent asks to pay someone, Tiba runs two separate checks through GonkaRouter: one reads the delivery note or invoice, the other reads our own records and never sees the note. Both have to name the same person and the same amount. If they disagree, Tiba refuses. No averaging, no tie-break. Then the operator's limits apply — a cap per payment, caps per hour and per day, a list of who can be paid, and a kill switch — and the payment settles on the Sui test network with a public receipt showing exactly why it was paid or refused.

Proof, on the test network, not a mock: 20 out of 20 legitimate payouts paid, 10 out of 10 tampered claims refused, no false refusals, about 13 seconds per decision.

Not included: real money, mainnet, KYC, cross-border compliance, image-based evidence. Settlement uses the network's own coin as a stand-in for USDC until test USDC is available.

**AI tools used during development.** This project was built by a team in which the founder directs AI coding agents rather than writing most code by hand. Tools used: Claude Code (Anthropic) — primary agent for architecture, implementation, review, and documentation; OpenAI Codex CLI — delegated implementation slices, research, and independent review of Claude Code's output. GonkaRouter is used inside the product as the verification layer, not as a development tool. Problem selection, product scope, every design decision, the pitch, and the demo were human-directed. No part of this submission is represented as entirely human-written code; most commits were agent-generated under human direction inside the hackathon window.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body: Tiba solves a real payment workflow: paying freelancers and contractors the moment a delivery is verified, instead of waiting for a human to open a banking app. An operator registers work orders and recipients once; the agent submits payout intents; Tiba verifies, applies policy, and settles on Sui testnet in one atomic step, with a PTB for batch payouts. The recipient opens a public receipt with the settlement digest and the reason if refused. Settlement today uses SUI as a stand-in for USDC on testnet; sponsored transactions so recipients never hold gas are the next step. Real digests are in the repo README.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body: You asked for AI agents with on-chain wallets executing agentic payments. Tiba is the harder half: agent-to-human. A person can't be rolled back, so the agent gets a bounded ability to pay — per-transfer ceiling, rolling caps, allowlist, kill switch, idempotency — enforced in one atomic debit before a Sui testnet transaction is signed. Verification runs through GonkaRouter; settlement is a real Sui transaction with a digest on every receipt. Complete rather than complex: an operator console, a ledger where refusals sit beside payments, and a public receipt page, all live at tiba-omega.vercel.app.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
Tiba lets software pay a person with no human approving each transfer, with policy caps as the boundary. GonkaRouter is load-bearing: two isolated channels — one reads the untrusted invoice text, one reads the payer's own records and never sees the invoice — must agree on who is owed and how much before money moves.
Disagreement is a refusal, never a tie-break. Every outcome gets a public receipt showing both Gonka request IDs. Proof on testnet: 20/20 clean payouts paid, 10/10 adversarial claims refused, 0 false refusals. The person paid gets paid in seconds; the operator is protected from an autonomous system paying the wrong claim.

muba-project-5d16.name: NutShell
muba-project-5d16.tagline: Options on Thetanuts Finance V4, in a nutshell🥜

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Four of the six assets looked identical to the SDK. Keying the order book on underlyingToken is the obvious move and it is wrong. On the live Base book only ETH and BTC carry a real token: SOL, BNB, XRP and AVAX are cash-settled and all four report the zero address, so keyed by token they collapse into one bucket and a trader asking for SOL gets BNB strikes at XRP prices. We re-keyed the book on the Chainlink price feed each order carries, using a registry that excludes any feed nobody has verified. The same bug had a second half: the payout asset was derived as isCall ? "WETH" : "USDC", which tells a SOL call buyer they will receive WETH.

A restart during a sealed-bid auction destroyed money. Opening a request commits a reserve price on-chain and then waits, sometimes an hour. The keypair that decrypts maker offers lived in memory, so any deploy or crash in that window left a funded, live quotation whose bids nobody could ever read, with no recovery. We now persist the request before the browser is handed anything to sign, and a request already open on-chain is kept and marked cancelled instead of deleted.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
The problem it solves
Someone holding crypto who expects a fall has two moves: sell, or ride it down. Options are the third, and almost nobody makes it, not because the idea is hard. Every options interface opens with strikes, expiries and greeks, and none of them answer the only question a beginner actually has: if I'm wrong, what does this cost me?

The fear behind that question is well founded. Options really can lose you more than you put in, but only if you sell them. Buying one has a floor: the premium, and nothing past it. Mainstream interfaces put the safe half and the dangerous half behind the same screen and leave you to work out which one you are doing.

Borrowers face a sharper version, because the first move is not available to them at all. Collateral deposited on Aave is locked, so a falling price is not something you can sell your way out of. You watch the health factor slide toward a liquidation penalty and hope. A put is the instrument that helps, but pricing one against your own loan means knowing your liquidation price, choosing a strike above it, and sizing it against your debt: three pieces of arithmetic before you have even opened an order book.

NutShell is two doors onto the same thing. Say what you think will happen, and it finds a real order on the live Thetanuts book, explains it in plain English, and states the most you can lose before you commit. Or hand it the address of an Aave loan, and it reads the position, derives the liquidation price Aave itself would use, and prices the put that pays out in USDC if the collateral falls past it. No sentence, no model, just arithmetic.

It only ever buys. That single constraint is what makes everything else honest: your maximum loss is exactly the premium you paid, it is knowable before you sign, and the interface can say so with no asterisk attached.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/526facf98c0f4cf4ac5263d1004ea168/7f8f9c9f-219a-40b5-95d7-8220e6fec7f7.png)

description.title: BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK
description.body: Liquidation Cover uses options for a lending problem rather than for trading. It reads a borrower's Aave V3 loan on Base, computes the liquidation price from Aave's own oracle, sets a strike 10% above it, and buys a cash-settled put. Thetanuts V4 options are European, so the cover does not stop the liquidation, it compensates for it: the payout arrives at expiry, and the 10% buffer widens the band of price outcomes on which it finishes in the money, so a borrower who is liquidated is paid back rather than paid nothing. The surface says exactly that, because a borrower who thinks they are protected in real time will not act.

description.title: AI × OPTIONS
description.body:
The Copilot turns a sentence into a real order from the live Thetanuts book on Base mainnet, priced against live orders rather than paper or testnet. A strategy agent reads technical indicators and suggests trades against the user's saved risk profile, and records which suggestions they accept.
The AI safety design is the part worth judging. The model selects which order to look at and never produces a number the trader reads: every price and payoff is recalculated server-side from the live book after the model has chosen. A suggestion crosses the agent boundary as a bare trade intent and nothing else, enforced by the schema. The review agent can only veto, never approve. Forecasts are kept out of the trade flow by the import graph, not by a prompt. Practice mode is a separate route whose module cannot reach a signer, with a test that walks the imports to keep it that way.

clubtreasuryai-de78.name: ClubTreasury AI
clubtreasuryai-de78.tagline: AI-powered club treasury with Sui payouts

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
University clubs manage event budgets, receipts, reimbursement claims, and approvals across spreadsheets and chat messages. Treasurers struggle to see remaining budgets, spot duplicate claims, and prove that approved payments were actually made.

ClubTreasury AI brings this into one auditable workflow:

1. A treasurer connects a Sui Testnet wallet and creates a persisted club treasury workspace.
2. Gemini turns natural-language budget instructions into editable categories. Deterministic rules verify the totals, and the treasurer confirms the budget before activating it through separate Create, Fund, and Allocate wallet-signed Sui transactions using native Circle Testnet USDC.
3. Members join the active treasury with a short code and submit reimbursement claims with private receipt images. Gemini extracts receipt facts and suggests categories; deterministic TypeScript checks amounts, duplicates, required evidence, and remaining budgets.
4. The human treasurer reviews the recommendation and approves or rejects the claim. AI cannot authorize or sign a payment.
5. For an approved claim, the treasurer explicitly signs a Sui transaction. Move enforces treasury authorization, category limits, and custody sufficiency. The application marks the claim paid only after verifying finality and the exact payout event.

**Why Sui:** Our Move Treasury<Asset> holds funds on-chain, TreasurerCap<Asset> controls authorization, and typed PayoutEvent records provide public execution evidence. Receipts remain private and off-chain.

**Why AI:** Gemini handles unstructured budget language and receipt images. Validated outputs support human decisions while deterministic rules remain authoritative for money.

**Track fit:** Payments & Stablecoins — a working USDC treasury and reimbursement workflow with spending controls. AI × Sui — useful financial understanding connected to Sui custody and human-approved execution.

**Demo video:** https://youtu.be/VLn7P-Cy6tQ

**AI tools declaration:** ChatGPT and OpenAI Codex were used for planning, coding, debugging, documentation, and verification. Google Gemini Developer API powers the product's budget parsing and receipt analysis. This is a Testnet MVP; zkLogin, sponsored transactions, and multisignature approval are future work.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
The hardest challenge was keeping a human-approved reimbursement consistent across the database, wallet, and Sui when a network response was interrupted or ambiguous. An early live acceptance test exposed a duplicate-payment defect. We preserved that incident in the repository and fixed the payment lifecycle: immutable approved payout snapshots, one active payment attempt, transaction-digest persistence before broadcast, and reconciliation of the same digest instead of blindly creating a replacement payment. The successful deployed rehearsal produced one confirmed payout; refreshing preserved its Paid state without another signature or payment attempt.

We also had to prevent stale database balances from producing a misleading payment request. A server-side Supabase-to-Sui consistency check now blocks signing if the treasury states disagree, and paid/budget updates happen only after finality and exact PayoutEvent verification.

AI receipt interpretation can be incomplete or ambiguous. We validate Gemini's structured responses, use integer/base-unit arithmetic for authoritative financial checks, and fall back to human Review when evidence is invalid or conflicting. AI never owns balances or wallet keys.

Receipt privacy required a separate off-chain evidence path. We use private Supabase Storage, row-level access policies, wallet-bound identity, image validation, and receipt hashing for duplicate detection, while publishing only the necessary on-chain payment evidence.

Another integration hurdle was allocation reconciliation: database row ordering could differ from the on-chain category order. We fixed it by matching exact category-reference/amount pairs independently of row order.

The final repository state is deployed and verified. Latest main commit: 5cba11397901d1710cf2dbb4fc86c5223739c356

GitHub Actions CI run #253 passed lint, TypeScript type checks, 290 unit tests, production build, Chromium setup, and all 10 Playwright smoke/E2E tests. The deployed Move package also retains 31/31 passing Move tests, and Vercel successfully deployed the latest main commit.

These challenges shaped our final architecture:

Gemini AI → Deterministic Rules → Human Decision → Sui On-chain

oronyx-8ece.name: Oronyx
oronyx-8ece.tagline: Policy-enforced AI agent wallets on Sui Blockchain

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
AI agents are increasingly being trusted to act autonomously with real money — trading, rebalancing, staking — but almost every "agentic finance" demo today relies on the same weak guarantee: a system prompt or app-level setting telling the agent what it's "supposed" to do. If the agent misbehaves, is prompt-injected, or the backend is compromised, there is nothing structurally stopping it from moving funds outside the user's intent.

Oronyx solves this by moving policy enforcement on-chain. When a user sets up an agent, they describe their rules in plain language — spending limits, which actions are allowed, which targets are whitelisted, how risk-averse the agent should be. This gets compiled into a Move capability object on Sui that structurally gates every action the agent can take. The agent's backend never holds a blank check — it holds a scoped, revocable, on-chain-enforced permission slip.

Concretely, this means:

- An agent literally *cannot* exceed a spending limit, act on a non-whitelisted address, or act past its expiry — not because it was told not to, but because the smart contract will abort the transaction.
- Anything above the user's risk threshold isn't silently auto-executed — it's parked on-chain for the user to explicitly approve or reject.
- The user can edit policy live (tighten a limit, revoke a target, deactivate the agent entirely) at any time, independent of whether the backend is online, trustworthy, or even compromised.

This is useful for anyone who wants the convenience of an autonomous financial agent — a rebalancer, a DCA bot, a staking optimizer — without having to fully trust the software running it.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
**Cetus testnet had no usable liquidity.** We built a full Programmable Transaction Block integration against Cetus's SDK, expecting to demo a real swap. Systematic testing — discovering real pools, correcting swap direction to match which side of the pool SUI actually sat on, verifying coin decimals — eventually surfaced Cetus's own zero-output abort (code 18) across every SUI-paired testnet pool we could find: the price ratios were too skewed to produce a meaningful output at reasonable test amounts. Rather than keep chasing a moving target, we built our own fixed-rate mock DEX as the demo's primary swap path, and kept the real Cetus integration fully implemented and reachable — a deliberate reliability decision, not an abandoned feature.

**Getting the trust model right took real iteration.** Our first design had the agent's capability object owned by the user's wallet address — which turned out to be a fundamental blocker: an address-owned object can only be used by a transaction that address itself signs, which would mean the user co-signing every single agent action, defeating the point of automation. We restructured to shared objects with explicit owner/operator fields checked in the contract logic instead, which is what actually enables autonomous execution while keeping the user as the sole authority over policy changes and approvals.

**Cetus's SDK doesn't compose the way we assumed.** We initially planned to chain our policy-check function's released funds directly into a Cetus swap call within one atomic transaction. Checking the SDK's actual installed type definitions (rather than trusting the docs) revealed it always builds its own transaction internally and selects its own input coins — there's no way to hand it an existing transaction or a specific coin. We resolved this by scoping the two-step, non-atomic pattern specifically to Cetus, while keeping every other action type (transfer, stake, mock swap) atomic and funds-never-leave-custody by default — this also became one of our core architectural principles going forward.

**Noodles.fi temporarily suspended on-chain API access for retail** We planned to use Noodles.fi API to poll market data in Sui Network, but in unfortunate turn of events, Noodles announced that they are temporarily suspending access to their API dashboard within the time frame of this hackathon. We instead opted to use market data from DeepBook.

**Reliably fine-tuning the agent decision-making to get desired action outcomes** The agent decision-making takes in real market trends data, agent cap, current vault balance and recent activity. Each variable input has to be carefully filtered to ensure predictable outcome for live demo simulation. For example, a long history of failed actions reinforces the agent's decision to withhold from making further actions, requiring clean up of activity logs or filtering redundant activities.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body:
Oronyx is built directly for this track's premise — Sui isn't an add-on storage layer here, it *is* the trust mechanism. The agent's authority is a Move capability object, not a database row; every policy check (spending limit, allowed target, risk threshold) is a contract-level assert, not application logic the agent could be tricked or misconfigured around.

We use several of the track's highlighted Sui features directly:
- **Programmable Transaction Blocks** are central to execution, not incidental — every atomic action type (transfer, stake, mock swap) completes policy-check-and-execute in a single PTB, so funds never leave the vault's custody boundary until they land at their real destination.
- **Sponsored transactions** using Enoki as sponsor remove gas as an onboarding barrier — a first-time user can create an agent and start using it without ever holding SUI themselves.
- **zkLogin** using Enoki service replaces wallet setup with a standard OAuth flow, so "connect" doesn't require the user to already be crypto-native.

The track asks for AI solving a real problem where Sui is integral, with thoughtful UX and a working live demo. Our real problem is trust: letting an AI agent act autonomously with money is currently a leap of faith. Oronyx turns that leap into a structural guarantee, backed by a live demo of an agent executing real policy-gated actions on testnet.

leaklens-b832.name: LeakLens
leaklens-b832.tagline: Know what's exposed. Know what to do.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
When your email shows up in a data leak, the existing tools tell you almost nothing useful. You get a list of company names and dates, no sense of how serious it actually is, no explanation of what was exposed, and no clear next step. Most people either panic over something minor or ignore something that actually matters.

There's also a trust problem most people don't think about: checking whether your own account was compromised means handing your email to whichever company runs the lookup, and trusting that they're not logging it themselves.

**LeakLens solves both problems.**

- Checks an email against known data leaks
- Runs the result through multiple independent AI models on Gonka Router, each one scores severity and explains in plain language what was actually exposed
- If the models disagree on how serious something is, that disagreement is shown rather than hidden, so you know when a verdict needs a second look
- Every inference step is backed by a visible Gonka Request ID, so the assessment can't be traced back to a centralised operator quietly logging your data

The result is a clear leak score, a plain-language explanation of what's actually at risk, and a prioritised checklist of what to secure first, instead of a bare list you have to interpret yourself.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
### **1. AI Rate-Limiting & Token Exhaustion**

While testing our multi-model consensus logic against the Gonka Router and XposedOrNot APIs, we quickly hit `429 Too Many Requests` errors. Spam-clicking the "Scan" button during UI testing was burning through our Gonka test network tokens and locking us out of the leak database.

* **How we got over it:** We implemented a strict client-side session cache (`SESSION_CACHE`) in our vanilla JavaScript frontend using Maps. If a user scans an email they've already checked during that session, the dashboard instantly serves the cached JSON payload instead of re-pinging the network. We paired this with strict UI debouncing, disabling the submit button and rendering a loading spinner while the dual-layer API pipeline resolves.

### **2. Decoupling the UI from Pending AI Logic**

Because we are a team of four, we couldn't afford to have the frontend developer sitting idle while the backend team engineered the Gonka API integration and cross-model prompt logic.

* **How we got over it:** We defined a strict JSON data contract on day one. We built the entire frontend using a hardcoded `MOCK_AI_VERDICT` object that mirrored the exact shape the Gonka Router would eventually return. We also engineered "graceful degradation" into the UI: if the AI consensus layer fails or the Gonka key isn't configured (returning a `503`), the dashboard doesn't crash. Instead, it gracefully displays an amber "Unavailable" badge for the AI score while still successfully rendering the underlying XposedOrNot breach data.

### **3. Late-Stage Git Merge Conflicts**

Working in a lightweight, zero-build-step environment (pure HTML/CSS/JS) meant multiple team members were frequently touching the same `app.js` and `style.css` files. Near the end of the build, pulling the backend API routes into the frontend branch resulted in a massive merge conflict that threatened to wipe out hours of UI styling.

* **How we got over it:** Rather than risking a broken file state by manually untangling Git conflict markers under a deadline, we executed a "clean clone" strategy. We cloned a fresh instance of the remote repository (`LeakLens-Clean`), manually injected our finalized UI files, and pushed the clean commit. We then had the whole team pull from `main`, resetting everyone to a unified, functional state.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
LeakLens fits the AI For Society track by democratizing personal cybersecurity and bridging the digital literacy gap.
Currently, when everyday internet users discover their data was exposed in a breach, they are met with technical jargon and intimidating statistics (e.g., "244 million records exposed"). They know they are at risk, but they do not understand the specific threat level, nor do they know what immediate actions to take.
LeakLens uses AI to translate raw breach data into personalized, actionable security intelligence. By leveraging the Gonka Router's multi-model consensus, our tool analyzes the specific combination of leaked data (e.g., plain-text passwords vs. just usernames) and outputs a plain-language Leak Score, a transparent Reasoning Trace, and concrete next steps.
Instead of fear-mongering, our decentralized AI provides unbiased, verifiable guidance. LeakLens empowers the average digital citizen to understand their actual risk exposure and take back control of their privacy without needing an IT background.

hackmate-ai-aipowered-hackathon-team-bui.name: HackMate AI — AI-Powered Hackathon Team Builder
hackmate-ai-aipowered-hackathon-team-bui.tagline: Smarter Matches. Stronger Teams. Better Hacks.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Turning "skills on paper" into a fair team split was harder than expected. Two 
people can list the same skill tag but mean very different levels of depth, so 
naive keyword matching gave misleading compatibility scores. We had to move 
toward embedding-based similarity and tune the balance between skill coverage 
and shared interest so the optimizer didn't just cluster people with identical 
skills together. Getting the explanation text to stay accurate to the actual 
scores — rather than generic filler — took a few iterations too.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Hackathon teams are usually formed by chance — whoever you happen to sit next to. 
That leads to overlapping skills, missing roles (no one covering design, or no one 
covering ML), and hours lost negotiating groups instead of building.

HackMate AI fixes this. Participants register their skills, interests, role, 
experience, availability, working style, and a short bio. The system uses NLP 
embeddings and skill-complementarity scoring to evaluate how well people's skills 
fit together, then an optimizer generates balanced teams — each with a skill 
coverage score, a compatibility score, and a plain-language explanation of why 
that group works. Participants can also use "Find My Teammates" to get ranked, 
individually-explained matches instead of a full team.

test-edc9.name: Puffer
test-edc9.tagline: A wallet that lets AI agents spend autonomously

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
AI agents can make valid on-chain transactions that are still unsafe.

For example, a trading agent may receive a convincing message to “claim a limited-time airdrop,” then send funds to an unfamiliar address. Nothing needs to hack the wallet or steal a private key—the agent simply misuses the authority it was given.

Puffer makes agent wallet automation safer without forcing a human to approve every routine action.

### What people can use it for

- Let an AI agent check balances and wallet status
- Retrieve live market data
- Dry-run transfers and trades before executing them
- Send SUI transfers
- Trade SUI/DBUSDC through DeepBook
- Review past wallet decisions and understand why an action was allowed, blocked, or escalated

### How it keeps those actions safe

Puffer gives agents a constrained MCP tool interface. They can request a transfer or swap, but they **cannot** submit arbitrary transaction code, change their own safety rules, add recipients, or approve a held transaction.

For each request, Puffer:

1. **Builds and simulates the real Sui transaction** before signing.
2. **Inspects predicted effects**—balance changes, recipients, invoked packages, object transfers, capability transfers, and failures.
3. **Applies hard guardrails** such as transaction limits, weekly spending caps, and recipient/package allowlists.
4. **Runs independent AI risk reviews** that can add caution, but can never bypass a safety rule.
5. **Routes risky actions to a human** for Ledger-backed approval.

### Why it matters

Puffer replaces the false choice between:

| Without Puffer | With Puffer |
| --- | --- |
| Give an agent unrestricted wallet access | Let the agent handle routine, policy-compliant actions |
| Approve every action manually | Escalate only unfamiliar, oversized, suspicious, or disputed actions |
| Trust an agent’s description of a transaction | Evaluate the simulated on-chain effects of the actual transaction |

The result is practical autonomy: agents can handle normal wallet tasks quickly, while the owner keeps hardware-backed control over actions that could put funds at risk.

> Currently built for MCP-compatible AI agents on **Sui testnet**.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
### Making AI risk checks reliable enough for wallet decisions

We use multiple AI models to review transaction risk, but inference was sometimes slow, timed out, or returned inconsistent responses. That was a problem because a wallet cannot safely treat an unavailable model as an approval.

We solved this by making AI reviews **fail closed**:

- Hard safety rules—such as spending caps, allowlists, and failed transaction simulations—always run independently of AI.
- Two separate low-risk model reviews are needed before an action can proceed automatically.
- If a review fails, times out, disagrees, or flags risk, the transaction is escalated to **Ledger-backed human approval**.

This means model instability reduces automation, not security.

### Enforcing human approval beyond a dashboard button

A major challenge was making sure a “human review required” decision could not be bypassed by the backend. If the server could still sign and submit the transaction on its own, the approval flow would only be a UI promise.

We addressed this using native Sui multisig wallets. Routine actions can use the spending wallet, while escalated actions are rebuilt from a protected wallet that requires both the platform signature and the owner’s Ledger signature. The human approval is therefore enforced directly by the wallet’s on-chain signing rule.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body:
Puffer is an **AI wallet agent safety layer built directly around Sui execution**.

Instead of merely showing blockchain data, Puffer lets MCP-compatible AI agents take real actions: inspect wallet balances, retrieve DeepBook market data, dry-run transfers and swaps, and execute approved transactions on **Sui testnet**.

Sui is integral to the product:

- **Programmable Transaction Blocks** are built server-side from typed agent intents, then simulated before signing.
- **Native Sui multisig** enforces Puffer’s two-level approval model:
  - a spending wallet for routine, policy-compliant actions;
  - a protected wallet for escalated actions that requires a human Ledger signature.
- **On-chain simulation** lets Puffer assess the predicted effects of the *actual transaction*—including balance changes, recipients, invoked packages, and object/capability transfers.
- **DeepBook v3** provides live SUI/DBUSDC market data and swap execution.
- **Sponsored transactions** remove gas-management friction for the agent-wallet workflow.

Puffer addresses a real problem in agentic finance: AI agents need enough authority to be useful, but not so much that one manipulated or mistaken request can move funds unchecked. It makes Sui-based wallet automation practical by allowing routine actions to proceed while routing unfamiliar, oversized, suspicious, or disputed transactions to hardware-backed human approval.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
Puffer is an AI safety tool for a growing public-interest problem: **how people can safely delegate financial actions to AI agents**.

As agents become able to pay, trade, and execute on-chain actions, users face an unsafe trade-off: either give the agent unrestricted wallet control, or manually approve every transaction and lose the benefits of automation. Puffer creates a safer middle ground.

For every requested transfer or swap, Puffer uses the **Gonka Router** to obtain independent AI risk reviews from multiple model providers. The models assess evidence from the simulated transaction, such as the destination, amount, invoked packages, and asset/object movements.

The AI review system is designed to be cautious and explainable:

- **Two independent low-risk reviews** are required for automatic execution.
- A model timeout, failure, disagreement, or risk flag causes the action to escalate to human review.
- AI can **add caution**, but it can never bypass deterministic protections such as spending caps, allowlists, or failed simulations.
- Puffer records the decision, the agent’s reason, and the rule/evidence behind the outcome for later inspection.

This makes Gonka-powered AI verification useful in a high-stakes setting: not as an opaque “trust the model” decision-maker, but as a multi-model safety layer that helps prevent AI agents from misusing delegated financial authority.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
SmartWaste: Transforming Waste Management Through Digital Innovation

A Comprehensive Digital Recycling Ecosystem

SmartWaste is a digital platform designed to make recycling more convenient, rewarding, and accessible. It connects users with verified recycling centers through an integrated mapping system while allowing them to track their recycling history, monitor environmental impact, and earn money from recyclable materials.

A key innovation is the Group Pickup feature, which allows users heading to the same recycling center to coordinate and share transportation. This reduces individual transportation costs while minimizing unnecessary trips and associated carbon emissions. By turning recycling into a collaborative activity, SmartWaste makes sustainable waste management more affordable and accessible to communities.

SmartWaste also uses a points-based reward system to encourage consistent recycling habits. Users earn points through recycling activities and can redeem them for rewards from participating brands such as GrabFood, McDonald's, KFC, Tealive, and Starbucks.

Operational Efficiency and Economic Value

SmartWaste provides real-time pricing information for recyclable materials such as aluminum, copper, and electronic waste, helping users understand the potential value of their materials and make informed recycling decisions.

Users can track their earnings, recycling history, and estimated carbon savings through a centralized dashboard. The Group Pickup system also automatically calculates how transportation costs are shared between participants, providing transparency over individual costs and savings.

Safety, Security, and Community Trust

SmartWaste prioritizes user security through secure authentication, password hashing, session management, and transaction records. Notifications provide users with updates on important activities such as completed transactions and payment confirmations.

The platform also promotes community engagement through leaderboards and achievement systems, encouraging positive competition and recognizing users for their environmental contributions.

Creating Measurable Impact

SmartWaste brings recycling-center discovery, shared transportation, material pricing, digital payments, rewards, and environmental tracking together in one platform. By combining convenience with financial and social incentives, SmartWaste transforms recycling from an inconvenient task into a rewarding community experience.

Ultimately, SmartWaste aims to turn waste into value while encouraging sustainable habits and supporting a more efficient circular economy.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Development Challenges & Solutions

Map Rendering and Location Services

The Problem

One of the main challenges I encountered was getting the interactive map to render reliably. SmartWaste uses Leaflet.js with OpenStreetMap to display recycling centers and user locations, but the map would sometimes appear as a grey box, with tiles failing to load or markers appearing in incorrect positions.

The main cause was that the map was initialized while its container was hidden inside a page tab. Since the container had no dimensions at the time, Leaflet could not correctly calculate the map's size and positioning. This caused rendering issues when users later opened the Locator page.

The Solution

I solved this using a lazy initialization and forced recalculation approach. Instead of initializing the map immediately, it is created when the Locator tab is first opened, ensuring that the container has proper dimensions. I also trigger a map resize whenever users return to the Locator tab to prevent rendering issues when switching between pages.

I implemented a fallback location system as well. If users deny location permissions or location services are unavailable, the map still loads using default coordinates and displays the available recycling centers instead of failing completely.

The Geolocation Challenge

Another challenge was providing users with clear feedback while their location was being obtained. Geolocation can take several seconds because the browser must request permission and acquire the user's coordinates.

To improve the experience, I implemented status indicators that show different stages such as "Waiting," "Requesting," "Success," and "Error." Once the location is obtained, the user's coordinates and location marker are displayed on the map. This makes the process more transparent and prevents users from assuming the application is unresponsive.

### The Distance Calculation Challenge

I also needed an accurate way to calculate the distance between users and recycling centers. I implemented the haversine formula to calculate distances based on latitude and longitude coordinates.

For usability, distances below one kilometer are displayed in meters, while longer distances are displayed in kilometers. I also implemented dynamic sorting so that recycling centers are automatically arranged from nearest to farthest based on the user's current location.

This required recalculating distances whenever the user's location changed and updating the displayed results without refreshing the page. As a result, users can immediately see the most convenient recycling options based on their location.

mova-c2ae.name: MOVA
mova-c2ae.tagline: The Intelligent Layer of Digital Money Movement

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
The Problem: **Fragmentation & Trust Friction in Digital Money Movement**

- Both small merchants (SMEs) and retail users face heavy friction when moving money across disconnected financial ecosystems. From payment methods and compliance to AI-generated reports and on-chain execution, four key barriers limit seamless and trusted money movement.

- First, funds and payment options are fragmented across multiple platforms, making everyday retail checkouts, QR payments, and SME asset transfers slow and inefficient.

- In addition, traditional compliance checks remain manual and cumbersome, creating operational bottlenecks when enforcing strict AML/CFT regulatory standards before payment execution.

- Also, businesses relying on AI-generated financial audit reports lack cryptographic verification, leaving them uncertain about the accuracy and legal authenticity of their records.

- Finally, navigating cross-chain and off-chain execution introduces technical risks, latency, and security vulnerabilities during final settlement. Web3 still lacks smart financial systems that can understand what users want and automatically complete transactions. This makes it difficult to connect digital assets smoothly with the existing Web2 economy.
