description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
**1. Gonka Router does not support vision/image inputs**
We initially designed the medicine scanner to send photos directly to vision-capable AI models on Gonka. After deployment, every attempt returned a 400 error — Gonka's current models don't accept image_url content. We rebuilt the pipeline to use Tesseract.js for local OCR first, then send the extracted text to Gonka for structuring and medical knowledge enrichment. This actually improved accuracy for text-heavy labels.

**2. DeepSeek's <think> blocks swallowed the JSON**
DeepSeek V4 Flash generates a long internal reasoning block wrapped in <think>...</think> before outputting the answer. Our original code stripped these blocks before JSON parsing — but for complex prompts like fact-checking, DeepSeek placed the JSON *inside* the think block. Stripping it deleted the answer entirely. We fixed this by returning both the raw and stripped content from every model call, then searching for JSON in three passes: after the last </think> tag, in the stripped text, and anywhere in the raw response.

**3. max_tokens too low caused truncated responses**
Setting max_tokens: 450 for the fact-checker wasn't enough for DeepSeek to finish reasoning AND output JSON. The response was cut off mid-think with no JSON produced. Raising to max_tokens: 1200 resolved this.

**4. False consensus from a single model**
When one model failed, the system calculated scoreDiff as 0 (one model agreeing with itself) and showed "Models agree" — which was misleading. We fixed this by tracking twoModels as a boolean, only computing real consensus when both models respond, and using the tertiary model as a genuine second opinion when needed.

**5. iOS Safari camera bug**
The medicine scanner used JavaScript .click() on a hidden file input to open the camera. iOS Safari silently blocked this when called through a function chain. We fixed it by using a <label for="medicine-photo-input"> element instead, which creates a direct browser-native link to the file input that iOS Safari always respects.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Millions of elderly people in Southeast Asia are cared for by families who live far away and caregivers who lack efficient tools. Three problems go unsolved every day:

**1. Medication confusion** — Elderly users manage multiple medicines with complex instructions in languages they may not read well. Missed doses and misread labels are common and dangerous.

**2. Social isolation and language barriers** — Most AI companions only speak English or Mandarin. Grandparents who speak Cantonese, Hokkien, Hakka, or Bahasa Melayu are left out entirely.

**3. Health misinformation** — Elderly users regularly receive unverified health claims through WhatsApp groups with no way to fact-check them.

MORY solves all three: a voice-first elderly companion in 6 Southeast Asian dialects, an AI-powered medicine scanner that reads labels and explains what each medicine does in plain language, and a Health Fact Checker that uses Gonka's decentralised multi-model consensus to return a verified Truth Score for any health claim — with transparent Gonka Request IDs proving every inference ran on the decentralised network.

medifindaiengine-1d2a.name: medifind-ai-engine
medifindaiengine-1d2a.tagline: Verifying local drug availability and bio-equivale

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
### High Healthcare Costs & Generic Unawareness

Patients frequently overpay for expensive branded medications simply because they lack clear, instant visibility into lower-cost generic alternatives that contain identical active ingredients and deliver 50% to 75% cost savings.

### Local Inventory Uncertainty

Finding specific formulations or available generic substitutes often forces patients to physically visit multiple retail pharmacies, resulting in wasted time, frustration, and potential treatment delays caused by localized stockouts.

### Verification Overhead for Healthcare Providers

Patients and pharmacists need a fast, centralized way to verify active ingredient bio-equivalence, check dosage instructions, and review key clinical warnings before safely switching to a generic alternative.

---

### How MediFind Solves This

* **Instant Generic Alternative Engine:** Automatically indexes thousands of drug formulations, mapping brand-name medications to their active ingredients to display direct, bio-equivalent generic substitutes.
* **Dual-AI Safety & Supply Verification:** Orchestrates parallel AI inference via Gonka Gateway—utilizing **Kimi-K2.6** for clinical bio-equivalence and dosage evaluation, alongside **DeepSeek-V4** for regional retail store stock estimations.
* **Dynamic Consumer Cost Savings Calculator:** Calculates immediate monthly and annual cost savings (in RM), empowering patients to make financially informed healthcare choices.
* **Automated Pharmacist Brief Generation:** Produces downloadable, audit-ready clinical summaries with unique request IDs to ensure safe consultation between patients and healthcare professionals.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
### Dual-Model API Concurrency & Rate Limits (HTTP 429)

* **The Challenge:** Running dual-model orchestration (Kimi-K2.6 for safety and DeepSeek-V4 for supply) via `ThreadPoolExecutor` triggered API rate limits (`429 Too Many Concurrent Requests`).
* **The Fix:** Implemented exponential backoff retry loops, thread submission staggering (`time.sleep(0.3)`), and graceful fallback data structures to prevent complete application failure during rate limit bursts.

### Multithread Exception Handling & UI Stability

* **The Challenge:** Uncaught exceptions inside parallel thread execution caused `ValueError` unpack crashes on `f_a.result()`, bringing down the entire Streamlit UI.
* **The Fix:** Wrapped all future result calls (`f_a.result()` and `f_b.result()`) in isolated `try-except` blocks to guarantee valid tuple returns and preserve UI responsiveness.

### Memory Optimization on Streamlit Cloud

* **The Challenge:** Ingesting the full production dataset (~147,000 medicine records) repeatedly exceeded Streamlit Cloud’s free-tier memory allocation limit (~1 GB RAM).
* **The Fix:** Optimized dataset handling using `@st.cache_data`, compressed `.csv.gz` storage, and added a dual-mode toggle ("Sample ~10k" vs. "Full ~147k") to keep memory footprints low during active user sessions.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
### Democratizing Healthcare Affordability

MediFind leverages AI to address prescription drug inflation by instantly mapping expensive brand-name medications to their unbranded generic equivalents. This provides patients with direct access to **50%–75% cost savings**, significantly reducing healthcare inequality for low-income families and chronic illness patients.

### Enhancing Patient Safety & Health Literacy

By utilizing clinical AI models (Kimi-K2.6), MediFind translates complex active ingredient data into accessible, audit-ready safety briefs. It equips everyday consumers with clear bio-equivalence evaluations, dosage guidance, and critical clinical warnings, empowering them to hold informed, safe consultations with healthcare professionals.

### Improving Local Essential Access

The platform dynamically maps regional pharmacy inventory (via DeepSeek-V4), eliminating the physical and financial burden on vulnerable populations searching for necessary medications during local stockouts. MediFind directly applies AI to solve real-world public health challenges through cost transparency, health literacy, and equitable access to essential medicine.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Sending money across a border is easy. Turning it back into money you can actually spend is not.

An international student in Kuala Lumpur needs living expenses from home. A migrant worker needs to send wages back to their family. Both are stuck with the same broken options.

**The problems:**

- Bank wires cost ~USD 45 and take 2–5 days.
- Money changers take a cut on the rate and a fee.
- Both need a bank account a new arrival cannot open.
- Crypto sends fast, but the money is stuck as a token.
- Cashing out means seed phrases, exchanges and KYC.
- The last mile is ignored — money must land as local currency.

**What Mizan does:**

- A Sui account from a Google sign-in. No seed phrase.
- Sends in ~2 seconds for about two cents.
- Shows your balance in 11 local currencies.
- Cashes out to a bank account or e-wallet, fees shown.
- Compares three licensed on-ramps before you buy.
- Splits rent and bills with housemates.
- Pays by voice — *"Hey Trisha, send twenty five to Ayesha."*

Built for Malaysia's 130,000+ international students and 2.7 million migrant workers.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
We had a week, a team that came together late, and a product that touches a blockchain, a browser microphone and an OAuth popup — three things that each fail in their own way.

Most of our time went on the parts that looked simple and were not.

- **Forming the team late.** Scoped hard on day one and cut everything else.
- **The assistant answered itself.** Chrome sends every phrase twice; we now strip her name wherever it appears.
- **Spoken numbers were wrong.** "Twenty five to Ayesha" parsed as 27. Removed homophones, added spoken confirmation.
- **Google's popup was blocked.** It must open straight from the click, so the setup animation runs behind it.
- **A transfer recorded as zero.** The screen and the ledger used different field names. No error, just a wrong number.
- **No route from SUI to a bank.** It cannot be one step, so we built two and showed both fees.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body:
Mizan is a payments product built entirely on Sui — a cross-border remittance account for people who cannot open a bank account yet.

- **Payments are the product.** Every transfer is a native SUI transfer, verifiable on Suiscan.
- **Stablecoins are the last mile.** Cashing out swaps SUI to USDT, then sells it for local currency.
- **Onboarding without a seed phrase.** The account is derived from a Google sign-in.
- **Small transfers work.** ~2 second finality, sub-cent fees.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
The bug: we shipped an approver capability we could never take back.

Large payments need a human signature, so we issued each approver an ApproverCap — an owned object carrying its own max_single ceiling. It looked right, it tested fine, and we deployed it to testnet.

Then we tried to lower one approver's limit and hit a wall that isn't a bug in our code, it's how Sui works: only an object's owner may mutate an object. Once that cap was transferred, the admin couldn't touch it. We couldn't lower the ceiling, and we couldn't revoke it — there was no revocation function in the module, and there couldn't be one, because revoking means mutating an object we no longer owned. The cap sitting live on testnet authorized $25,000,000 against a vault holding $88,200.

The fix was a principle we'd already applied elsewhere and failed to apply here: state the admin owns is state the admin can change. Agent limits were never inside AgentCap — they live in Treasury.agents, which is exactly why an agent can't rewrite them. Approvers needed the same shape. We wrote approve_scoped, which keys authority by the approver's address in treasury state: per-payment ceiling, daily ceiling, expiry, recipient allowlist, enabled flag — all mutable by the admin.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Accounts payable is slow, and the obvious fix is dangerous.

Paying suppliers is repetitive judgment work: read the invoice, check the supplier is real, check the wallet is the one on file, decide whether paying today still leaves enough cash for payroll, catch the 2% early-payment discount before it expires. Finance teams do this by hand across inboxes and spreadsheets, so invoices sit unpaid, discounts lapse, late fees accrue, and nobody has a live answer to "can we afford this right now."

The tempting fix is to hand it to an AI agent. That's the dangerous part. Today an agent's spending authority lives in its prompt and its API key — both of which an attacker can reach. A prompt injection buried in an invoice PDF, a hijacked supplier email thread, or a plain hallucination, and the money is already gone. Invoice-redirection fraud is one of the most expensive attacks in business today; an autonomous agent with a wallet just makes it faster.

AI Payflow's answer: let the AI decide, but never let it be the authority.

The model does judgment — parsing invoices, forecasting cash position, weighing discounts, flagging anomalies. The Sui smart contract decides what actually happens. Every payment is judged by ten checks before a coin moves, and the agent's capability object has no mutable field at all, so even an attacker in full control of the prompt and the API key cannot raise a limit, approve a supplier, or reach the vault.

Built for finance and ops teams processing recurring supplier invoices — and for anyone piloting AI agents with real spending authority who needs the limits to live somewhere the agent cannot edit them.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body: AI Payflow uses USDC for making payment to suppliers, Sui acted as an escrow that hold the USDC until the items delivered then only release the payment.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body: AI payflow uses AI as AI CFO to understand the invoice and business context, forecasts liquidity under different payment dates, compares the options, and give recommendations; while Sui enforces the company's rules, approve/rejects transactions based on the limit. Sui also acted as an escrow, it only release the payment once the items delivered.

pharmatrust-5388.name: PharmaTrust
pharmatrust-5388.tagline: On-chain pharma custody, verified by AI on Sui

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Counterfeit and diverted pharmaceuticals are hard to catch with paper records or private databases. A paper trail can be forged, and a database can be silently edited by whoever controls it. Neither gives a patient, pharmacist, or regulator a way to independently verify a specific package's history before use.

PharmaTrust puts the entire custody chain on Sui instead, so it's public, tamper-evident, and permanently attributed to whoever signed each step. Manufacturers register a batch on-chain, optionally backing it with staked SUI as collateral, and print QR codes straight onto packaging. Distributors and pharmacies record every hand-off as a checkpoint, including cold-chain temperature readings, permanently tied to their wallet with no way to forge who touched it. Anyone can scan a package, with no wallet needed, and instantly see its full custody history, run an independent AI cross-check across two different models for tampering or timing anomalies, and check a public recall registry before dispensing or buying. Regulators or pharmacy staff can place a hold the moment something looks wrong, and it immediately blocks further sales and checkpoints rather than just flagging paperwork, with graduated financial penalties in the form of slashed stake scaled to how serious the finding is. Customers pay for medicine with a single-use QR plus a scratch code that's physically deleted from the blockchain the instant it's redeemed, so the same package can never be sold twice off one photo of the QR.

In short, it turns "trust me, this is genuine" into "verify it yourself, for free, in seconds."

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
A stale environment variable silently broke every write transaction in production. After adding staking, suspicion reports, and single-use sale QRs to the Move contract, we discovered VITE_PACKAGE_ID on our Vercel deployment still pointed at a much older contract version published before any of those features existed, one that even gated place_hold behind a RegulatorCap we'd since removed. Every write transaction was failing with argument-count mismatches while every read still worked, which is exactly why it went unnoticed: the site looked fine until you tried to actually submit something. We caught it by disassembling the deployed package bytecode directly and diffing its function signatures against our current contract, which taught us never to trust "the site loads" as proof a deployment is actually current.

A hosted AI model silently substituted itself for another. Our two-model AI cross-check depends on genuinely independent verdicts, but we found that requests to one model, Kimi-K2.6, were being silently served by a completely different model on the router's side, with no error and no indication in the response, which defeated the whole point of cross-checking two models. We fixed it by adding an X-Gonka-No-Fallback header, which turned the silent substitution into an honest error revealing the model had zero capacity, and swapped in a model we verified was genuinely distinct.

Sui's public JSON-RPC endpoints deprecated the API our wallet-kit version depends on partway through the project, returning "Method not found" with no CORS headers, which broke every browser call outright. We solved it by pointing at a CORS-enabled public RPC provider instead of Mysten's own endpoint.

Move package upgrades quietly break event-based indexing. A minor contract change that only tightened a validation check, with no struct changes, looked like a safe sui client upgrade instead of a fresh publish, until we discovered every event's package ID switches to the new address after an upgrade, silently orphaning every dashboard that filters events by a fixed package ID. We now always publish fresh rather than upgrade, trading batch and unit continuity for a single reliable source of truth in the event log.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body:
PharmaTrust is built natively on Sui and leans on its object model as the actual mechanism, not as a bolt-on ledger sitting behind a normal backend. A Batch is a shared Sui object that every party in the supply chain (manufacturer, distributor, pharmacy) attaches a checkpoint to directly, giving the whole custody chain a single, permissionless, tamper-evident source of truth without needing a centralized database anywhere.

The single-use sale QR is the clearest example of thinking in Sui's terms rather than porting over a generic smart-contract pattern. Instead of an "already sold" boolean that a bug or race condition could bypass, the QR is backed by a Unit object that gets deleted outright the instant it's paid for. An object that no longer exists on-chain simply can't be referenced by a future transaction, so the single-use guarantee comes from the object model itself, not from application logic hoping nobody finds a way around a flag.

The AI side is genuinely wired into that on-chain state, not bolted onto a demo. Two independently-queried models reason directly over a batch's live checkpoint and hold history read straight from Sui, cross-checking for tampering or timing anomalies, and a second pass reasons across every batch from one manufacturer at once to catch patterns a single-batch check would never see. The point of the AI is specifically to notice things the on-chain record makes visible but that a person skimming it wouldn't catch.

There's also a real economic layer built on actual Coin<SUI> transfers, not a UI-only score: manufacturers post SUI as collateral when they register a batch, and a confirmed hold slashes a graduated share of it straight to whoever caught the problem, so reporting a counterfeit is directly rewarded instead of being unpaid diligence.

Building this also meant running into Sui's real constraints rather than staying on a happy path: chunking multiGetObjects calls under the 50-ID cap, paginating queryEvents thousands of events deep instead of quietly truncating at the first page, and learning the hard way that sui client upgrade changes an event's package ID, which would have silently broken every dashboard built on event history. And finally, there's no access control anywhere in the contract on purpose. Any wallet can register a batch, scan a checkpoint, place a hold, or buy, with no admin approval step standing between a first-time visitor and trying the whole flow immediately.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
* When converting from the **localhost URL to the public URL**, the generated AI output was different from what we expected. We checked the project from beginning to end and discovered that we had **not pulled the latest commit from Git**, which caused the issue. **Pulling the latest changes fixed the output.**
* We also found that **generating the output initially took a long time**. To improve this, we **modified the AI prompt and added restrictions to prevent unnecessary processing**, making the generation more efficient.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
**Silent Voice** is an **AI-powered communication tool** for people living with **aphasia** — a condition (often caused by stroke or brain injury) where a person can think and understand language normally, but struggles to speak or write.

Instead of requiring typing or speech, Silent Voice lets a user **build a message by tapping simple icons** (emotions, body sensations, needs). An **AI model** then converts that icon sequence into a **natural, complete, warm sentence** — which is **displayed on screen and read aloud** — so the person can be understood by **family members, caregivers, or medical staff** without needing to produce the words themselves.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body: Silent Voice applies AI to make communication more accessible for people with aphasia. It transforms visual icon selections into meaningful messages and uses text-to-speech to help users express their thoughts, feelings, and needs. This demonstrates how AI can address real-world accessibility challenges and promote more inclusive communication.

trusthire-42a6.name: TrustHire
trusthire-42a6.tagline: AI decides who to trust. Sui enforces it.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
### The Trust Deficit in the Gig Economy

In today's digital economy, a massive amount of freelance work happens informally. Clients and talent connecting directly through social media, Discord, or WhatsApp. While this bypasses the massive 20% fees of traditional platforms, it creates a severe trust deficit with zero protection for either side:
- **Freelancers** constantly worry about clients defaulting on payments, or ghosting them entirely after the final work is delivered.
- **Clients** worry about hiring fake profiles, encountering fabricated portfolios, or receiving subpar work because they have no formal recourse or arbitration.
- **Pay-to-play barriers:** Even when users try to rely on traditional platforms, freelancers are often forced to buy virtual "tokens" or "connects" just for the privilege of applying to a job, and face manual dispute systems that are easily manipulated.

### How TrustHire Solves This

TrustHire completely removes the need for expensive, subjective middlemen. It replaces them with trustless Web3 infrastructure and unbiased AI, providing institutional-grade safety for independent and direct hires.

People can use TrustHire to securely hire talent or accept freelance work with zero anxiety about getting scammed. It makes gig work radically safer through four core pillars:

1. **Guaranteed Payments (Sui Escrow):** Clients securely lock project funds in an on-chain Sui Move contract *before* work begins. The platform never holds custody of the funds, and the freelancer knows the money is guaranteed the moment they meet the requirements.
2. **Unbiased AI Arbitration (Gonka Router):** Instead of relying on a biased human support agent during disputes, TrustHire routes milestone submissions (like a GitHub PR or Figma link) through a multi-model AI consensus engine. The AI neutrally evaluates the work against the initial project spec, outputs a "Truth Score," and automatically authorizes the release of the escrowed funds. 
3. **Immutable Reputation:** Freelancers build a permanent, on-chain work history that proves their skills and track record, completely eliminating the "fake profile" problem.
4. **Zero-Cost, Walletless Onboarding:** Unlike legacy platforms that charge freelancers just to apply, TrustHire removes all friction. Using **zkLogin** and **Enoki Sponsored Transactions**, talent can sign in with a simple Google account and start working instantly. Gas fees are fully sponsored, meaning freelancers don't even need a crypto wallet or SUI tokens to get started.

By combining Web3 payment guarantees with AI verification, TrustHire makes freelance work fairer, safer, and completely trustless.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
### 1. The Enoki Gas Sponsorship vs. Coin Splitting Hurdle
**The Challenge:** 
Our goal was to make the platform 100% gasless using Enoki Sponsored Transactions. However, when we attempted to sponsor the `create_escrow` transaction (where a client locks SUI funds into the smart contract), the transaction kept failing. We discovered a core limitation: Enoki gas pools cannot sponsor transactions that involve splitting the primary gas-paying coin itself, which is exactly what happens when you try to extract funds to lock into an escrow.

**The Solution:** 
We had to deeply rethink our transaction architecture. We leveraged **Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs)** to elegantly solve this. Instead of a clumsy two-step process, we used a PTB to atomically execute `tx.splitCoins` and pass the newly created coin object directly into the `tx.moveCall` for the escrow in a single execution. We then explicitly restricted Enoki sponsorship to the *freelancer* side (onboarding and milestone submissions), ensuring the talent experience remained 100% frictionless and gasless, while clients handle standard gas for their funding transactions.

### 2. Preventing AI Hallucinations in Financial Decisions
**The Challenge:**
Since our smart contracts release real escrowed funds based on the AI's verdict, relying on a single AI model to verify complex milestone deliverables (like analyzing a GitHub PR) was too risky. A single model might hallucinate or provide a subjective, lenient approval.

**The Solution:**
We implemented a strict **Multi-Model Consensus** mechanism using the Gonka Router. Instead of one model, we cross-reference the milestone proof across multiple distinct models (e.g., DeepSeek and MiniMax). Only when the models reach a consensus on the requirements does the system output a definitive "Truth Score." If the models disagree, the system flags it for manual review, ensuring that no funds are released on a hallucinated verdict.

### 3. Cost-Efficient Hybrid Architecture (Off-chain DB + On-chain Execution)
**The Challenge:**
Storing extensive project requirements, freelancer portfolios, and AI reasoning traces directly on the Sui blockchain would have resulted in astronomically high gas fees. Furthermore, we needed a way to render complex UI data instantly on page load without waiting for wallet connections or slow RPC nodes to hydrate the state.

**The Solution:**
We implemented a hybrid architecture to solve both problems. We use **Supabase** as a lightning-fast off-chain database to store all heavy metadata (project descriptions, profile text, AI analysis). 

When a critical financial action occurs (like creating an escrow or approving a milestone), the transaction is executed on the Sui blockchain. We then capture the resulting **on-chain transaction hash (txDigest)** and store it directly in our off-chain Supabase database as an irrefutable reference. 

This approach drastically minimized gas fees while giving us Web2 load speeds. We render the heavy UI from Supabase instantly, and use the stored transaction hashes to cross-verify the financial state on-chain exactly when needed.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body:
TrustHire perfectly aligns with the Payments & Stablecoins track by building the future of automated, trustless "creator payouts" and escrow.

We built a real-world ready payout workflow that eliminates platform custody risk. By utilizing Sui's **Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs)**, clients securely split and lock their project funds into an on-chain milestone escrow in a single click. 

To guarantee a "fast, intuitive UX" for non-crypto native freelancers, we utilized **zkLogin** (Google onboarding) and **Enoki Sponsored Transactions**. This completely removes all Web3 friction—freelancers never have to worry about gas fees, seed phrases, or managing wallets when receiving their payouts.

While our current prototype utilizes the SUI token for escrow funding, our `escrow.move` smart contract is fully built around Sui's generic `Coin<T>` standard. This makes our entire payment architecture natively **stablecoin-ready**. In production, clients will fund the escrow using stablecoins (like USDC), protecting freelancers from crypto volatility while still enjoying automated, AI-verified payouts.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body:
TrustHire is an **AI-powered freelance marketplace** that perfectly intersects AI and Sui to solve the problem of trust and payment fairness in the gig economy. 

**AI acts as the brain:** The Gonka AI Router extracts structured project requirements, intelligently matches freelancers to jobs, and generates Trust Scores based on verified skills and portfolio data. 

**Sui acts as the muscle:** AI alone cannot hold or distribute funds, making Sui absolutely integral to our platform. We use **Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs)** to securely fund **On-Chain Escrow** Move contracts. Payments are locked in advance and automatically released upon milestone approval, eliminating platform custody and payment default risks.

Additionally, to ensure a seamless "Web2-like" user experience for non-crypto native freelancers, we heavily utilize **zkLogin** for passwordless Google onboarding and **Enoki Sponsored Transactions** so talent can interact with the blockchain with zero gas fees.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
TrustHire applies the **Gonka AI Fact Checker** pattern to solve a genuine public value issue: preventing scams and unpaid work in the gig economy. 

When a freelancer completes a job (a milestone), they submit a URL (e.g., a GitHub PR or Figma link) or text snippet. Instead of leaving the client to manually verify, which often leads to disputes or unpaid labor, TrustHire routes the submission through the **Gonka Router** (`gonkarouter.io`) for **Decentralized Verification**.

To guarantee absolute neutrality, we utilize **Multi-Model Consensus**, cross-verifying the submission using at least two different models. The AI analyzes the submitted work against the original project requirements and outputs a **Truth Score (0-100%)** along with a detailed **Reasoning Trace**. This unbiased AI verdict empowers the client to confidently approve the milestone and release the on-chain payment.

For complete transparency, all AI judgments are rendered on the dashboard alongside their specific **Gonka Request IDs**, proving that the verification was untampered and decentralized.

bukti-ad19.name: Bukti
bukti-ad19.tagline: AI fact-checking with Gonka, Sui & Walrus

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Public claims are easy to share but difficult to verify later. Context changes, sources disappear, and an AI answer by itself does not provide a durable audit trail.

Bukti makes this workflow safer and easier by:

- Accepting either a text claim or a public URL for checking.
- Retrieving bounded evidence from public pages and social posts while defending against unsafe URLs and oversized responses.
- Searching for supporting and contradicting sources, with Malaysian official and established news domains ranked first when relevant.
- Asking multiple Gonka models to assess the claim and surfacing their scores, verdicts, reasoning, citations, request IDs, and disagreements.
- Limiting unsupported claims to a cautious score ceiling when no evidence can be retrieved.
- Storing the canonical result as a public Walrus snapshot and committing its SHA-256 digest to an immutable Sui `TruthReportV3` object.
- Providing public report pages and a Sui event-backed report index so anyone can inspect the receipt without trusting Bukti's database.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
- **Keeping the receipt reproducible:** Browser and server serialization can differ if object ordering or formatting is left implicit. We solved this with a deterministic canonical JSON serializer and hash the exact bytes before and after the Walrus round trip.
- **Handling unreliable storage propagation:** A Walrus blob may not be immediately readable after upload. The publisher retries short-lived 404/5xx responses, then refuses to continue if the downloaded bytes do not hash to the original digest.
- **Making user-supplied URLs safe:** Claims can point to attacker-controlled URLs, including private-network targets or redirect chains. Direct retrieval validates schemes, credentials, DNS results, redirects, response size, content type, and timeouts before returning a bounded text excerpt.
- **Preventing unsupported certainty:** Models can produce a confident answer even when no source is available. Bukti caps scores without retrieved evidence and validates every model citation against the sources actually supplied to it.
- **Building a public report list from immutable objects:** Frozen Sui objects are not edited in place and are not convenient to enumerate directly. The Move package emits a permanent `ReportPublishedV3` event, which powers the public reports index while preserving the immutable receipt invariant.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body:
Bukti uses Sui as the trust and provenance layer for AI-generated claim analysis. Each completed verification can be published as a frozen `TruthReportV3` object containing the claim commitment, aggregate score, verdict, model/request metadata, Walrus blob ID, and digest of the canonical report. Because reports are immutable, a re-check creates a new receipt instead of silently changing the original result.

Walrus stores the full public evidence snapshot, while Sui provides the durable on-chain commitment that lets anyone verify the snapshot has not been altered. This makes AI output inspectable rather than a transient answer in a chat interface.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
Bukti applies Gonka Router to a practical public-interest problem: helping people assess claims that affect civic information, public policy, health, prices, and everyday decision-making. The server can query multiple configured Gonka models through the Anthropic Messages API, capture each `X-Request-Id`, compare their assessments, and expose disagreement instead of hiding uncertainty behind one answer.

The project is designed for cautious use: it prefers recent official Malaysian sources, preserves contradicting evidence, validates model citations, and lowers confidence when no live evidence is available. The result is a transparent verification workflow that communities, journalists, researchers, and ordinary users can inspect and share.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
**1. Network needs change by activity**
Normal connectivity may be enough for browsing, but gaming, livestreaming, video calls, or crowded events may require lower latency, better stability, or stronger uplink performance.

**2. Users do not know when premium network capabilities are useful**
Telecom providers may already have QoS or other programmable network capabilities, but users usually do not know when they need them or whether they will actually improve the experience.

**3. Premium network services are not context-aware**
Existing add-ons are often static. Our platform uses provider-supplied user and network context to generate a purchase offer only when the customer is likely to benefit.

**4. Multi-provider sessions are difficult to manage and settle**
If one provider can no longer meet the required service level, the session may need to continue through another provider while keeping one customer purchase and fairly splitting the payment.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
**1. Autonomous payment on Sui**
We initially wanted the AI agent to fully control payment, but non-custodial transactions still require user authorization. We had to redesign the flow so the user approves the purchase while the agent manages the session and settlement.

**2. Integrating off-chain network data with on-chain payment**
Network quality, session duration, and provider switching happen off-chain, while settlement happens on Sui. We needed a clear way to connect verified service results with smart-contract payment logic.

**3. Defining the business model**
We initially considered acting as a reseller of network capacity, but this created dependency on provider availability and weak margins. We later repositioned the platform as provider-facing infrastructure for selling premium network experiences.

**4. Handling one session across multiple providers**
We had to define how a user keeps the same paid session when Provider A becomes unsuitable, how Provider B takes over, and how one final payment is split based on each provider’s actual contribution.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body:
- Customers pay for actual premium-network usage.
- One session can involve multiple providers.
- Customer receives one final charge.
- Payment is split according to verified provider contribution.
- Stablecoins support predictable settlement value.
- Smart contracts reduce manual reconciliation.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body:
- AI evaluates user activity, network quality, eligibility, and available capabilities.
- AI decides whether an upgrade is needed and which service is suitable.
- AI monitors the session and can trigger provider switching.
- Sui records session transactions and provider contributions.
- Smart contracts automate transparent multi-provider settlement.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
- AI recommends upgrades only when users genuinely need them.
- Avoids unnecessary or generic upselling.
- Helps users access better performance for gaming, livestreaming, work, and events.
- Makes advanced network capabilities easier for normal users to access.
- Encourages more efficient use of provider network services.

thesisfun-68be.name: Thesis.fun
thesisfun-68be.tagline: Say it. Trade it. Real onchain options on Base.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## The SDK comment about which side the maker is on was backwards

We decoded production fills from Base bytes and pinned the real rule with tests: `isLong` is the maker's flag, so `false` means the taker buys.

## Maker signatures expire in about a minute

The ticket approves first, then re-quotes right before the fill, and refuses to broadcast stale calldata.

## Thetanuts publishes no price history

The market page draws Binance hourly spot and says so on the chart, because Thetanuts settles on a Chainlink TWAP that can differ. No number on a position comes from the chart: every figure is derived from the fill event and the raw order, never from the quote.

## Recording a fill had to fail closed

A mismatched event, an unprovable contract count, or a structure that vanished from the book refuses instead of guessing. The ticket is held while the last fill is still being recorded, and the server re-checks the chain for this wallet's recent fills before it issues another ticket.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
## Options on chain are hard to find and harder to talk about

**Thesis.fun makes a trade a post.** Pick any market Thetanuts has liquidity for on Base, take a side with your own wallet, and the position gets its own page with a live P&L card. Say why in a post; link the trade and it unfurls into a card, X-style.

- **Every market Thetanuts has liquidity for.** Assets, strikes and expiries come from live OptionBook orders, never a hardcoded list.
- **Both sides.** Buy an option (loss bounded by the premium) or sell one (lock collateral, receive the premium), each with honest sizing and copy.
- **A social layer built only from onchain fills.** Likes, comments, follows and a leaderboard from real positions, so a track record cannot be faked and a losing thesis cannot be deleted.
- **Every new user gets a name and a face on day one.** Generated names and avatars, editable later.
- **An AI agent that explains any thesis and proposes trades** within a hard loss limit and daily caps. The wallet signs everything; the agent never does.

description.title: BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK
description.body: Thesis.fun is built end to end on the Thetanuts SDK: live OptionBook orders drive every market, strike and expiry; quotes, approvals and fills go through the SDK's calldata builders and are recorded from the on-chain `OrderFilled` event; both taker sides ship with sizing derived from decoded production fills. Every quote and fill carries the platform referrer.

description.title: AI × OPTIONS
description.body: An approval-gated AI agent explains any thesis, proposes a trade on a live Thetanuts structure, prepares the real calldata through the same path as the ticket, and hands it to the user's wallet to sign. Hard loss ceiling and daily caps are enforced server-side on the prepared economics; the agent never signs.

trustlayer-58c9.name: TrustLayer
trustlayer-58c9.tagline: Performance Bonds for a More Trustworthy Tomorrow

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Abandoning our original custody model

Our first design locked 100% of a consumer’s prepayment in a Sui Move contract and released it when milestones were completed. We ultimately rejected this approach for three reasons:

It created adverse selection: responsible merchants would not want all their working capital locked.

Service fulfilment can be subjective, and a smart contract cannot reliably decide whether an experience was “good.”

Holding customer funds could introduce serious regulatory and licensing concerns in Malaysia.

We kept the underlying trust problem but replaced full payment custody with a dynamic merchant performance bond. Customer payments remain on existing payment rails, while Sui provides the transparent commitment and enforcement layer.

2. Finding a gap in our original risk trigger

Our initial concept relied heavily on refund requests accumulating. We realised this was incomplete: a merchant could disappear before customers had time to request refunds.

We expanded the design to consider multiple independent operational signals, including attendance anomalies, unresolved maintenance issues, and merchant disappearance. In the current prototype, these inputs are clearly labelled simulations used to demonstrate deterministic health scoring and the on-chain challenge flow.

3. Confronting the oracle and incentive problem

TrustLayer ultimately depends on operational data supplied by merchants or SaaS/POS platforms. That creates a difficult incentive problem: a platform may benefit from keeping its merchants’ scores healthy, and a blockchain cannot force an external platform to report an event it chooses to omit.

We did not pretend to solve this completely. Our proposed future design treats prolonged data silence as a negative signal rather than allowing missing data to appear healthy. This remains a roadmap concept, not a live integration in the current prototype.

4. Recognising the limits of the kiosk approach

We explored a standalone kiosk as a cold-start option for merchants without an integrated SaaS platform. However, a kiosk can still receive inaccurate data before anything reaches the blockchain.

Sui can prove that submitted records were not altered afterward, but it cannot guarantee that every original input was truthful. We therefore present the kiosk honestly as a simulated, imperfect onboarding bridge, not a fully trustless data source.

What we learned

The hardest part was not writing the first contract. It was identifying where our original assumptions failed, discarding mechanisms that created new risks, and clearly separating what the prototype proves today from what still requires stronger oracle design, governance, and regulatory analysis.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Prepaid service businesses such as gyms, beauty salons, and tuition centres ask customers to pay today for services delivered over the following weeks or months. This creates a trust gap: a business may begin deteriorating operationally while customers continue buying packages because they cannot see the warning signs.

TrustLayer turns operational risk signals into a verifiable performance commitment.

The system derives a merchant health score from operational data, uses that score to determine a dynamic performance-bond requirement, and records the merchant’s commitment on Sui. If risk increases, the required protection can increase and the smart contract can initiate a rule-based slash-and-challenge process.

Customer payments do not need to move onto the blockchain. They can remain on traditional payment rails while Sui provides a transparent commitment and enforcement layer.

TrustLayer helps:

- Consumers assess the risk behind prepaid purchases.
- Merchants turn strong operational performance into a visible trust signal and potentially lower bond requirements.
- SaaS and POS platforms transform operational data they already manage into a new trust feature.

Our hackathon prototype runs on Sui Testnet. It demonstrates clearly labelled simulated operational events, deterministic health scoring, live shared Merchant objects, wallet-signed bond deposits, health updates, slash initiation, and counter-evidence. The browser derives the health score, while the authorized wallet submits the resulting score on-chain.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body:
TrustLayer adds a programmable trust layer to prepaid payments for services such as gyms, salons and tuition centres.

Customer payments can remain on existing fiat or stablecoin payment rails, while merchants place a performance bond on Sui. The required bond changes according to a health score derived from operational indicators such as attendance decline and unresolved maintenance issues.

Our Sui Testnet prototype demonstrates shared Merchant objects, wallet-signed bond deposits, health updates, and a rule-based slash-and-challenge process. If operational risk increases, the merchant’s required protection increases and the contract can enter a transparent challenge period.

TrustLayer does not issue a stablecoin or process customer payments directly. Instead, it demonstrates how Sui-based performance bonds could complement existing payment and stablecoin systems by making future service fulfilment more transparent and accountable.

custodia-393d.name: Custodia
custodia-393d.tagline: On-chain trust for what AI agents do

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Giving an AI agent your wallet to act on your behalf is currently an all-or-nothing choice: either hand over full control and hope it doesn't overspend or pay the wrong party, or supervise every single transaction yourself which defeats the point of automation in the first place.

Custodia gives people a middle ground: a Mandate, a real on-chain spending permit with a hard cap, an expiry, and a fixed list of allowed task categories. An agent can act freely and autonomously within that boundary, and the boundary itself is enforced by a Move smart contract, not by trusting the app's frontend to behave.

What people can actually use it for:
Hiring specialists without micromanaging payment. Ask for something done like a document translated, a contract reviewed, an item picked up and repaired and the agent finds a real specialist, escrows payment, and only releases it once delivery is verified. You never manually wire money or chase an invoice.
Multi-step jobs that need different specialists in sequence. A single request like pick up my broken laptop, get it repaired, send it back gets split into several linked deals which is pickup, repair, return. Each automatically triggering the next once the last one's delivery is proven on-chain, with no manual hand-off required.
Trusting who you're hiring, without a middleman. Specialists are ranked by a reputation score built entirely from real completed-vs-disputed deals, not a profile they wrote themselves, not a platform's opaque rating.
Keeping sensitive job details private. Task briefs and delivered work are encrypted so only the client and the assigned specialist can ever read them, not a backend, not Custodia itself, because there is no backend holding that data.
How it makes things safer, concretely:

Money can never move outside the Mandate's cap, categories, or expiry, enforced on-chain, not just in the UI.
Payment and proof-of-delivery are locked together in one atomic transaction, so there's no window where a specialist gets paid without delivering, or delivers without ever getting paid.
Every reputation score is a real, auditable history of completed and disputed deals, not a number anyone can inflate by hand.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Package upgrades broke object lookups silently. When we upgraded our Move package to add a new module, an older module's objects were still typed under the original package id, not the new one but our query used the new id. Transactions succeeded every time; our own code just never found what it created. We found the real cause by pulling the raw transaction JSON via the Sui CLI and reading the object's actual type string.

Seal requires the original package id, always. After that same upgrade, encryption started throwing InvalidPackageError. Turned out Seal's SDK hard-requires the package's version-1 id specifically, even though the function itself works fine on the newer package. We only found this by reading Seal's own SDK source.

A budget check passed, but the real transaction still failed. Our on-screen "Mandate check passed" message and the actual escrow transaction were silently reading two different Mandate objects, one freshly fetched, one cached from earlier in the session. Once a user had two Mandates, the check and the real transaction could disagree.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body:
Custodia is escrow and payout infrastructure for agent driven money movement, settling in stablecoins so payouts are stable, predictable, and instant.

The problem: 
Automated payouts like payroll, creator tips, marketplace escrow, campus payments need money to move the moment work is verified, with no human in the loop and no risk of paying out before the job is actually done, and no exposure to price swings while funds sit in escrow. Custodia's Mandate is an on-chain spending permit with a hard cap, expiry, and allowed categories, enforced by a Move contract nothing on the frontend can bypass. An agent can release stablecoin funds freely inside that boundary and nowhere else.

Why Sui matters here: 
Escrow-lock, delivery verification, and stablecoin payout are one atomic Move transaction like funds and proof-of-work can never drift out of sync, and reputation only grows when a payout genuinely lands. Sponsored transactions mean the person receiving a payout never needs to hold SUI for gas just to get paid, and zkLogin means onboarding a payee is a Google sign-in, not a seed phrase.

The demo: 
A client escrows a stablecoin payment the moment a task is accepted, watches real on-chain checkpoints as the work happens, and the moment delivery is verified, payout fires automatically and atomically to the payee's wallet and no invoice, no manual transfer as well as no waiting on a human to notice the job is done.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body:
Custodia is a trust and settlement layer that lets AI agents hire other agents and actually pay them safely.

The problem: 
Giving an AI agent your wallet key is reckless; supervising every transaction defeats the point of automation. Custodia's answer is a Mandate which is an on-chain spending permit with a hard cap, expiry and allowed categories, enforced by a Move contract the frontend can't bypass. The agent (Envoy) can act freely inside that boundary and nowhere else.

Why Sui matters here: 
Every real state change like escrow, delivery verification, payout, reputation update is a single atomic Move transaction, so money and trust can never drift out of sync. Specialists are ranked by a reputation score that only grows when a deal is genuinely completed and paid. Deliverables are Seal-encrypted and Walrus-stored, readable only by the two parties on that exact deal.

The demo isn't just locked to one workflow. Envoy decomposes whatever the user asks into however many sequential deals it needs, matches each to the right specialist type from six real categories, and chains them automatically. The laptop repair example is just one instance of a general pattern.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
Custodia verify it's escrow and reputation contracts, repointed at fact-checking instead of task delivery.

The problem: 
Fact-checking has no accountability layer. A model (or a human reviewer) can call a claim true or false and face no consequence if they're wrong. Custodia already has a contract for exactly this shape of problem that pay someone only once their output is verified, and track their track record on-chain that it's just been used for task delivery, not truth verification until now.

What would be built using Custodia's real contracts is a claim that gets checked by at least two independent models via Gonka Router. Custodia's existing Mandate would fund that inference cost per claim, the same way it funds a specialist's payout today. The Truth Score and reasoning trace Gonka returns would be Seal-encrypted and stored on Walrus which is the same storage path Custodia that already uses for a specialist's deliverable, so the reasoning behind a verdict is provenance-anchored, not just displayed and forgotten. And Custodia's Reputation object, the same Move module that already scores a specialist by completed-vs-disputed deals would score each model or verifier by how often its calls hold up over time, using the identical record_completed/record_disputed mechanism.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
**The Problem It Solves**

Financial fraud is becoming harder to detect because criminals **use complex company networks, shell entities, fake transactions, and hidden ownership structures.**

Today, investigators spend a lot of time manually collecting and connecting information from different sources, which can lead to **slow investigations and missed fraud connections.**

**FinTrace solves this by providing an AI-powered financial investigation platform that:**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f5480803823e41e29d8ab00e3b4ed073/e35f45d2-2bb9-4b45-9b45-a7b13e3553ce.jpeg)

**1.Detects financial fraud patterns** such as shell companies, GST fraud, loan fraud, and suspicious networks.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f5480803823e41e29d8ab00e3b4ed073/f13ebfe2-14d7-4a33-8cfa-bd6afdc6d835.jpeg)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f5480803823e41e29d8ab00e3b4ed073/04bacdb6-3be7-432e-993b-1dedee208c53.jpeg)
