 **3.Uses AI verification** to analyze claims and provide explainable insights.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f5480803823e41e29d8ab00e3b4ed073/acc43566-ee0a-4fde-97ba-67972b7cb6dc.jpeg)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f5480803823e41e29d8ab00e3b4ed073/6c0f2da8-7236-4a9d-a562-da23559c2f65.jpeg)

**4.Creates evidence-based fraud reports** that help investigators make faster decisions.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f5480803823e41e29d8ab00e3b4ed073/c4fdd4cd-c418-4328-9f28-f5d35e52070d.jpeg)

**5.Reduces manual investigation time** by bringing multiple analysis techniques into one platform.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f5480803823e41e29d8ab00e3b4ed073/6b8511dc-4749-436a-b0c3-2c79d8492b6f.jpeg)

**In simple terms: FinTrace helps banks, auditors, and investigators find hidden fraud connections faster, with AI-powered evidence and transparent reasoning.**

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
**Challenges We Ran Into**

**The backend was not publicly deployed because FinTrace depends on multiple infrastructure components, including Neo4j graph database services and AI API integrations that require secure environment configuration. For the final demonstration, we prioritized a stable and fully functional setup instead of exposing an unstable deployment with external dependency risks. The complete backend is deployment-ready and can be hosted with the required infrastructure configuration.**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f5480803823e41e29d8ab00e3b4ed073/df92bc75-45b9-49bf-ab63-5cd2b054e275.png)

Building FinTrace involved solving several technical challenges while combining AI, machine learning, and graph intelligence into one platform.

**🕸️ 1. Building a Real-Time Fraud Relationship Graph**

**Challenge:**
Financial fraud is not limited to one transaction or company. The difficult part was identifying hidden relationships between companies, directors, transactions, and suspicious entities.

**Solution:**
We implemented a **Neo4j-based graph intelligence layer** to represent entities and relationships as connected data. This allowed us to visualize fraud networks and identify suspicious clusters instead of analyzing isolated records.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f5480803823e41e29d8ab00e3b4ed073/dbc1beaf-5eb2-4359-aa8b-caa94d19bb1b.jpeg)

**🤖 2. Integrating AI Verification with Reliable Outputs**

**Challenge:**
AI models can produce inconsistent responses, and financial decisions require explainable and trustworthy results.

**Solution:**
We integrated** Gonka Router with multi-model verification, **structured JSON responses, **Truth Score calculation,** and Request ID tracking to make AI decisions more transparent and traceable.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f5480803823e41e29d8ab00e3b4ed073/3b84ca66-d201-4aac-a215-5e92d7b14bfe.jpeg)

**🔍 3. Combining Multiple Fraud Detection Approaches**

**Challenge:**
Different fraud types require different detection strategies, such as loan fraud, GST fraud, and shell company networks.

**Solution:**
We combined rule-based detection with machine learning models and graph analysis to create a unified fraud intelligence system.

**⚡ 4. Making the System Fast and Demo-Ready**

**Challenge:**
Processing multiple data sources and AI analysis pipelines while maintaining a smooth user experience was challenging.

**Solution:**
We optimized API workflows, handled failures gracefully, and designed an interactive dashboard that presents complex investigations in a simple way.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
**Gonka Router**
FinTrace integrates the **Gonka Router API** to intelligently orchestrate requests across multiple microservices and external data sources. The router handles:

**Dynamic failover** between MCA21, CERSAI, GSTN, and RBI wilful-defaulter endpoints, automatically switching to backup mirrors (e.g., data.gov.in bulk) when primary APIs are unavailable or throttled.

**Secure credential rotation** and rate-limiting per source, ensuring compliance with government API usage policies while maximizing throughput.

This router layer is critical for FinTrace’s real‑time fraud screening, as it allows the engine to aggregate evidence from fragmented public records without exposing the analyst to the complexity of each source’s authentication and rate‑limit quirks.

**AI For Society**
**FinTrace directly addresses the societal harm** caused by financial fraud. By democratising forensic‑grade fraud detection, it:

**1.Protects taxpayers** by flagging GST ITC carousel fraud, which the Ministry of Finance valued at ₹61,545 crore in FY25 — money that could otherwise fund public welfare.

**2.Safeguards SMEs** from predatory evergreening and fabricated financials, preventing the collapse of small businesses and protecting jobs.

**3.Reduces the burden on public‑sector banks**, which bear 71% of fraud losses, ultimately saving taxpayer money and improving bank stability.

**4.Strengthens governance by providing transparent,** court‑defensible evidence chains, restoring civic trust in financial oversight and regulatory bodies.

The **Gonka Router** provides the data plumbing that feeds the **AI For Society engine**. Without reliable, real‑time access to government data, the AI would be guessing. Without the AI’s societal mission, the router would just be a technical curiosity. Together, they make FinTrace a practical, scalable, and trustworthy fraud‑fighting tool—ready for deployment in India’s financial regulatory landscape today.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body: While building Payung, we faced challenges connecting plain-language requests to live options and handling blockchain transactions. We solved this by using AI only to understand the request, while Thetanuts handles live pricing and execution. We also added checks for incomplete or unsupported requests.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# The Problem Payung Solves

Payung helps people protect the value of crypto they want to keep.

For example, imagine I own **1 ETH** worth about **$2,450**. I need its value to stay above **$2,300** for the next two weeks.

With Payung, I can simply say:

> I need my ETH to be worth at least $2,300 in two weeks.

Payung finds a real put option from the live Thetanuts orderbook. It shows the actual price of the protection and the possible payout, then lets me buy it.

If ETH is below $2,300 at the deadline, the option pays cash to help cover the difference. I still keep my ETH, so I can benefit if its price goes back up later.

## Why this is different from a stop-loss

A stop-loss sells the ETH when the price reaches a certain level. During a market crash, the sale may happen at a worse price because of slippage.

Payung does not sell the ETH. The protection is a separate contract, so I can keep ownership of my ETH while protecting its minimum value.

## What the AI does

The AI understands the request and converts it into protection settings such as:

- the asset: ETH
- the amount: 1 ETH
- the minimum value: $2,300
- the deadline: two weeks

The AI does not predict the market or set the price. Pricing and execution come directly from the live Thetanuts protocol.

description.title: BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK
description.body: Payung is built on the Thetanuts SDK to provide simple crypto downside protection. It reads the live Thetanuts orderbook, finds buyable put options, calculates the real premium, simulates the transaction, and lets the user execute the trade on Base mainnet.

description.title: AI × OPTIONS
description.body: Payung lets users describe their protection goal in plain language, such as “Protect my 1 ETH below $2,300 for two weeks.” The AI converts this request into structured parameters, then Payung finds a real matching put option using live Thetanuts data. After user confirmation, the trade is executed on-chain through the user’s wallet.

flamebase-173b.name: FlameBase
flamebase-173b.tagline: Fully on-chain social network on Base — every post

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body: Social apps today own your posts, your followers, and your money — the platform can delete your content, freeze your account, or take a cut of every tip. FlameBase puts all of it on-chain on Base: posts, likes, comments, and tips are real transactions, not database rows. Nobody can silently delete your history or seize your tips. On top of that, FlameBase ships a built-in AI agent (with x402 pay-per-use pricing and MCP support) that can post, like, tip, and trade on your behalf — the first social app agents can natively act inside.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Vercel's serverless functions cap request bodies at 4.5MB, which silently broke media uploads above that size and surfaced as a confusing JSON parse error. We fixed it by moving uploads to a direct browser-to-IPFS flow with short-lived, scoped credentials, keeping our backend out of the data path entirely.

Wiring an AI agent into real on-chain actions (tipping, trading, posting) safely was the other hard part — the agent never holds a private key; it prepares unsigned calldata and the user approves and signs every transaction themselves via MCP.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Blockchain is still too complicated for everyday users. Simple actions like sending tokens require users to understand wallet addresses, transaction details, gas fees, networks, and other technical concepts. This creates friction and makes Web3 intimidating for people who are not familiar with blockchain.

At the same time, AI can understand what users mean in natural language, but simply understanding a request is not enough — there needs to be a trusted way to turn that intent into an actual on-chain action.

Our project solves this by allowing users to interact with Sui through natural language. Instead of manually navigating complicated blockchain interfaces, users can simply describe what they want to do. The AI interprets their intent and prepares the action, while the user reviews and approves it before it is executed on-chain.

In short: we make blockchain interactions simpler and more accessible without taking control away from the user.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1)Incorrect SUI Amount Display

During development, we encountered an issue where the application consistently displayed 0.02 SUI regardless of the user's actual balance or transaction amount. This was caused by an issue in how the SUI balance and transaction amount were being retrieved and displayed by the frontend.


2)Gas Fee Not Included in Balance Calculation

We initially did not account for the Sui network gas fee when calculating and displaying the available SUI amount. This could result in the interface showing an amount that did not accurately represent the user's spendable balance after transaction fees. We identified this as an important issue because users need to know the actual cost of a transaction before approving it.


3)Difficulty Integrating with an Actual Sui Wallet

Another challenge we encountered was connecting the application to an actual Sui-compatible wallet and using it to execute real on-chain transactions. While the AI transaction flow could be demonstrated successfully, integrating wallet connection, transaction signing, user approval, and actual blockchain execution required additional Sui wallet and transaction integration work.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body: We are building an AI-powered transaction assistant that makes blockchain easier for everyday users. Users can describe what they want to do in natural language, such as “Send 5 SUI to Alice for dinner,” and the AI understands the intent and prepares the transaction for the user to review and approve. Sui then handles the trusted on-chain execution and provides a verifiable result. Our goal is to bridge the gap between AI’s ability to understand human intent and blockchain’s ability to securely execute transactions, making Web3 interactions simpler, more accessible, and user-friendly.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Options can protect crypto holders from large losses, but most people don't know how to build an options hedge themselves.

The goal of RiskShield is simple:

Make options protection understandable for humans, while keeping financial calculations and execution under strict deterministic rules

A user may understand their goal clearly eg.

“I have a $10,000 ETH position. Protect me if ETH falls 20% or more, cover at least half of that downside, and do not spend more than $200.”

But turning that simple request into a real hedge requires understanding put options, strike prices, expiry dates and more fancy technical terms. 

RiskShield makes that process easier.

**The user describes the risk they care about in normal language. AI translates that request into a clear set of rules**, such as:

· what asset they want to protect
· how large their position is
· how much they are willing to spend

After that, RiskShield's deterministic risk engine analyses live ETH put options from Thetanuts Finance on Base, calculates how much protection each one provides, checks the cost, rejects options that violate the user's limits, and selects a compliant hedge.

RiskShield supports two execution modes:

A) Copilot
RiskShield recommends a hedge, but the user reviews the exact transaction and approves it through MetaMask.

B) Autonomous
The user first sets strict safety limits, such as:
· Only protect ETH
· Only use USDC
· Never exceed a total spending limit

RiskShield can then monitor the market and determine whether an action is allowed under those rules.

For the hackathon, autonomous execution is kept in simulation mode so it cannot automatically spend real money. However, we separately proved that the underlying execution path works by successfully purchasing a real ETH put option through Thetanuts Finance on Base mainnet.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Different options could share the same identifier

At first, we assumed that the order nonce provided by the options market uniquely identified an option. When we tested against live Thetanuts data, we discovered that this was not true. Hundreds of orders could share the same nonce, and multiple ETH put options with different strike prices could have the same one.

This created a serious risk: the system could recommend one option but later retrieve another option that shared the same nonce. We solved this by creating our own cryptographic fingerprint using all of the important details of an option, including its strike price, expiry, price and maker signature.

This ensures that the option the user approved is exactly the option the system later prepares for execution.


2. We joined the hackathon only a few days before submission, while both of us are university students preparing for exams.

This meant we had to be extremely selective about what we built. We focused on proving the most important parts properly, such as real Thetanuts market data, deterministic financial calculations, and extensive automated testing. 

Some parts, such as fully automatic live trading, persistent storage and further UI/UX polish, were deliberately left for future development rather than being rushed into the hackathon version.

description.title: BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK
description.body:
RiskShield is built directly on top of the Thetanuts Finance SDK. In short, Thetanuts provides the actual options market and execution infrastructure, while RiskShield adds the risk engine and user experience.

The SDK is the live market and execution layer that RiskShield depends on.

We use Thetanuts to:

1. Fetch live options orders from the market
2. Identify suitable ETH put options
3. Inspect option details such as strike price, expiry and available size
4. Preview and simulate fills before execution
5. Prepare real option transactions
6. Manage exact USDC approvals
7. Verify positions after execution

RiskShield adds a decision and safety layer on top of this.

The user describes the protection they want in normal language, such as:

“Protect my $10,000 ETH position if ETH falls 20%, cover at least half of that downside, and spend no more than $200.”

RiskShield then converts that request into a strict policy, runs deterministic calculations against live Thetanuts options, and chooses a hedge that satisfies the user's limits.

We also built safeguards around the SDK integration after testing it against the live market. For example, we discovered that different orders could share the same nonce, so we created a cryptographic fingerprint over the economically important order fields to make sure the exact option being recommended is the one later prepared for execution.

We also use Base blockchain time instead of the local computer clock, because even a few minutes of clock difference can incorrectly make short-lived option quotes appear expired.

Finally, we proved the integration on Base mainnet by successfully purchasing a real ETH put option through Thetanuts Finance.

description.title: AI × OPTIONS
description.body:
RiskShield uses AI to make options hedging easier for people who understand the risk they're worried about, but not all the fancy financial terminology needed to build a hedge themselves.

“I have a $10,000 ETH position. Protect me if ETH falls 20% or more, cover at least half of that downside, and don't spend more than $200”

Normally, converting that request into options hedge needs understanding on financial terms such as strike prices, expiries, wallet permissions and more. 

RiskShield turns that human risk goal into a strict machine-readable format. A deterministic risk layer then evaluates live ETH put options from Thetanuts Finance on Base, calculates the required hedge size, rejects options that violate the user's constraints and selects a compliant hedge.

First, AI translates the user's everyday language into a clear set of rules that the system can understand.

Then RiskShield uses a deterministic risk engine, without AI, to analyse live ETH put options from Thetanuts Finance on Base. It calculates how much protection each option provides, how much it costs, and whether it satisfies the user's limits.

AI therefore handles the language, while normal code handles the financial calculations.

RiskShield supports two execution models:

A) Copilot
RiskShield recommends a hedge, but the user sees the exact transaction and approves it through MetaMask.

B) Autonomous
The user first sets strict safety limits such as: only protect ETH, only spend USDC,  never spend more than $100 in total, etc

RiskShield can then automatically check the market and decide what it would do, but only if every safety rule is satisfied.

For our hackathon, so it doesn't automatically spend real money. However, we separately proved that the underlying execution system works by successfully purchasing a real ETH put option through Thetanuts Finance on Base mainnet.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Challenges

**Measuring ρ at query time, with no corpus to measure against.**
Kish's formula needs a correlation between observations, and published inter-model agreement figures are benchmark averages — useless for *this* claim. So ρ comes from the evidence the models themselves name, scored by overlap. That leaves one free parameter, and we set it to **err against our own thesis**: in doubt, models count as *independent*, which raises the score and weakens our headline. `npm run sweep:threshold` reproduces the argument from runs on disk in two seconds, zero inferences.

**Every constant had to survive "why 50, why not 40?"**
Each number on screen is labelled **definition**, **standard** (published, source named), or **chosen** (our call, with the reasoning and which way it errs). One argument for the shrinkage prior turned out circular — `METHOD.md` says so instead of dressing it up.

**Our own failure paths were manufacturing evidence.**
An unparseable probe fell through to a recovery that accepted a draft *missing the key we asked for* — a **failed** probe reported as a witness that "named no source", counting toward the verdict. Failure laundered into data. Caught in review, fixed, replayed over 62 captured responses to prove nothing real was lost.

**"No evidence" is not "not measurable".**
Treating an unmeasurable witness as a disproven one makes the demo sharper and is a lie. Where overlap can't be measured, the prior is used **and labelled as assumed** — on screen, and in what the adjudicating model is told.

**The visualisation couldn't draw what it claimed to show.**
Dark seats on the sphere mean *this model didn't answer* — but the ring filled by count (`i < landed`), so it could never render a gap. Structurally incapable of telling the truth its caption claimed. Rebuilt per-probe; a real arrival order now shows gaps in 7 of 9 states.

**Neutrality had to live in the protocol, not the prompt.**
"Be objective" is not a mechanism. No probe sees the others; the mirror probe is a **separate request with no shared context**, so a model can't stay consistent with an answer it never saw.

**Building against a network we didn't control.**
Cached completions replayed one truncated answer forever; timeouts were non-retryable, costing a witness per slow node; the concurrency ceiling moved with everyone else's load. Fixes were the boring correct ones — cache-busting probes, retry budgets clipped to the deadline, and an **AIMD gate** (halve on refusal, widen after three clean calls) instead of a constant that would be wrong an hour later. **477 probes since: zero lost to parsing.**

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
## The problem it solves

*Five models agreeing is often one opinion repeated five times.* They share training data and failure modes, so they are wrong together — and averaging is most confident exactly when the panel is most likely to be wrong.

NEFF asks each model three questions, in separate requests with no shared context:

| Probe | Question | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| *Direct* | Is the claim true? | the vote |
| *Mirror* | Is the negation true? (asked blind) | a model reading the sentence, not the fact |
| *Anchor* | What evidence is this resting on? | three models reading one page |

Say yes to both a claim and its opposite → *echo, vote zeroed. Name the same evidence as another model* → *one witness, not two*. What survives is N_eff, computed with [Kish's design effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Design_effect) (1965):


N_eff = k / (1 + (k−1)·ρ)        ρ measured per claim, from the evidence
Truth Score = 50 + 50 × balance × n/(n+1)      n = N_eff


*Proof, from the live app:* three models returned *SUPPORTED at 95%, 95%, 85%*. A vote-counter calls that unanimous. All three *also affirmed the opposite claim.*

> NEFF scores it *NO SIGNAL — 0.0 effective witnesses*, and prints the six answers that prove it.

Every one of the 11 inferences shows its Gonka Request ID, serving node, latency and exact request body. No verdict reaches 0 or 100: a panel of language models is evidence, never proof.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
We are entering a world where generating information is becoming effortless.

**Knowing what to trust is becoming harder.**

Neff is designed as a transparency layer between AI-generated answers and the humans relying on them.

Instead of showing users a mysterious:

> “95% confident this is true.”

Neff shows:

- Who agreed?
- Did they survive the opposite-claim test?
- Did they rely on the same evidence?
- How many independent witnesses are they actually worth?

This makes AI verification more useful for journalists, researchers, educators, social platforms, and everyday users confronting misinformation.

Neff's goal isn't to become another AI that tells society what is true.

**It's to show society how much trust an AI answer has actually earned.**

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body: Most users understand the outcome they want, such as protecting their ETH from a large price drop while staying within a fixed budget, but they do not understand the technical options parameters needed to achieve it. They must choose the correct PUT or CALL, BUY or SELL direction, strike price, expiry, premium, contract size, and live order, which makes on-chain options difficult and risky for non-expert users. HedgeOS solves this by allowing users to describe their risk goal in natural language, then converting that goal into structured financial intent and matching it with suitable live Thetanuts options.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Thetanuts options.

Challenges We Ran Into: The biggest challenge was making AI useful without allowing it to silently make unsafe financial decisions. We had to separate AI interpretation from deterministic verification, preserve the user’s original intent when browsing alternative contracts, correctly handle PUT/CALL and BUY/SELL mappings, support structures such as PHYSICAL_PUT, maintain correct USDC decimal conversions, and prevent portfolio values such as 2 ETH from being misinterpreted. We also had to handle live market changes, revalidate the selected Thetanuts order before authorization, fix false ORDER_CHANGED detections, and design the system so that HedgeOS can prepare and verify the exact transaction while keeping final financial authorization outside the AI boundary.

description.title: BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK
description.body: HedgeOS directly uses the Thetanuts SDK and live OptionBook as the core market layer of the product. The main problem we solve is that users may know the protection outcome they want, but they may not know how to choose the correct option type, strike, expiry, premium, or contract size. This makes HedgeOS strongly related to this track because Thetanuts is not just an added feature; its SDK, live pricing, option orders, and transaction data are essential to the entire protection workflow.

description.title: AI × OPTIONS
description.body: HedgeOS applies AI to simplify and improve the options decision process while keeping the financial logic verifiable. The user can describe a goal such as protecting 2 ETH within a fixed premium budget, and the AI converts that natural-language request into structured intent. HedgeOS then uses deterministic logic together with live Thetanuts options to validate the request, find suitable PUT or CALL strategies, calculate contract sizing and premium requirements, and revalidate the selected order before preparing the transaction. This fits the AI × Options track because AI is used to understand and explain the user’s risk objective, while Thetanuts provides the live on-chain options market that turns the AI-generated intent into a real, execution-ready options strategy.

fortifi-44af.name: FortiFi
fortifi-44af.tagline: Financial Firewall Between Information and Action

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
## The problem it solves

Financial information can move markets quickly, but users often have to make decisions based on claims, headlines, or articles that may be misleading, incomplete, or difficult to verify. Even when a claim is identified as risky, users may not have a clear way to understand how that risk could affect their ETH holdings or what protection options are available.

FortiFi addresses this by combining multi-model AI verification with evidence gathering, portfolio risk assessment, and live options protection. It helps users evaluate financial claims before acting, understand potential downside exposure, and discover suitable ETH protection strategies through Thetanuts. The system also provides an auditable record of its analysis and completed protection actions through Sui, making the decision-making process more transparent and verifiable.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Challenges we ran into

One of our biggest challenges was our team's background. We are all cybersecurity students rather than software engineering students, and most of us had limited experience building a complete application involving AI, blockchain, frontend, backend, and smart-contract integrations.

This was also the first or second hackathon for everyone on the team, so we had to learn how to work with unfamiliar technologies while developing the product under a strict time constraint. Integrating multiple external technologies such as Gonka, Thetanuts, Base, and Sui required us to understand APIs, wallet interactions, blockchain transactions, and different development environments simultaneously.

Testing the blockchain components presented another practical challenge. We did not have sufficient funds in our wallets to freely test every on-chain operation, particularly automated contract interactions on Sui. As a result, we had to be careful with testing and work within the available testnet resources while ensuring that the core functionality could still be demonstrated.

Despite these limitations, the challenges forced us to simplify our architecture, divide responsibilities across the team, and focus on delivering a working end-to-end prototype rather than attempting to build every feature to production scale.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body: FortiFi uses Sui to create tamper-evident records of AI-assisted financial analysis and subsequent protection actions. Financial claims are assessed by multiple AI models through Gonka Router, and users can authorize anchoring a report hash through a Move contract on Sui testnet. After an options purchase on Base, a separate protection record links the analysis report hash to the associated Base transaction. The contract prevents duplicate report hashes, while the backend sponsors the Sui transaction. This gives users a traceable connection between the assessment and the recorded action, allowing saved reports to be checked for changes without publishing their full contents on-chain.

description.title: BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK
description.body: FortiFi integrates the Thetanuts SDK into a guided ETH protection workflow, from live option discovery to wallet-confirmed purchase on Base mainnet. It retrieves OptionBook orders and market data, filters eligible ETH puts, and presents Basic, Balanced, and Strong protection choices based on the user's budget and preferences. Users can compare strike prices, expiry dates, estimated costs, and settlement types before selecting an option. Before execution, FortiFi refreshes the selected order and checks for material changes in price or quantity. The SDK then handles USDC allowance and order execution through the user's wallet, making options protection more accessible through a single interface.

description.title: AI × OPTIONS
description.body: FortiFi connects AI-assisted financial claim assessment with actionable ETH options protection. Through Gonka Router, multiple AI models evaluate submitted claims against retrieved evidence and provide assessments of credibility, potential market impact, and missing context. Connected users can review their ETH exposure and estimated losses under hypothetical price declines. Claim-impact assessments and ETH allocation inform an initial protection preference, which users can adjust alongside their budget. FortiFi then uses live Thetanuts data and rule-based selection to suggest eligible ETH puts. Users review the terms and confirm purchases through their own Base wallet, bringing evidence review, risk awareness, and options execution into one workflow.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body: FortiFi helps users assess potentially misleading financial information before making decisions that could affect their savings or crypto holdings. It uses Gonka Router to compare assessments from multiple AI models alongside retrieved news evidence and available article content. Results present model verdicts, confidence, reasoning summaries, and missing context, helping users understand uncertainty and identify what needs further verification. A faster mode uses two successful model responses, while an optional mode waits for all three. By combining accessible claim assessment with ETH downside scenarios and user-controlled protection choices, FortiFi aims to support financial literacy and more informed decisions when users encounter uncertain or conflicting information.

suiroll-ab11.name: SuiRoll
suiroll-ab11.tagline: AI prepares payroll. You approve. Sui settles.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# The Problem Suiroll Solves

**Paying contractors involves more than sending money.** Teams must collect invoices, calculate adjustments, verify wallet addresses, approve payments, and confirm that everyone received the correct amount.

For small teams that already hold stablecoins, this work can be scattered across spreadsheets, messaging threads, wallets, and blockchain explorers. The operator must manually connect what should be paid with what actually settled.

This creates four recurring problems:

- **Repeated manual work:** Moving payment information between tools takes time and introduces opportunities for mistakes.
- **Payment errors:** Duplicate invoices, conflicting amounts, and unexpected adjustments can go unnoticed before authorization.
- **Fragmented execution:** Sending individual transfers means repeated actions and more transactions to track.
- **Uncertain outcomes:** A submitted transaction still needs confirmation and reconciliation. Retrying without checking can risk duplicate payment.

## How Suiroll Helps

Suiroll connects contractor-payroll preparation, review, authorization, and settlement in one workflow:

1. **Prepare:** Save contractor details and import CSV/XLSX payroll files or enter payments manually.
2. **Review:** Calculate exact amounts, exclude duplicate invoices, block conflicting inputs, and flag unusual increases.
3. **Approve:** Review the payment plan, check readiness, and authorize it with the treasury wallet.
4. **Pay:** Execute multiple contractor payments through one Sui Programmable Transaction Block.
5. **Reconcile:** Verify settlement against the approved plan and retain exportable payment records.

The user controls authorization. Suiroll provides checks and evidence to support that decision.

## Why Sui

Sui’s Programmable Transaction Blocks allow the payroll transfers to execute atomically: the batch’s transfers complete together or none complete. Failed transactions can still incur gas costs.

Suiroll uses on-chain evidence to verify the result before marking payroll **Paid & reconciled**, connecting the original payment plan to confirmed execution.

## Who It Serves

Our initial customers are small Sui ecosystem teams, agencies, and distributed businesses that already hold stablecoins and pay contractors willing to receive them.

For founders and finance operators, Suiroll offers a repeatable process with less tool switching, clearer payment controls, and traceable records.

The current prototype demonstrates this workflow on **Sui Testnet with testnet USDC**. It focuses on contractor payouts, not statutory payroll, tax filing, or bank withdrawals.

> **Suiroll turns a contractor spreadsheet into an approved, verified stablecoin payday.**

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
# Challenges We Ran Into

Although we had explored blockchain before, building Suiroll was our first time bringing Sui, wallet integration, and payroll operations together in a complete application. Turning our existing knowledge into a reliable payment workflow presented several challenges.

## Sui and wallet integration

Connecting a wallet was only the beginning. We needed to handle transaction construction, gas fees, signature verification, and settlement confirmation.

One bug appeared after wallet approval: the payroll was approved, but submission failed. We traced it to social-login signature verification, which required a configured Sui client to validate zkLogin signatures. We corrected the integration and added regression tests.

## Reliable payroll execution

Sending tokens was not enough—we also needed exact calculations, duplicate-invoice protection, and safe recovery from network errors.

We implemented integer-based calculations, database-backed invoice reservations, and settlement verification. Separating uncertain transaction outcomes from confirmed failures helped prevent unsafe payment retries.

## Connecting the full workflow

Integrating the frontend, Supabase, AI-assisted imports, and Sui introduced issues with database setup, unexpected AI response formats, and development-server state.

We resolved these through documentation, debugging, isolated integration checks, and workflow testing. We ultimately completed a three-recipient testnet payroll and reconciled its payments.

The biggest lesson was turning separate technologies into one dependable experience, where every step from importing payroll to confirming payment works together.

poke-c84d.name: Poké
poke-c84d.tagline: One address. Every chain. Every claim, provable.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body: Our main hurdle was GonkaRouter's 30-second inference timeout. Scam Detection and Whistleblow both ask Gonka to reason over real evidence, and with dual-model consensus running two inferences at once, that timeout shaped how we built every request in both features.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
**The Problem**

Web3 today forces you to trust things you can't verify. Checking a wallet, exploring a transaction, and running a suspicious link through an AI "scam checker" all live in separate tools — and when any of them use AI, you get back a bare risk percentage with zero evidence behind it. You're left with two bad options: blindly believe a black-box verdict, or dig through raw block data yourself with no guidance at all.

**The Whistleblower Gap**

It gets worse if you're the one who actually catches fraud on-chain. There's no safe way to prove what you saw and when you saw it without exposing your identity — so people who spot real fraud are stuck choosing between staying silent or putting a target on their own back. That's a gap nobody in this space has meaningfully closed.

**Why Poké Is Different**

Poké closes both gaps at once, and does it by changing what "trust" means rather than just adding another AI feature on top. Scam Detection doesn't hand you a bare score — it shows the evidence, the reasoning trace, and a Gonka Request ID you can independently verify against Gonka's own records, so you're checking the verdict instead of believing it. Whistleblow doesn't ask for a name — it anchors a cryptographic commitment of the report and evidence on-chain, so the timing and content can never be disputed later, and the person behind it never has to be identified.

**The Net Result**

One command center where inspecting a wallet, judging a scam, and proving fraud all work the same way: nothing asks for your trust, everything hands you a receipt.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body: Poké fits the "AI for Society" challenge's preferred Truth Engine Pattern almost exactly, where a wrong verdict costs real money. Every AI call routes through GonkaRouter, Scam Detection can run a multi-model consensus and results are labeled with Truth Scores. Every inference ships a model name plus a Gonka request ID users can identify on their own. The whistleblower goes a step further than the challenge's "on-chain proof" by anchoring cryptographic commitment of the evidence itself on chain rather than only displaying a request ID.

blocks-and-scissors-c165.name: Blocks And Scissors
blocks-and-scissors-c165.tagline: Trust the cut not the promise

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Blocks & Scissors solves the trust problem that happens when a customer and a barber disagree over whether the final haircut actually matches the reference that was agreed on beforehand. Normally, the customer has to either pay despite being unhappy, or refuse payment and leave the barber with no guaranteed protection.

Our solution uses an AI-verified escrow system. The customer locks the payment in a Sui smart contract before the service. After the haircut, the reference image and final result are compared by our AI scoring pipeline. If the score meets the agreed threshold, the barber is paid automatically. If it does not, the customer is refunded.

This makes the process safer for both sides: customers get protection against clearly mismatched results, while barbers get protection against customers refusing to pay after an acceptable service. The same model could later be applied to other reference-based services such as tailoring, tattoos, detailing, repairs, and commissioned work.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges was getting the AI score to react to the haircut itself rather than differences in the photos. Raw image similarity was too sensitive to lighting, backgrounds, camera angle and styling. I improved this by adding hair-focused crops, grayscale and blurred shape comparisons, mirrored side-profile matching, and separate checks for haircut family, texture, back length and fade/taper structure. I also added confidence-aware penalties so uncertain classifications do not affect the score too aggressively.
Another challenge was connecting the off-chain AI result to an actual on-chain payment. The AI runs in the FastAPI backend, while the escrow lives on Sui. I built an oracle flow where the backend submits the final score through an authorized OracleCap, and the Move contract decides whether to pay the barber or refund the customer. I tested the flow using Sui dry-runs and live testnet transactions, and also handled issues such as network mismatches, gas configuration and preventing an escrow from being settled twice.
The final MVP works end-to-end, but the AI is still optimized mainly for side-profile fade and taper comparisons, so broader hairstyle support and multi-angle verification would be the next major improvement.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body:
Blocks & Scissors fits the AI × SUI track because the project combines AI-based verification with on-chain payment settlement. The AI backend compares a customer’s reference haircut with the completed haircut using OpenCLIP and custom haircut-specific scoring logic, including hairstyle structure, texture, back length, fade/taper characteristics, and confidence-aware penalties. This produces a similarity score from 0–100.

Sui is then used as the settlement layer. Before the service, the customer locks the payment inside a Move escrow object containing the customer, barber, funds, and agreed threshold. After the AI produces its score, an authorized backend oracle submits that score to the smart contract. If the score meets or exceeds the threshold, the contract releases the escrowed SUI to the barber; otherwise, it refunds the customer.

This means AI is responsible for evaluating the real-world result, while Sui provides neutral, transparent, and enforceable settlement. The project demonstrates a broader pattern of AI-verified service escrow, where AI can assess completion and Sui can automatically enforce the pre-agreed payment outcome.

makanloop-cab6.name: MakanLoop
makanloop-cab6.tagline: "We turn food waste from an invisible cost"

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Building MakanLoop required combining AI, Sui blockchain, and a real-world sustainability workflow, which created several technical challenges. The biggest challenge was designing a system where blockchain adds genuine value without making the user experience complicated. We solved this by using Sui for verifiable sustainability records and rewards, while keeping detailed application data off-chain.

We also faced challenges with AI-based food-waste estimation, since food quantity cannot always be accurately determined from an image alone. We addressed this by making the AI an assistance layer, allowing the hawker to confirm or correct the result before verification.

Another challenge was keeping the experience simple for non-Web3 users. We designed the flow around QR codes and a simple onboarding experience, so users can interact with MakanLoop without needing deep blockchain knowledge.

These challenges helped us build a more practical architecture combining AI for intelligence, Sui for trust, and a simple UX for adoption.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Singapore has a strong and globally recognized hawker culture, but food waste remains a significant environmental and economic challenge. Hawkers often lack simple, efficient tools to track what food is being wasted, how much is being wasted, and how their waste changes over time. At the same time, customers have limited visibility into a hawker's sustainability efforts and few incentives to actively participate in reducing waste.

Existing food-rescue, ordering, and loyalty platforms address individual parts of the ecosystem, but they do not connect "waste measurement, sustainability verification, customer participation, and rewards" to one continuous system.

MakanLoop aims to solve this gap by using "AI to assist hawkers in tracking food waste, Sui blockchain to create transparent and verifiable sustainability records, and a reward system to encourage customers and hawkers to adopt sustainable behaviours."

This creates a simple loop:

"Eat → Measure → Verify → Reward → Improve → Repeat"

The goal is to turn everyday hawker activities into "measurable sustainability impact" while helping hawkers reduce waste, save resources, build sustainability reputation, and encouraging customers to become active participants.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body: MakanLoop combines AI and Sui blockchain to tackle food waste in Singapore’s hawker ecosystem. Our AI-assisted system analyzes food-waste images to classify food and estimate quantities, helping hawkers track and reduce waste. Verified sustainability actions are recorded on Sui, creating transparent and tamper-resistant impact records. Customers can then earn digital rewards for participating in sustainable actions, creating a continuous Measure → Verify → Reward → Improve loop.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. What if the AI gets tricked? (Math over promises)
The Challenge: If a scammer jailbreaks the LLM or it hallucinates and calls a real scam "LOW risk", a wallet that blindly trusts AI loses her life savings.
How We Overcame It: We enforced safety in Sui Move with one line of math: effective_tier = max(amount_tier, claimed_tier). Even if the AI claims a $600 transfer is completely safe, the contract independently detects it crossed her personal ceiling and forces it to HIGH escrow anyway. The chain never has to trust the AI to protect her.

2. Real-world AI infrastructure is unpredictable
The Challenge: Decentralized AI inference has real-world latency spikes (measuring up to 26s+ on cold calls and 524 timeouts on Kimi model). We couldn't let network lag leave her unprotected during a live scam.
How We Overcame It: We decoupled safety from AI availability. Instant deterministic threat floors (authority impersonation + urgency + secrecy demands) run locally on-device. If Gonka models lag, disagree, or go offline, the hard floor automatically takes over and holds the funds. Safety never depends on Wi-Fi holding up.

3. Passive chat scanning vs. Spyware & Family abuse
The Challenge: Passively monitoring WhatsApp sounds like spyware. Worse, family members are statistically a leading vector for elder financial abuse—handing her son her chat transcripts would just replace an online scammer with family coercion.
How We Overcame It: We built structural privacy. Identifying PII (names, IC, phone numbers) is stripped on-device before transmission. Scoring runs inside a confidential enclave that only emits an opaque hash and signature. And the Guardian Dashboard only shows transfer amounts and recipients—never her private conversations.

. "Just push to Vercel" broke our security architecture
The Challenge: Serverless platforms wipe in-memory state on cold starts. Our enclave holds an active signing key in memory; a cold start would mint a new key mid-demo and instantly invalidate every on-chain attestation.
How We Overcame It: We rejected the serverless shortcut. We containerized our persistent Node services with Docker and deployed on Railway, preserving in-memory enclave keys, loopback network security, and cryptographic integrity with zero broken sessions.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
She isn't hacked. She's talked into sending it herself — "manufactured consent."

RM2.97 billion lost to scams in just 11 months of 2025 (67,735 cases). Bank Negara Malaysia's 2025 Annual Report puts 95% of Malaysia's online fraud cases as "authorised transactions" — the victim approved the transfer herself, no key stolen. Bukit Aman CCID logged RM3.11 billion in total commercial crime losses for 2024 alone, RM2.45 billion of it fraud across 37,240 investigation papers. Seniors are the sharpest edge of that curve: only 6.4% of victims (5,533 of 86,266, 2021–2023) but 20% of total losses (RM552.5M of RM2.7B) — and by mid-2024 that gap had widened to 8.3% of victims vs. 27.7% of losses.

RM1.47 billion from investment scams alone — over half of all losses. Investment scam losses jumped from RM848.6M (6,337 cases) in 2024 to RM1.47B (9,603 cases) in 2025, a ~73% year-over-year rise, with syndicates moving victims from Facebook/ Instagram into WhatsApp or Telegram "trading groups" before blocking withdrawals. Love scams cost RM45.9M in 2024 (up from RM43.9M in 2023), 75.6% of victims women 61+, and 370 cases started on Facebook, 332 on WhatsApp in 2023 — the two most common contact points. The US shows the same shape: FBI IC3 logged 147,000+ complaints from adults 60+ in 2024 — more than any other age group — for $4.8–4.9B, up 43% YoY, averaging $83,000 per victim.

70% of victims never report — real losses may hit RM54 billion. And what does get spent goes to the wrong category: banks blocked RM383M in fraudulent transactions in 2023 alone (RM780M+ combined 2023–2024), and the National Scam Response Centre froze 162,642 mule accounts in the latest reporting year — none of it touching the 95% "authorised transaction" category, because it's all built to catch stolen credentials, not manufactured consent. Once sent, instant payment rails move funds irreversibly within seconds, and no existing tool sits at that exact point: ScamShield/Truecaller warn on known numbers but go silent once a chat moves to WhatsApp; BioCatch reads banking-session hesitation, not the conversation that caused it. Nobody else sits in the top-right — blocking it before, at the moment money is given away.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body:
SHOU aligns perfectly with Sui Track 01 (Payments & Stablecoins) because it is fundamentally a stablecoin wallet engineered with programmable, on-chain controls. The track specifically highlights "stablecoin wallets, treasury, escrow" as core ideas, and our underlying Move architecture (SeniorityPolicy and TransferRequest) directly delivers on this premise. We are not an AI project with a blockchain bolted on; we are a functional on-chain fund gate.

Specifically, we leverage Sui's payment rails to hit the track's judging criteria:

Frictionless Payments (Product UX): By integrating Sui zkLogin, we replace complex seed phrases with standard Google sign-in, making stablecoin wallets accessible to our target demographic (elderly parents receiving family remittances).

Secure Escrow & Routing (Technical Implementation): We utilize Sui Move's shared objects and capabilities to create a wallet-level circuit breaker. This allows us to actively halt fraudulent USDC transfers on-chain before they execute, backed by a fully tested 7-step testnet flow.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
SHOU aligns perfectly with Gonka — AI for Society because it directly applies AI to solve a critical societal failure: the billions lost by elderly victims to "manufactured consent" scams. We utilize the Gonka Network as the core intelligence layer to proactively prevent financial ruin.

Specifically, we leverage the Gonka Router to meet the track's mandatory requirements:

Zero Third-Party Proxies: All AI reasoning runs directly on the Gonka Network via the official gateway (api.gonkarouter.io/v1/chat/completions).

Multi-Model Consensus: We utilize a dual-model pipeline (DeepSeek-V4-Flash as the classifier and MiniMax-M2.7 as the skeptical cross-verifier) to independently analyze redacted messages passively extracted from WhatsApp DOMs.

Itemized Reasoning & Transparency: The system provides a 0-100% truth score based on specific vectors (urgency, authority-impersonation, secrecy). Every inference call is auditable via the exact Gonka Request ID displayed on the user's dashboard.

Fail-Safe Innovation: Unlike most AI safety products that fail open, our implementation degrades safely. If a model returns a bad verdict or is unavailable, it raises the risk tier to MEDIUM, ensuring the user's base on-chain spending rules still apply rather than silently clearing a fraudulent transfer.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Building Konfirm required overcoming complex technical and design hurdles across model orchestration, output sanitization, and Web3 abstraction. Structuring multi-model parallel execution across DeepSeek, Kimi, and MiniMax demanded custom promise racing logic to eliminate sub-second latency while avoiding empty payload returns. We also had to engineer robust regex parsers to strip out DeepSeek <think> reasoning blocks and markdown artifacts for deterministic JSON output, design prompt frameworks that generate empathetic, non-confrontational native-language refutations, and seamlessly abstract Sui blockchain record creation using zkLogin and Enoki gas sponsorship so everyday users can verify claims on-chain without managing cryptographic wallets or seed phrases

THere were a few challenges on Sui’s side too. First, zkLogin's OAuth options are narrower than a normal web login, only a handful of providers are supported and Google was the only one practical for our users, which meant no fallback if the salt service or prover misbehaved, so we went through Enoki (which bundles salt, prover, and sponsored gas behind one key) and built a mock useKonfirmIdentity hook with a hard cutoff date so the rest of the app was never blocked on auth. Second, Sui's object model is fundamentally different from account-based chains: we had to unlearn msg.sender-style checks and understand ownership types, the key/store/copy/drop abilities, and shared-object contention before we could design the Verdict correctly. Our first draft used a shared Registry object for indexing, which would have serialised every write, and we replaced it with events indexed off-chain. Third, Walrus was the least documented piece: setting up the publisher, deploying to testnet, and working out whether we needed WAL tokens cost more time than expected, until we switched to the public HTTP publisher (unsigned PUT) which removed the token dependency entirely, with a hash-verified fetch so tampered blobs are detected on read and a Vercel Blob fallback in case testnet quota ran out on demo day.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Konfirm solves a two-layer problem in how misinformation spreads through Malaysian WhatsApp family groups and Facebook. 

Konfirm’s judgment layer handles forwarded information (news articles, health information, etc.) that mixes English, Malay and Chinese that does not contain a source or date, A tool such as Konfirm is superior compared to existing tools, such as Sebenarnya.my which is slow and only handles information in English and Malay. One may attempt to use international fact-checkers instead, but they miss out on local context. Aside from that, using a single AI for verification is not reliable as information is coming from only one source. Konfirm is built upon these drawbacks by having five independent models judge in parallel and surface their disagreement as a Truth Score.

Meanwhile, Konfirm’s trust layer solves the issue of data integrity. This is important as even a correct verdict is worthless if it can be silently edited later. This is helpful for a young person who identifies that the rumour has no credible artifact, to convince the elder who believes it. Sui is used so if there is no public way to contest a wrong verdict. then writing each verdict as a Sui shared object with its reasoning trace on Walrus allows anyone to verify the claim, even without a wallet. This is because users can share the results as a card or as a polite refutation in their own language, see how many times the same claim was already checked. Although this does not guarantee the validity of a claim, using Sui ensures all records are appended as a public challenge that can't be deleted or modified,

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body:
AI fact-checking has a trust problem that no database can fix, this refers to two scenarios: One where a verdict stored in Postgres is only as trustworthy as the operator, who is also allowed to quietly edit, retract, or re-score the information. and another in Malaysia where Sebenarnya.my's credibility can be speculated as it may be influenced by the government’s narrative of the news. 

Konfirm solves this by making each AI verdict a Sui shared object rather than a log entry. The object ID is the permalink on the shareable card, the reasoning trace lives on Walrus with its hash committed on-chain, claim_hash deduplicates recirculating rumours at the object level, and a permissionless add_challenge entry function lets anyone append an objection that is as undeletable as the verdict itself. zkLogin plus sponsored gas means a 58-year-old with only WhatsApp on her phone can open, read, and verify a verdict on-chain in under 60 seconds with zero wallet, zero gas. However, as mentioned earlier, a record being on-chain doesn't prove the AI was right; it proves what we said, when we said it, and who challenged it are three things we can't change

description.title: AI For Society
description.body: Misinformation and scams in Malaysia spread through WhatsApp family groups and Facebook forwards, in content that mixes English, Malay and Chinese with no source or date and the people who receive it split into elders who believe it and forward it, and younger family members who know it's false but have nothing convincing to reply with, causing them to they stay silent. Meanwhile as mentioned earlier, existing options fail this exact scene. Sebenarnya.my is slow and only in English and Malay languages, international fact-checkers miss local context, and a single AI claiming information is false is just one more unverifiable assertion. Konfirm routes every claim through five independent models via Gonka and Gemini in parallel, aggregating their votes into a Truth Score that shows the divergence rather than hiding it, then generates a debunking card in the recipient's own language. This gives the younger user a credible rebuttal and the elder something they can read and check themselves, with checking kept free forever.

nutshell-8558.name: NutShell
nutshell-8558.tagline: Verified crisis detection that buys real downside

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
### The evidence layer was confidently wrong before it was useful

Our biggest failure was not a crash. It was a correct measurement driving a wrong
conclusion.

A scripted claim said $40M had been drained from a Base bridge. Our oracle check
compared Base DEX spot against Chainlink, found them agreeing to within 0.14%,
and returned CONTRADICTS. Both models then scored the claim FAKE at 22 and 25,
both citing that exact reading, and the decision fell from HEDGE_SMALL to REJECT.

The measurement was right. The inference was garbage. $40M is roughly 0.014% of
ETH's market cap, so a drain that size need not move the price at all. Price
agreement is not evidence that no drain occurred, but the model had no way to
know that.

We fixed it by classifying what a claim actually asserts (price, custody, or
halt) and letting each check contradict only claims about the thing it measures.
Corroboration stays unrestricted, because finding real distress is always worth
surfacing, while wrongly ruling out a true report is the error that costs someone
a hedge. After the fix the same scenario returned zero contradicting checks and
MiniMax scored it 68 REAL.

A related one: we pointed a balance check at Aave v3's `Pool` contract and it
reported 114 USDC while DeFiLlama showed billions in TVL. Aave v3 holds reserves
in aTokens. We were measuring an address that never custodies anything and
reporting "no drain" with total confidence. Now an address below a custody floor
returns INCONCLUSIVE instead of a reassuring zero.

### Thetanuts: the order book has traps that only fail on-chain

**Spreads look like puts.** Filtering on `isCall === false` seemed obviously
right. Every longer dated order we selected that way reverted with
`Panic(17) OVERFLOW` inside the contract. Their calldata carries two or three
strikes: they are spreads, not vanilla puts. We now require exactly one strike
before an order is fillable.

**`previewFillOrder` echoes your own input back.** Its `totalCollateral` field
returns the budget you passed in, not a computed charge, so it can never reveal a
shortfall. We had been approving against it and were only accidentally correct,
because integer flooring means the real charge always lands just under the
budget. Worth knowing before it bites someone else.

**A fill reverted with "transfer amount exceeds allowance" against an allowance
that was sufficient.** We chased four wrong theories (unmined approval, wrong
variable, rounding, a referrer fee) before static calling the fill against every
candidate order and finding all of them would succeed. The approval had mined on
one node while our `eth_call` was served by another a block behind. A stale read,
not a logic bug. Retrying filled it.

**There is no early exit.** We tested it rather than assuming: `close()` reverts
unless one address holds both sides, `reclaimCollateral()` is seller only, and
nothing bids for puts. Recovery on abandoning a hedge is 0%. That single fact
reshaped the product, because if you cannot undo a purchase then the only place
you can save money is before you make it. It is why agreement gates spending.

### Gonka: the model catalogue can lie to you

`GET /models` listed `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6`. Every `POST /chat` against it
returned `400 unsupported model`, naming in its own error body the two models it
would actually serve. A health check that trusts the catalogue reports a full
three model panel while live runs quietly fail quorum, which is exactly what
happened to us.

So we stopped asking the catalogue and started judging on outcomes. The call path
records success and failure per model in a rolling window, and a model that
resolves but has answered nothing is reported as unusable. The health endpoint
cannot be contradicted by the thing it is checking.

Two more, both measured: **streaming silently disables the SDK timeout**, because
the HTTP response opens immediately, so one queued call ran 600s past a 120s
budget. We stayed non-streaming. And **node selection happens upstream**, so the
same model answers in under a second or in 40 seconds depending which node takes
it. We send a duplicate request at 14s and take whichever lands first, which
turns a straggler into a fast vote instead of a lost one.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
**Crypto moves on news before it moves on price.**

When a bridge is drained or a lending market halts, the information is public
minutes before the oracle catches up. If you are asleep, at work, or just not
refreshing Twitter, you absorb the entire move.

The obvious defence is to hold put options all the time. Almost nobody does,
because permanent protection costs several percent of notional a year against a
yield of a few percent. It is negative carry by construction, so protection has
to be event driven. That moves the hard part somewhere else: an event driven
hedger is only as good as its trigger. Fire on rumour and you burn premium on
every false alarm. Wait for confirmation and you buy insurance after the crash.

**NutShell is the trigger.** It reads eight public newswires continuously,
measures each claim against Base mainnet itself, has three independent AI models
score it, and buys a real protective put on Thetanuts only when the evidence and
the models agree.

### Who it is for

- **Anyone holding ETH, BTC or SOL who cannot watch the news 24/7.** The agent
  watches instead, and it can only ever spend a capped premium budget.
- **Small DAO treasuries with no risk desk.** Automated, bounded downside cover
  with a written reason attached to every trade.
- **Anyone who just wants a claim checked.** The verification page is public and
  needs no wallet. Paste a headline, get three named models scoring it with their
  request ids.

### What it actually changes

| Before | With NutShell |
|---|---|
| You find out when the price already moved | The agent reads the wire and the chain in the same minute |
| Protection costs more than the position earns | One dollar of premium bought $912 of ETH downside cover, about 0.1% of notional |
| "The AI said so" | Every verdict names its model, shows its request id, and the id resolves on Gonka's chain |
| A hedge is a number in a spreadsheet | Every position traces back to the exact sentence that bought it, under one id |

Premiums come out of vault yield. Principal is never touched. The agent runs on a
policy bounded burner wallet that can do exactly one thing, buy a protective put,
against exactly one allowlisted contract, under a hard per trade ceiling.

**Live on Base mainnet.** Four real fills, real USDC, all verifiable on BaseScan.

description.title: BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK
description.body:
**Does it work?** Yes, and it is running, not described. Four options bought on
Base mainnet with real USDC, each one a deployed contract with an entry
transaction on BaseScan. One ETH put is open right now. An earlier position was
held to expiry and settled out of the money, recovering nothing, which is the
honest outcome for insurance that was not needed.

**Are the options load-bearing?** Stub out Thetanuts and there is no product
left. The entire thesis is that a trustworthy trigger makes event driven
protection affordable, and the put is the protection. We use the SDK for order
book reads, quote decoding, exact approvals and fills, and the selection funnel is
built around the venue's real constraints: single strike vanilla puts only, a
quote TTL near 60 seconds that the whole select, approve, sign and broadcast path
has to fit inside, a delta band, a minimum expiry horizon, and available depth.
Cash settled synthetics gave us BTC and SOL cover without those assets existing
on Base.

**Does it fit the market?** Protective puts are the most understood hedge in
finance and almost nobody in crypto holds them, for one reason: you cannot afford
to hold them permanently. That makes the trigger the product, not the option. We
built the trigger and used Thetanuts to act on it. The users are retail holders
and small treasuries who want a floor under a position without watching a feed
all night. What happens after the hackathon is that this needs a real yield
source plugged into the vault interface, which already accepts one unchanged.

description.title: AI × OPTIONS
description.body:
**The bar is one real on-chain trade against live pricing, and we cleared it four
times.**

| Asset | Strike | Entry transaction |
|---|---|---|
| ETH | $2,340 | `0x9c4bb145…828f8c` (open) |
| BTC | $75,500 | `0xbbb8b74b…c06309` |
| SOL | $97 | `0xda94b0b8…c385a7` |
| ETH | $2,380 | `0xe2d5fcce…d62c1b2d` (settled OTM) |

This is an autonomous hedging agent in the sense the track describes. The AI is
not a natural language wrapper over a trade button. It is the thing that decides
whether money moves at all, and the decision is a real one that says no far more
often than yes.

The interesting part is the refusal. Three models score a claim, and consensus
produces two numbers: a truth score and an agreement score. Both have thresholds.
Two readings of the same event can share a truth score of 91 while agreement
falls from 86% to 31%, and the second buys nothing. You can drag that agreement
slider yourself on our landing page and watch the live policy engine flip
HEDGE_FULL to ESCALATE.

Size is then bound by whichever of five caps bites first: premium reserve, daily
cap, per trade hard ceiling, book depth, or the tier. The incident record names
which one bound it. In our worked example, policy cleared full size and the per
trade ceiling cut it to three dollars, and the page says so.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
The challenge names an **AI Fact Checker** as the preferred application: a
decentralized truth engine using multi-model inference, producing a Truth Score
with a traceable reasoning trail. That is precisely what NutShell's verification
layer is, and we then did something no other fact checker does. We put money
behind the verdict.

Against the stated requirements:

| Requirement | How we meet it |
|---|---|
| All AI reasoning on Gonka via gonkarouter.io | Every inference in the product. No other provider appears anywhere in the verification path. |
| Multi-model consensus, at least two models | Three: MiniMax, Kimi and DeepSeek, called in parallel on an identical prompt, with model substitution disabled so the panel is genuinely three different models. |
| Claim extraction from a URL, tweet or text | Public paste box at `/`, no wallet and no signup. Also fed automatically by eight RSS newswires. |
| Truth Score 0 to 100 and a reasoning trace | Both, from a second layer synthesizer that explains but is never allowed to set the score. |
| Transparency UI showing Gonka Request IDs per step | Every verdict card shows its request id, copyable, with a link that resolves the shard on Gonka's own chain API. The chain record names the model, which independently confirms which model answered. |
| Neutrality prompting | Temperature 0, models instructed to cite specific evidence, and grounded in measured chain state rather than their own priors. |
| Consensus logic when models disagree (noted as a major plus) | Agreement is a first class metric with its own policy threshold, shown at equal visual weight to the score. When the panel splits, a challenge round runs, and disagreement alone can veto an action the truth score would have allowed. |

**Why this matters for society, in one line.** A fact checker that only prints a
score costs nothing to be wrong. Ours commits real money on the strength of its
verdict and refuses to commit when its own models disagree, which is the
strongest honesty guarantee a verification system can offer.

The same engine also degrades honestly. One of our three models left the router
mid build while still being advertised by its catalogue. The health panel reports
that from observed call outcomes rather than from the listing, and the UI says
"two of three answered" instead of quietly averaging what is left.

muba-b6b1.name: LockPay
muba-b6b1.tagline: Lock the deal. Trust the chain.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body: With a tight build window, one of our biggest challenges was deciding where to spend limited time. We prioritized getting the core escrow flow working end-to-end via the Sui CLI first — split a coin, lock it, release or cancel — before touching the frontend, so we'd have a guaranteed working demo even if the UI wasn't finished in time. This also surfaced a real technical hurdle: the newly created Escrow object's ID isn't returned directly by the transaction, so we had to inspect the transaction's object changes to extract it before it could be shown in the UI. Time pressure meant we treated the frontend wallet integration as a "nice to have" layered on top of a proven CLI flow, rather than something to debug from scratch under deadline.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body: Sending a payment to someone you don't fully trust means one side has to go first: pay upfront and hope for delivery, or deliver first and hope for payment. Our escrow app removes that risk using a Sui smart contract. The sender locks a coin on-chain for a specific recipient, and only that recipient can claim it (release). If the deal falls through, the sender can reclaim the funds themselves (cancel) at any time before release, so there's no need for a third-party arbitrator. It works with any coin type on Sui, including stablecoins like testnet USDC, so it's directly usable for freelance payments, marketplace deals, or any peer-to-peer transaction where neither side wants to go first.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Challenges we ran into
1. Abstracting the "Crypto" out of Web3 Our biggest hurdle was achieving a true Web2 UX. Early on, the app felt clunky because users needed SUI tokens just to pay for gas to send their USDC stablecoins.

How we solved it: We dove deep into the Sui documentation and implemented Sponsored Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs). We restructured our frontend to build the transaction bytes locally, which are then passed to a backend relayer that co-signs and pays the SUI gas fee on behalf of the user.

2. Optimizing Complex Group Settlements On-Chain When a group of 5 friends go on a trip, the cross-debts become a tangled web. Executing 10 different transactions on-chain is inefficient and expensive.

How we solved it: We implemented a greedy debt-simplification algorithm locally that calculates everyone's net balance first. It then pairs the highest debtors with the highest creditors, compressing the debts into the absolute minimum number of transfers. We then batch all of these simplified transfers into a single PTB, settling the entire group simultaneously in under a second.

3. Strict CI/CD Deployment Failures During our final Vercel deployment, our production builds began failing mysteriously despite working perfectly on our local development servers.

How we solved it: We traced the Vercel logs and discovered that Next.js enforces extremely strict ESLint rules in CI environments (specifically regarding unescaped punctuation entities in React). We systematically audited our entire component library, refactored the codebase to be 100% compliant, and successfully achieved a flawless, zero-error production build just in time for submission.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
The problem it solves
**EquiSettle** bridges the gap between everyday Web2 consumer finance and the raw power of the Sui blockchain. In Southeast Asia, millions rely on centralized e-wallets (like Touch 'n Go or GrabPay) to split bills and pay merchants. However, these systems are siloed, incur heavy FX fees across borders, and have the centralized power to arbitrarily freeze user funds without warning. Furthermore, high-trust transactions—like apartment rental deposits—still force users to hand over raw cash to strangers.

**EquiSettle** makes these existing tasks significantly easier and mathematically safer:

**Frictionless Web3 Onboarding:** We eliminated seed phrases. By integrating Sui zkLogin, users generate a self-custodial wallet instantly using just their Google account. It feels exactly like a Web2 app.

**Erasing Group Debt (Easier):** Splitting bills among friends is tedious. Our app calculates the absolute minimum number of transfers required to settle a group's debt, and settles it instantly on-chain in USDC stablecoins.

**Gasless Transactions (Easier):** Users shouldn't have to understand "gas." We utilize Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs) and act as a Gas Station, sponsoring the transaction fees so users experience zero crypto friction.

**Trustless Escrows (Safer):** Instead of handing a landlord a cash deposit, users lock their funds in our custom TimeLockedEscrow Sui Move Smart Contract. The funds are secured immutably on-chain and rely entirely on the decentralized Sui Clock for release, ensuring neither party can steal the money.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body:
How EquiSettle fits the "Payments & Stablecoins" Track
EquiSettle was built from the ground up to prove that stablecoins on Sui are ready to replace traditional fiat e-wallets today. We chose Track 1 because our entire product architecture is dedicated to solving real-world consumer payments using stablecoins as the primary medium of exchange.

Here is exactly how EquiSettle utilizes the Sui network to revolutionize payments:

1. Stablecoin-Native Daily Transactions Unlike trading platforms or DeFi yields, EquiSettle targets everyday consumer activity—paying for a coffee, splitting a dinner bill, or paying a rental deposit. By using USDC as the default currency, we protect users from crypto volatility while offering the borderless, permissionless benefits of Web3.

2. Leveraging Sui's Sub-Second Finality for Retail For stablecoins to compete with Visa or Mastercard, merchant payments must settle instantly. We integrated a Unified DuitNow-style QR Scanner that relies on Sui's unparalleled sub-second finality. When a user scans to pay a merchant, the stablecoins are settled and finalized instantly, completely bypassing legacy 3% credit card processing fees and 3-day bank settlement delays.

3. Utilizing Sui's Unique Technical Primitives for Payments We didn't just build a generic crypto app; we used Sui's unique infrastructure to solve the biggest UX hurdles in stablecoin payments:

zkLogin: We eliminated the need for consumer payment apps to require seed phrases. Users access their stablecoins via standard Google OAuth.
Sponsored PTBs: We use Programmable Transaction Blocks to batch complex group debt settlements into a single transaction. By sponsoring the gas, users only ever think in terms of USDC, completely removing the friction of needing to hold SUI tokens just to pay network fees.
Programmable Stablecoins (Sui Move): We took payments a step further by introducing programmable trust. Using a native Sui Move Smart Contract, we allow users to lock their stablecoins in a TimeLockedEscrow for security deposits, relying on the decentralized Sui Clock rather than trusting centralized middlemen.

ykpzch-64a9.name: CrisisRoute AI
ykpzch-64a9.tagline: From unverified crisis reports to verified, human-

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of our biggest challenges was designing a crisis verification system that remains useful even when information is incomplete. In real emergencies, low verification cannot automatically mean low priority, because an unverified report may still describe a life-threatening situation.
