mandateagent-59fd.name: MandateAgent
mandateagent-59fd.tagline: AI proposes. Policy constrains. Base settles.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Keeping live options quotes valid
Thetanuts orders can change or disappear between market analysis and wallet confirmation. We addressed this by refreshing the selected order immediately before execution. The transaction is rejected if its premium, strikes, expiry, quantity, venue, or contract differs from the approved proposal.
Making AI safe enough for wallet actions
AI recommendations are probabilistic, while financial limits must be deterministic. We separated the AI committee from the policy engine. Agents can recommend a strategy, but they cannot increase the budget, approve an unverified contract, bypass the verifier, ignore an expired mandate, or disable the emergency stop.
Preventing duplicate spending
Manual MetaMask execution and autonomous execution could attempt to use the same mandate budget concurrently. We introduced atomic budget reservations and idempotency keys. Pending, submitted, and confirmed transactions all count toward the cumulative spending ceiling.
Explaining what the agents are doing
An early interface only showed that the committee was “waiting,” which made it difficult to understand its progress. We added named agent stages, current tasks, completion percentages, evidence summaries, sources, timestamps, reliability labels, and verifier conclusions.
Handling incomplete data and unavailable liquidity
News services, model providers, market APIs, and OptionBook liquidity can fail independently. Each source is time-bounded and scored for freshness and reliability. Missing evidence, model disagreement, or a lack of qualifying liquidity produces HOLD instead of a fabricated trade opportunity.
Building reliable transaction tracking
A transaction request can time out even when it was submitted successfully, so blindly retrying could create a duplicate trade. MandateAgent stores transaction hashes and reconciles receipts before deciding whether another submission is safe. Every lifecycle change is written to an append-only execution ledger.
Integrating changing on-chain SDKs
Thetanuts orders use signed structures, contract-specific units, and live allowlists. We used the official client for discovery, previews, and calldata encoding, normalized token decimals explicitly, and kept OptionFactory settlement fail-closed until its production parameters can be independently verified.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Trading on-chain options requires users to complete several complex tasks at the same time: understand market conditions, compare strategies, find live liquidity, calculate potential loss, verify contract details, manage token approvals, and submit a transaction before the quote expires.
MandateAgent makes this workflow easier and safer by:
- Turning a natural-language trading objective into clear, reviewable rules, including strategy type, expiry range, spending limit, maximum fills, and prohibited actions.
- Combining live ETH prices, volatility indicators, market news, public on-chain activity, and Thetanuts liquidity in one command center.
- Using a committee of specialist AI agents to research the market, recommend a strategy, and independently verify the recommendation.
- Showing evidence sources, confidence scores, payoff outcomes, policy checks, and agent progress so users understand exactly what they are approving.
- Enforcing deterministic safety controls that AI cannot override, including a maximum 25 USDC cumulative budget, quote freshness, contract allowlists, strike ordering, wallet balances, and an emergency stop.
- Preparing live Thetanuts OptionBook transactions on Base mainnet through MetaMask, with a bounded Coinbase CDP wallet path for autonomous execution.
- Recording every prepared, submitted, confirmed, failed, or cancelled execution in an auditable trade ledger.
If the evidence is unreliable, the quote is stale, liquidity is unavailable, or any rule fails, MandateAgent returns HOLD and refuses to prepare the transaction.

description.title: AI × OPTIONS
description.body:
MandateAgent combines AI decision-making with decentralized options on Base. Users describe their ETH exposure, risk tolerance, budget, and mandate duration in natural language. A committee of specialist agents then:

Collects cited market evidence.

Measures ETH momentum and realized volatility.

Searches Thetanuts OptionBook for live options liquidity.

Selects a suitable strategy, such as an ETH put debit spread.

Sends the recommendation to an independent AI verifier.

Applies deterministic risk checks before preparing the transaction.

Supports signing through MetaMask or bounded automation with a Coinbase CDP wallet.

The AI can propose a trade, but it cannot override the user’s budget, approved strategy, expiry range, contract allowlist, fill limit, or emergency stop. The execution flow uses live Thetanuts pricing and prepares OptionBook transactions for settlement on Base mainnet.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
MandateAgent uses GonkaRouter as the inference layer for a multi-agent ETH options risk committee. Specialist agents analyze cited evidence, live market conditions, historical momentum, and realized volatility. A Strategy Head combines these findings into a BUY PUT, SELL PUT, or HOLD recommendation, while an independent Verifier recalculates the decision and challenges unsupported assumptions.

GonkaRouter enables MandateAgent to separate research, strategy selection, and verification into distinct inference stages. Every model response is validated against a strict schema, and unavailable or invalid inference causes the system to fail closed. AI produces the recommendation, while deterministic policy code controls whether a transaction may proceed.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One major challenge was keeping multiple AI models consistent. Different Gonka models sometimes returned different verdicts, invalid JSON or explanations in different languages. We addressed this with strict response schemas, English-language validation, automatic retries and deterministic consensus rules. When evidence is insufficient, the system returns Unverified rather than forcing a conclusion.
We also encountered changing model availability. For example, Kimi appeared in the Gonka model catalogue but initially rejected inference requests. We created smoke tests to verify each configured model and designed a safe fallback that records failed calls without allowing them to influence the result. Kimi later became available and was successfully integrated as the final decision reviewer.
Web evidence introduced another challenge. Search results can be duplicated, outdated, inaccessible or copied across multiple websites. We added URL deduplication, source-quality scoring, publication-date checks, official-source identification and syndication-risk detection.
Multi-claim articles were also difficult because evidence from one claim must never affect another. We solved this by creating separate reports, evidence IDs, model calls and verdicts for every extracted claim.
Finally, creating meaningful transparency required more than displaying a final score. We built a SQLite audit ledger that stores model IDs, public reasoning summaries, evidence sources, latency, failures and Gonka request IDs—without exposing API keys or private chain-of-thought.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Misinformation spreads faster than traditional fact-checking. People often encounter viral articles, social-media posts and images without knowing whether the claims are accurate, outdated or presented without context. Manually checking multiple sources is slow, while relying on a single AI model can produce confident but unsupported answers.
Verity Desk makes verification faster, safer and more transparent. Users can submit a URL, text claim or image. The platform then:
- Extracts the main factual claims.
- Searches for supporting and contradicting evidence.
- Evaluates source quality and independence.
- Cross-checks the evidence using multiple Gonka-hosted AI models.
- Returns Unverified instead of guessing when evidence is insufficient.
- Records every source, model response and Gonka request ID in a transparency ledger.
Each AI model has a separate responsibility:
- MiniMax M2.7 extracts checkable claims, plans evidence searches and identifies research gaps. It also performs one independent evidence review.
- DeepSeek V4 Flash acts as another independent verifier, checking the evidence for support, contradictions, incorrect dates and missing context.
- Kimi K2.6 performs the final decision review. It compares both verifier outputs against the evidence and source-credibility assessment before producing its recommendation.
- Deterministic safety rules then calculate the final result and can override model confidence by returning Unverified when reliable evidence is insufficient.
Citizens can check viral stories before sharing them. Governments can monitor public misinformation. Traders can investigate market-moving news, while researchers can review claims and their supporting sources more efficiently.
Unlike a simple AI chatbot, Verity Desk shows users how a conclusion was reached. This reduces blind trust in AI and helps people make evidence-based decisions.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
Verity Desk fits the AI for Society track by addressing the social harm caused by online misinformation. It helps citizens, governments, traders and researchers verify claims, articles and images before making important decisions.
Instead of trusting one AI model, Verity Desk uses a transparent, evidence-first process. MiniMax extracts claims and plans the investigation, DeepSeek and MiniMax independently analyse web evidence, and Kimi performs a final decision review. All models operate through Gonka Router. Deterministic safety rules return Unverified when reliable evidence is insufficient, preventing the system from simply guessing.
Every source, model response and Gonka request ID is stored in a transparency ledger, allowing users to understand how the result was produced.
By making fact-checking faster, accessible and auditable, Verity Desk can reduce misinformation, improve digital literacy and support better public and professional decision-making. Our goal is not to tell society what to believe, but to help people examine the evidence behind what they see online.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# GASX - Ethereum Gas Futures Exchange on Sui

> **AI-native gas futures exchange on Sui, hedged with Thetanuts**

## The Idea

GASX makes Ethereum congestion tradeable. It tracks one index - the **Ethereum Gas Stress Index (EGSI, 0–1000)**, that measures blockspace stress (base fee, block utilization, mempool pressure, etc). AI forecasts EGSI; users trade futures on it with USDC.

---

### Problem Statement

Every single day, thousands of builders, traders, and protocols get **blindsided by gas**. You size a trade, you queue a mint, you schedule a DAO payout; and then the mempool erupts, base fee 10x's in six blocks, and your "$4 transaction" clears at "$60 and my dignity." Ethereum's blockspace is the most valuable real estate in Web3, and it is priced **live, with zero forward guidance, for everyone who touches it.**

It's a **structural, economy-wide volatility tax** on the entire on-chain economy, and until now, nobody has built the instrument to price it, forecast it, or hedge it.

### Market Gap

Every mature market hedges its core input cost. Airlines hedge jet fuel. Farmers hedge wheat. Exporters hedge FX. **On-chain, there is no equivalent for gas** - despite gas being the single most universal, unavoidable, and violently volatile cost of doing business in crypto.

That gap is enormous, and it is sitting in plain sight:

- **DeFi protocols** eat unhedged gas risk on every keeper job, liquidation bot, and rebalance.
- **NFT projects** watch mint margins evaporate the second a drop goes viral and gas spikes with it.
- **DAOs** budget treasury operations in a currency (gas) with no forward curve.
- **Retail traders** - literally anyone who has ever smashed "confirm" during a gas spike - are exposed, unhedged, every single time.

If you have ever watched a gas fee eat your alpha: **you are the market.** GASX exists because that market has never had a product built for it.

### Target Users

- **DeFi-native power users & bots** - keepers, arbitrageurs, liquidators who eat gas cost as a line item and want to hedge it like any other operating expense.
- **NFT & dApp teams** - need predictable unit economics around mint/interaction windows, not a coin flip on network conditions.
- **DAOs & treasuries** - want to budget and hedge blockspace exposure the same disciplined way they'd hedge FX or interest rate risk.
- **Quant / degen traders** - want a clean, liquid, AI-forecasted volatility product that isn't just "another perp on a coin."
- **Anyone who has ever rage-quit a transaction because gas 5x'd mid-confirm.** (Yes, you. We see you.)

### Business Model

GASX monetizes the exact thing it creates: a liquid market for a previously unpriced risk.

- **Trading fees** - a basis-point take on every winning EGSI-1H contract opened and settled. Classic exchange economics, applied to a brand-new asset class.
- **Protocol-owned hedge spread** - GASX's own book captures the spread between what it collects in premium and what it pays to hedge on Thetanuts, turning risk management into a revenue center instead of a cost center.
- **Premium AI insights** - deeper EGSI forecasting, historical analytics, and Kora-powered "gas advisory" for power users, DAOs, and protocols who want to plan treasury ops around a forward curve, not a guess.
- **B2B/API licensing** - the EGSI feed itself is a product: wallets, dApps, and gas estimators can license the index and forecast to power their own UX, the way market data terminals license price feeds today.
- **Expansion flywheel** - every new blockspace market (BASE-GAS, ARB-GAS, BLOB-GAS) reuses the same engine, the same hedge rail, and the same user base, compounding distribution instead of resetting it.

TL;DR: **first-mover in an entirely uncontested category** - gas derivatives, with a credibly neutral settlement layer, a real hedge rail, and a reliable growth path.

---

**Problem, restated simply.** Gas congestion risk is hard to quantify, and there is no direct price discovery for future blockspace stress. Companies need predictable gas costs.

**Solution, restated simply.** Bet on EGSI. If the bet wins, the payout offsets real gas fees.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Sui pulled the rug on us mid-build - JSON-RPC just stopped working.
Every chain read started failing with "JSON-RPC on public fullnodes has been deprecated." Not a bug we introduced, Sui switched it off network-wide. We migrated the entire read path to gRPC, which turned out to be the right call anyway since it's the same transport the frontend's wallet SDK already used.

2. We built an on-chain oracle publisher and then realized we didn't need one.
Getting the AI's price feed onto Sui meant wrestling a Python SDK through three separate bugs; a config bootstrap that silently required a file that couldn't exist yet, a protocol mismatch, a missing await that let a transaction silently do nothing. We fixed all three.

3. Our first real options trade on Thetanuts kept dying one step from the finish line.
We got all the way to signing a real RFQ on Base mainnet, and it failed with "option expiry must be after offer deadline" - we were pricing the hedge's expiry off the wrong timestamp. Fixed that, then hit a second, sneakier bug: the transaction builder itself was never awaited, so it silently did nothing instead of erroring. Once both were fixed, the trade actually landed on-chain.

4. The trading UI and the smart contract quietly disagreed about "the price", so every single order failed.
The frontend priced trades off the AI's forecast; the contract validated them against the live oracle. Two different numbers, both "correct" in isolation, meant every order tripped a slippage guard. We traced it down to one line and made both sides read from the same source of truth.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body:
Every trade on GASX is collateralized and settled in USDC, a stablecoin on Sui.

Why that matters: if you're trying to hedge against unpredictable costs, the last thing you want is your hedge itself to be unpredictable. A stablecoin means when you win a bet, you know exactly what you're getting, not "some crypto, worth who-knows-what today."

And doing it on Sui specifically means those payments settle in under a second for a fraction of a cent. There's a nice irony we like pointing out: it would be pretty embarrassing to build a tool for gas-fee volatility and then make people pay volatile gas fees just to use it.

description.title: AI × SUI
description.body:
The real problem: nobody can plan for Ethereum gas fees. They spike without warning and eat into real money - a trade, a mint, a DAO payment.

AI's job is to sense and predict that problem. It watches live Ethereum data non-stop and turns raw chaos (base fee, mempool, congestion) into one clean number, EGSI, plus a forecast of where it's heading next.

Sui's job is to host the solution. It's where people actually trade a bet on that forecast - cheaply, in under a second, using a language (Move) that makes it much harder to lose or duplicate funds by accident. And crucially, Sui isn't the chain that's congested, so the market itself never distorts the thing it's measuring.

Put together: AI tells you what's coming, Sui gives you a fast, safe place to do something about it.

description.title: BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK
description.body:
Most integrations use an SDK for one thing — pull a price, show a number. We use Thetanuts as real infrastructure across the whole loop:

We pull live ETH options data from Thetanuts and feed it into our own AI forecast, it's not just displayed; it makes our predictions better.
Our risk engine uses Thetanuts to actually request real price quotes from market makers when it needs to hedge.
And we don't stop at requesting a quote, we settle a real trade with real funds on Base mainnet.

That's sensing, deciding, and acting, all built on the SDK. And because Thetanuts has no testnet, that last step is real money with no dry run.

description.title: AI × OPTIONS
description.body:
When enough people bet the same direction on GASX, our own book ends up exposed, if gas spikes, we could owe more than we collect. The AI watches for that risk continuously. When it crosses a threshold, the AI itself decides to hedge, it requests a real options quote from Thetanuts and, if the quote clears our safety checks, executes the trade, no human clicks "buy."

It's not unlimited, though. The AI can request an action, but it can never break the rules: hard caps on position size, a minimum confidence bar before it's allowed to act, a tiny fixed budget it can't exceed. So you get real autonomy, inside a fence it can't climb over.

civicpulse-5549.name: CivicPulse
civicpulse-5549.tagline: Dual AI Public Fact-Checking & Phishing Guard

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
### The Hurdle: Dual-Engine Latency Bottlenecks & Node Timeouts

Because CivicPulse relies on a parallel cross-audit pipeline querying two distinct models on the Gonka network (DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M2.7), our total response time was fundamentally bottlenecked by the slowest responding node. During peak network loads or decentralized cold starts, one engine would occasionally hang or take 6+ seconds, causing frontend request timeouts and broken consensus calculations.

### How We Overcame It

1. **Parallel Execution via Promise Orchestration:** We refactored the verification pipeline to dispatch both inference requests concurrently rather than sequentially, cutting nominal response latency in half.
2. **Hedged Timeout & Fallback Architecture:** We implemented a strict 3.5-second timeout window per node. If a model fails to return within this threshold, the system automatically triggers a retry against an alternate node or falls back safely rather than hanging indefinitely.
3. **Graceful Degradation:** Instead of failing silently or crashing the client session, the frontend transparently flags the verdict as a partial audit when a node fails to respond, maintaining transparency without giving users false certainties.

📖 **Want to know more?**  
 Check out our comprehensive [`README.md`](./README.md) for full technical specifications, architecture diagrams, and local setup instructions.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
### What People Can Use CivicPulse For

CivicPulse acts as a real-time, decentralized digital safety filter against viral misinformation and cyber fraud. Key use cases include:

* **Verifying Private Scams & Phishing Alerts:** Citizens can paste suspicious bank warnings, parcel delivery alerts, or tax notices directly into the app to detect malicious links and phishing attempts before clicking.
* **Debunking Viral Family Chat Rumors:** Users can inspect forwarded WhatsApp/Telegram claims or breaking news headlines to verify their factual accuracy before sharing them further.
* **Instant Peer Education:** Users can generate a clean, visual Share Card with clear safety advice to counter fake news directly in community or group chats.
* **Auditing Digital Claims:** Journalists, researchers, and skeptical users can independently trace every verification back to an auditable decentralized execution ID.

---

### How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier and Safer

* **Sub-3-Second Turnaround (vs. Hours or Days):** Traditional fact-checking agencies take hours or days to research and publish editorial debunks. CivicPulse provides instant verification in under 3 seconds, stopping fraud before panic sets in.
* **Reaches Dark Social & Private Channels:** Most existing verification tools only monitor public platforms (like Twitter/X or news feeds). CivicPulse allows users to paste raw private messages directly, bypassing website scrapers and anti-bot firewalls.
* **Removes "Blind Trust" with Multi-AI Consensus:** Instead of relying on a single black-box AI that can hallucinate or exhibit bias, CivicPulse cross-audits claims across two independent models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M2.7). If the models disagree by more than 25 points, the system explicitly flags the uncertainty rather than forcing a misleading answer.
* **Actionable Evidence Over Vague Labels:** Rather than merely labeling a message as "Fake," CivicPulse breaks down specific forensic markers—such as fake lookalike domains, manufactured urgency, and credential-harvesting tactics—making it easy for non-technical users and seniors to understand *why* it is dangerous.
* **Auditable Verification Trail:** Every verification is linked to a Gonka Request ID and stored with an integrity hash, giving users a tamper-evident receipt that proves the verdict was generated transparently and honestly.
* **Zero-Friction Accessibility:** Delivered as a lightweight web app supporting English, Bahasa Melayu, Chinese, and Tamil, with high-contrast options for seniors, ensuring protection is accessible across generations without requiring complex installations.

📖 **Want to know more?**  
 Check out our comprehensive [`README.md`](./README.md) for full technical specifications, architecture diagrams, and local setup instructions.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
CivicPulse is an installable Progressive Web App (PWA) designed for zero-friction citizen media literacy and fraud protection.

Instead of relying on a single AI model or asking users to trust a centralized authority, CivicPulse routes claims to two independent AI models from different model families running on the decentralized Gonka inference network.

Model 1 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) extracts structural context, impact, and safety advice.
Model 2 (MiniMax-M2.7) independently audits the claim for financial traps, phishing URLs, and manipulative urgency.
If the two models disagree by >25 points, CivicPulse surfaces the score gap explicitly to warn the user. Every verification generates a public Gonka Request ID and node receipt, ensuring that truth verification is auditable, transparent, and decentralized.

cekgu-acad.name: Cekgu
cekgu-acad.tagline: Two blind AI readers. One fairer assessment.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
A wrong answer key does not cost the person who wrote it. It costs every learner who sat the paper — the ones who understood the material and were marked wrong, and the ones who guessed the setter's intent and were rewarded for it. A question with two defensible options does the same thing more quietly. Both are usually found **after** publication, from a complaint rather than from the paper.

### Who this is for

Educators who write multiple-choice questions again and again: lecturers running weekly practice sets, independent tutors publishing question banks, anyone maintaining items that get reused. They are simultaneously the most exposed to their own defects and the least resourced to catch them.

### Why the existing options do not work

- **Self-review is anchored.** You read the question already knowing the answer you meant to write, which is exactly what makes the second defensible option invisible to you.
- **Asking a colleague to re-solve every item works** — and spends the scarcest resource in any department, another subject expert's time.
- **A single AI chat gives one opaque opinion.** One model agreeing with you is not evidence, and there is nothing behind the answer to check.

### What Cekgu does

Each question goes to **two distinct model families through GonkaRouter with the answer key withheld**, so neither reader can be anchored by it. A fixed rule compares the two readings *with each other* before either is compared with the key, and returns one of five verdicts:

- **Clear** — both verified readings agree with the key
- **Possible Key Error** — both agree with each other, and neither matches the key
- **Possible Ambiguity** — both readings list more than one defensible option
- **Split Opinion** — the two readings differ
- **Unverified** — fewer than two receipt-verified readings, so no verdict is claimed

Every admitted reading carries a Gonka Request ID and a public gateway receipt naming the model that actually served it, so a reviewer can check any claim against the gateway instead of taking ours.

### What it does not claim

Cekgu does not grade, does not certify a paper, and does not change a key. It directs human attention to the few items that warrant a second look, and leaves the decision — and the record of that decision — with the educator.

It is a risk signal for practice assessments, not proof of correctness. Two confident readers who agree are indistinguishable from an unambiguous question, and the public sample record carries a real instance of exactly that: a question written to be ambiguous came back **Clear**. We left it in the demo rather than hiding it.

### Where it goes

The commercial wedge is high-volume, lower-sensitivity work — tutors and lecturers repeatedly publishing practice MCQs, where a defect has real cost but the material is not confidential. That shape is self-serve prosumer SaaS, not an enterprise assessment contract.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
### The receipt arrived after the answer

GonkaRouter is not an ordinary low-latency API, and our first client assumed it was. In measurement, a completion could arrive **before its public receipt existed** — the receipt followed **664–808 ms** later. A one-shot receipt lookup was therefore rejecting genuine readings as unverifiable.

The client now polls inside a bounded **five-second receipt budget** and **fails closed**: a reading whose receipt never appears never enters a verdict. Bounded rather than unbounded matters, because the case being defended against is a gateway that simply never answers.

### A hedge that amplified the problem it existed to solve

Our first hedge fired below the observed completion floor. Instead of rescuing slow calls it duplicated them, and helped trigger the rate limiting it was meant to survive.

The hedge moved to **45 seconds**, behind a hard **90-second evidence cutoff**. Both the winner and the loser are recorded, so a duplicate is visible in the trail rather than quietly dropped.

### Health filtering that could strand a round

The subtlest one. Removing every recently-failing model family sounds obviously correct, and is wrong: it can leave a single candidate, and one family cannot produce two *distinct* readings. Every item would return Unverified without a second call ever being attempted.

The scheduler now **demotes an unhealthy family rather than dropping it**, so a round always retains enough candidates to pair two distinct readers. A round that still cannot obtain two receipt-verified readings ends as Unverified rather than guessing.

That design earned itself on submission day: the network took one of the three families we had built against offline, and calls to it began returning HTTP 400. Because the rule is two distinct verified readings rather than three, and because the scheduler pairs whatever remains, the product absorbed a change to the model catalogue we did not control.

### Everything that failed is still on the record

The habit underneath all three: **every attempt — failed, duplicated, refused, or admitted — stays visible** in the evidence trail. Showing only the winning call would have been easier, and would have made the receipts worth less. A trail you can only inspect when it flatters us is not a trail.

description.title: AI For Society
description.body:
**Every reasoning and verification decision runs through GonkaRouter.** `src/server/gateway/only-gonkarouter.test.ts` fails the build if a provider host appears anywhere else in the codebase. Two narrow exemptions are documented and neither can reach a verdict: OCR of an uploaded image, and phrasing the record assistant's replies from facts the Gonka readers already produced. Neither may import the verdict rule, and the test enforces that too.

**The models answer independently.** Each question is sent to two distinct model families with the educator's answer key withheld. Neither reader sees the key, and neither sees the other's reading. Anchoring is prevented by construction, not by instruction.

**Distinctness is proven, not asserted.** Two readings count as independent only if the public receipts name two different *served* models. We compare the served-model identity recorded in the receipt, not the model we requested — a substituted model is a different reader wearing the requested one's name.

**Gonka Request IDs are displayed beside every reading**, together with the public receipt and the model that actually served the call, including the attempts that failed or timed out. Anyone can open the gateway's public receipts endpoint and check a request ID without an account or an API key.

**No fallback response enters consensus.** A reading without a receipt-verified request ID is not admitted. The system fails closed to Unverified rather than manufacturing agreement out of whatever came back.

**Explicit consensus logic.** Five outcomes, evaluated in a fixed order: Unverified (fewer than two receipt-verified readings), Split Opinion (the readings differ), Possible Ambiguity (both list more than one option), Possible Key Error (both agree, neither matches the key), Clear. Disagreement is surfaced to a human, never averaged away.

**The public web is consulted, and quoted.** Before the readers run, one search fetches pages relevant to the question and shows the same snippets to both of them as background rather than authority. The supplied key is never in the query — searching for the key returns pages that agree with the key. Where a record was checked with retrieval, every page is listed under the readings with a live link and the quoted text; a record checked before retrieval shipped says so on itself rather than leaving the feature looking absent. This is a search API, not a model: `include_answer` is hard-coded false, because a generated answer would be reasoning on a provider that is not the gateway, and a test asserts both that flag and that no generated answer is ever read off the response. Retrieval never blocks a verdict — no key, a timeout or an unreadable reply all return nothing and the round proceeds on the readers alone.

**A score puts a number on it.** The same two readings produce a Truth Score from 0 to 100, computed by a pure function over them: no extra inference call, and no model asked how confident it feels. Where retrieval ran, each reader also reports what the pages did to its own answer, and that folds in as a confidence adjustment rather than a vote — corroboration makes a reading count for more, contradiction for half, and neither can flip a reading into meaning its opposite. A web page must not be able to outrank two receipt-verified readings. **Unverified carries no score at all, never zero**: zero is what two readers agreeing against the key earns, and an item nobody could read has not earned it.

**Three ways in.** A paper can be typed, pasted as a link to a page that already holds the questions, or uploaded as a scan. The link path is reduced to its words by a parser that runs no model; the scan path is the one documented exemption where an image becomes text before any reasoning begins.

**The educator makes and records the final decision.** Cekgu produces a risk signal for practice assessments. It does not grade, certify a question as correct, or prove a question unambiguous — two confident readers who agree are indistinguishable from an unambiguous question, and the public sample record carries a real instance of that. The final call, and the record of who made it, stays with the educator.

The public value is direct: a wrong answer key takes marks from every learner who sits the paper, and the people writing practice papers are the least resourced to catch it.

ai-adversarial-fact-verification-8e50.name: AI Adversarial Fact Verification
ai-adversarial-fact-verification-8e50.tagline: Three AI models argue, one truth emerges

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# GONKA AI Fact Checker

### Verify claims. See the evidence. Prove the result.

GONKA AI Fact Checker is a decentralized AI-powered fact-checking application.

It helps you verify whether a claim or article is **true, false, misleading, or unverified**.

Instead of relying on a single AI model, the system uses three different AI agents to debate the claim.

## 🔍 How It Works

### 1. Submit a Claim

Enter either:

* A text claim
* A public HTTPS article URL

If you submit an article, the system extracts the readable article content automatically.

### 2. Gather Evidence

The system analyzes the claim and can search for additional real-time sources.

Article content, search results, and model-provided references are collected as supporting evidence.

### 3. AI Debate

Three AI agents independently play different roles:

* **Pro Agent — Kimi:** looks for evidence supporting the claim.
* **Con Agent — DeepSeek:** looks for evidence against the claim.
* **Judge Agent — MiniMax:** compares both sides and makes the final decision.

### 4. Gonka Verification

All AI model requests are routed through the **Gonka Router**.

Each successful request produces a unique **Gonka Request ID**, allowing the AI inference process to be traced and verified.

### 5. Final Verdict

The system combines the three-agent results into a final verdict:

**TRUE · FALSE · MISLEADING · UNVERIFIED**

It also generates a **Truth Score from 0–100** and a confidence score.

### 6. Understand the Result

The result includes:

* Final conclusion
* Truth Score
* Confidence
* Pro / Con / Judge summaries
* Evidence and references
* Reasoning metrics
* Risk warnings
* Model request IDs

Metrics include factual accuracy, source quality, logical consistency, neutrality, temporal consistency, and model consensus.

## ⛓️ On-Chain Proof

Once a verification is eligible, the result can be permanently attested on **Arbitrum Sepolia**.

The system creates a cryptographic hash of the claim and prepares the verification evidence for **IPFS**.

You can connect an EVM wallet such as MetaMask and submit the result to the **TruthRegistry** smart contract.

The on-chain record stores the claim hash, Truth Score, verdict, Gonka Request IDs, IPFS metadata, attester, and timestamp.

After the transaction is confirmed, anyone can verify the attestation from the blockchain.

## 📊 Live Dashboard

The application can also display recent on-chain fact-checking attestations directly from the TruthRegistry contract.

This makes verified results transparent and publicly traceable.

## 💡 Why It Matters

GONKA AI Fact Checker combines:

**Multi-Agent AI Debate**

* **Gonka Inference Proof**
* **Evidence & Reasoning**
* **IPFS Storage**
* **Blockchain Attestation**

The goal is simple:

> **Don't just tell people what is true. Show them why — and let them verify the proof.**

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
The trickiest bug we hit wasn't in the AI logic — it was a **silent data-integrity bug in our on-chain attestation pipeline**. Two files responsible for hashing the same claim text had quietly drifted apart: our production endpoint was hashing with SHA-256, while another module used Keccak-256 — the algorithm Solidity actually uses under the hood. Both ran without errors, so nothing failed loudly. We only caught it by inspecting an attestation certificate directly and noticing the "Claim Hash" field rendering two different values side by side, meaning the hash we were verifying and the hash actually stored on-chain weren't the same thing.

Digging further, we found the root cause: the project had two parallel backend implementations, and one had been edited without the other keeping up. The drift wasn't limited to hashing either — the contract was deployed on Arbitrum Sepolia, but leftover strings elsewhere still referenced a different chain, and even a different attestation protocol we'd already decided not to use.

We fixed it by establishing a **single source of truth** instead of patching each occurrence individually: one shared hashing function matching Solidity's Keccak-256, one shared chain-config constant imported everywhere rather than hardcoded per file, and deprecating the unused backend entirely so future edits can't silently diverge again. It was a good reminder that in a system whose whole pitch is verifiable, tamper-evident data, an internal inconsistency is just as damaging as a wrong AI answer — so we now treat "does this value match everywhere it's displayed" as its own test case, not just something to eyeball.

optionarena-2e2f.name: OptionArena
optionarena-2e2f.tagline: Options for people who don't speak options

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Options are the biggest market in traditional finance and almost nobody in crypto touches them, because every interface assumes you already speak the language: strike, expiry, delta, implied volatility.

OptionArena takes a plain-English market view, turns it into a defined-risk options position on the live Thetanuts V4 book on Base mainnet, and shows the maximum loss as a dollar figure before anything is signed. Around that sits a social layer: handles, friends, head-to-head battles on a shared expiry, and a leaderboard where you choose what "winning" means.

Copy trading is sourced from Deribit rather than Thetanuts. A young venue has nobody worth copying yet, so we rank live Deribit flow and map each trade onto the nearest fillable Thetanuts contract, surfacing every difference in strike, expiry or direction rather than silently substituting. That direction came from the Thetanuts team directly, and it means the product brings Thetanuts order flow it doesn't currently have.

We deploy no contracts of our own — only calls to Thetanuts' deployed OptionBook on Base (chain 8453).

The buyable side of the book is physically settled and reverts on-chain with Panic(0x11). We ruled out size, order choice, expiry, SDK version, RPC and allowance across 62 orders, then decoded a successful fill against our own calldata word by word; the Thetanuts team confirmed physical settlement is not yet routed into the SDK. Execution therefore routes through the sell side. The full investigation is in docs/decisions.md §14.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
The buyable side of the book reverts. Every order we could buy failed with Panic(0x11), a Solidity arithmetic overflow raised inside the OptionBook. We ruled out trade size across nine amounts, all 62 USDC-priced buyable orders, order expiry, SDK version, three independent RPCs and the token allowance. Then we decoded a fill that had succeeded an hour earlier against our own calldata, word by word, and found ours was one 32-byte word longer — the extraOptionData a physically settled contract carries. The fills that work are cash-settled and collateralised in plain USDC; everything we could buy was physical. The Thetanuts team confirmed physical settlement isn't routed into the SDK yet. We built a sell path around it and made the app refuse physicals outright rather than broadcast a transaction we already know reverts.

Decimals nearly bit us. We assumed a fixed size decimal and read a call's remaining size as 4099251066830 USDC instead of 4.09 WETH. The real rule — a contract count uses the same decimals as its collateral token — is documented nowhere and had to be derived from the live book.

Order identity was wrong twice. We first keyed orders by nonce, but 72 orders shared 13 nonces and one nonce spanned 18 contracts across different strikes and expiries. We switched to a content hash — then found it expired within seconds, because makers requote about once a minute. Excluding price and nonce from the hash and adding a 2% slippage check fixed it.

Cold start on copy trading. Thetanuts has under $1M TVL, so there is nobody to copy. We source signals from Deribit instead and map them onto Thetanuts contracts, reporting every difference in strike, expiry or direction rather than silently substituting.

description.title: BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK
description.body:
OptionArena is built entirely on @thetanuts-finance/thetanuts-client v0.3.0. We deploy no contracts of our own; every position is a call into Thetanuts' deployed OptionBook on Base mainnet (chain 8453).

The SDK does the work end to end: fetchBook reads the live order book, previewFillOrder prices a real contract, callStaticFillOrder simulates against live chain state before anything is signed, ensureAllowance handles approvals, and fillOrder executes.

Two things we treated as non-negotiable. First, decimals: the Thetanuts team told us this is what builders most often get wrong, so every amount is a bigint routed through one file, formatting happens last, and an assertMagnitude check proves the order of magnitude before signing. We derived and documented a rule that appears nowhere in the docs — a contract count uses the same decimals as its collateral token. Assuming otherwise read a call's remaining size as 4099251066830 USDC instead of 4.09 WETH. There is a regression test for it.

Second, honesty about what the SDK can currently do. Every buyable order on the book is physically settled and reverts on-chain with Panic(0x11). We ruled out size, order choice, expiry, SDK version, RPC and allowance across 62 orders, then decoded a successful fill against our own calldata word by word and found ours carried one extra 32-byte word: the physical-settlement extraOptionData. The Thetanuts team confirmed physical settlement is not yet routed into the SDK. We built a sell path around it, and the app refuses physicals rather than broadcasting a transaction we know fails.

We also bring Thetanuts order flow it doesn't currently have, by sourcing copyable trades from Deribit and mapping them onto fillable Thetanuts contracts — a direction the Thetanuts team suggested to us directly.

description.title: AI × OPTIONS
description.body:
The agent's job is narrow on purpose: turn a plain-English market view into a real, defined-risk options position on the live Thetanuts book, and never invent anything.

You type something like "I think ETH drops before the weekend" and choose how much you're willing to lose. The agent reads the live OptionBook, picks a contract that actually exists and can actually be filled, and returns it as structured output validated with zod. It never names a strike, expiry or price of its own — it selects from what the book contains, so a hallucinated contract cannot reach the signing path.

The user then sees the maximum loss as a dollar figure, priced against real resting orders, before anything is signed. The number you approve is the number at risk.

Four decisions shaped how we used the model:

The model sits behind an adapter, and when no API key is present a rule-based selector runs instead — and labels itself as one in the interface. The product never pretends a heuristic was a model.

Prompts are versioned files in the repo (lib/agent/prompts/interpret.v1.md), not inline strings, so a prompt change is a reviewable diff.

The model does not decide what "winning" means. Our leaderboard ranks sourced Deribit trades by a criterion the user picks — realised profit, risk-adjusted return, consistency — because there is no single honest definition, and burying that judgement inside a model output would hide it. Nothing ranks by raw percentage return, which would just reward whoever took the most risk and got lucky.

The model is never asked for a number it cannot know. Before expiry we show no running score, because we have no mid-life valuation and any figure would be invented; we compare what each side risked against what each pays if right. After expiry, outcomes settle against the price Deribit published — the number the option actually paid out against.

The AI layer is also where copy trading works despite a cold start. We rank live Deribit flow and map each trade onto the nearest fillable Thetanuts contract, reporting every difference in strike, expiry or direction in plain language rather than silently substituting. On the day we measured, all 39 buyable Thetanuts puts had an exact strike-and-expiry match on Deribit.

shield-47a2.name: Shield
shield-47a2.tagline: Zero-cost collars for everyday ETH holders

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Everyday ETH holders keep crypto as savings not as a trade. Today ETH holders face a choice: sell all ETH to avoid a crash (and lose all future upside) or hold ETH and hope risking a large part of ETH holders’ savings overnight with no safety net. Buying insurance‑style protection like a put option can help,. It costs a recurring premium that is wasted most of the time it is not needed just like paying for insurance you never use.

What Shield Does

Shield lets ordinary ETH holders protect ETH holders’ savings from a crash at zero cost. Shield uses an idea from traditional finance called a collar now turned into an easy tool through Thetanuts’ on‑chain options protocol on Base.

Of paying an ongoing premium the user gives up a small amount of extreme upside that the user probably would not have captured anyway. That trade‑off pays for downside protection so the net cost of the whole Shield deal is close to zero.

How People Use It

Describe the goal in English, for example "I have 2 ETH I cannot afford to lose more than 10% and I am fine with capping my gains at 15% this month." No need to understand strike prices, expiries or options terminology.

Shield finds the deal automatically. Shield pulls pricing from Thetanuts’ market makers and calculates the exact floor (protection level) and cap (gains limit) where the cost cancels out to near zero.

See the deal explained in language before committing. "Your range is locked: floor $2,700 cap $3,350. Net cost: $2.”

Confirm and execute. Shield runs a safety check—verifying the contract, approval amount and transaction details—and only executes after confirmation directly on Base mainnet.

Why It Makes This Safer and Easier

No manual options knowledge required. The AI layer translates a plain‑language goal into the trade parameters and a deterministic solver and safety validator double‑check every number before any transaction is signed.

No recurring cost that goes to waste. Unlike insurance protection is funded by the trade itself not by an out‑of‑pocket premium paid every cycle.

No surprise. Forced sales. This is not a loan; there is no bot monitoring ratios. The only outcomes are: stay protected stay unaffected or sell at a price the user explicitly agreed to.

Transparent, on‑chain and verifiable. Every position is backed by collateralized options on Thetanuts not by a promise from a company. Anyone can verify it on Base.

Who It's For

Anyone holding ETH as savings who wants a safety net without becoming an options trader. People who have never touched DeFi derivatives but understand "I do not want to lose more, than X.”

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
The most critical bug: clicking "Process Request" on the Protect page always returned "Failed to interpret goal".

The root cause was subtle. The Gemini API key in .env.local started with AQ. — a malformed key. Valid Gemini API keys start with AIza. Because the route called generateObject() unconditionally, it always threw a 500 with no fallback, leaving users stuck at the very first step.

The fix: We rewrote the API route with a two-tier strategy:

AI parsing is only attempted if a valid AIza... key is present.
A deterministic regex parser runs as the guaranteed fallback — no API key needed.
But even the regex parser had a bug: "protect 2 ETH below $3,900" returned desiredFloorPct: 2 instead of 3900. The generic number regex was greedily matching the ETH size (2) before reaching the floor price. We fixed it by anchoring the size regex to N ETH / N BTC patterns only.

description.title: BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK
description.body:
Shield is built entirely on the Thetanuts SDK as its core execution layer. The product’s main feature. A zero-cost collar. Is made by combining two Thetanuts primitives: a PUT purchase for protection and a CALL sale for upside. These are executed using client.optionBook.fillOrder with RFQ fallback handled through client.optionFactory. Real-time pricing, from client.mmPricing feeds into a solver. This solver finds the strike pair where the premiums of both legs exactly cancel each other out. So the SDK’s pricing data doesn’t just show value. It actually powers the product’s value.

We also use client.api to discover orders and client.events to track positions all the way through settlement. Since Thetanuts hasn’t yet released a multi-leg collar (client.collar writes are blocked until v12) we currently sequence the two legs safely.. We’re designing for smooth, direct adoption of the atomic module once it ships. This shows we’re not just using the SDK. We’re actively engaged with its roadmap.

On top of this foundation an AI layer. Powered by Gemini. Turns plain-language protection goals into SDK parameters. That means someone who’s never heard of a "strike price" can still set up protection. Shield doesn’t just call the SDK. It builds a self-funding protection product on top of Thetanuts’ composable options primitives.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
##

People often struggle to understand medical information because symptoms, medical reports, medicines, and health terminology can be complex and difficult to interpret. Searching online can also lead to confusing, unreliable, or misleading information.

**MediMatrix AI** helps make healthcare information easier to understand and access by providing AI-powered explanations in simple language. Users can use it to:

* Understand symptoms and possible health concerns
*  Get easy-to-understand explanations of medical reports
* Learn about medicines, their common uses, and precautions
* Ask health-related questions through an AI assistant
*  Find relevant and understandable medical information
*  Identify situations where professional medical attention may be important
*  Organize and review personal health information

By simplifying complex medical information and providing structured guidance, MediMatrix AI can help people make more informed decisions, reduce confusion, and prepare better questions for healthcare professionals.

MediMatrix AI is designed for health information and guidance, not for replacing doctors or providing definitive medical diagnoses.

While developing **MediMatrix AI**, we faced several challenges:

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## 🛠️ Challenges We Ran Into

Building ReliefChain as a genuinely Web3-native disaster-relief protocol came with several challenges — especially around making **on-chain funds, verification logic, and decentralized evidence work together reliably.**

### 1. Designing Non-Custodial Fund Management

One of our biggest challenges was ensuring that donated funds were **not simply transferred to a campaign creator's wallet**.

We redesigned the flow around a Move smart-contract treasury where donations remain controlled by the protocol. Instead of relying on the frontend to enforce rules, the Move contract becomes the source of truth for:

**Donation → Campaign Treasury → Milestone Verification → Fund Release**

This forced us to think carefully about authorization, object ownership, treasury accounting, and preventing unauthorized withdrawals.

### 2. Connecting On-Chain State With the Frontend

Another hurdle was keeping the frontend synchronized with blockchain state.

Initially, some UI state could become stale after transactions or page refreshes. We moved toward treating **Sui as the source of truth**, fetching campaign and transaction state from the blockchain rather than relying on temporary frontend state.

This was especially important for ensuring that campaigns and donation history remain verifiable after a refresh.

### 3. Wallet & Transaction Handling

Wallet integration introduced another layer of complexity.

Transaction signing, gas management, network configuration, wallet connection state, and transaction confirmation all had to work together. A transaction could be successfully submitted while the frontend was still waiting for confirmation or displaying stale information.

We addressed this by improving transaction lifecycle handling:

`Connect → Build Transaction → Sign → Execute → Confirm → Refresh On-Chain State`

This made the application much more resilient to delayed confirmations and RPC responses.

### 4. Making Relief Evidence Verifiable

Disaster-relief evidence can include large files such as photographs, invoices, delivery manifests, and reports. Storing everything directly on-chain would be inefficient and expensive.

We therefore separated the architecture into two layers:

**Sui = Financial & Verification Layer**
**Decentralized Storage = Evidence Layer**

Instead of putting large files on-chain, the system stores the evidence off-chain in decentralized storage and anchors its identifier/hash to the corresponding on-chain milestone.

This gives us the scalability of decentralized storage while preserving a verifiable connection between **evidence and fund releases.**

### 5. Designing for Real-World Failure

A disaster-relief application cannot assume that every transaction, upload, RPC request, or verification step will succeed.

We added explicit handling for failed transactions, rejected wallet signatures, missing evidence, invalid campaign states, and incomplete milestone flows.

The result is a system where failures are treated as expected protocol states rather than silent frontend errors.

### 💡 Biggest Lesson

The hardest part wasn't simply putting a donation button on a blockchain.

It was designing the system so that **money, evidence, permissions, and verification all share the same source of truth.**

That led us to our core design principle:

> **The frontend can display the truth — but the smart contract must enforce it.**

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
**## 🌍 The Problem It Solves

When disaster strikes, **people donate fast — but accountability moves slowly.**

Traditional disaster-relief funding relies on banks, crowdfunding platforms, organizations, spreadsheets, and centralized databases. Donors often have no way to independently verify:

* **Where their money went**
* **Who received it**
* **What it was spent on**
* **Whether the reported relief actually happened**

This creates a fundamental problem:

> **You can trust the intention of a donation without being able to verify its journey.**

ReliefChain changes that by turning disaster relief into a **transparent, programmable, and auditable on-chain process.**

### 🚨 What ReliefChain Enables

**For Donors**

Donate directly through Sui and follow the movement of funds on-chain — from the campaign treasury to verified relief milestones.

**For Relief Organizations**

Create structured campaigns with defined funding milestones such as:

`Emergency Supplies → Medical Aid → Food Distribution → Reconstruction`

Funds are managed by Move smart contracts rather than being immediately handed to a campaign creator.

**For Verifiers**

Authorized verifiers can review submitted relief evidence and approve milestone-based fund releases, creating an additional accountability layer between donations and spending.

**For Auditors & the Public**

Every important financial action can be independently inspected on-chain, creating a permanent and transparent audit trail.

### 🔐 Making Disaster Relief Safer

| Traditional Relief                        | ReliefChain                                           |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Trust the organization to report spending | **Verify transactions on-chain**                      |
| Funds controlled by intermediaries        | **Funds governed by Move smart contracts**            |
| Manual milestone tracking                 | **Programmable milestone-based releases**             |
| Centralized records                       | **Public blockchain audit trail**                     |
| Difficult to trace donations              | **Trackable fund flow from donation to disbursement** |
| Evidence disconnected from payments       | **Relief evidence linked to on-chain milestones**     |

### ⚡ The Core Idea

**ReliefChain separates *trust* from *transparency*.**

Instead of asking donors to simply believe that their donation reached the right place, the protocol makes the financial journey **cryptographically verifiable**.

**Donate → Verify → Release → Audit**

The result is a disaster-relief system designed to make humanitarian funding **more transparent, accountable, and programmable.**

> **Don't just donate. Know where your relief goes.****

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body:
## 💸 How ReliefChain Fits the Payments & Stablecoin Track

ReliefChain applies blockchain payments to one of the most important real-world payment problems: **getting humanitarian money to the right people quickly, transparently, and with less dependence on intermediaries.**

Today, international disaster relief can involve multiple payment processors, banks, organizations, and manual reconciliation steps. ReliefChain turns this process into a **programmable payment flow secured by smart contracts.**

### 🌍 Stablecoins as the Humanitarian Payment Rail

While SUI can be used for native on-chain payments, the protocol is designed to support **stablecoin-based humanitarian funding** as the ecosystem evolves.

A stablecoin such as a USD-pegged asset can provide a predictable unit of account for:

* International donations
* NGO and relief-organization funding
* Contractor payments
* Medical and emergency-supply procurement
* Cross-border humanitarian disbursements

This is particularly useful when donors and relief providers operate across different currencies and financial systems.

### 🔄 From Donation to Real-World Payment

ReliefChain transforms a donation into a programmable payment lifecycle:

**Donor → Campaign Treasury → Verified Milestone → Relief Provider → On-Chain Settlement**

Instead of releasing an entire campaign balance upfront, funds can be tied to predefined milestones.

For example:

> **$10,000 stablecoin campaign**
>
> → $3,000 for emergency food & water
> → $2,500 for medical supplies
> → $2,000 for temporary shelter
> → $2,500 for reconstruction

Each payment can be governed by the campaign's smart-contract rules and released when the corresponding milestone is approved.

### 🔐 Why Blockchain Payments Matter Here

ReliefChain combines **payments + programmable money + verification**.

Traditional payment systems answer:

> **“Did the payment happen?”**

ReliefChain aims to additionally answer:

> **“Why was the payment released, who authorized it, where did it go, and which relief milestone did it fund?”**

Because the financial activity is recorded on-chain, donors, verifiers, and auditors can independently inspect the payment trail.

### 🚀 Why This Belongs in the Stablecoin Track

Stablecoins make the model particularly powerful for **cross-border disaster response**.

A donor in one country can fund a relief campaign while a verified organization or contractor in another country receives a blockchain-native payment — without requiring the entire payment flow to depend on traditional correspondent banking infrastructure.

The long-term vision is:

**Global donations → Stablecoin settlement → Programmable escrow → Verified milestone → Direct humanitarian payment**

ReliefChain therefore isn't simply using crypto as a donation method.

**It is exploring how stablecoins can become programmable infrastructure for faster, more transparent humanitarian payments.**

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body: AI Hallucinations in Contract Terms: The language model initially assumed missing details, such as fabricating wallet addresses or guessing review deadlines. We resolved this by constraining the AI strictly to data structuring, adding a deterministic Zod validation layer, and introducing an explicit "Help us fill in the gaps" step for mandatory human input.  Upstream AI Outages & Timeouts: Live API calls to the LLM backend occasionally timed out or returned unexpected formats. We fixed this by saving raw terms as local drafts first and adding a fallback manual entry path that enforces the same strict validation rules.  Balancing Privacy with On-Chain Integrity: Writing plain-text contracts and evidence to the blockchain would expose private business data and increase costs. We implemented a hybrid architecture where sensitive records remain off-chain in PostgreSQL, while only an immutable SHA-256 agreement hash and coordination anchors interact with Sui.  Escrow Math & State Safety in Move: Ensuring locked funds could never be double-spent across multi-milestone lifecycles or disputes required rigid accounting. We built and verified 18 Move unit tests to strictly enforce single-release invariant checks and freeze disputed milestones until resolved.  Mobile Key Management: Exposing private keys or burdening users with seed phrases undermines mobile security and UX. We decoupled custody by leveraging native Google sign-in with Enoki nonces, generating unsigned transaction builders locally, and never storing keys on the backend.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body: In freelance and service-based work, trust frequently breaks down before any payment actually occurs because informal communication over chat, email, or calls leaves payment conditions, deliverables, and revision rules open to conflicting interpretations. This creates a stalemate where clients risk losing their money by paying upfront for incomplete or substandard work, while contractors risk working without compensation if payment is withheld. Without a shared, objective source of truth, vague agreements inevitably result in payment friction, stalled projects, and contentious disputes. TrustFlow resolves this dilemma by bridging casual conversational terms into deterministic, milestone-structured agreements backed by non-custodial smart contracts, protecting both parties with clear review windows, objective evidence requirements, and controlled fund releases.

description.title: PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS
description.body: TrustFlow integrates Sui’s payment infrastructure through a dedicated PaymentFlow Move smart contract that operates as an autonomous, non-custodial escrow using native SUI tokens scaled to nine decimal places. When an agreement is finalized, the client locks the full project deposit into the contract via create_flow, ensuring funds cannot be withdrawn arbitrarily once the contractor accepts. The contract coordinates sequential milestone progression: funds are released either through explicit client approval or automatically claimed by the contractor via claim_after_review if the client fails to review the work before the deadline expires. If a dispute arises, the milestone freezes until an authorized resolver determines a precise fund split, backed by strict invariant math ensuring no locked balance can ever be released twice. On the client side, the Android application binds user identities using Enoki and constructs unsigned Sui transaction builders locally, keeping private key custody and execution authority entirely in the user's hands rather than on the backend.

beaconsar-d85b.name: BeaconSAR
beaconsar-d85b.tagline: Autonomous Multi-Modal AI Search and Rescue OP

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Zero-Shot Visual Disambiguation Without Heavy Fine-Tuning:
   Hurdle: In real-world missing person scenarios, you don't have hours to train or fine-tune an object detection model on the specific individual. Furthermore, CCTV footage often suffers from varying angles, motion blur, and uneven lighting.
   Solution: We leveraged the multi-modal reasoning capabilities of Gemini to perform semantic attribute-level matching (identifying distinctive color histograms, accessories like walking canes, and gait patterns) rather than relying solely on rigid facial recognition.

2. Client-Side GIS Rendering Without Proprietary API Blockers:
   Hurdle: Proprietary map providers frequently impose strict rate limits, credit-card requirements, or fail during field deployments under poor network connectivity.
   Solution: We implemented an open-source mapping pipeline using Leaflet.js and OpenStreetMap dark tiles. We engineered custom mathematical projections to compute dynamic concentric drift circles and trajectory polylines directly on the client, ensuring the console remains responsive even on low-bandwidth field laptops.

3. Predictive Downstream Camera Handoff Logic:
   Hurdle: Once a subject is spotted on camera, they frequently disappear into crowd blind spots before searchers arrive.
   Solution: We designed a directional vector calculation between sequential verified timestamps. By extrapolating the subject's heading and walking velocity (e.g., 2.2 km/h for elderly dementia wanderers), the system identifies the next downstream surveillance nodes along that linear road corridor and raises their sensitivity threshold, establishing a continuous tracking chain.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
In missing person investigations and emergency search-and-rescue (SAR) operations, the first 24 hours determines the survival rate. When an elder with dementia wanders off, a child goes missing in a crowded transit hub, or families are separated during a natural disaster, survival probability plummets with every passing hour.

Currently, rescue agencies and families face four critical bottlenecks:
1. Surveillance Data Overload: Officers must manually scrub through hundreds of hours of grainy, unindexed CCTV footage across disparate camera networks.
2. Fragmented & Conflicting Tips: Civilian eyewitness reports arrive out of sequence, lacking verified chronological or spatial anchoring.
3. Static Search Radii: Ground teams rely on flat geometric circles rather than terrain-weighted and mobility-adjusted drift models (ISRID standard).
4. Delayed Ground Dispatch: Converting sightings into actionable squad sector assignments (Sector Alpha, Bravo, Charlie) takes hours of manual coordination.

How BeaconSAR Solves This:

BeaconSAR is an autonomous tactical command console that turns fragmented clues into immediate, lifesaving ground action:

1. Zero-Shot Multi-Modal Triage: Users upload a reference photo and clothing descriptors (e.g., "yellow kitenge headscarf, dark green dress, walking cane"). Powered by multimodal AI, it cross-examines surveillance feeds to extract and score matching visual features in seconds without requiring prior model training.

2. Geospatial Probability & Drift Modeling: Incorporates pedestrian velocity profiles and urban transit topography to compute live 1 km, 2.5 km, and 5 km probability search rings anchored to the Last Known Location (LKL).

3. Trajectory Lock & Camera Handoff: Once sequential sightings are confirmed, the system calculates the subject's directional vector and pre-alerts downstream camera nodes along their predicted path so visual contact is never lost.

4. Autonomous SAR Action Brief & Printable Dossier: Generates an immediate 60-minute tactical incident plan allocating ground search squads, police checkpoints, and drone sweeps, complete with a one-click printable official field bulletin.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:

Instead of depending on a full physical CCTV infrastructure, we created a simulated CCTV/event engine that generates safety events and sends them to the control-room dashboard. We also had to make sure that the user-side interface and security dashboard clearly communicated the changing alert status.

We overcame these challenges by separating the system into independent frontend and backend components and using simulated events to demonstrate the complete **Sense → Verify → Escalate** workflow reliably during the demo.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
**Running Models Locally on Mobile Hardware:** Standard language models require massive cloud servers to operate. Getting natural language processing to run directly on an Android device without draining memory, causing UI lag, or demanding active internet connectivity required extensive optimization and lightweight architecture.

**Parsing Mixed Regional Dialects (Romanized version of Hindi and Telugu):** Standard NLP models are primarily trained on formal English and miss colloquial, code-mixed nuances. People regularly blend languages in everyday texts, so building pattern-detection rules that accurately interpret informal phrasing across English, Hindi, and Telugu without generating false flags was a major technical hurdle.

**Ensuring Explainability and Objective Feedback:** We had to make sure the app never acted as an arbitrary "black box" or assigned clinical psychological labels to people. Structuring the engine to extract and visually highlight exact textual evidence while providing calm, de-escalating response suggestions required careful prompt and UI design.

**Time-Constrained Build and Gradle Synchronization:** Building native Android UI across multiple tabs, configuring speech input, and integrating local inference within a strict 2-hour hackathon window meant resolving Gradle dependency conflicts and catalog errors rapidly under tight time pressure.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
**Hidden Toxic Dynamics:** Unhealthy communication patterns such as gaslighting, blame-shifting, and dismissive language frequently hide inside everyday, casual conversations. Because these phrases sound ordinary, they are difficult to recognize in the moment, cause intense self-doubt, and easily become normalized over time.

**The Privacy Barrier:** People want clarity and a neutral perspective on confusing messages, but personal chats are deeply sensitive. Users cannot, and should not, upload private conversations to cloud-based AI systems where personal data could be harvested, logged, or exposed.

**On-Device Clarity Without Compromise:** UNSAID solves this dilemma by keeping all language analysis 100% on the user's phone. It functions entirely offline, detecting manipulative dynamics across English and regional dialects like romanized versions of Hindi and Telugu while highlighting the exact words that triggered the alert. Users get objective clarity and psychological safety with zero cloud exposure and complete data privacy.
