description.body:
1. API connections

2. Real-time testing, especially cross-language

3. Integrating it into web extension

description.title: Gemini
description.body: SafeSphere is a strong fit for the Gemini Track because Google Gemini serves as the core intelligence engine powering both the platform and its browser extension. Through the SafeSphere web extension, users can instantly analyze suspicious content from websites, social media platforms, emails, and online chats with a single click. Gemini's advanced reasoning and natural language understanding capabilities enable SafeSphere to go beyond keyword-based detection by analyzing context, intent, power dynamics, emotional manipulation, and conversational patterns. It accurately identifies threats such as cyberbullying, grooming, sextortion, blackmail, harassment, and coercion, while generating severity scores and personalized safety recommendations in real time. Gemini also helps explain threats in a clear, user-friendly manner, allowing users to understand not just what is harmful, but why it is harmful. By embedding Gemini-powered intelligence directly into a browser extension and digital safety platform, SafeSphere demonstrates a practical, scalable, and impactful application of Gemini technology to proactively protect users from online harm.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body: SafeSphere is an excellent fit for the Sarvam AI Track because Sarvam AI enables the platform to break language barriers in digital safety. Online abuse, harassment, blackmail, grooming, and manipulation often occur in regional languages and dialects that traditional moderation systems struggle to understand. By integrating Sarvam AI's multilingual capabilities, SafeSphere can process and translate content across multiple Indian languages, perform speech-to-text conversion for audio messages, and identify culturally specific abuse patterns, honor-based threats, coercion tactics, and regional linguistic nuances. This allows SafeSphere to detect threats regardless of the language in which they are communicated and explain them in a clear, understandable manner to users. Through its browser extension and digital safety platform, SafeSphere leverages Sarvam AI to make digital protection more inclusive, accessible, and effective for India's diverse linguistic population, demonstrating a high-impact real-world application of multilingual AI technology.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body: SafeSphere aligns strongly with the Open Innovation theme by combining advanced external technologies, collaborative ecosystems, and real-world safety infrastructures to address the growing challenge of digital abuse and online harassment. The platform integrates cutting-edge AI models such as Google Gemini for contextual threat analysis and Sarvam AI for multilingual understanding, speech processing, and cultural-context awareness. Beyond technology integration, SafeSphere is designed to work alongside social media platforms, educational institutions, cybercrime portals, NGOs, mental health organizations, and law-enforcement agencies, creating a connected digital safety ecosystem. By enabling multilingual threat detection, evidence preservation, actionable guidance, and future interoperability with existing reporting and support systems, SafeSphere demonstrates how open collaboration and shared innovation can be leveraged to create a scalable, inclusive, and impactful solution for protecting individuals in the digital world.

agent-grid-fe76.name: AGENTGRID
agent-grid-fe76.tagline: An Autonomous Multi-Agent Energy Operating System

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Renewable energy adoption is growing rapidly, but residential communities still operate in a highly inefficient manner.

Solar panels generate energy unpredictably, batteries are often underutilized, electric vehicles are charged during expensive peak hours, and households consume electricity independently without any coordination. Existing energy dashboards only display information — they do not actively make decisions.

As a result:

* Communities pay higher electricity bills.
* Renewable energy is wasted when generation exceeds demand.
* Peak-hour grid dependence increases costs and carbon emissions.
* EV charging occurs at suboptimal times.
* Residents receive little to no actionable sustainability guidance.
* Non-technical and multilingual communities struggle to access energy insights.

AGENTGRID addresses this challenge by introducing an Autonomous Multi-Agent Energy Operating System that continuously coordinates households, renewable generation, batteries, EV charging, and grid interactions in real time.

Instead of simply monitoring energy consumption, AGENTGRID actively analyzes forecasts, negotiates resource allocation, predicts future demand, and recommends optimal actions that reduce costs, maximize renewable utilization, and improve sustainability across the entire community.

The platform combines Multi-Agent AI, Energy Forecasting, Digital Twin Simulation, Multilingual AI Assistance, and Community Gamification into a single intelligent operating system for sustainable neighborhoods.

Our vision is to transform residential communities from passive energy consumers into self-optimizing energy ecosystems.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/89acf4fe26594b6abc46ebec356e364f/fc914110-938f-4cdc-943d-c396cb54fdcf.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/89acf4fe26594b6abc46ebec356e364f/fbb9f4a3-ca14-4edd-865e-48f083a4f49f.png)

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Building AGENTGRID required solving challenges across AI, simulation, forecasting, and real-time system design.

One of the biggest challenges was designing a Multi-Agent System capable of coordinating multiple energy assets simultaneously. We needed autonomous agents representing households, solar generation, battery storage, EV charging, and grid infrastructure, while ensuring that decisions remained explainable, deterministic, and suitable for real-time execution.

Another major challenge was integrating forecasting with optimization. Renewable generation and energy demand are highly dynamic, so our forecasting models needed to provide reliable predictions that could directly influence agent decisions without introducing instability into the system.

Creating a real-time Digital Twin posed additional challenges. The platform visualizes an entire community through an interactive 3D environment where changes in generation, demand, battery usage, and optimization decisions are reflected dynamically. Maintaining responsiveness while displaying multiple interconnected assets required careful system design.

Multilingual accessibility was another challenge. Energy management systems are often inaccessible to non-technical users. By integrating multilingual conversational AI, we ensured that sustainability recommendations and savings plans could be understood by a much broader audience.

These challenges ultimately shaped AGENTGRID into a scalable and modular platform capable of supporting future smart-city and community-energy applications.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
AGENTGRID closely aligns with Sarvam's vision of making advanced AI accessible to India's diverse linguistic population.

Energy management systems are typically designed for technical users and are often available only in English. However, real residential communities consist of families that communicate in different regional languages. For large-scale adoption of sustainable technologies, language must not become a barrier.

AGENTGRID uses Sarvam's ecosystem to ensure that every resident can interact with the platform naturally in their preferred language, making energy intelligence truly inclusive.

### Sarvam Technologies Used

**1. Sarvam 105B – Multilingual Large Language Model**

Sarvam 105B serves as the primary intelligence layer of AGENTGRID.

It powers:

* Energy recommendations
* Sustainability guidance
* Savings planning
* Community energy insights
* What-if scenario analysis
* Personalized action plans

Residents can ask questions such as:

* "How can I save ₹1500 this month?"
* "When should I charge my EV?"
* "How can I reduce my electricity bill?"
* "What happens if I install rooftop solar?"

and receive actionable recommendations in their preferred language.

---

**2. Sarvam Bulbul V3 – Text-to-Speech**

AGENTGRID uses Bulbul V3 to provide natural and expressive voice responses across Indian languages.

This enables:

* Voice-based sustainability guidance
* Accessibility for non-technical users
* Support for elderly residents
* Hands-free interaction with the system

Residents can listen to energy recommendations and savings plans instead of reading complex dashboards.

---

**3. Sarvam Saras V3 – Speech Recognition**

AGENTGRID uses Saras V3 for low-latency multilingual speech recognition.

This allows residents to communicate naturally with the platform through voice.

Capabilities include:

* Voice queries in regional languages
* Multilingual speech recognition
* Code-mixed language support
* Real-time conversational interaction

Users can simply speak questions in Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Marathi, Bengali, Malayalam, or other supported languages and instantly receive intelligent responses.

---

By integrating Sarvam 105B, Bulbul V3, and Saras V3, AGENTGRID transforms a technically complex energy optimization system into a multilingual, voice-enabled, and highly accessible community platform.

The result is an AI-powered sustainability solution that can be adopted not only by urban English-speaking users, but also by diverse communities across India, ensuring that the benefits of clean energy and intelligent resource management are available to everyone, regardless of language.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/89acf4fe26594b6abc46ebec356e364f/2968fc37-ec06-40cf-9946-7267f6f77495.png)

description.title: Sustainable Development
description.body:
AGENTGRID directly addresses one of the biggest challenges in sustainable development: the perceived trade-off between environmental responsibility and economic benefit.

Traditionally, sustainability initiatives are often viewed as activities that require additional investment, lifestyle changes, or financial sacrifice. AGENTGRID challenges this assumption by demonstrating that sustainable behavior can also be economically beneficial. Through intelligent coordination of renewable energy generation, battery storage, EV charging, and household demand, the platform helps communities reduce electricity costs while simultaneously lowering carbon emissions.

By maximizing renewable energy utilization, minimizing peak-hour grid dependence, and optimizing community-wide energy allocation, AGENTGRID enables households to save money while contributing to environmental sustainability. In other words, sustainability is no longer a cost—it becomes a source of measurable financial savings.

The project aligns strongly with multiple United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):

**SDG 7 – Affordable and Clean Energy**

* Increases renewable energy utilization.
* Optimizes solar generation and battery storage.
* Reduces dependence on expensive grid electricity.

**SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities**

* Creates intelligent, self-optimizing residential communities.
* Promotes community-wide coordination instead of isolated household decision-making.

**SDG 12 – Responsible Consumption and Production**

* Encourages efficient energy consumption.
* Reduces energy wastage through AI-driven scheduling and optimization.

**SDG 13 – Climate Action**

* Lowers carbon emissions by prioritizing renewable energy sources.
* Reduces reliance on carbon-intensive grid electricity.

**SDG 9 – Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure**

* Introduces a next-generation AI-powered energy operating system.
* Combines Multi-Agent AI, forecasting, digital twins, and intelligent optimization for modern energy infrastructure.

Through AGENTGRID, sustainability becomes accessible, measurable, economically rewarding, and scalable, creating a model for future smart communities and energy-resilient cities.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# The Problem It Solves

## The gap

India runs **thousands of central and state welfare schemes** — pensions, scholarships, maternity benefits, housing, crop support, disability aid, health cover. The money exists. The problem is the **last mile**: the people who need these schemes most often have no idea they exist, can't tell which ones they qualify for, can't read the eligibility rules or fill the forms, and don't speak the language the portals are written in.

So today, claiming a benefit usually means one of three things:

1. Spending hours navigating confusing government websites (in English/Hindi, behind logins, full of jargon).
2. Standing in a queue at an office, only to be told you don't qualify.
3. Paying a middleman or agent who takes a cut to do something the citizen was entitled to for free.

> **The result:** eligible families never claim what's rightfully theirs, and those who try often waste a day's wages and a long trip on a scheme they were never eligible for.

---

## Who it's for

- **Rural, elderly, and non literate citizens** who can speak but can't read forms or type.
- **Anyone overwhelmed by the bureaucracy** — first time applicants, or caregivers applying on behalf of a parent or child.
- **Frontline helpers** — ASHA workers, Common Service Centre operators, and NGO volunteers — who can use it as an instant eligibility checker for the people they serve.

---

## What people can use it for

**Yojana Saathi is a voice helpline you can simply talk to.** You describe your situation out loud in **any of 23 Indian languages**, and through a short conversation it figures out exactly which government schemes you and your family qualify for — then explains each one back to you in your own language and hands you a document you can carry to the office.

A user can:

- **Discover schemes they never knew existed**, without reading anything.
- **Check whether they actually qualify** before travelling anywhere.
- **Cover the whole family in one conversation** — the caller, a pregnant daughter, an elderly parent, a school going child — and get a separate, grouped list of schemes for each person.
- **Download a clean PDF** for each scheme with the benefit, why they qualify, the exact documents and certificates to carry, and the official portal link.

---

## How it makes existing tasks *easier*

| Before | With Yojana Saathi |
| --- | --- |
| Read English forms, type details | Just **speak**; it replies aloud and on screen in your language |
| Generic list, you guess what fits | It **asks follow up questions** and matches you precisely |
| Research each family member separately | **One conversation** covers the whole household |
| "You might be eligible" | A **downloadable checklist** of documents and where to apply |

- **Voice instead of forms.** No reading, no typing, no English required.
- **It asks instead of assuming.** A real back and forth — *"Are you a widow or married? What is your yearly income? Which caste category?"* — gathering only what's needed to match you accurately.
- **Actionable output.** The PDF turns "you might be eligible" into a clear next step.

---

## How it makes things *safer*

- **No false hope.** Every recommendation passes a strict eligibility audit, so the app **never tells someone they qualify for a scheme they don't** (for example, it won't suggest an 18 to 40 farmer pension to a 55 year old, or a widow pension to someone who isn't a widow). When it isn't sure, it says so honestly instead of guessing. This is the difference between a wasted trip and a successful claim.
- **Cuts out the middleman.** By giving citizens the same answer an agent would — free, instant, and in their language — it removes the incentive to pay touts and bribes for information that should be public.
- **Transparent.** It shows *why* you qualify and links the **official government portal**, so people apply through the right channel instead of a lookalike scam site.

---

## A real example

A 58 year old woman calls and says, in Telugu:

> *"I'm a widow, we're a poor family with a ration card. My daughter is pregnant, and my son is 16 and still in school."*

In one conversation, Yojana Saathi asks a couple of clarifying questions, then returns:

- **For her:** Widow Pension + National Old Age support
- **For her daughter:** PM Matru Vandana + Janani Suraksha (maternity benefits)
- **For her son:** a Post Matric scholarship

…each explained aloud in Telugu, each with a downloadable document listing the papers to carry and where to apply.

> What used to take days of confusion, literacy, and possibly a paid agent now takes a **two minute conversation**.

---

## Why it matters

Welfare schemes only work if the right people can find and claim them. Yojana Saathi attacks the exact point where the system breaks down — the gap between a scheme **existing** and a citizen actually **receiving** it — and it does so for the people the system most often leaves behind: those who can speak but can't r

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
# Challenges We Ran Into

Building a voice first, multilingual welfare assistant meant almost every layer of the stack fought back at some point. The big ones:

### Speech recognition
Our first model (Saarika) had limited language coverage and turned English into Hindi script. We switched to **Saaras v3** in translate mode, which auto detects all 23 languages and returns clean English.

### Reasoning model
Gemini Flash kept hitting **429 quota walls**, so we moved to a hybrid of **Sarvam 30B** (fast fact extraction) and **Sarvam 105B** (eligibility reasoning). The hidden catch: these are reasoning models that returned empty JSON until we disabled their thinking mode, which also made them far cheaper and faster.

### Embeddings
Our first embedding model was retired mid build, so we moved to Gemini's embedding model at **768 dimensions** with manual L2 normalisation, so cosine similarity stayed correct.

### MongoDB Atlas
Atlas threw SSL and rate limit errors, and our seeding script silently deleted the vector index every time it dropped the collection. We switched to **deleteMany** and batched the embeddings, which made vector search reliable.

### 3D Spline assistant
The bot glided across the page instead of staying put. We pinned it to a fixed corner, drove only its orientation with the cursor, and masked out the watermark.

### Glassmorphism frontend
The look was incoherent (purple on top, green below), so we rebuilt it around one unified emerald theme with consistent blur surfaces and a floating backdrop of the 23 language letters.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body:
**MongoDB Atlas is the retrieval backbone of the whole system — it *is* the "R" in our RAG.** Every welfare scheme lives as a single document in one `schemes` collection that holds both the human readable fields (name, benefit, eligibility text, required documents, apply URL) **and** its 768 dimensional embedding vector side by side. That co location is the key architectural win: we don't run a separate vector store plus a separate metadata database and stitch them together — Atlas is simultaneously our **operational document store and our vector database**, so a single query returns the match *and* everything needed to explain and act on it.

Retrieval runs through Atlas's native **`$vectorSearch` aggregation stage**, backed by a `vectorSearch` index (`numDimensions: 768`, `similarity: cosine`) on the `embedding` field. At query time we embed the user's situation, push the vector into the pipeline with `numCandidates` for recall and `limit` for the top matches, and project the scheme fields plus a `vectorSearchScore` in one round trip. Because it's a normal aggregation pipeline, we can chain it with ordinary Mongo filtering and projection — semantic retrieval and structured data access in the same query language, which is exactly why a vague spoken phrase resolves to the right scheme without any keyword overlap.

It also taught us its sharp edges, which made the integration stronger: dropping the collection silently destroys the Atlas Search index, so we moved seeding to `deleteMany()` and batched the embedding writes to stay reliable, and locked down network access for the cloud deployment. Net result — **MongoDB Atlas Vector Search is the piece that turns a pile of scheme text into an instant, similarity ranked, explainable retrieval engine**, and it carries the core ML workload of the product.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
# How Yojana Saathi Uses Sarvam AI

**Sarvam AI is the entire language brain of Yojana Saathi — not one feature, but the foundation every single turn runs through.** We use three different Sarvam model families end to end, so from the moment a user opens their mouth to the moment they hear a scheme read back to them, it is Sarvam the whole way.

---

## 1. Saaras v3 — speech understanding (input)

The user speaks freely in **any of 23 Indian languages**. We call Sarvam's **`saaras:v3` in `mode=translate`**, deliberately omitting a `language_code` so Saaras **auto detects the spoken language and returns clean English** in a single step.

- Collapses **transcription + language detection + translation** into one call, instead of three separate models stitched together.
- Robust to the things that break Western models on Indian speech — **code mixing ("Hinglish"), regional accents, and dialects**.
- We keep the detected language code **per turn**, which lets the assistant reply *in the language the question was asked in* (English question → English answer, then Telugu question → Telugu answer, in the same conversation).

---

## 2. Sarvam LLMs (30B + 105B) — the reasoning core

Most of our engineering went here. We run a **hybrid of `sarvam-30b` and `sarvam-105b`** through Sarvam's OpenAI compatible `/v1/chat/completions` API, each doing what it's best at:

- **`sarvam-30b` (fast, cheap)** turns messy translated speech into a **structured JSON profile** every turn, and tracks **multiple family members** (the caller plus relatives) by merging new facts into the right person.
- **`sarvam-105b` (heavy reasoning)** is the conversational agent and the eligibility judge. It decides whether to **ask a clarifying question or recommend**, generates the questions and scheme explanations **in the user's own language**, and runs a **strict eligibility audit** — an adversarial "find a reason this person does *not* qualify" pass that stops the system from ever claiming eligibility it can't justify.

> **A non obvious win that made it viable:** Sarvam's chat models are *reasoning* models, and left at default they spent their whole token budget on hidden chain of thought and returned **empty JSON** on long prompts. Setting **`enable_thinking=false`** fixed correctness and made responses roughly **10× cheaper and ~5× faster** (≈140 tokens and ~1s instead of ~1,800 tokens and 5 to 19s).

Splitting cheap extraction (30B) from expensive reasoning (105B) is a deliberate cost vs quality trade that keeps the agent fast and affordable while staying accurate.

---

## 3. Bulbul v2 — speech generation (output)

Every reply — clarifying questions and the final grouped scheme recommendations — is spoken back through Sarvam's **`bulbul:v2`** TTS in the **same language the user spoke**, so a non literate caller never has to read anything. This closes the loop into a true **speech to speech experience**, which is the entire point of a helpline for rural and elderly users.

---

## Why Sarvam, specifically

A generic LLM/ASR stack simply cannot do this for Bharat. Sarvam is **built for India** — 23 languages, code mixing, accents, and Indic scripts as first class citizens — and it is the only stack that let us run the **complete pipeline (understand → reason → verify → speak) natively in Indian languages**.

In short, **Sarvam powers the STT, the structured extraction, the multi turn agent, the eligibility verification, and the TTS.** It is the layer that turns a voice in any Indian language into a verified, spoken government scheme recommendation. That depth of integration — three model families, a hybrid reasoning design, and a real correctness safeguard — is what makes Yojana Saathi a genuine **Sarvam native** product, not an app that merely calls an API.

---

## Sarvam footprint at a glance

| Stage | Sarvam model | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Listen | `saaras:v3` (translate) | Speech → clean English, auto language detect (23 langs) |
| Extract | `sarvam-30b` | Speech → structured JSON profile, multi beneficiary tracking |
| Reason | `sarvam-105b` | Ask vs recommend, explanations, strict eligibility audit |
| Speak | `bulbul:v2` | Replies spoken in the user's own language |

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
**Yojana Saathi is an end to end generative AI system** — specifically a *multilingual, speech to speech, agentic RAG pipeline*. The entire interaction is mediated by ML models: spoken input in any of 23 Indian languages is transcribed and translated to a normalized representation (Saaras v3 ASR + speech translation), a hybrid LLM stack (Sarvam 30B for fast structured extraction, Sarvam 105B for heavier reasoning) converts messy free speech into a typed profile and drives the dialogue, and the response is rendered back as natural speech (Bulbul v2 TTS). It is genuinely multimodal generative AI — audio in, structured reasoning in the middle, audio out — rather than a thin LLM wrapper.

At its core sits a **retrieval augmented generation (RAG) architecture**, which is the heart of the ML track fit. Every welfare scheme is embedded with `gemini-embedding-001` into 768 dimensional vectors (manually L2 normalized so cosine similarity stays well defined at the truncated dimension), indexed in **MongoDB Atlas Vector Search**, and retrieved by semantic similarity against the user's situation. This is what lets a phrase like *"poor widow farmer"* match a scheme described as *"BPL female cultivator with spousal bereavement"* even with zero lexical overlap. On top of retrieval, the LLM performs **grounded generation** — it only explains schemes pulled from the indexed corpus, which keeps outputs factual and traceable rather than hallucinated.

What pushes it beyond a standard RAG demo is the **agentic and responsible AI layer**. The system runs a stateful, multi turn conversational agent that does *slot filling* — it identifies missing eligibility signals and asks targeted clarifying questions instead of assuming — and it tracks multiple beneficiaries in a single dialogue. Critically, recommendations pass through an **eligibility verification stage** that combines an LLM as judge audit with deterministic guardrails (for example, hard numeric age gating), so the model never asserts eligibility it cannot justify. That blend of generative reasoning, vector retrieval, conversational state, and verifiable, safety constrained output is exactly the kind of applied Gen AI and ML work the track is meant to showcase.

kavachai-3bed.name: Kavach-AI
kavachai-3bed.tagline: AI Powered Multilingual Fraud Intelligence Engine

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Kavach-AI (कवच-AI) acts as an intelligent, localized digital armor designed to protect vulnerable demographics—such as elderly citizens and non-tech-savvy individuals—from the rapidly growing epidemic of voice phishing (vishing), SMS spam scams, and social engineering frauds.

How it makes tasks safer and easier:
Deciphers Local Language Scams: Most financial fraudsters in India target victims in regional Indic dialects (Hindi, Telugu, etc.) to induce panic. Kavach-AI utilizes advanced AI translation and transcription to ingest regional voice recordings or texts and translate them into normalized English.
Cognitive Fraud Assessment: Instead of just blocking numbers based on a static list, Kavach-AI uses Google Gemini Flash to run a cognitive assessment on the message context—flagging scam patterns like fake bank blocks (SBI Yono), Kaun Banega Crorepati (KBC) lottery winnings, and urgent electricity bill disconnection threats.
De-escalates Panic in Real-Time: If a high threat is detected, the system immediately plays a localized voice alarm (synthesized via Sarvam TTS) to warning the user in their preferred regional language (e.g. Hindi), keeping them calm and alert.
Guardian Alert Safety Net: Simultaneously, Kavach-AI routes an emergency SMS notification to a registered trusted family member (guardian) using the Twilio SMS API. This allows guardians to intervene immediately and prevent the protected user from completing a fraudulent transfer.
Seamless Authentication: Integrates Twilio Verify OTP authentication to bind user configurations securely to verified physical devices.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Building an end-to-end multi-language AI pipeline comes with real integration hurdles. Here are the key challenges we faced and how we overcame them:

1. Next.js CSS Transform Build Crashes
The Hurdle: During initial development, the Next.js dev server and production builds kept throwing fatal errors (Uncaught Error: globals.css: Parsing CSS source code failed). The parser was failing because the @import statements for Google Fonts were placed below normal CSS rules, violating standard PostCSS rules.
The Solution: We removed the @import font rule from globals.css and loaded the Google Fonts (Inter and JetBrains Mono) natively using the Next.js App Router next/font/google configuration in layout.js. This fixed build performance and ensured 100% compilation success.
2. Infinite Loop and Recursion Errors
The Hurdle: During API stress testing, state updates on the dashboard were triggering endless render loops, leading to recursion depth exceeded exceptions. Setting profile configs or triggering a threat analysis caused state modifications that recursively re-ran the logic.
The Solution: We audited and cleaned up the useEffect dependencies across the main components, decoupling state hooks from triggering mechanisms, ensuring data workflows proceed in a linear, single-direction path.
3. Profile Onboarding State Synchronization Bug
The Hurdle: After completing the Twilio OTP verification, the onboarding setup data (Protected Name, Guardian Number, preferred language) was occasionally getting dropped, causing the Settings page to appear empty when the dashboard launched.
The Solution: We consolidated all profile information into a single unified profile state object in the parent component as the single source of truth. We also created a hard dashboard route guard useEffect that checks local storage and the backend API, forcing the setup page if the profile setup isn't complete (profile_completed !== true).
4. Render Python Version Maturin Build Failures
The Hurdle: When deploying the FastAPI backend to Render, the build server failed during package installation with metadata-generation-failed: pydantic-core maturin failed because Render's default environment was utilizing Python 3.14, which was incompatible with the pydantic compiler.
The Solution: We created a runtime.txt file in the backend directory locking the execution container environment to python-3.11.9, forcing Render to build on a stable Python environment and resolving compilation issues.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
How Gemini AI fits into Kavach-AI

Google Gemini API serves as the core cognitive threat intelligence engine of Kavach-AI and is responsible for analyzing whether an incoming message or call represents a cybersecurity threat. After suspicious audio or SMS content is processed and normalized into English through Sarvam AI, Gemini performs deep contextual analysis instead of simple keyword matching. It evaluates the intent behind the communication by identifying patterns commonly used in cyber fraud such as phishing attempts, impersonation of trusted authorities, fake urgency tactics, unauthorized payment requests, social engineering manipulation, and scam language designed to trigger panic in victims. Based on this behavioral and contextual analysis, Gemini classifies the interaction into categories such as Safe, Suspicious, or High Threat while assigning a confidence score and identifying the probable fraud type. This allows Kavach-AI to move beyond traditional spam detection systems and build an intelligent real-time cybersecurity defense layer capable of understanding human manipulation tactics used in modern AI-driven fraud attacks before financial damage occurs. 🚀

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
How Sarvam AI fits into Kavach-AI
Kavach-AI is designed to protect users from AI-powered scam calls and fraudulent SMS attacks that are increasingly being executed in Indian regional languages, mixed dialects, and colloquial speech patterns that traditional security systems fail to understand. sarvam.ai⁠� serves as the core linguistic intelligence layer of our system by enabling multilingual processing at multiple stages of the pipeline. When a suspicious SMS or audio input is received, Sarvam AI first performs speech-to-text conversion for audio and translation or normalization for text written in languages such as Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Hinglish, or other regional variants, converting them into clean standardized English text. This normalized output is then sent to Gemini API, which performs contextual threat analysis to identify scam intent, urgency manipulation, impersonation attempts, or fraudulent financial requests and assigns a threat level such as Safe, Suspicious, or High Risk. Once a threat is detected, Sarvam AI is again used through text-to-speech generation to convert the warning message back into the user’s preferred local language and play an immediate voice alert, ensuring accessibility even for elderly, rural, or digitally vulnerable users. By acting as the bridge between India’s diverse linguistic ecosystem and our AI threat detection engine, Sarvam AI enables Kavach-AI to deliver an India-first, multilingual, real-time fraud prevention system that directly addresses one of the biggest gaps in existing cybersecurity solutions.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
India has over 900 million UPI users — but that number hides a massive gap. The 250+ million Indians who are elderly, illiterate, visually
  impaired, or simply unfamiliar with smartphones are completely locked out of the digital payments revolution. For them, UPI apps require
  reading menus, navigating touchscreens, and typing in English or Hindi script — barriers that are invisible to urban users but insurmountable
  for a 70-year-old farmer in rural Andhra Pradesh or a daily wage worker who never went to school.

  Existing "solutions" don't actually solve this. Basic feature phones can dial numbers but can't run apps. Bank agents exist but charge fees
  and aren't always trustworthy. *99# USSD banking works without internet but requires navigating numeric menus in English — still a literacy
  barrier. None of these solutions offer the most natural human interface of all: your own voice, in your own language.

  SwaramPay turns any phone call into a secure, intelligent banking session. A user calls a single number, speaks naturally in Telugu, Hindi,
  Tamil, or 6 other Indian languages, and authenticates using their voice — no PIN to remember, no screen to read, no app to download. The same
  technology that makes voice assistants feel magical is now accessible to people who have never owned a smartphone, making financial inclusion
  not just a policy goal but a working product.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
The hardest technical problem we hit was voice authentication on low-quality phone audio. Our initial implementation used Resemblyzer for
  speaker embeddings, which worked fine on clean microphone recordings but completely fell apart on Twilio's 8kHz compressed phone audio. We
  were getting false accepts and false rejects at near-random rates, making biometric auth essentially useless. The fix required switching to
  SpeechBrain's ECAPA-TDNN model, which was specifically trained on telephone-quality speech, and adding a resampling pipeline to normalize all
  audio to 16kHz before embedding extraction. That single change took the cosine similarity scores from noisy and unreliable to consistently
  landing in the 0.6 to 0.77 range for the correct speaker.

  The second major hurdle was DTMF digit interference during MPIN registration. When we nested the audio prompt inside Twilio's Gather verb,
  which is the standard pattern, the TTS audio playback was generating frequencies that Twilio's DTMF detector was misreading as keypad presses.
   A user typing "1234" would arrive at the server as "13", two digits silently dropped. We caught this through debug logging that printed
  exactly what digits Twilio received, which made the pattern obvious. The fix was to play the audio on the response object first, add a
  one-second pause, and only then start the Gather, keeping audio and digit detection completely separate.

  Latency was a third ongoing battle. The initial login flow took 26 seconds from call connect to authenticated main menu, which felt unusable.
  By profiling every stage, Twilio's silence timeout, recording download time, SpeechBrain inference, we identified that 4 seconds of pure dead
  silence after the user stopped speaking was the single biggest waste. Tuning the silence timeout from 4 seconds down to 2 seconds, and
  applying similar reductions across all voice input points in the app, brought the end-to-end login time down to a consistent 20 seconds with
  no speech getting cut off, a 23% improvement with a one-line change.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
SwaramPay's core thesis is that the largest barrier to digital financial inclusion in India isn't connectivity or smartphones — it's language and literacy. UPI apps assume a smartphone, a screen, and comfort reading English/transliterated text. SwaramPay strips all of that away: a user just calls a phone number, and conducts an entire banking session — registration, voice authentication, balance checks, P2P transfers, contact management — by speaking in their own language (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Punjabi, etc.) over a basic Twilio voice call. There's no app to install and no script to read.

This is where Sarvam's models aren't an add-on but the load-bearing infrastructure of the product. Every conversational turn runs through Sarvam's Saaras speech-to-text (translating native-language speech directly to English for intent/amount/recipient extraction, while also transcribing in the user's own script for voice-auth anti-replay checks) and Bulbul TTS (for natural-sounding prompts and dynamic responses — balance readbacks, payment confirmations, contact echoes — in 10 Indian languages). Because Sarvam's models are explicitly tuned for 8kHz telephony audio and code-mixed speech, they hold up on real phone-call audio quality, which is the actual deployment environment for this use case — unlike general-purpose STT/TTS that's optimized for clean studio/mic audio.

For the Sarvam track specifically, SwaramPay demonstrates a complete, demo-able end-to-end application of Sarvam's Indic-language stack to a high-stakes, real-world domain (financial services) for the exact population — rural, elderly, non-English-speaking, low-smartphone-literacy users — that voice-first Indic AI is positioned to serve. It pairs Sarvam's STT/TTS with SpeechBrain voice biometrics for hands-free authentication and a guardian companion web portal for family oversight, showing how Sarvam's language models can sit at the center of a genuinely useful product rather than a translation gimmick bolted onto an English-first app.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body:
SwaramPay is built entirely by composing openly accessible tools rather than proprietary technology — Sarvam's Saaras STT and Bulbul TTS APIs, SpeechBrain's open-source ECAPA-TDNN voice biometrics, and Twilio for telephony. The open innovation bet here is that the frontier models are already good enough, and the real gap is in the application layer: assembling the right pieces to solve a problem nobody had solved for this specific user population.
That problem is a structural artifact of closed design. UPI and India's digital payments stack are technically open protocols, but every interface implementation assumes a smartphone, a readable screen, and English literacy — which de facto excludes the rural and low-literacy users those protocols were meant to serve. SwaramPay opens the interface itself: replace the visual app with a voice call and a language model, and the financial inclusion promise of open protocols actually reaches the people it was designed for. The architecture is intentionally modular so others can extend it — new languages, new financial operations, new regional deployments — without touching the IVR core.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# The Problem It Solves

Many students can solve coding questions but struggle to apply those concepts in real-world projects. Traditional learning platforms often focus on theory and isolated problems, leaving learners unsure about how data structures and algorithms are used in practical software development.

This challenge becomes even bigger for students who are more comfortable learning in their native language. Most technical resources, coding explanations, and interview preparation content are available only in English, creating a learning barrier for millions of students.

PrayogShala bridges this gap by transforming DSA learning into a practical, project-based journey. Students first understand concepts through guided questions, then apply those concepts in hands-on projects, write and execute code in an integrated workspace, and finally defend their implementation through an AI-powered viva.

The platform also supports multilingual learning and voice-based interaction, making technical education more accessible and inclusive. Instead of simply memorizing solutions, learners gain practical experience, improve problem-solving skills, and develop the confidence to explain their coding decisions like they would in a real technical interview.

PrayogShala makes learning more engaging, application-oriented, and accessible, helping students move from "I know the concept" to "I can build and explain it."

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
# Challenges We Ran Into

Building PrayogShala in a hackathon environment came with several technical and product challenges.

### 1. AI-Powered Viva Generation

One of our biggest goals was to create a viva system that generates personalized questions based on a student's actual code. Making the AI understand different coding styles, identify data structures and algorithms used, and generate meaningful follow-up questions proved to be more complex than expected.

To overcome this, we designed a fallback architecture that ensures the viva workflow remains functional even if AI analysis is unavailable, allowing users to continue the learning journey without interruptions.

### 2. End-to-End Workflow Integration

PrayogShala combines multiple components including learning modules, project unlocking, code editing, code execution, progress tracking, and viva evaluation. Ensuring smooth communication between these components while maintaining a clean user experience required careful planning of the frontend and backend architecture.

We solved this by creating a modular service-based architecture and defining clear workflows between each stage of the learning process.

### 3. Project Generation vs Reliability

Initially, we explored dynamically generating projects using AI. However, during development we realized that reliability and consistency were more important for the MVP than dynamic generation.

We introduced a curated project bank mapped to specific DSA topics, ensuring every user receives meaningful, relevant projects while preserving a smooth and predictable learning experience.

### 4. Voice-Based Multilingual Experience

Supporting multilingual learning and voice interactions introduced additional complexity. Managing language preferences, speech recognition, and text-to-speech while keeping the experience intuitive required several iterations of the UI and workflow design.

### 5. Hackathon Time Constraints

Like many hackathon teams, balancing ambitious ideas with limited development time was a challenge. We continuously prioritized features that delivered the highest impact to learners, focusing on building a complete working journey from learning concepts to defending code through an AI-powered viva.

These challenges ultimately helped us refine the product vision and focus on creating a practical, reliable, and engaging learning platform rather than simply adding more features.

without directly giving away the complete solution.

### Project Reflection

Once a project is completed, Gemini helps summarize:

* Concepts applied
* Skills practiced

This creates a more personalized learning journey and helps learners understand their progress.

By using Gemini to structure and guide project-based learning, PrayogShala helps students move beyond solving isolated coding problems and start building real-world software solutions.

MongoDB Atlas stores:

* Current streaks
* Maximum streaks
* Completed modules
* Completed topics
* Project completion status

This allows learners to resume their progress seamlessly across sessions.

### Curriculum Management

Our DSA learning path is organized into modules and topics stored in MongoDB Atlas.

Examples include:

* Arrays & Hashing
* Two Pointers
* Sliding Window
* Stack
* Binary Search
* Linked List
* Trees
* Heap
* Tries

This structure enables dynamic content delivery without hardcoding learning paths into the frontend.

### Project Unlock System

PrayogShala uses MongoDB Atlas to manage project progression.

When a learner successfully completes prerequisite questions:

* Question completion status is stored
* Project unlock state is updated
* Milestone progress is tracked

This creates a structured learning experience where projects are unlocked based on demonstrated understanding.

### Code Submission Storage

Every coding attempt made inside the Monaco Editor is stored in MongoDB Atlas.

Stored data includes:

* Source code
* Programming language
* Submission timestamps
* Associated topic and project

This allows learners to revisit, improve, and compare previous solutions.

### Judge0 Execution Results

After code execution, MongoDB Atlas stores:

* Execution status
* Runtime
* Memory usage
* Compilation errors
* Output logs

This creates a historical record of learner performance and project progress.

### AI Viva Sessions

MongoDB Atlas stores the complete viva lifecycle:

* Generated questions
* Student answers
* Evaluation results
* Scores
* Feedback

This enables personalized assessment and progress analysis over time.

### Skill Reports & Analytics

Using the collected learning data, MongoDB Atlas powers:

* Topic mastery tracking
* Progress analytics
* Skill reports
* Learning history
* Performance insights

This helps learners understand their strengths and identify areas that need improvement.

### Why MongoDB Atlas?

PrayogShala deals with highly dynamic and evolving data, including code submissions, project milestones, viva sessions, and learning progress. MongoDB Atlas allows us to model these relationships efficiently while maintaining flexibility as the platform grows.

MongoDB Atlas acts as the backbone of PrayogShala, enabling a complete end-to-end learning journey from learning concepts, building projects, writing code, and defending solutions through AI-powered vivas.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Currently, city data and citizen complaints (like broken roads, garbage, and faulty streetlights) are scattered across different departments. Because authorities lack a unified view, complaints are handled individually rather than analyzed collectively. This leads to inefficient resource allocation, leaving critical issues regarding water, sanitation, and infrastructure unresolved for long periods.
SDGround is a centralized, AI-powered platform that unifies scattered government data and citizen reports onto an interactive city map.  
For Citizens: It simplifies reporting by allowing users to upload a photo/video with their location. By integrating Sarvam.ai, citizens can report issues using their voice in local regional languages (like Telugu), making civic participation highly inclusive.  

For Authorities: The AI automatically categorizes and clusters similar complaints to reveal major problem hotspots. Municipal officers receive real-time, prioritized alerts and actionable insights on a dashboard, helping them deploy resources efficiently and resolve urban issues much faster.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
**Data Ingestion and Standardization**: Combining unstructured citizen inputs (photos/videos/text) with highly structured government API datasets  was a major hurdle. Incoming data streams were completely disorganized, which initially broke our analytical models. We overcame this by building a dedicated *Data Pipeline* to strictly ingest, clean, and standardize the data before it hits the storage layer.

**Integrating SDGround with Drishti**: Merging the city intelligence logic of SDGround with the data visualization framework of Drishti posed significant architectural challenges. Syncing the live, multi-source data feeds from SDGround with Drishti's geospatial maps in real time caused performance bottlenecks and state-management conflicts. We had to heavily optimize our backend engineering and implement strict client-side state logic to ensure that incoming citizen alerts would trigger map updates without lagging the entire authority dashboard.

**Multilingual Localization and Audio Processing**: Integrating *Sarvam.ai* for voice-based reporting and translation brought up audio latency issues, especially when handling regional accents like Telugu. We had to refine our backend engineering to ensure the translation and Text-to-Speech processes occurred seamlessly in real-time without delaying critical dashboard alerts for municipal authorities.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: SDGround aligns with the Gemini track by integrating Gemini throughout our development workflow to enhance productivity and accelerate innovation. We leveraged Gemini to generate and refine code for several key components of the platform, enabling faster implementation and iteration. Gemini was also instrumental in summarizing technical documentation, guiding API integration, and helping establish the complete process for acquiring and configuring the required API keys. By utilizing Gemini as an AI-powered development assistant, we streamlined research, reduced development time, and improved the overall quality and efficiency of our project.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
SDGround uses Sarvam.ai to remove the language barrier that keeps a huge number of citizens from engaging with civic platforms in the first place — most government and civic apps default to English or Hindi, which excludes a large share of users who are most affected by issues like water contamination and sanitation failures.
We integrate Sarvam.ai's speech and translation models in two places:

Voice-based reporting: Citizens can describe a civic issue by speaking in their regional language (e.g. Telugu). Sarvam.ai converts and translates this into structured text, which then flows into our AI-prioritization pipeline alongside photo/location data — so someone who isn't comfortable typing in English can still file a report with full context.
Drishti groundwater alerts: When Drishti flags a high-risk groundwater zone, the alert is converted into a Telugu audio message via Sarvam.ai's text-to-speech and pushed to residents in that area — turning a dashboard warning that only an official would see into something an everyday citizen can actually hear and act on.

description.title: Sustainable Development
description.body:
SDGround is built around the idea that the UN Sustainable Development Goals shouldn't just live in policy documents — they should be something a city actively tracks and improves, issue by issue, in real time. The platform maps every citizen complaint directly to the SDGs it affects, turning abstract national targets into a live, ward-level scoreboard.
The project directly addresses:

SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation): Citizen reports of leaks, sewage overflow, and contamination are AI-classified and prioritized, while Drishti continuously monitors groundwater quality across 4,300+ stations in 36 states — catching contamination risks before they become a public health issue.
SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities): By giving municipal authorities a prioritized, evidence-backed dashboard instead of an unsorted complaint queue, civic issues — potholes, waste management, infrastructure failures — get resolved faster and with clear accountability.
SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being): Early groundwater contamination alerts and faster resolution of sanitation issues directly reduce the waterborne illnesses that disproportionately affect low-income communities.
SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities): Multilingual voice reporting and alerts (via Sarvam.ai) ensure that citizens who can't engage in English — often the same citizens most affected by these issues — aren't left out of the system.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
## The Problem It Solves

Modern software is built by teams, but the tools developers use are still fundamentally solo experiences.

**Live Share** lets you share a terminal. **GitHub Copilot** gives you AI suggestions. **Git** tracks your history. But none of these talk to each other, and none of them were built for the way teams actually work: multiple people, multiple branches, multiple AI models, all at once.

Here's what developers deal with today:

- You share a Live Share link, but there's no concept of a *session*. Someone joins, someone leaves, and there's no record of what happened or who changed what.
- Your AI suggestions are invisible to your teammates. They see the result, never the reasoning.
- When you close VS Code mid-session, your collaborative work is gone. There's no draft, no recovery, no history.
- Every developer on your team uses a different AI model, but there's no way to combine their outputs into a shared, attributed context.

**The result?** Collaboration happens *around* the code: in Slack threads, Google Docs, and back-and-forth PR comments instead of *inside* it.

---

**Conduit** fixes this.

It brings real-time collaboration, Git-native session management, and per-user AI attribution into a single VS Code extension, so your entire team can write, review, and ship code together, with full visibility into what changed, who changed it, and what the AI contributed.

No more lost context. No more invisible AI. No more collaboration that lives outside your editor.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Challenges I Ran Into

Building Conduit meant solving problems that sit at the intersection of real-time systems, Git internals, and collaborative state management , which wasn't easy to figure out.

---

**Binding Yjs to VS Code without feedback loops**

The hardest early problem was making the two-way binding between a Yjs document and a VS Code TextEditor behave correctly. Every local edit needs to flow into Yjs. Every remote Yjs update needs to flow back into the editor. But VS Code fires `onDidChangeTextDocument` for every edit including the ones your own code applies. Without a precise guard flag, remote updates trigger local events that trigger more remote updates, and the document spirals into corruption within seconds. Getting the `isApplyingRemoteOp` flag placed at exactly the right points in the async chain not too early, not too late took far longer than expected.

---

**Sessions that survive the real world**

A collaborative session does not end cleanly. VS Code windows crash. Networks drop. Users force-quit. Every one of these scenarios needs to produce a recoverable draft silently, without blocking the main thread, with a local fallback if the API is unreachable. Designing a draft system that is both safe and non-intrusive meant layering clourflare R2 and supabase persistence with a VS Code globalState fallback, serializing Yjs binary state correctly, and ensuring that the filesystem operations log is always written in the right order so replay is deterministic.

---

**Git state as a precondition for everything**

Conduit has to validate four things before any user joins a session: the repository URL matches, the branch matches, the local HEAD is a valid ancestor of the session base commit, and the working tree is clean. Any one of these checks can fail in a way that silently corrupts the collaborative state if not caught. Making these checks fast, clear to the user, and non-destructive offering a stash instead of a hard block, prompting a branch switch instead of an error required careful sequencing of async Git operations that run before Yjs ever connects.

---

**Splitting room and session into the right mental model**

The original implementation created a room and a session in a single step. This felt simpler until it did not because a room is persistent and a session is ephemeral, and conflating them meant users had no stable workspace to return to between sessions. Splitting them into separate concepts, separate API routes, and separate UI states introduced a state machine that touches every part of the extension: every button, every command, every WebSocket event.

---

**Multi-file collaboration across an entire workspace**

Syncing a single file over Yjs is straightforward. Syncing an entire project with files being created, deleted, renamed, and moved by multiple users simultaneously is not. Each filesystem operation needs to update the Yjs document map atomically, broadcast to peers, be applied on the receiving end without triggering the local event listeners, and be logged in order so drafts can replay them correctly. Binary files, build artifacts, and ignored directories all need to be filtered before they touch the sync layer.

---

**Designing AI attribution that survives across sessions**

Tracking which AI model changed which line sounds simple until you consider that AI suggestions arrive as raw text, need to be diffed against the current document state, applied through the same Yjs pipeline as human edits, attributed to the triggering user and model, and stored in a way that remains queryable after the session ends. Every one of these steps can fail independently, and a failure at any point means the attribution record is incomplete or misleading which defeats the entire purpose.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
The language of input and the language of output are independently configurable. A developer can speak in Hindi and receive the explanation in English, or speak in English and hear the output in Telugu depending on what is most useful at that moment.

---

### The Bigger Picture

Most developer tools are built for a developer who looks, sounds, and types like the people who built the tool. Conduit and Sarvam AI together are a direct challenge to that assumption.

Voice-native, language-native AI collaboration is not a convenience feature. For a significant portion of the world's developer population, it is the difference between a tool that works for them and one that merely tolerates them.

Conduit is built for every developer. Sarvam AI makes that real.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body:
## Open Innovation Track

Open Innovation is for ideas that do not fit neatly into a single domain ideas that cut across disciplines, challenge existing workflows, and introduce new primitives that did not exist before.

Conduit is exactly that.

---

### A New Primitive for Software Development

Conduit is not a productivity tool. It is not a wrapper around an existing workflow. It introduces a concept that does not exist in the current developer tooling landscape the collaborative session as a first-class citizen of the development process.

Today, a Git commit is the smallest atomic unit of recorded developer work. Everything that happens before that commit the exploration, the back-and-forth, the AI suggestions accepted and rejected, the files created and deleted mid-thought disappears. It is invisible to the team, invisible to history, invisible to the AI.

Conduit makes all of it visible. The session is a new layer between the developer and Git persistent, recoverable, attributable, and AI-aware.

---

### It Crosses Every Boundary

Conduit does not belong to one track because it does not solve one problem.

It is a **real-time systems** problem CRDT conflict resolution, WebSocket state management, multi-user filesystem synchronization.

It is a **developer tooling** problem Git-native workflows, branch-scoped sessions, VS Code extension architecture.

It is a **GenAI** problem per-user model routing, graph-based context retrieval, AI provenance tracking across a shared session.

It is a **language accessibility** problem voice-native prompting in any language via Sarvam AI, spoken explanations for developers who do not think in English.

No single track contains it. Open Innovation does.

---

### The Gap It Fills

The tools developers use today Git, Live Share, Copilot, Slack were each built to solve one problem. None of them were built to work together. The result is that the most important parts of software development the collaboration, the reasoning, the AI-assisted iteration happen in the gaps between tools, leaving no trace.

Conduit is built specifically for that gap. It is the connective layer that makes the invisible work visible, the ephemeral work recoverable, and the individual work collaborative without replacing any of the tools developers already trust.

That is open innovation. Not a feature. A new foundation.

description.body:

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Challenges I Ran Into

While building VitalCare, several technical and system-level challenges arose, especially due to the complexity of integrating multiple modules, AI services, and real-time workflows.

🧠 1. AI Service Integration Complexity (Sarvam AI)

One of the biggest challenges was integrating Sarvam AI for speech-to-text, text-to-speech, translation, and document reading.

❌ Initial issue: API calls were inconsistent and sometimes failed due to network or key availability
❌ Document processing sometimes broke when external API was unavailable

✅ Solution:
I implemented a dedicated AI service layer (sarvamAI) that isolates all AI-related logic.
Additionally, I added a fallback mechanism using pdf-parse to ensure document reading still works even when the external API fails.

🔄 2. Ensuring System Stability Without Breaking Existing Features

Since the project already had multiple modules (dashboards, alerts, appointments, etc.), a major risk was unintentionally breaking existing workflows while adding new AI features.

❌ Issue:

Tight coupling between features could lead to cascading failures

✅ Solution:

Followed a strict modular architecture
Ensured Sarvam AI was added as an isolated service layer
Avoided modifying core modules like authentication, dashboards, and appointments
📄 3. Document Upload and Processing Issues

Handling base64 encoded PDFs and ensuring accurate text extraction was challenging.

❌ Issue:

External API failures caused incomplete responses
PDF parsing required proper buffer conversion

✅ Solution:

Implemented a hybrid processing pipeline
Primary: Sarvam AI document-read API
Fallback: Local pdf-parse extraction
Ensured graceful error handling instead of system crashes
🌐 4. Maintaining Role-Based Access Control

With multiple user roles (Patient, Doctor, Caretaker, Admin), managing access control and data visibility was complex.

❌ Issue:

Risk of unauthorized data access between roles

✅ Solution:

Implemented strict role-based access control (RBAC)
Ensured each role only accesses relevant dashboards and data:
Doctors → assigned patients only
Caretakers → linked patients only
Patients → personal data only
🚨 5. Emergency Alert Workflow Design

Designing a reliable emergency alert system that works across multiple user roles was challenging.

❌ Issue:

Ensuring alerts reach both caretakers and doctors in real time

✅ Solution:

Built a backend-triggered alert system
Designed event-based notification flow to ensure delivery to all linked users
🏁 Outcome

By solving these challenges, VitalCare evolved into a stable, modular, and AI-enhanced healthcare ecosystem that is resilient, scalable, and suitable for real-world deployment scenarios

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Production issues are often discovered only after customers report them or after they start affecting business operations. Engineers then have to manually check dashboards, analyze logs, identify the root cause, and apply fixes, which can be stressful and time-consuming, especially during critical incidents.

Siren AI acts as an intelligent 24/7 monitoring and incident-response assistant. It continuously watches application logs, infrastructure metrics, and system behavior to detect problems as soon as they occur.

When an issue is detected, Siren AI automatically analyzes the problem, identifies the most likely root cause, generates an incident report, and suggests possible solutions. It then calls on the phone to the responsible engineer with a clear summary of the issue. The engineer can either approve one of the suggested fixes or provide a custom solution. Once approved, Siren AI executes the fix and verifies whether the issue has been resolved.

By automating the first-response process, Siren AI helps teams detect and resolve incidents much faster, reduces downtime, minimizes manual troubleshooting, and allows engineers to focus on more important tasks. Instead of learning about failures from customers or managers, teams are informed immediately and can take action before the problem impacts users.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) in India often lose significant revenue due to missed calls, language barriers, and the inability to afford 24/7 human receptionists. When a customer calls to book a table, ask about opening hours, or check stock availability, an unanswered phone call usually means a lost customer.

Furthermore, existing AI phone agents are incredibly difficult to set up. Business owners are forced to navigate complex dashboards, write system prompts, configure webhooks, and map APIs—a process that requires technical expertise they simply don't have time for.

How VoiceClaw Makes it Easier
VoiceClaw completely eliminates the technical friction of building AI voice agents. It introduces a revolutionary "Talk and Build" interface where non-technical users can literally just talk to the platform to configure their AI.

Frictionless Setup: Instead of typing out prompts and mapping API keys, the user speaks their business requirements (e.g., "Hi, I run a vegan restaurant called Green Leaf. We are open from 9 AM to 10 PM. I want the AI to book tables for customers on my Google Calendar."). VoiceClaw automatically parses this natural speech, configures the backend, and injects the necessary tools.
Multilingual & Code-Mixing Support: The agent natively understands and mirrors Indian "code-mixed" speech (like Hinglish or Tenglish), automatically adapting its accent and language to match the caller's comfort zone, ensuring every customer feels understood.
Automated Operations: It connects seamlessly with everyday tools (like Google Calendar for bookings and Telegram for instant owner notifications), effectively serving as a 24/7 receptionist that never sleeps, never misses a call, and never drops a lead.
Ultimately, VoiceClaw democratizes enterprise-grade AI phone automation, allowing local businesses to scale their customer service effortlessly while they focus on running their actual business.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Building a seamless, continuous 2-way voice agent required overcoming several deep technical hurdles, particularly around latency, voice activity detection, and regional language processing.

1. Achieving Seamless "Talk and Build" Turn-Taking

The Hurdle: We wanted the user to build their agent purely through voice without constantly clicking a "record" button. However, basic microphone streaming either cut the user off while they were pausing to think, or resulted in awkward overlaps where the AI and human talked over each other.
The Solution: We built a custom Voice Activity Detection (VAD) system directly in the React frontend using AudioContext and AnalyserNode. We tuned the decibel threshold to ignore background noise and implemented a strict 1.5-second continuous silence timer. This allowed the user to pause naturally mid-sentence. We also tied the AI's Text-to-Speech (TTS) onended event to instantly toggle the VAD back on, creating a perfect, hands-free ping-pong conversational loop.
2. Handling "Code-Mixed" Indian Speech (Hinglish/Tenglish)

The Hurdle: Standard Speech-to-Text models struggled heavily when Indian users mixed English words into regional languages (e.g., Telugu + English = Tenglish). The generated text was often inaccurate, and the AI's spoken responses sounded robotic or used the wrong regional accent.
The Solution: We deeply integrated Sarvam AI's STT and Language ID endpoints. When an audio blob is processed, if the base STT fails to confidently identify the source language, we route the transcript through Sarvam's Language ID model. We then mapped these detected language codes to specific Sarvam Voice Personalities (te-IN -> amartya, hi-IN -> aravind). This ensured the AI dynamically replied in the exact localized accent the user was speaking.
3. Dynamic Tool Calling & Rejection Handling

The Hurdle: The agent needed to trigger real-world actions (booking Google Calendars or sending Telegram messages) based on voice intent, but basic LLMs would either call tools prematurely or rudely insist on calling a tool even if the user rejected the suggestion.
The Solution: We implemented a custom XML tag steering system in the RAG backend. The AI was strictly prompted to output invisible XML tags (e.g., <tools>calendar</tools>) only after gathering all required parameters. To fix the pushiness, we injected strict rejection-handling rules into the dynamic system prompt—instructing the LLM to instantly drop the goal and revert to a polite greeting if the user explicitly canceled or denied a booking.
4. Audio Payload Validation Errors

The Hurdle: While building the continuous STT pipeline, the FastAPI backend silently failed with 422 Unprocessable Content errors, causing transcription failures on the frontend.
The Solution: By diving into the backend logs, we discovered a strict schema mismatch: the frontend was appending the audio blob to the FormData under the generic key "file", while FastAPI strictly validated against the parameter name "audio". Aligning the payload keys and injecting a placeholder agent_id for the onboarding flow instantly resolved the bottleneck.
