description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
AdaptAble is an end-to-end ML system, and it uses generative AI exactly where generation earns its place: turning raw sensor signals into personalized, human guidance for bodies that no fixed template can serve.
The generative layer does the personalization. An LLM takes each user's profile (injury, available limbs and range of motion, target muscles, wearable baseline) and generates a structured, progressive rehab plan, then rewrites it week to week as pose and heart-rate data show what is working. The same model converts joint-angle and rep data into plain-language coaching and end-of-session summaries, proposes meals that respect allergies and the day's logged calories, and powers a coach that answers questions grounded in the user's own session history through retrieval (RAG), not generic advice.
The perception layer feeds it. Pose estimation extracts body landmarks per frame, a facial-expression classifier reads mood trends, a food-image classifier identifies meals, and signal processing handles rep counting.
Why it belongs here. The novel, hard problem is generative: producing safe, individualized rehab for bodies standard plans ignore, and grounding every word the model says in real sensor data so it personalizes without hallucinating. We constrain generation to a vetted exercise library and validate it against each user's calibrated range of motion, so the model never invents an unsafe movement. The CV gives it eyes. The GenAI gives it judgment.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# The Problem Kirana AI Solves

Indian Kirana stores, over 12 million of them, still operate primarily on handwritten ledgers, paper order slips, and WhatsApp messages that get lost in daily chaos. A customer sends a voice note ordering two kilos of flour, one litre of oil, and three packets of noodles while asking about their outstanding balance. The shopkeeper, busy with ten other customers, scribbles the order on a scrap of paper. By evening, the paper is lost, the customer disputes the order, and the khata balance becomes a source of conflict. This happens daily in thousands of stores, costing shopkeepers time, money, and customer trust.

The khata system itself is a nightmare of manual tracking. A customer named Ramesh owes two thousand five hundred rupees for forty-five days. The shopkeeper must flip through a dog-eared notebook to find Ramesh's page, then remember to ask him for payment. But Ramesh visits only once a week, and the shopkeeper forgets every time. Meanwhile, other customers accumulate debt silently. The average Kirana store loses fifty thousand rupees or more annually to unrecovered credit simply because there is no systematic way to track and recover debts.

Split bills create another layer of chaos. Four friends walk in together. One wants rice, another wants noodles, a third wants milk, and they all want to split the total equally. The shopkeeper spends ten minutes calculating, writing four separate entries in the khata, and still makes a math error that leads to an argument later. Customers argue over who owes what, and the shopkeeper gets caught in the middle, losing goodwill and wasting precious time that could be spent serving other customers.

Stockouts are equally damaging. A customer asks for a popular brand of noodles. The shopkeeper checks the shelf and finds it empty because he forgot to reorder. The customer walks to the competitor across the street. This happens five to ten times daily. Each lost sale is fifty to two hundred rupees, and each lost customer may never return. Shopkeepers have no way of predicting demand or knowing when to reorder beyond gut feeling and memory, both of which fail under the pressure of a busy store.

Handwritten lists and voice notes are impossible to process at scale. A customer sends a photo of a list scribbled in a mix of Hindi, English, and Kannada script. Another sends a thirty-second voice note rattling off twelve items. The shopkeeper must listen or decipher, then type everything into some system manually, inevitably missing items or misinterpreting quantities. What should take seconds ends up taking minutes, and the shopkeeper falls behind on other tasks.

Kirana AI solves all of these problems by creating an autonomous operating system that never loses an order, never forgets a debt, and never misses a reorder. It automatically transcribes voice notes, extracts text from handwritten photos, and parses messy multilingual messages into structured orders. It maintains a digital khata ledger where every transaction is logged instantly, and when a customer's debt exceeds a threshold, it automatically sends escalating voice reminders directly to their phone. It splits bills among multiple customers without math errors and updates each person's ledger individually. It analyzes sales patterns to predict stockouts days in advance and suggests exactly how much to reorder. The shopkeeper does nothing except approve the occasional purchase order. Everything else runs automatically.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Twilio Credit Ran Out During Testing

While testing the end-to-end order pipeline with a batch of fifty simulated WhatsApp messages, I discovered that Twilio's trial account credit had been completely exhausted. Each test order was sending real WhatsApp receipts and generating actual Vasooli voice notes through ElevenLabs, which consumed both Twilio messaging credits and ElevenLabs character quotas. Had to create multiple accounts and request Twilio for permission.

## Gemini API Quota Exhaustion During Testing
The free tier allows hundred requests per day, but each complex order required two to three Gemini calls due to retries and fallbacks, meaning ten concurrent orders could exceed the quota within seconds. The service would crash with unhandled exceptions, leaving half the orders unprocessed. I solved this by adding a fallback chain to Groq and the heuristic parser ensures that when Gemini is temporarily unavailable, orders still get processed with lower but acceptable accuracy. This made the test suite reliable and the production service resilient to API rate limits.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: Gemini Flash acts as the semantic parsing engine that converts chaotic customer messages into clean, structured order data. The system sends a production-grade system instruction defining operational parameters: multilingual adaptability across 10+ Indian languages, number word normalization (converting "do", "teen", "paanch" to 2, 3, 5), unit mapping ("kilo"->"kg", "doodh"->"litre"), payment intent detection (setting payment_intent to "khata" when phrases like "khate mein daal do" appear), and split grouping (detecting when customers say "Abhi ke saath split karo"). The response schema is strictly typed via Pydantic models - ParsedOrderPayload with payment_intent, request_pdf, raw_splits (each with buyer_name and raw_items), and language. If Gemini fails or returns no items, the system gracefully falls back to Groq's Qwen model, then to a heuristic parser with regex patterns for khata phrases, PDF requests, and item extraction. Gemini enables natural language ordering that works exactly like customers already talk - no forms, no rigid syntax, just "2 kilo aata aur ek doodh ka packet, Rahul ke saath split karo" converted instantly into structured data.

description.title: ElevenLabs
description.body: ElevenLabs transforms the khata debt collection process from a passive reminder into an escalating, emotionally-aware voice intervention. When a customer's outstanding balance exceeds ₹1500, the system automatically triggers a Vasooli (debt recovery) voice note. The send_vasooli_alert function selects a tone based on reminder_count: Level 1 uses calm, friendly settings (stability=0.70, style=0.00) for a polite nudge; Level 2 uses firmer settings (stability=0.50, style=0.40) for a serious reminder; Level 3 uses stern, urgent settings (stability=0.30, style=0.80) for a final warning. Each level has a distinct multilingual script - Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, or English - generated dynamically with the customer's name and exact outstanding amount inserted. The system then calls ElevenLabs' text-to-speech API with the selected voice settings, saves the MP3 to audio_files/, and serves it to Twilio for WhatsApp delivery. This isn't a static template; it's generative output that adapts tone, content, and language per customer and escalation stage, dramatically improving collection rates over generic reminders.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body: MongoDB Atlas serves as the persistent storage backbone for the entire Kirana AI system, hosting five core collections. The orders collection stores every processed order with enriched pricing, applied discounts, split shares, and timestamps. The khata collection tracks the double-entry credit ledger where each customer has an outstanding balance, an array of transaction entries (each with order ID, amount, date, and settlement status), and a reminder_count field that drives ElevenLabs voice escalation. The customers collection maintains lifetime spend, order counts, and last purchase dates for loyalty analytics. The products collection holds real-time stock quantities and pricing used for dynamic order enrichment, while purchase_orders and suppliers manage the B2B restocking workflow. Every write operation uses atomic find_one_and_update with $inc for balance changes, ensuring no race conditions when multiple orders arrive simultaneously — critical for a busy Kirana store. MongoDB's document model perfectly matches the nested structure of orders with line items and splits, and the jsonSchema validation in schema.json enforces data integrity at the database level.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body: Kirana AI integrates Sarvam AI's specialized language models to solve two real-world retail problems that traditional software cannot address: voice notes and handwritten lists. When a customer sends a WhatsApp voice order in Hinglish, Kannada, Tamil, or any of the ten supported Indian languages, the system downloads the audio from Twilio and sends it to Sarvam's Saaras STT API, which returns accurate transcribed text even with background noise, Indian accents, and code-switching between languages. Similarly, when a customer sends a photo of a handwritten grocery list in mixed scripts, Sarvam's Vision OCR (optimized specifically for Indian handwriting) extracts the messy text and normalizes it into machine-readable form. Without Sarvam, Kirana AI would either reject voice and image inputs entirely or force customers to type perfect English orders - neither is acceptable for a real Indian Kirana store. By embedding Sarvam's multilingual STT and handwriting-aware OCR as the first step of its ingestion pipeline, the system enables natural multimodal communication that matches how actual customers already interact, then feeds the extracted text into Gemini for structured parsing. This is applied GenAI: using purpose-built Indian language models as critical infrastructure, not superficial wrappers.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body: This Kirana AI project qualifies for the GenAI track because it embeds multiple generative AI models as core business logic components, not superficial wrappers. The system uses Gemini Flash with a production-grade system instruction to parse unstructured, multilingual WhatsApp text (supporting 10+ Indian languages) into structured orders containing items, quantities, split parties, and payment intent - replacing traditional forms with natural language understanding. It integrates Sarvam AI for speech-to-text conversion of customer voice notes and Google Cloud Vision OCR for handwritten order extraction, enabling multimodal inputs that conventional CRUD applications cannot handle. For generative outputs, ElevenLabs dynamically produces escalating debt-collection voice notes (Vasooli) where the tone shifts from polite to stern based on reminder count, not static templates. The semantic SKU matching with multilingual aliases and script variations further demonstrates GenAI's role in handling real-world linguistic ambiguity. This is applied GenAI - using foundation models to solve authentic retail automation problems that rule-based systems cannot address, deployed in a scalable microservices architecture with proper fallback chains (Gemini -> Groq -> heuristics).

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Problem It Solves -
Legal professionals handle some of the most sensitive and confidential information in the world. Client statements, case strategies, evidence, contracts, court documents, and internal communications often cannot be safely shared with cloud-based AI systems due to privacy, compliance, and confidentiality concerns.
As a result, lawyers still spend countless hours manually reviewing documents, organizing case information, taking notes during client meetings, preparing arguments, managing schedules, and searching through large amounts of case data.
Al AqL solves this problem by providing a completely offline AI-powered legal assistant that runs locally on the firm's own systems. No internet connection is required, and sensitive client information never leaves the organization's control.

What Can People Use It For?
1. Secure Legal Research and Case Analysis - 
Lawyers can ask questions about case files, contracts, evidence, and legal documents using natural language. The system retrieves relevant information from locally stored documents and provides contextual answers without exposing data to external servers.
2. Client Case Management -
Each client receives a dedicated workspace with separate conversations, memories, documents, and case history. This helps lawyers keep information organized and prevents accidental mixing of case data.
3. Real-Time Meeting and Call Documentation - 
With client consent, lawyers can record consultations and meetings. Al AqL automatically transcribes conversations, extracts important facts, and updates case records, reducing the need for manual note-taking.
4. Contradiction Detection - 
The system identifies inconsistencies across statements, timelines, documents, and evidence. This helps lawyers discover potential issues early and prepare stronger legal strategies.
5. Visual Case Understanding - 
Al AqL automatically builds knowledge graphs that show relationships between clients, witnesses, evidence, events, and legal entities. Lawyers can also manually edit nodes and connections to reflect their professional understanding of the case.
6. Scheduling and Conflict Detection - 
Through calendar integration, the system can detect scheduling conflicts such as overlapping client meetings, court hearings, or important deadlines, helping lawyers avoid costly mistakes.
7. Automated Communication - 
Lawyers can generate case summaries, updates, and professional communications using simple prompts and send them directly through integrated email systems.
8. Firm Performance Monitoring -
The dashboard provides insights into active cases, completed matters, client statistics, success rates, and overall firm productivity, helping legal teams make better operational decisions.
9. How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier and Safer -
* Eliminates the need to upload confidential legal data to cloud AI services.
* Reduces hours spent searching through documents and case files.
* Minimizes manual note-taking during consultations and meetings.
* Helps identify contradictions and inconsistencies before court proceedings.
* Prevents scheduling conflicts and missed appointments.
* Provides a visual understanding of complex cases through editable knowledge graphs.
* Improves collaboration through automated summaries and communications.
* Keeps all sensitive information under the firm's direct control.

Why Al AqL Matters
Al AqL combines artificial intelligence, privacy, and legal workflow automation into a single platform. By operating entirely offline, it allows legal professionals to benefit from modern AI capabilities while maintaining the confidentiality and trust that their clients expect.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/e3f45def95b3406aaca545aa9aaf52c5/fb701701-62c6-4d4a-9b81-8add16b7dc08.jpeg)pabilities while maintaining the confidentiality and trust that their clients expect.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Running a Reliable Legal Assistant on a Small Offline Model - 
Our biggest challenge was that we wanted the entire system to run offline using TinyLlama 1.1B. While lightweight and fast, small models often struggle with accurate reasoning, structured outputs, and consistency.
2. Knowledge Graph Generation -
Automatically generating knowledge graphs from conversations was difficult because small language models often produce inconsistent entities and relationships.
3. Vector Database Stability Issues -
Initially, we planned to use ChromaDB for document retrieval and memory storage. However, we encountered database corruption and compatibility issues during development, which affected retrieval reliability.
4. Privacy-First Design -
Many AI features rely on cloud services, but our goal was complete privacy. Building email, scheduling, retrieval, memory management, and legal assistance without sending client data to external servers required significant architectural redesign.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body: Al AqL combines both **Generative AI (GenAI)** and **Machine Learning (ML)** to provide an intelligent offline legal assistant for law firms. It uses a locally hosted Large Language Model (TinyLlama 1.1B) to understand natural language, answer legal queries, generate summaries, draft emails, and assist lawyers conversationally. At the same time, it applies Machine Learning techniques such as embeddings, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), semantic search, knowledge graph generation, memory retrieval, and contradiction detection to analyze legal documents, recall relevant case information, identify inconsistencies, and organize relationships between clients, witnesses, evidence, and events. By combining GenAI with ML-driven retrieval and reasoning systems, Al AqL delivers secure, context-aware legal assistance while keeping all sensitive client data completely offline and private.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
People with diabetes often do not notice early signs of foot problems, leading to painful ulcers and serious complications. Our smart slipper helps by continuously checking foot pressure and temperature while the user walks or stands. If it detects unusual changes, it immediately alerts the user with a buzzer and sends data for monitoring. 
This allows for early identification of problems, reducing the risk of severe infections and hospital visits. The device makes foot care for diabetics easier, safer, and more convenient for everyday use.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Connecting the ESP32 to Firebase was the tricky hurdle.After troubleshooting Wi-Fi and Firebase settings, we achieved a stable link.
This fix made the system more accurate and reliable overall.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: The Google Gemini API adds intelligence to our system by analyzing sensor data and spotting meaningful patterns. Instead of just showing raw values, it provides clear health insights and recommendations, making the solution smarter and easier for users to understand.

description.title: ElevenLabs
description.body: We used ElevenLabs to give the system a natural voice, delivering clear spoken alerts whenever a risk is detected. This makes warnings easier to understand, especially for elderly users, and adds an interactive, accessible touch to the experience.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body: We brought in Sarvam AI to make our system more inclusive and easy to use. It converts sensor data and risk alerts into clear messages in regional languages, so patients who aren’t comfortable with English can still understand them. With voice-based communication, users receive spoken health updates in a natural way. This improves accessibility and ensures the technology can support a wider range of diabetic patients.

description.title: IoT and Embedded System
description.body: Our project sits right at the intersection of embedded systems and IoT. On the embedded side, the ESP32 gathers data from the pressure sensors and potentiometer, processes it, and triggers the buzzer whenever a risk is detected. At the same time, it connects to Firebase over Wi-Fi, sending the data for real-time monitoring. This means caregivers and users can check the information remotely, without being physically present. By linking sensors, a microcontroller, and cloud services, we’ve built a practical IoT-based healthcare solution that blends local processing with remote accessibility.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
1. Campus "Last-Mile" Inconvenience: Students waste significant time walking long distances across campus just to buy basic canteen meals, snacks, or daily supplies.

2. Inefficient Peer-to-Peer Lending: When a student urgently needs a short-term item (like a calculator for an exam or a lab coat), they have no secure, reliable way to find a nearby peer willing to lend it.

3. Reliance on Chaotic Networks: Students are forced to rely on disorganized, unverified WhatsApp or Telegram groups to ask for help or coordinate item drop-offs.

4. Untapped Student Time: Students who are already walking across campus have no structured way to monetize their movement and free time.

5. Lack of a Campus Micro-Economy: There is no hyper-local, safe ecosystem that incentivizes students to help each other while allowing them to earn pocket money and rewards.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/280e48c059eb4a818ceb96a477d96e26/f178f69f-9142-435d-9e24-19ec22ea7398.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/280e48c059eb4a818ceb96a477d96e26/714461e1-bd05-4edc-a0d6-8f6af02d0d34.png)

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. AI Matching Speed: Balancing accurate AI matching (Gemini/Sarvam) with fast, low-latency API responses to avoid keeping users waiting.

2. Complex State Management: Handling the multi-step lending timeline (Requested → Matched → Accepted → OTP Handover → Returned) without race conditions.

3. Secure Physical Handovers: Implementing a reliable OTP verification system to safely track the physical exchange of items on campus.

4. Dual Database Workflows: Structuring MongoDB to efficiently handle both permanent merchant shop inventories and dynamic, temporary peer-to-peer listings.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
Smart Matching & Routing: Campus Flow uses Gemini to instantly analyze delivery requests and generate intelligent, logical campus routes and courier recommendations.
Dynamic UI Generation: We leverage Gemini's speed to automatically generate relevant emojis and tags for user-uploaded products on the fly, creating a polished, zero-effort user experience.
Automated Analytics: Gemini powers our merchant dashboard by analyzing raw sales and inventory data to generate plain-English, actionable business reports for campus shop owners.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body:
1. Geospatial Queries: MongoDB's native geospatial indexing helps us find the nearest courier, lender, or available item on campus using real-time location data.

2. Flexible Schema: CampusFlow supports both merchant products and peer-to-peer lending. MongoDB's document model allows us to store different types of data without rigid table structures.

3. Real-Time Tracking:Courier locations, order updates, and lending activities generate frequent updates. MongoDB efficiently handles these high-velocity write operations.

4. JSON-Based Development:Since our frontend (React) and backend (Flask) communicate using JSON, MongoDB's BSON format provides a seamless data flow, enabling faster development and easier integration.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
Intelligent Data Processing: CampusFlow uses Sarvam AI to process raw, unstructured campus inventory and sales data into structured, meaningful insights.
Actionable Merchant Reports: It powers our "Inventory Intelligence" feature, automatically generating plain-text, actionable business health reports for campus shop owners.
Optimized Local Context: By utilizing Sarvam, CampusFlow can better understand and generate recommendations that are highly contextualized for local, fast-moving Indian campus environments.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body:
1. Identifies an Unaddressed, Niche Problem Open Innovation is about finding gaps that standard solutions miss. Big delivery apps (like Swiggy or Zomato) stop at the campus gate, and standard e-commerce doesn't handle short-term peer lending. Campus Flow identifies and solves a highly specific problem: the "last-mile" logistics within a closed campus ecosystem.

2. Combines Multiple Domains Creatively Instead of just being one thing, Campus Flow creatively merges three distinct models:

- Quick Commerce (shop-to-student delivery)
- The Sharing Economy (peer-to-peer lending of emergency items)
- AI Optimization (smart matching and route logic) This cross-pollination of ideas is exactly what Open Innovation looks for.

3. Creates a Self-Sustaining Micro-Economy Campus Flow doesn't just provide a service; it creates a community-driven economy. It turns an existing resource (students walking around campus with free time) into a logistical network. It incentivizes students to help each other through gamification, XP, and pocket money, making the ecosystem completely self-sustaining.

4. Highly Scalable to Other Communities Open Innovation projects need to show future potential. While Campus Flow is built for a college campus, the exact same architecture can be scaled horizontally to any closed community—such as massive corporate tech parks, large residential townships, or hospital complexes.

bhumi-agentic-climate-digital-twin-dcce.name: Bhumi — Agentic Climate Digital Twin
bhumi-agentic-climate-digital-twin-dcce.tagline: See Tomorrow Before You Build It.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# Bhumi — Problem, Solution & Future Scope

## The core problem
Cities like Hyderabad are getting hotter, flooding more, losing green cover and lakes — fast. The data to act on this **exists** (satellites, surveys, reports), but it's scattered, technical, and locked away from the people who actually make decisions. So a city official is left asking three questions they can't easily answer:

> **Where is it worst? Why is it happening? And with the limited money I have — where do I act first?**

Today that means weeks of consultants, spreadsheets, and guesswork. The result: climate action is **slow, reactive, and poorly prioritized** — money often goes where there's political noise, not where it does the most good.

## What Bhumi solves
Bhumi is a **living digital twin of the city's climate** — it mirrors every neighborhood's real conditions on **one map you can simply talk to**, by voice or text, in your own language.

- **See** — the digital twin instantly shows which neighborhoods are worst-hit and how things have changed over the years.
- **Ask** — ask a plain question ("why is this area flooding?") and get a clear answer **backed by real evidence and sources**, not opinion.
- **Plan** — tell it your budget, and the twin tells you **exactly which areas to act on for the biggest impact per rupee** — *"this ₹10 crore protects ~700,000 people."*
- **Justify** — one click produces a ready, costed action plan to take to the council.

In short: **Bhumi turns climate data into a decision.** It's a digital twin that doesn't just *show* the city — it compresses what takes a planning department weeks into a few minutes, and makes climate action **proactive and money-smart**, usable by any officer, not just data scientists.

## Future scope
- **Any city, any country** — the same digital-twin engine works for any region with satellite coverage; onboard a new city by pointing it at the map.
- **Live & predictive** — a real-time twin with monsoon/heatwave **early-warning alerts** and "what-if" scenario planning before disasters hit.
- **Citizen edition** — a public version of the twin so residents can see their own neighborhood's risk and push for action.
- **Plug into city systems** — connect the twin to municipal budgets, work orders, and IoT/ground sensors so a plan becomes actual on-ground execution and tracking.
- **Broader decisions** — extend the twin beyond climate to water, air quality, and urban-planning approvals — a true decision twin for the whole city.

**One line for the form:**
*"Climate data exists but cities can't act on it. Bhumi is a living digital twin of the city's climate you can ask — and it tells a city exactly where to spend its limited budget for the most impact, in any language."*

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Challenges

* **Data reliability:** Satellite data can have cloud cover, missing values, and noisy signals.
* **Real-time forecasting:** GEE gives observations; forecasting needs ML + weather inputs.
* **Model accuracy:** Flood/heat prediction needs validation with real ground data.
* **Complex UI:** Too many features can make the dashboard cluttered.
* **GEE setup:** Authentication, quotas, and service-account setup can be tricky.
* **Explainability:** AI outputs must clearly show measured vs modeled vs predicted data.
* **Scalability:** Moving from Hyderabad MVP to many cities needs better data pipelines.
* **Sarvam integration:** Voice, TTS, and multilingual responses need stable API handling.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
## How Bhumi Uses **Sarvam AI + LangGraph Orchestration**

* **Sarvam AI is the core reasoning brain** that understands user voice/text queries and decides what the user wants: risk analysis, planning, forecasting, what-if simulation, or report generation.

* **LangGraph orchestrates the multi-agent workflow**, routing Sarvam’s decision through the right tools and maintaining state across the full journey: **See → Ask → Plan → Justify**.

* **Voice-enabled interaction:** Sarvam STT converts Indian-language speech into text, Sarvam Chat reasons over it, and Sarvam TTS speaks the final answer back to the user.

* **Tool-grounded decisions:** Instead of giving generic answers, Sarvam triggers **12 specialized tools** through LangGraph/MCP to produce map actions, risk scores, plans, forecasts, and reports.

## 12 Tools in Bhumi

1. **GEE Satellite Tool** — gets NDVI, NDWI, LST, and satellite indicators.
2. **Ward Risk Tool** — fetches flood, heat, water, and vegetation risk scores.
3. **Top Risk Wards Tool** — ranks highest-risk Hyderabad wards.
4. **Map Control Tool** — highlights wards, changes layers, and flies camera.
5. **XGBoost Forecast Tool** — predicts next-year climate-risk trend.
6. **Diffusion Scenario Tool** — generates multiple plausible future-risk scenarios.
7. **What-if Simulation Tool** — tests trees, drains, cool roofs, and lake restoration.
8. **Budget Planner Tool** — ranks interventions by impact per rupee.
9. **Population Impact Tool** — estimates people helped by each action.
10. **Evidence Tool** — explains measured vs modeled vs projected data.
11. **Voice Tool** — handles Sarvam STT and TTS.
12. **Report Generator Tool** — creates a council-ready action PDF.

**One-line fit:**

> Sarvam AI acts as Bhumi’s voice-enabled reasoning brain, while LangGraph orchestrates 12 MCP-powered tools to convert climate-risk questions into map actions, forecasts, simulations, budget plans, and reports.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
## How BhumiAI Fits the **GenAI & ML Track**

* **GenAI Layer:** Bhumi uses **Sarvam.AI** as a multilingual assistant where users can ask questions in voice/text and get climate-risk explanations in local languages.

* **Agentic AI:** **LangGraph** coordinates multiple agents for intent routing, map control, planning, what-if simulation, and report generation.

* **ML Forecasting:** **XGBoost** predicts next-year climate-risk trends using satellite and rainfall features like NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, LST, and rainfall.

* **Generative Modeling:** A **diffusion model** generates multiple plausible future climate-risk scenarios, helping users understand uncertainty instead of relying on one fixed prediction.

* **Tool-Augmented AI:** **MCP tools** connect the AI system with Google Earth Engine, risk scoring, budget planning, scenario generation, and PDF reporting.

* **Decision Intelligence:** The system converts GenAI + ML outputs into practical actions: **which ward to fix first, what intervention to choose, and how much impact per rupee.**

**One-line fit:**

> Bhumi combines GenAI agents, ML forecasting, diffusion-based scenario generation, and tool-calling workflows to turn climate data into actionable urban resilience decisions.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Problem Statement
Urban flooding is often detected only after roads become submerged and drains overflow. Existing systems mainly monitor reservoirs, rivers, and rainfall but lack visibility into local drainage networks where flooding actually begins. Citizens receive limited hyperlocal warnings, authorities struggle to identify vulnerable drainage assets, and sanitation workers face life-threatening risks from toxic sewer gases. There is currently no unified platform that combines flood prediction, drainage intelligence, sewer safety, citizen awareness, and municipal decision support.
Solution
HydroMind Sentinel is an AI-powered Urban Drainage Intelligence and Sewer Safety Platform.
The system uses an ESP32, waterproof ultrasonic sensor, and methane sensor to continuously monitor drainage conditions. Combined with government rainfall data, machine learning models predict flood risk, estimate Time-To-Flood, forecast future water levels, detect drainage anomalies, and evaluate sewer safety conditions.

Real-time Drain Monitoring
Time-To-Flood Prediction
Flood Escalation Forecasting
AI Flood Risk Assessment
Drainage Digital Twin
Drain Health Score
Urban Risk Score
Sewer Safety Index
Worker Entry Clearance System
Anomaly Detection for Possible Blockages
Safe Zone Finder

Community Reporting System
Gemini AI Situation Summary & Decision Support
Sarvam AI Multilingual Voice Alerts
MongoDB Flood Memory Layer

The platform includes both a Citizen Portal and a Municipal Command Center, enabling proactive disaster management and public safety.

Receive early flood warnings before overflow occurs
Access live risk maps and AI-generated safety guidance
Find nearby safe zones and safer travel routes
Receive alerts through voice, SMS, WhatsApp, and web notifications
Report flooding and waterlogging directly from the platform
For Municipal Authorities
Monitor drainage assets in real time
Prioritize maintenance using Drain Health Scores
Detect drainage anomalies and possible obstructions
Forecast flood escalation and recovery timelines

Receive worker safety alerts

Social Impact
HydroMind Sentinel helps transform flood management from reactive response to proactive prevention. By combining AI, IoT, multilingual communication, and smart-city analytics, it can reduce flood damage, improve public safety, protect sanitation workers, and support resilient urban infrastructure for flood-prone cities like Chennai.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges was obtaining reliable drainage and flood-related datasets. While government sources provide rainfall and flood-event information, detailed drainage-level sensor data and sewer safety datasets were not publicly available. To overcome this, we combined official rainfall records with domain-driven synthetic data generation and built realistic datasets for flood-risk prediction, drainage behavior, recovery estimation, and sewer safety analysis.
Another challenge was integrating multiple technologies including ESP32 hardware, ultrasonic water-level sensing, methane monitoring, AI services, automation workflows, and database systems into a single platform. We solved this by designing a modular architecture where MongoDB Atlas acts as the data layer, n8n manages automation, Gemini generates AI-driven insights, and Sarvam provides multilingual voice alerts.
We also faced challenges in making complex flood analytics understandable for both citizens and municipal authorities. To address this, we developed separate Citizen and Admin portals, ensuring that citizens receive simple AI-generated summaries and safety recommendations, while authorities gain access to advanced analytics, digital twin monitoring, and decision-support tools.
Finally, ensuring real-time communication between sensors, predictive models, AI services, and the dashboard required careful optimization of data flow, API integration, and alert automation to create a seamless end-to-end system.

description.title: Best Hack Built using n8n
description.body:
HydroMind Sentinel uses n8n as its central automation and orchestration engine, enabling fully automated flood monitoring and emergency response workflows.
The platform continuously receives sensor data from ESP32-based drainage monitoring nodes. n8n automatically processes incoming data, stores it in MongoDB Atlas, triggers machine learning predictions, invokes Gemini AI for flood analysis and decision support, and uses Sarvam AI to generate multilingual voice alerts.

ESP32 Sensor Data → MongoDB Atlas Storage → Flood Risk Prediction → Time-To-Flood Calculation → Gemini AI Situation Analysis → Sarvam AI Voice Alert Generation → SMS / WhatsApp / Voice Notification → Incident Logging → Dashboard Updates
Additional n8n Workflows
Automatic incident report generation
Community report processing
Critical risk escalation workflows
Alert distribution and notification management
Historical event archival
Recovery monitoring and updates
By using n8n as the automation backbone, HydroMind Sentinel reduces manual intervention, enables real-time decision-making, and creates an end-to-end intelligent emergency response system capable of scaling from a single drainage node to a city-wide deployment.
Impact
n8n transforms HydroMind from a monitoring dashboard into an autonomous flood intelligence platform that can sense, analyze, communicate, and respond to flood risks in real time. This significantly improves emergency preparedness, response speed, and public safety.

description.title: Gemini

The system continuously receives water level, rainfall, methane, and flood-risk data. Gemini analyzes these inputs and generates real-time situation summaries, root-cause analysis, risk explanations, and recommended actions.

By acting as an AI Flood Analyst, Decision Assistant, and Incident Reporting Engine, Gemini becomes the intelligence layer that powers the entire platform.

By combining real-time flood intelligence with multilingual voice alerts, HydroMind improves public awareness, emergency preparedness, and community safety, making disaster communication more inclusive and effective.

description.title: Sustainable Development
description.body:
Sustainable Development Impact
HydroMind Sentinel directly contributes to multiple United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by improving urban resilience, public safety, and sustainable infrastructure management.
SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities
HydroMind helps cities become more resilient to flooding by providing early warning systems, hyperlocal flood prediction, drainage intelligence, and safe-zone recommendations. This enables proactive disaster management and reduces the impact of urban flooding on communities.
SDG 9 – Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure
The platform creates a digital twin of urban drainage infrastructure and uses AI, IoT, and predictive analytics to improve infrastructure monitoring, maintenance planning, and operational efficiency.
SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being
HydroMind enhances public safety through early flood alerts and protects sanitation workers by monitoring methane hazards and providing sewer safety recommendations before maintenance activities.
SDG 13 – Climate Action
As extreme weather events become more frequent due to climate change, HydroMind enables climate adaptation through real-time monitoring, flood forecasting, and risk-based decision support for authorities and citizens.
SDG 6 – Clean Water and Sanitation
By monitoring drainage systems and identifying anomalies that may indicate reduced drainage efficiency or potential blockages, HydroMind supports safer and more effective urban water management.
Long-Term Impact
HydroMind Sentinel transforms flood management from reactive disaster response to proactive prevention. Through AI-powered decision support, multilingual communication, and smart-city analytics, it helps reduce flood-related losses, improve emergency preparedness, protect vulnerable populations, and build more sustainable and resilient urban communities.

The platform uses an ESP32 microcontroller connected to a waterproof ultrasonic sensor and an MQ-4 methane sensor. These sensors collect live environmental data and transmit it to the cloud for analysis, prediction, and automated decision-making.

HydroMind Sentinel extends IoT monitoring directly to the drainage level, enabling earlier flood detection, improved infrastructure visibility, enhanced worker safety, and smarter urban flood management.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Emergency departments often struggle with overcrowding, fragmented patient information, delayed triage decisions, and communication barriers during high-pressure situations. Existing hospital systems are mostly static and centralized, making it difficult to respond dynamically during sudden patient surges or emergencies.

Our project, the Vitality Triage System, addresses these challenges through an AI-powered hospital intelligence platform that combines multilingual voice triage, computer vision distress detection, AI-assisted clinical summaries, and real-time hospital coordination.

The system helps solve several critical healthcare problems:

1. Patients frequently fail to communicate complete medical history, allergies, or prescriptions during emergencies.
2. Nurses experience alarm fatigue due to excessive generic alerts from monitoring systems.
3. Traditional hospital redirection systems are rigid and unable to adapt to real-time conditions like staffing shortages or equipment failures.
4. Many patients communicate using regional or code-mixed languages such as Hinglish, which standard systems fail to interpret accurately.

To address this, our platform integrates:

1. AI-powered prescription OCR and RAG-based patient history retrieval
2. Real-time computer vision distress detection
3. Autonomous hospital negotiation workflows for patient redistribution
4. Indic multilingual voice triage using Sarvam AI
5. AI telemetry and audit logging for observability and governance

The result is a scalable, intelligent, and human-in-the-loop triage ecosystem that improves emergency response efficiency, patient safety, and healthcare accessibility.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges was integrating multiple AI systems into a single unified architecture within a limited hackathon timeline. Our project combines Java Spring Boot, FastAPI microservices, MongoDB telemetry logging, Supabase, OpenCV pipelines, RAG workflows, and multilingual voice AI, which created significant orchestration and synchronization challenges.

Some of the key difficulties included:

1. Designing a clean hybrid architecture between the Java transactional core and Python AI sidecar services
2. Integrating multiple AI workflows such as OCR, RAG retrieval, computer vision, and multilingual voice processing into one unified backend
3. Managing frontend synchronization across multiple live dashboard pages during simulation events
4. Handling real-time state updates consistently between simulations, patient queues, alerts, and monitoring systems
5. Creating a polished frontend dashboard with scalable component architecture while avoiding performance bottlenecks
6. Balancing cinematic UI ambitions with stability and responsiveness during development
7. Managing API compatibility and maintaining clean contracts between backend services and frontend components
8. Ensuring AI outputs remained explainable, observable, and governed through telemetry and audit logs
9. Working with diverse technologies and frameworks under hackathon time constraints while keeping the system modular and maintainable

Another major challenge was ensuring the platform remained reliable even when AI confidence scores dropped or services failed. We implemented fail-safe mechanisms and maintained a strict human-in-the-loop approach to ensure medical staff always retained final control over critical decisions.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
Our project heavily relies on Gemini APIs as the core reasoning and multimodal intelligence engine powering several major workflows across the platform.

Gemini Flash is used for:

1. handwritten prescription understanding
2. multimodal OCR processing
3. contextual clinical summarization
4. emergency distress interpretation
5. AI-assisted reasoning workflows
6. structured healthcare data extraction

One of the system’s key features is converting messy handwritten prescriptions and clinical sheets into structured medical data. Gemini processes visual prescription inputs and generates structured JSON outputs that are later embedded into a RAG pipeline for historical patient retrieval.

Gemini is also used in the distress monitoring workflow, where computer vision events from waiting room surveillance are combined with patient context to generate intelligent explanations for medical staff. This helps reduce alarm fatigue and improves prioritization during emergencies.

Additionally, Gemini powers several agentic reasoning workflows that assist with:

1. patient prioritization
2. contextual medical summaries
3. AI-assisted triage recommendations
4. healthcare workflow orchestration

The project demonstrates practical multimodal Generative AI usage in a real-world healthcare operations system rather than a standalone chatbot application.

description.title: ElevenLabs
description.body:
Our project fits into the Eleven Labs track through the integration of expressive AI-generated voice communication within emergency healthcare workflows.

After multilingual voice triage is processed, Eleven Labs is used to generate natural and human-like audio responses for patients and healthcare environments.

The platform uses Eleven Labs for:

1. multilingual patient confirmations
2. emergency guidance announcements
3. AI-generated clinical floor alerts
4. accessible voice-assisted navigation
5. emotionally expressive audio communication

In high-stress emergency situations, clear and natural communication is critical. Instead of robotic system prompts, Eleven Labs enables the platform to provide more human-centered and understandable voice interactions.

For example:

1. patients receive spoken guidance in their preferred language
2. emergency alerts can be broadcast clearly to staff
3. triage instructions become more accessible for elderly or stressed patients

This improves accessibility, patient experience, and communication efficiency within hospital environments.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body:
Our project fits strongly into the MongoDB track because MongoDB serves as the core AI telemetry and audit logging engine of the platform.

Instead of using MongoDB as a traditional relational database replacement, we designed it specifically for high-volume unstructured AI observability data. Every AI pipeline execution generates telemetry documents containing:

1. AI execution metadata
2. latency metrics
3. confidence scores
4. token usage
5. OCR extraction details
6. distress analysis outputs
7. workflow audit logs
8. payload snapshots

These telemetry events are written asynchronously into MongoDB to create a scalable audit and monitoring system for all AI-driven workflows inside the hospital platform.

MongoDB was chosen because:

1. telemetry payloads are highly dynamic and schema-flexible
2. AI outputs vary across workflows
3. observability pipelines require scalable document storage
4. audit logging demands efficient querying of nested execution data

This architecture allows us to:

1. track AI system reliability
2. monitor model confidence
3. debug workflows
4. ensure governance and traceability
5. support real-time operational observability

MongoDB therefore acts as the backbone for AI monitoring, telemetry, and compliance within the system.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
Our project strongly fits into the Sarvam AI track because multilingual and code-mixed voice intelligence is one of the core pillars of the system.

The platform includes an AI-powered voice triage kiosk designed specifically for diverse Indian healthcare environments where patients often communicate using regional languages and mixed dialects such as Hinglish or Marathi-English blends.

We use Sarvam AI’s speech and language models to:

1. Transcribe multilingual patient speech during triage check-in
2. Understand code-mixed medical conversations
3. Convert natural speech into structured clinical intake data
4. Improve accessibility for patients who may struggle with traditional text-based interfaces

This directly addresses a major real-world healthcare challenge in India: communication barriers during emergency intake and triage.

The system allows patients to speak naturally in their preferred language while the AI structures the information for hospital staff in real time. This improves inclusivity, reduces misunderstandings, and accelerates emergency workflows in multilingual environments.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
Our project fits strongly into the Generative AI and Machine Learning track because it combines multiple AI-driven systems to solve real-world healthcare triage and emergency management problems.

The platform uses Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Computer Vision, multilingual speech intelligence, and agentic workflows to create an intelligent hospital operations ecosystem.

Key AI/ML integrations include:

1. Generative AI Clinical Reasoning: We use Gemini Flash to process handwritten prescriptions, generate structured medical summaries, explain emergency alerts, and assist clinicians with contextual patient insights.
2. RAG-Based Patient History Retrieval: Historical prescriptions and clinical records are converted into vector embeddings using sentence-transformer models and stored in ChromaDB. When a patient arrives, the system retrieves the most relevant historical context to generate AI-assisted summaries for clinicians.
3. Computer Vision Distress Detection: OpenCV and AI-assisted analysis are used to detect abnormal patient behavior such as collapses, seizures, or distress events from waiting room video feeds. The AI then generates contextual explanations to reduce alarm fatigue for medical staff.
4. Multilingual AI Voice Triage: The system supports Indic and code-mixed languages such as Hinglish using Sarvam AI’s speech models. Patients can speak naturally during check-in, and the AI converts speech into structured clinical intake information.
5. Agentic AI Workflows: Autonomous negotiation agents coordinate hospital redirection workflows during capacity surges by exchanging structured healthcare payloads and evaluating real-time operational constraints.
6. AI Telemetry & Observability: Every AI execution is logged into MongoDB telemetry pipelines for auditability, confidence monitoring, latency tracking, and governance.

The project demonstrates practical real-world AI usage beyond chatbots by integrating machine learning and generative AI directly into healthcare operations, emergency triage workflows, and hospital decision support systems.

description.title: The problem it solves

WHAT IS RAKSHA AI

A loyalty and rewards system is planned to recognize and incentivize regular donors.

NGO ADMINS

HOW AI MAKES IT BETTER AND SAFER

— replaced by — Real-time automated donor matching

WHAT IS COMING NEXT

Raksha AI transforms a stressful, manual, and time-critical process into a proactive, intelligent, and coordinated support system — giving Thalassemia patients and their families peace of mind.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Bugs & Hurdles We Encountered — Raksha AI

Building Raksha AI — a blood intelligence and care coordination platform for Thalassemia patients — came with a unique set of technical challenges. Here is an honest look at what slowed us down and how we pushed through.


1. Hyperparameter Tuning & Grid Search

The problem: Grid search was computationally expensive, and we often could not tell if poor results were due to the model, the parameters, or the data itself.

How we got over it: We narrowed the search space by first running quick experiments with randomized search, then zooming into promising ranges with grid search. We tracked all runs using accuracy logs to avoid repeating failed configurations.


2. Chunking Data in the RAG Pipeline

The problem: Chunks were either too small, losing context, or too large, diluting relevance in the embedding space. Poor chunking led to broken context, missed embeddings, and incoherent retrieved results.

How we got over it: We experimented with overlap-based chunking strategies and tuned chunk sizes based on the nature of the medical content, eventually landing on a chunk size and overlap combination that preserved semantic meaning across boundaries.


3. Multilingual Support

The problem: Embeddings trained on English-heavy corpora performed poorly on regional language inputs, leading to retrieval mismatches and inaccurate responses.

How we got over it: We evaluated multilingual embedding models and tested cross-lingual retrieval quality before settling on a model that handled the primary languages our users needed.


4. Tracking Accuracy & Model Selection

The problem: With multiple models in the mix, keeping track of accuracy scores across experiments was messy. It was easy to lose sight of which version was performing best and why.

How we got over it: We introduced a disciplined logging system, tracking model name, parameters, dataset split, and accuracy per run, which made comparisons much cleaner.


5. Churn in the Pipeline

The problem: Components kept breaking or needing rework as upstream changes propagated downstream through the pipeline.

How we got over it: We modularized the pipeline more deliberately so changes in one layer, such as chunking logic, did not silently break downstream steps like retrieval quality. Better separation of concerns saved us significant debugging time late in the project.


These were real engineering problems. Working through them gave the team a much deeper understanding of production ML systems, RAG architecture, and the nuances of building AI for healthcare in a multilingual context.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
Raksha AI — How It Fits the Gen AI & ML Track


GENERATIVE AI USAGE

AI-Powered Chatbot
Raksha AI uses a Generative AI chatbot to handle natural language conversations with patients, caregivers, and donors. Users can type requests like "I need blood urgently" or "Register me as a donor" and the AI understands intent and routes them accordingly — no forms, no friction.

Automated FAQ & Education Engine
A Gen AI module generates personalized responses to questions about Thalassemia, treatment options, and blood donation. Instead of static content, patients receive answers tailored to their specific situation and literacy level.

Multilingual Support (Planned)
Gen AI enables the platform to converse in regional Indian languages, making it accessible beyond English-speaking users — a critical factor for rural and semi-urban Thalassemia communities.


 MACHINE LEARNING USAGE

Predictive Donor Availability — LSTM Neural Network
The platform uses an LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) model trained on historical donor behavior to predict when a donor is likely to be available and when a patient will need their next transfusion. This shifts the system from reactive to proactive.

AI-Driven Donor Matching
An ML model evaluates blood type compatibility, donor proximity, and real-time availability to rank and suggest the most suitable donors for each patient request — automatically, within seconds.

Transfusion Need Prediction
Based on a patient's historical transfusion data, the ML model forecasts upcoming blood requirements and triggers early outreach to potential donors before the need becomes critical.

Intent Classification
Natural language understanding classifies every incoming message into actionable categories — request blood, register as donor, check status, ask a question — and routes it to the right workflow without human intervention.


 WHERE GEN AI AND ML WORK TOGETHER

Gen AI handles the conversation layer — understanding what the user wants and responding naturally.
ML handles the intelligence layer — predicting, matching, and ranking behind the scenes.
Together they eliminate the manual effort that currently makes Thalassemia care coordination slow, stressful, and unreliable.


WHY THIS STRONGLY FITS THE GEN AI & ML TRACK

The project is not using AI as a feature. AI is the core infrastructure of Raksha AI. Every critical function — donor matching, transfusion prediction, patient communication, care education — is driven by either a Generative AI model or a trained ML model. The platform would not function without it.

This is a real-world, high-stakes healthcare application of Gen AI and ML solving a problem that affects over one million Thalassemia patients in India.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
## The Problem It Solves

Students, job seekers, farmers, and entrepreneurs often struggle to find genuine opportunities because information is scattered across multiple websites, eligibility criteria are complex, and fraudulent or misleading links are common. Many people miss scholarships, internships, government schemes, grants, and training programs simply because they do not know where to look or cannot verify the authenticity of the information.

AshaAI is an AI-powered Opportunity Navigator that simplifies this process. Users can interact through text or voice, describe their profile in natural language, and instantly receive personalized opportunities matched to their eligibility.

### Key Features

#### AI-Powered Eligibility Engine

Users enter details such as age, education, income, location, occupation, and interests. AshaAI analyzes their profile and recommends relevant opportunities with eligibility explanations and match scores.

#### AI Voice Assistant

Users can speak naturally instead of filling long forms. The AI assistant understands the user's profile, extracts important information, and helps them discover opportunities through a conversational experience.

#### Verified Original Links Only

AshaAI prioritizes official and authentic application links, helping users avoid misleading, outdated, or fraudulent websites. Users are directed to the original source whenever possible.

#### Personalized Opportunity Recommendations

Different users receive different recommendations based on their profile. A student, unemployed graduate, farmer, and entrepreneur will each see opportunities tailored to their specific needs.

### Who Can Benefit?

* **Students:** Scholarships, internships, fellowships, certification programs.
* **Job Seekers:** Employment opportunities, apprenticeships, training programs, skill development initiatives.
* **Farmers:** Agricultural schemes, subsidies, insurance programs, financial assistance.
* **Entrepreneurs:** Startup grants, MSME support, incubation programs, innovation challenges, funding opportunities.

### How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier

* Eliminates the need to search across multiple portals.
* Provides AI-powered personalized recommendations.
* Supports both voice and text interactions.
* Explains eligibility criteria in simple language.
* Recommends which opportunity to apply for first.
* Directs users to verified official sources.
* Reduces the risk of scams and misinformation.

### Impact

AshaAI acts as a personal AI opportunity advisor, helping people discover genuine opportunities, understand their eligibility, and confidently access scholarships, jobs, government schemes, startup support, and skill-development programs through a single intelligent platform.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Challenges We Ran Into

Building AshaAI involved several technical and integration challenges that required multiple iterations and debugging.

### 1. Integrating AI Services

One of the biggest challenges was integrating Gemini AI into the application for eligibility analysis, opportunity recommendations, and conversational assistance. We initially faced API authentication issues, response format inconsistencies, and challenges parsing structured JSON responses from AI-generated content.

**How we solved it:**

* Updated the integration to use the latest Gemini API request format.
* Added validation and fallback handling for unexpected AI responses.
* Implemented structured JSON extraction and error recovery mechanisms.

### 2. Personalized Opportunity Matching

Different users should receive different recommendations based on factors such as age, income, education, location, and occupation. Creating a reliable matching system while keeping recommendations relevant was challenging.

**How we solved it:**

* Built a profile-based eligibility engine.
* Combined user attributes with AI-powered analysis.
* Added match scores and eligibility explanations for transparency.

### 3. Official Link Verification

Many opportunities are listed across multiple websites, making it difficult to ensure users are directed to authentic sources.

**How we solved it:**

* Designed the platform to prioritize verified and official application links.
* Added validation checks before displaying opportunity URLs.
* Ensured users are directed to original sources whenever possible.

### 4. Authentication and User Personalization

We wanted each user to have a personalized dashboard rather than showing the same information to everyone. Integrating authentication with profile-based recommendations required coordination across frontend and backend systems.

**How we solved it:**

* Integrated Firebase authentication.
* Connected user sessions with MongoDB data storage.
* Enabled personalized opportunity feeds and dashboards.

### 5. Team Collaboration and Merge Conflicts

Since multiple team members worked on different modules simultaneously, we encountered merge conflicts while combining frontend, backend, notification, and authentication features.

**How we solved it:**

* Used Git branches and pull requests for safer collaboration.
* Performed manual conflict resolution where required.
* Created backup branches before major merges to prevent data loss.

### 6. Building a Real-Time User Experience

Our goal was to make the platform feel like a real AI product rather than a static eligibility checker. This required dynamic recommendations, responsive interfaces, and conversational interactions.

**How we solved it:**

* Added AI-powered recommendations and explanations.
* Built an interactive dashboard with personalized results.
* Integrated voice-based interaction capabilities to improve accessibility.

### Key Learning

The project pushed us beyond our comfort zone by requiring us to combine AI, authentication, databases, APIs, frontend development, backend services, and collaborative software engineering into a single working platform. The experience taught us how to design, debug, integrate, and deploy a real-world AI application under hackathon time constraints.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
