description.title: Gemini
description.body: PaperMind uses the Google Gemini API to transform raw research data into actionable insights. Gemini is used to analyze rapidly growing research topics and generate research-gap recommendations, helping users identify under explored opportunities and future research directions. By combining topic modeling, trend analysis, and Gemini-powered reasoning, PaperPulse goes beyond paper discovery to provide intelligent research intelligence and innovation guidance.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body: PaperMind is fundamentally an AI/ML powered research intelligence platform. It uses machine learning techniques such as BERTopic, Sentence Transformers, UMAP, and HDBSCAN to automatically discover research topics from thousands of paper abstracts. It then applies trend analysis and forecasting models to identify emerging and accelerating areas of research. On top of this, Google Gemini is used for generative AI-powered research gap analysis, helping users uncover under explored opportunities, potential future directions, and novel intersections between topics. Together, ML handles large-scale topic discovery and trend detection, while Gen AI provides high-level reasoning and insight generation, making research exploration faster and more actionable.

foresight-66b9.name: Foresight
foresight-66b9.tagline: Your plan walks in. Only the truth walks out.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Most strategic decisions a market-entry plan, a pitch deck, a product bet get pressure-tested only *after* they fail. Internal reviews are biased toward agreement, and founders rarely have a CFO, a competitive analyst, a lawyer, and an ops lead in the room at once.

**Foresight stress-tests a decision from the inside, before you commit.** Upload a business plan, pitch deck, or memo and:

- **Five adversarial AI agents**  CFO, Market, Competitor, Legal, and Execution - attack it in parallel from distinct angles, each grounded in *your own document* plus live web evidence (Competitor and Market Agents)
- A **swarm simulation** plays the decision forward across hundreds of
  personality-driven agents to produce bull / base / bear outcome bands.
- You get a **deterministic risk score (0–100)**, a clear verdict
  (DO NOT PROCEED / CAUTION / PROCEED), the 3 questions your team must answer, an India-specific go-to-market strategy, and a remediation roadmap mapping every top finding to a concrete fix.

**Who it's for:** founders validating a pitch before raising, product/strategy teams de-risking a launch, consultants and analysts who need a fast, structure second opinion. It turns a vague gut-check into a defensible, evidence-cited decision review in minutes making high-stakes calls *safer* and faster.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
**1. Swarm memory quota kept blowing up.** The MiroFish swarm simulation logs every agent interaction as an "episode" in Zep Cloud, and re-running an analysis re-ingested the whole knowledge graph each time we hit the episode quota mid-demo. We fixed it by making the bridge *stateful*: it detects an already-built graph and skips the two graph-construction steps (1-2) on repeat runs, reusing the existing graph instead of rebuilding it. Re-runs now consume zero new episodes.

**2. The swarm returned Chinese.** MiroFish's underlying engine emitted simulation reports in Chinese, which broke our verdict synthesis downstream. We added an auto-translation step in the 7-step async pipeline that translates the swarm output to English *before* it's persisted to MongoDB, so everything downstream stays consistent.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: Our LLM layer is OpenAI-SDK-compatible and fully env-swappable, and we run it on Google's Gemini models to drive all five adversarial agents, the adaptive intake Q&A, GTM generation, and verdict synthesis. Gemini's speed and large context let every agent reason over the full document plus live web evidence in parallel without truncation.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body: MongoDB Atlas is our system of record and our retrieval backbone. We use Atlas (M0) with the async Motor driver to store decision contexts, agent findings, simulation results, knowledge-base docs, and reports, and we use Atlas Vector Search to power the two-layer RAG (a "decision" layer over the uploaded doc and an "internal" layer over the company knowledge base).

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body: The core is a multi-agent generative system: five role-specialized adversarial LLM agents running in parallel over SSE, an adaptive intake that generates follow-up questions from gaps in your document, a two-layer RAG pipeline, and a forward-looking agent-swarm simulation. It's GenAI applied to real decision-making, not a chatbot wrapper.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
### Problem Statement

Millions of people have valuable thoughts, opinions, experiences, and ideas every day, but most of those ideas never get shared.

Creating meaningful content requires more than having an idea. Users must organize their thoughts, understand relevant discussions, research context, structure their message, and adapt it for different platforms. This process creates significant friction, causing many people to consume content passively rather than contribute their own perspectives.

Existing AI tools can generate content, but they typically require users to know exactly what they want to say and how to prompt the AI. As a result, generated content often feels generic, disconnected from the user's authentic voice, and detached from the thoughts that inspired it.

Detea addresses this problem by helping users move from unstructured thinking to structured expression. It captures thoughts, surfaces relevant discussions and community perspectives, generates insights, and transforms ideas into platform-ready content while preserving the user's voice and intent.

In short, Detea solves the gap between thinking and expressing by reducing the friction required to turn ideas into meaningful content.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Building Detea involved several technical and product challenges:

Preserving authenticity: One of the biggest challenges was ensuring AI-generated content reflected the user's actual thoughts and opinions rather than producing generic content that could be generated for anyone.
Reducing friction: We wanted users to express ideas naturally instead of learning prompt engineering. Designing an experience that felt conversational while still producing high-quality content required multiple iterations.
Content discovery and summarization: Aggregating information from news sources, community discussions, and trending topics while presenting concise and useful insights was a significant challenge.
Generating platform-specific content: Different platforms require different writing styles and formats. We had to build workflows that could transform the same idea into content suitable for LinkedIn, X, and other platforms.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: We used gemini api for image generation, post generation, day reflect as an thereapist and assistant.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
Detea is an AI-powered thinking and expression platform that helps users transform unstructured thoughts, conversations, and information into structured insights and platform-ready content.

The core innovation of Detea is that it combines AI-assisted reflection, content discovery, and content creation into a single workflow. Instead of requiring users to manually prompt an AI model, Detea continuously helps users capture thoughts, explore trending discussions, understand community perspectives, and convert those ideas into authentic posts for platforms such as LinkedIn and X.

The platform uses generative AI to:

* Analyze and summarize trending discussions, news, and community conversations.
* Generate AI-powered insights and reflections from user thoughts.
* Create platform-optimized content while preserving the user's voice and perspective.
* Generate custom AI visuals for discussion topics.
* Help users discover patterns in their thinking and build a consistent personal brand.

Unlike traditional AI chat tools that focus primarily on answering questions, Detea focuses on the entire journey from thought to expression. The system acts as both a thinking partner and an expression engine, helping users move from ideas to meaningful content with minimal friction.

By combining generative AI, content understanding, summarization, personalization, and AI-generated media, Detea demonstrates how modern AI can be used not only to generate content but also to enhance self-expression, creativity, and knowledge discovery.

decisionx-ab52.name: DecisionX
decisionx-ab52.tagline: Measure the consequences before you Decide.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Most high-stakes decisions—whether building a metro line, redeveloping a city block, or launching a public policy—are still driven by first-order thinking. Decision-makers evaluate cost, feasibility, and timelines, but often overlook the cascading second- and third-order consequences: community displacement, fiscal overruns, environmental degradation, stakeholder resistance, and long-term economic trade-offs

**DecisionX** is an AI-powered decision intelligence platform that helps governments, planners, and organizations evaluate critical decisions *before* implementation. Instead of relying on a single AI response, DecisionX orchestrates a dynamic team of specialized AI experts—such as economic, social, environmental, stakeholder, risk, and future-impact analysts—tailored to the decision being evaluated.

The platform enriches every analysis with location intelligence from OpenStreetMap, simulates cross-domain impacts, models downstream consequences, and synthesizes every perspective into a single executive verdict. Rather than providing just a prediction, DecisionX delivers transparent reasoning, evidence-backed assumptions, confidence scores, expert debates, and actionable recommendations—enabling leaders to defend complex decisions with confidence before a single brick is laid.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
**Multi-agent orchestration without chaos**
Six specialists run in parallel, then the CDO synthesizes prior outputs. We built a strict per-agent JSON schema, shared project context, and event-stream simulation theater so users see each agent’s status in real time.

**Grounding AI in real geography**
Generic “AI analysis” wasn’t acceptable. We added OpenStreetMap enrichment (POIs, density, radius impacts) and required agents to cite location facts in evidence[], separating facts from predictions in assumptions[].

**Trust & explainability**
Users need to know why a score exists. We built an evidence pack: confidence badges, reasoning timeline, trust panel, and per-metric explanations linked to agent outputs and geo sources.

**End-to-end product polish under time pressure**
We shipped a premium marketing site (agents page, dark/light theme), workspace wizard, live simulation UI, and Supabase-backed project persistence — while keeping the core loop: create project → enrich → simulate → report.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: DecisionX uses Gemini as the reasoning core for a seven-agent decision council, where each specialist (economic, social, environmental, stakeholder, risk, future-shock) runs with its own system prompt and returns strict structured JSON — a strong fit for Gemini’s instruction-following and schema-style outputs. Specialists run in parallel, then the Chief Decision Officer reads all prior agent outputs and synthesizes a weighted executive verdict, showcasing Gemini’s multi-step, context-rich reasoning across long, interconnected tasks. Every agent is grounded in real project metadata and OpenStreetMap location intelligence, so Gemini reasons over specific sites, budgets, and communities instead of producing generic analysis. The Future Shock Agent chains second- and third-order consequences, demonstrating Gemini’s strength in causal reasoning and long-horizon impact modeling. End-to-end, DecisionX turns Gemini from a chat tool into a production decision-intelligence system with live simulation UI, evidence trails, and confidence scoring that teams can act on.

description.title: Sustainable Development
description.body: DecisionX helps teams evaluate infrastructure and policy decisions before they are approved, surfacing environmental, social, and economic consequences in one workspace. Its Environmental Agent quantifies emissions, ecological risk, and sustainability trade-offs for real project sites using location intelligence. The Social Agent and Stakeholder Agent map who benefits and who is harmed, supporting equitable, community-aware planning. The Future Shock Agent traces second- and third-order ripple effects that often cause long-term environmental and social damage after implementation. By turning fragmented impact analysis into evidence-backed recommendations, DecisionX supports smarter, more sustainable development aligned with responsible growth and SDG-style decision-making.

athena-e8ef.name: Athena
athena-e8ef.tagline: An Execution Intelligence for AI Agents

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
AI agents today are powerful but inefficient. They repeat the same workflows, use expensive models even for simple tasks, and lack memory of past executions. This leads to higher costs, slower performance, and unpredictable results.

Athena solves this by giving agents visibility and memory. It tracks how agents behave, learns from past runs, and helps optimize future ones. This means agents can avoid repeating mistakes, choose better models for each task, and complete workflows faster and cheaper.

In short, Athena makes AI agents more efficient, predictable, and scalable by turning execution data into actionable intelligence.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges was finding an AI agent setup that actually supports proper observability and then getting it to work cleanly with Athena. Capturing useful execution data across runs and making it consistent was harder than expected and took a lot of trial and error.

Another issue was working with multiple models. We had to figure out how to connect different LLMs and decide when to use each one.

We solved this by using Ollama and model SDKs to standardize integrations and adding simple routing logic to switch between models based on task complexity.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: Athena uses Gemini as a fast and reliable model for agent tasks like reasoning, search, and summarization. It tracks how Gemini performs across runs and learns from this data to improve future executions. This allows Athena to choose when Gemini is the best option and optimize for better performance and lower cost over time.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
Athena sits on top of Generative AI agents and turns their execution data into a continuous learning system.
We use embeddings and similarity search to learn from past runs, predict future outcomes and optimize cost, latency, and success rates.
Instead of just running LLMs, Athena makes them smarter over time.

meditrust-ai-6659.name: MediTrust AI
meditrust-ai-6659.tagline: Zero fake medicines. Verified by AI.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
MediTrust AI makes buying medicine safer and simpler for everyone involved.

For patients, the biggest worry is whether their medicine is real. Our platform removes that guesswork. Before you buy, AI scans your prescription to confirm it's genuine and not AI-generated or forged. During purchase, you see pharmacies ranked by trust score, not just price, so you don't accidentally buy from a risky seller. After delivery, you scan the medicine packaging and our AI checks if it's authentic before you ever open it. If you need a doctor, you can consult one through voice chat in your own language. And if you're recovering from injury, AI rehab tracks your exercise form and corrects you in real time.

For pharmacies, the platform cuts down manual work. Prescriptions are verified automatically, reducing liability from fraudulent sales. Their trust score is built from actual operational data, not fake reviews, so good pharmacies naturally rise to the top. Offline shops can join the verified network, show live stock online, and accept click-and-collect orders with QR code verification at pickup.

For the healthcare system, the impact is structural. Counterfeit medicines that currently slip through at every stage get intercepted before they reach the patient. The 20 to 30 percent fake medicine penetration in India becomes traceable, blockable, and ultimately eliminable. Every verified transaction strengthens the network. Every detected fake triggers investigation. Over time, the system becomes self-reinforcing, driving counterfeit penetration toward zero.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
The biggest hurdle we ran into was connecting the frontend to the backend and getting the API layer to work reliably. We built the UI first and it looked great, but when we tried to send prescription images from the React frontend to the FastAPI backend, everything broke. We hit CORS errors constantly because the frontend ran on localhost 3000 and the backend on localhost 8000, and the browser blocked every request. On top of that, the async PostgreSQL connection kept dropping when we tried to save large prescription files, and the multipart file upload for handwritten prescriptions would either timeout or return garbled responses. It was frustrating because the UI was ready but the data simply would not flow.

We got past this by using Google's AI Studio and Firebase Studio to scaffold the backend properly. Instead of writing the FastAPI boilerplate and database connection code manually, we fed the full API contract into Google AI Studio and had it generate the complete async SQLAlchemy setup, the CORS middleware configuration, and the multipart upload handlers. Firebase Studio helped us spin up a working Docker Compose setup with PostgreSQL and Redis in minutes, which eliminated the connection drop issues. The AI also caught that we were missing proper lifespan events in FastAPI for database startup, which was why our async sessions were failing. Once the AI-generated backend skeleton was in place, we only had to tweak the endpoints rather than build them from scratch. That saved us hours and let us focus on the prescription verification logic instead of fighting connection errors.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
We used Gemini at its best by making it do things no basic AI tool can handle.

First, prescription fraud detection. Most apps just read text from a prescription image. We use Gemini to understand the whole document. It looks at the image layout, the text content, and cross-checks everything together. It asks questions like does this doctor's registration number match the medical council database, is the dosage right for the patient's age, and does the handwriting pattern look human or AI-generated. It catches fake prescriptions that other tools miss because they only do text extraction without reasoning.

Second, AI-generated prescription detection. People now use ChatGPT to create fake prescriptions that look real. Gemini spots these by finding patterns that humans cannot see. It checks if the text is too perfect, if the spacing is uniform like a computer made it, and if the medical logic actually makes sense for that doctor's specialty. This is not keyword matching. It is forensic document analysis.

Third, post-delivery medicine verification. After the medicine arrives, the user scans the front, back, and barcode. Gemini analyzes all three images together. It checks if the logo on the front matches the composition text on the back. It flags if the barcode is valid but the packaging colors are wrong. It catches mismatches that only a multimodal AI can see because it reasons across images and text at the same time.

Fourth, the big advantage is context size. Gemini can hold one million tokens in memory. This means we load entire regional doctor registries, drug databases, and known counterfeit patterns into one single analysis. Other models have to break this into pieces and lose connections between data. Gemini sees everything at once and finds hidden relationships.

We did not use Gemini as a chatbot. We used it as a forensic analyst that reads handwriting, detects synthetic fraud, cross-references databases, and reasons across images and text simultaneously. That is using Gemini at its best.

description.title: ElevenLabs
description.body:
We used ElevenLabs at its best by building a live AI call assistant trained under full medical guidance.

Instead of making patients wait for doctor appointments or struggle with text-based chat, our AI assistant calls them directly. It speaks in natural regional languages with human-like voice quality, asks about symptoms, explains medicines, and reminds patients about dosages. The conversation feels like talking to a real nurse or doctor, not a robot.

The medical guidance layer is critical. Every response the AI gives is constrained by verified medical protocols. It cannot suggest random treatments or misdiagnose. If a symptom is serious, it immediately escalates to a real doctor. For common issues like fever, cold, or medicine reminders, it handles the conversation fully.

This saves doctor time, helps patients who cannot read or type, and provides 24/7 support when clinics are closed. The voice is warm, clear, and culturally familiar because ElevenLabs clones natural speech patterns rather than sounding synthetic.

That is using it at its best. Not as a text-to-speech tool, but as a medically governed, always-available voice health companion.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
We used Sarvam AI at its best by solving a problem that breaks every other OCR tool on the market. Indian doctors do not write prescriptions in clean English. They scribble in a mix of English, Latin medical abbreviations, and regional shorthand that looks like random lines to standard AI. Tesseract fails. Google Vision fails. Even basic PaddleOCR chokes on the handwriting.

Saravam AI was built specifically for Indian language chaos. It understands that "OD" means once daily, "BD" means twice daily, and "SOS" means as needed. It recognizes when a doctor writes "Tab. Dolo 650" in half-cursive, half-print, with the dosage squeezed into the margin. It handles Hindi-English code switching where the diagnosis is in Hindi and the medicine name is in English. No generic OCR does this because no generic OCR was trained on ten million Indian medical prescriptions.

Other teams building voice chatbots use Sarvam AI as a basic speech-to-text wrapper. They speak into a microphone and get text back. That is using ten percent of what Sarvam can do. We pushed it to its actual limit.

We feed Sarvam AI raw prescription photographs taken under bad lighting with shaky hands at a medical shop counter. It converts those scribbles into structured digital data. Doctor name. Registration number. Medicine names with exact dosages. Date. Quantity. Everything extracted cleanly so our Gemini layer can verify it against medical council databases.

The real differentiator is the feedback loop. When Sarvam extracts text with low confidence, our system flags it for manual review instead of guessing. Over time, these corrections retrain the extraction model for that specific region's doctor handwriting patterns. The system gets smarter with every prescription uploaded in Tamil Nadu, in Kerala, in Punjab. Each state has different scribble cultures and Sarvam adapts because it was born from Indian data.

Other teams use Sarvam to make talking easier. We use it to read what was never meant to be read by machines. We use it to prevent deaths from misread prescriptions. That is using Sarvam AI at its best potential.

description.title: Sustainable Development
description.body:
Our project fits the sustainable development theme because it protects people's health and makes healthcare systems stronger over time.

It targets SDG 3 which is Good Health and Well-being. Right now twenty to thirty percent of medicines in India are fake or substandard. Our platform stops this by verifying prescriptions before purchase, scoring pharmacies by trust, and checking medicine authenticity after delivery. This means fewer people get sick from counterfeit drugs, fewer hospital visits due to wrong medicines, and less money wasted on fake treatments.

It also helps reduce inequality because people in rural areas or small towns can use the app to find verified nearby medical shops instead of depending on unknown online sellers. They get the same safety checks as people in big cities.

The trust score system is sustainable because it runs on AI and real data, not fake reviews. Good pharmacies stay in business and bad ones get filtered out naturally. This creates a healthcare market that rewards honesty and punishes fraud without needing constant manual policing.

By connecting offline medical shops to the digital verification network, we keep local businesses alive while modernizing the system. This supports strong local institutions and responsible consumption of medicines.

In short, we are building a health system that is safer, fairer, and self-improving over time. That is what sustainable development means for healthcare.--

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Metalytics AI addresses one of the biggest challenges in the metal industry: the generation of large amounts of industrial waste and the inefficient utilization of valuable resources. Across industries such as aluminium, iron, steel, titanium, and other metal processing sectors, waste streams often contain recoverable materials that remain unused, leading to environmental degradation, increased waste management costs, regulatory pressure, and significant economic losses.

Currently, sustainability assessment, circularity analysis, environmental impact evaluation, and financial impact calculations are performed using fragmented tools and manual processes. This makes it difficult for industries to understand the true environmental and economic impact of their operations.

Metalytics AI solves this problem by providing a unified platform that measures sustainability metrics, identifies recovery opportunities, calculates monetary losses and gains, compares metal recovery pathways, generates AI-powered recommendations, and visualizes environmental impact geographically. By helping industries recover more resources, reduce waste, improve operational efficiency, and support circular economy practices, Metalytics AI transforms industrial waste from a liability into a valuable asset.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges was integrating multiple sustainability and circularity analysis modules into a single platform while ensuring that all metrics remained synchronized across different pages. Since the dashboard, circularity gap analysis, metal comparison, monetary impact analysis, and PDF reporting modules all depend on shared data, maintaining consistency across the application was challenging.

Another hurdle was designing meaningful sustainability metrics and visualizations that could present complex environmental and economic data in a simple and actionable way for users. We also faced challenges while integrating AI-generated insights and ensuring that recommendations were relevant to the calculated metrics.

To overcome these issues, we implemented a centralized data flow architecture, optimized backend calculations, and extensively tested data synchronization between modules. We refined our visualizations through multiple iterations and carefully engineered prompts and validation mechanisms to improve the quality and reliability of AI-generated insights. The result is a unified platform that provides accurate, real-time sustainability analysis and decision support.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: Gemini is a core component of Metalytics AI and is used across multiple parts of the platform. It powers AI-generated sustainability insights by analyzing environmental and circularity metrics and providing actionable recommendations. Gemini is also utilized for intelligent interpretation of sustainability data, report generation, and summarizing key findings for decision-makers. Additionally, it assists in processing and analyzing data collected from various sources, enabling users to better understand environmental impact, recovery opportunities, and economic potential. By integrating Gemini throughout the workflow, Metalytics AI transforms complex sustainability data into clear, actionable business intelligence.

description.title: Sustainable Development
description.body:
Metalytics AI strongly aligns with the Sustainable Development domain by promoting resource efficiency, waste reduction, circular economy practices, and responsible industrial production. The platform addresses the challenge of industrial waste, particularly red mud generated during aluminium production, by helping industries identify valuable materials that can be recovered instead of discarded.

By measuring environmental indicators such as carbon footprint, energy consumption, water usage, and waste generation, Metalytics AI enables organizations to make data-driven sustainability decisions. Its circularity analysis encourages the reuse and recovery of resources, reducing the need for raw material extraction and minimizing environmental impact.

The platform also supports economic sustainability by identifying the monetary value hidden within industrial waste streams, helping industries transform waste from a liability into an opportunity. Through AI-powered insights and impact assessment tools, Metalytics AI contributes towards cleaner production systems, reduced environmental degradation, and a more sustainable and circular industrial ecosystem.

The project directly supports the goals of sustainable development by balancing environmental responsibility, economic growth, and efficient resource utilization for future generations.

opptrax-b052.name: OppTrax
opptrax-b052.tagline: Discover, Track, and Never Miss an Opportunity.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
## Problem Statement

Students and young professionals often miss valuable opportunities such as internships, hackathons, scholarships, jobs, and competitions because information is scattered across multiple platforms, websites, social media channels, and communities.

Finding relevant opportunities requires significant time and effort, while understanding eligibility criteria, tracking deadlines, and managing applications becomes overwhelming. Many users also face language barriers and struggle to stay updated on opportunities that match their interests and goals.

As a result, countless opportunities are missed not due to a lack of talent, but due to a lack of awareness, organization, and timely action.

OppTrax addresses this problem by providing a single AI-powered WhatsApp assistant that discovers relevant opportunities, summarizes important details, answers user questions, tracks progress, and sends timely reminders—ensuring users never miss opportunities that matter to them.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Challenges Faced

* Integrating the WhatsApp business cloud API and designing a seamless conversational experience for users.
* Aggregating opportunities from multiple sources through web scraping and handling inconsistent data formats(time limit error returned by google and google bot blocking our request)
* Extracting structured information from posters, screenshots, and unstructured content using Sarvam OCR .
* Personalizing opportunity recommendations while maintaining relevance for user and reducing information overload.
* Implementing reliable tracking and reminder systems for deadlines, applications, and events.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
### Gemini Integration in OppTrax

OppTrax uses Gemini as its core AI engine to understand user needs, discover relevant opportunities, and provide intelligent assistance throughout the opportunity journey.

* **AI-Powered User Onboarding:** Analyzes user goals, skills, interests, preferences, and career aspirations to build a personalized opportunity profile.
* **Personalized Opportunity Discovery:** Generates intelligent search queries and matches users with relevant internships, jobs, hackathons, scholarships, and competitions.
* **Opportunity Summarization:** Converts lengthy opportunity descriptions into concise summaries containing eligibility, deadlines, rewards, location, and key requirements.
* **Opportunity Q&A Assistant:** Answers user questions such as eligibility, deadlines, application requirements, remote availability, and other opportunity-specific queries.
* **Context-Aware Conversations:** Maintains conversational context to provide personalized recommendations and guidance based on the user's profile and previous interactions.
* **Intelligent Information Extraction:** Processes content from links, documents, posters, and screenshots to identify and structure important opportunity details.

By leveraging Gemini, OppTrax transforms raw opportunity data into actionable insights, helping users discover, understand, and act on the most relevant opportunities through a simple WhatsApp-based experience.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body:
### MongoDB Integration in OppTrax

OppTrax uses MongoDB as its primary database to store and manage user profiles, opportunities, tracking data, and interaction history.

* **User Profile Management:** Stores onboarding information such as goals, skills, interests, preferred location, language, and user preferences.
* **Opportunity Storage:** Maintains a centralized repository of internships, jobs, hackathons, scholarships, and other opportunities discovered by the platform.
* **Opportunity Tracking:** Stores user-specific tracking statuses such as Interested, Applied, Rejected, and Completed.
* **Reminder Management:** Maintains application deadlines, interview schedules, and event dates to enable timely WhatsApp reminders.
* **Conversation & Activity History:** Preserves user interactions and feedback to provide personalized recommendations and improve future opportunity matching.
* **Scalable & Flexible Data Model:** MongoDB's document-based architecture allows OppTrax to efficiently handle diverse opportunity formats, user-generated content, and rapidly evolving platform requirements.

By leveraging MongoDB, OppTrax ensures reliable storage, fast retrieval, and scalable management of opportunity and user data, enabling a seamless experience from discovery to application tracking.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
### Sarvam AI Integration in OppTrax

OppTrax leverages Sarvam AI to make opportunity discovery accessible to users across India through multilingual and voice-first interactions on WhatsApp.

* **Multilingual Text Understanding:** Users can communicate in any supported Indian language, and Sarvam AI interprets their requests accurately.
* **Voice Input & Output:** Users can send voice messages to search for opportunities, while responses can be delivered back as text or audio in their preferred language.
* **OCR-Based Opportunity Extraction:** When users share posters, screenshots, or flyers of internships, hackathons, scholarships, or jobs, Sarvam AI extracts key details such as deadlines, eligibility criteria, rewards, and registration links, allowing the opportunity to be tracked instantly.
* **Localized User Experience:** Opportunity summaries, reminders, and AI assistance are delivered in the user's preferred language, making the platform accessible to a wider audience.

By integrating Sarvam AI, OppTrax becomes a multilingual, voice-enabled opportunity copilot that helps users discover, understand, and track opportunities seamlessly through WhatsApp.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body:
## OppTrax – AI Opportunity Copilot on WhatsApp

OppTrax is a multilingual, AI-powered WhatsApp assistant that helps users discover, understand, track, and manage opportunities such as internships, jobs, hackathons, scholarships, fellowships, and competitions.

After a simple AI onboarding process, OppTrax learns a user's goals, skills, interests, and preferences to deliver highly personalized opportunities. Users can interact through text or voice in their preferred language, while AI summarizes opportunities, answers eligibility-related questions, and provides actionable insights.

Users can also share posters, screenshots, or links, and OppTrax automatically extracts key details using AI and converts them into trackable opportunities. With built-in tracking statuses and smart deadline reminders, users can manage their entire opportunity journey directly from WhatsApp.

Unlike traditional opportunity portals that only list opportunities, OppTrax acts as an AI Opportunity Copilot, supporting users from discovery to application and completion.

**Tagline:** *Discover, Track, and Never Miss an Opportunity.*

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
RoadSense AI is an AI-powered civic issue reporting platform that enables citizens to quickly report public infrastructure problems such as damaged roads, drainage issues, overflowing dustbins, streetlight failures, and other municipal concerns. Users can submit complaints through text, voice commands, or images, making the reporting process simple and accessible for everyone.

The platform uses AI to automatically understand, categorize, and prioritize complaints, reducing manual effort and ensuring faster issue resolution. With integrated voice support and an AI chatbot powered by Sarvam AI, users can interact naturally in their preferred language, making the system inclusive and user-friendly.

How it makes existing tasks easier
Eliminates the need to visit government offices or navigate complex complaint portals.
Allows citizens to report issues instantly using voice, text, or images.
Automatically categorizes complaints, reducing administrative workload.
Provides real-time complaint tracking and status updates.
Enables faster communication between citizens and authorities.
How it makes communities safer
Promotes quick reporting of hazardous road conditions, open drains, and damaged infrastructure.
Helps authorities identify and resolve issues before they become major safety risks.
Encourages active citizen participation in maintaining public infrastructure.
Creates cleaner, safer, and more sustainable urban environments.
Key Benefits

* Faster complaint registration and resolution
* AI-powered issue categorization and prioritization
* Voice-enabled accessibility for all users
* Improved transparency and accountability

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Major Hurdle We Faced

One of the biggest challenges while developing RoadSense AI was integrating voice-based complaint registration with the AI complaint processing system.

Initially, voice inputs were not being converted accurately into structured complaints. Different accents, background noise, and variations in how users described issues caused the AI to misclassify complaints. For example, a user reporting a "blocked drainage" could be categorized incorrectly as a general sanitation issue.

How We Solved It

To overcome this, we integrated Sarvam AI for speech-to-text processing and added an AI-based complaint categorization layer. We created predefined civic issue categories such as:

Road Damage
Drainage Problems
Waste Management
Streetlight Issues
Water Supply Issues

After converting the user's voice into text, the AI analyzes the complaint and automatically maps it to the most relevant category. We also tested the system with multiple voice samples and refined the prompts to improve classification accuracy.

Result

This solution significantly improved the reliability of voice-based complaint submission, making the platform more accessible and user-friendly. Citizens can now report issues naturally through voice commands, while authorities receive properly categorized complaints for faster resolution.

Key Learning: We learned that integrating AI models is not just about connecting APIs—it requires careful handling of real-world user inputs, testing, and prompt engineering to achieve accurate and reliable results.

RoadSense AI handles different types of data, including:

Text complaints
Voice-generated complaint transcripts
Image URLs and metadata
User information
Complaint status updates
Location details

Since this data can vary in structure, MongoDB's flexible document-based model is ideal for storing and managing it efficiently.

How MongoDB Is Used in the Project

{

MongoDB stores status changes such as:
Pending
In Progress
Resolved
Users can track complaint progress in real time.
3. User Management
Stores citizen profiles and complaint history.
Enables users to view previously submitted complaints.
4. Dashboard Analytics

Authorities can retrieve complaint data from MongoDB to:

View active complaints.
Filter by category.
Analyze issue trends in different locations.
Prioritize urgent problems.
5. Integration with AI Components
Sarvam AI converts voice to text.
Gemini processes and categorizes the complaint.
MongoDB stores the final structured complaint for future retrieval and analysis.

Citizen Complaint (Text / Voice / Image)
↓
Sarvam AI → Speech-to-Text
↓
Google Gemini → Classification & Summary
↓
MongoDB → Stores Complaint Data
↓
Authority Dashboard
↓
Status Updates & Resolution

"MongoDB acts as the central data storage layer of RoadSense AI, securely storing citizen complaints, AI-generated classifications, complaint statuses, and location data, enabling efficient tracking, management, and analysis of civic issues."

✅ Flexible schema for different complaint types

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Legal awareness and access in India is still fragmented and difficult for most people to navigate. When someone faces a legal issue, the first and most important challenge is not taking action, but understanding what the problem actually means in legal terms. Real-world situations like scams, fraud, threats, or disputes don’t naturally map into clear legal categories for an average person, which creates immediate confusion at the very beginning itself.

Even when legal help exists, it is often not accessible in a way that supports quick early-stage understanding. Consulting a professional can be expensive, and most available resources are not designed to guide users step-by-step from their raw situation to a structured legal interpretation. On top of that, legal language and processes are typically complex, making it harder for non-lawyers to clearly understand their rights or possible next steps.

Because of this gap, many people either delay taking action, misunderstand the seriousness or nature of their situation, or fail to properly structure their information when they eventually seek help. This weakens their ability to respond effectively and can reduce the quality of any legal support they later receive.

Overall, there is a missing first layer of support — a simple, intelligent system that can take a user’s real-world problem and convert it into structured legal understanding in real time, before the need for formal legal intervention.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
During development, we initially built BharatLex using a RAG-based approach, but after mentor feedback, we were asked to shift towards a multi-agent system. This required us to redesign the architecture so that different agents could handle specific responsibilities like classification, legal reasoning, and response generation. While this improved structure and modularity, it also introduced complexity in coordination between agents.

We also faced frequent token exhaustion issues while using Gemini, especially since our pipeline involves multiple LLM calls per user request. To address this, we integrated Ollama for local model execution, which allowed us to run certain components directly on local machines. This reduced dependency on external APIs, improved speed during development, and made the system more cost-efficient.

Another challenge was that the multi-agent system was taking too long due to extended internal discussions between agents. In some cases, agents were iterating excessively and consuming unnecessary tokens. To solve this, we optimized the system by limiting interactions to a maximum of two reasoning rounds, ensuring faster responses while still maintaining structured output quality.

Overall, these adjustments helped us balance performance, cost, and system complexity, making BharatLex more efficient and practical for real-world use.

description.title: Vultr
description.body: Our backend is deployed on Vultr Cloud Infrastructure, which provides low-latency compute and reliable scalability for our FastAPI-based system. This ensures that every stage — from transcription to classification to legal reasoning — runs efficiently even under load, making the system deployment-ready rather than just a prototype.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body: For data persistence and structured legal memory, we use MongoDB Atlas. It stores user queries, case classifications, analysis outputs, and generated legal insights in a flexible schema. This is essential for handling unstructured legal narratives and also prepares BharatLex for future RAG-based legal retrieval, where past cases and knowledge can be intelligently reused.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body: We use Sarvam AI – Saaras v3 as our core speech-to-text engine. It enables highly accurate transcription of real-world Indian speech, including mixed languages and informal phrasing. This is critical because users don’t “type legal problems”, they speak them. Saaras v3 allows BharatLex to convert raw voice input into structured text, forming the first step of our legal intelligence pipeline.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body: BharatLex uses Generative AI to transform how consumers understand and respond to legal issues in real time. It leverages large language models to analyze user complaints, classify legal categories, generate structured legal insights, and simulate opposing arguments from the other party. By combining speech-to-text, intelligent reasoning, and text-to-speech systems, the platform provides an end-to-end conversational legal assistance experience that simplifies complex legal scenarios into clear, actionable guidance for everyday users.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
JADU – The VayuSync

Joint AI-Driven Utility for Touchless Human-Computer Interaction

Tagline: Control Beyond Touch

The Problem It Solves
Modern desktop workflows still rely heavily on manual point-and-click navigation and memorized keyboard shortcuts, which can be slow, repetitive, and mentally taxing. JADU – The VayuSync bridges the gap between natural human intent and digital execution by acting as a universal, hands-free operating system agent that combines gesture-based input with voice-driven automation.
AirMouse AI lets you control your computer — or your phone — entirely through hand gestures, no physical contact required. All gesture detection runs locally in the browser via MediaPipe WASM — no cloud, no remote inference latency, and no privacy concerns.
Who it's for and what it replaces:

Accessibility: Users with motor impairments who can't easily use a mouse or touchpad can navigate their entire desktop through mid-air gestures detected by a standard webcam.
Hygiene-sensitive environments: Doctors, lab workers, or anyone in a clean room can interact with a screen without touching peripherals.
Presenters & teachers: Control slides or a whiteboard app from across the room without needing a clicker or assistant.
Mobile users without a stylus: Use your phone's front camera as a gesture input device — no extra hardware needed.

AirMouse AI runs in three modes:

Laptop mode — your laptop's webcam drives your mouse cursor via hand gestures, system-wide.
Mobile-as-camera mode — point your phone at yourself; the video streams to your laptop over WebRTC and controls your desktop cursor remotely.
Mobile-native mode — gestures detected on your phone control the phone itself through an Android Accessibility Service, replacing touch entirely.

JADU complements gesture control by handling natural language commands. By routing voice input through Whisper and Gemini 2.5 Flash and executing intent directly at the OS level via PyAutoGUI, JADU makes interacting with your computer faster, intuitive, and deeply integrated.
What people use it for:

Hands-free multitasking: Execute complex system or browser sequences (e.g., "Open Chrome and go to Instagram") while keeping your hands on the keyboard for actual work.
Enhanced accessibility: A seamless, voice-first alternative for users with mobility or dexterity challenges, making standard OS navigation completely accessible without a mouse.
Frictionless workflow automation: Inject keystrokes, manage active windows, mute audio, and navigate the web without digging through nested menus.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Keeping tracking alive when the browser tab is hidden

requestAnimationFrame and setInterval on the main thread are throttled by browsers when you switch away from the tab — which breaks the entire point of a system-wide mouse controller. The fix was moving the tick loop into a Web Worker. Worker timers (setInterval inside a worker) are not throttled, so gesture frames keep firing at 20 fps even when the user switches to VS Code or a game.
2. Mouse control without native bindings that break on install

robotjs and nut-js both failed to build reliably on Windows due to native N-API and node-gyp issues. Rather than fight the build toolchain, we embedded the mouse controller as a Python subprocess (pyautogui + ctypes) spawned from Node.js. Python is widely available and the script is reliable across Windows versions. The subprocess stays alive for the session and receives JSON commands over stdin.
3. Cursor jitter from raw landmark coordinates

MediaPipe's raw index-fingertip coordinates jitter several pixels frame-to-frame even on a still hand. Applying a simple moving average added lag. We implemented a One Euro Filter — a well-known adaptive low-pass filter that minimizes lag at high velocity and smooths aggressively at low velocity — which made the cursor feel close to a real mouse.
4. WebRTC from a mobile browser to a desktop over LAN

Mobile browsers require HTTPS to access the camera. Setting up a self-signed cert on the Express server and serving the mobile page on a separate HTTPS port (3443) solved camera access, but then Socket.IO signaling had to handle the mixed HTTP/HTTPS context. The /api/server-info endpoint dynamically resolves the LAN IP so the dashboard can generate the correct https://<LAN-IP>:3443/mobile URL for the user to scan.
5. Ghost WebSocket connections

The frontend UI would show a permanent loading spinner even though the Python backend successfully executed the command. React 18's Strict Mode was mounting the component twice, creating a "ghost" WebSocket connection. This was solved by adding aggressive connection-state checks (ws.current?.readyState) and strictly cleaning up socket instances on unmount.
6. AI pipeline bottlenecks

During live testing, the Gemini API would occasionally throw 503 Service Unavailable errors due to high server demand, completely breaking the intent-parsing pipeline. We built a resilient task queue UI that gracefully catches the JSON errors and marks the task as "Failed" rather than crashing the application.
7. UI/hardware syncing

Keeping the React UI perfectly synced with physical hardware execution (like human-mimicking typing delays) was tricky. We solved this by moving the WebSocket listener into a global Zustand store, ensuring the loading animations turned off the exact millisecond the backend broadcast a success message.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body: What happens to your digital life when you're no longer here? LastLogin helps families securely access important digital assets, financial information, and final messages without the confusion of lost passwords or lengthy legal processes. By combining AI and blockchain, it makes digital inheritance simple, transparent, and secure.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Making a live death-trigger land on-chain, on cue, was our biggest demo hurdle. Solana Devnet faucets are heavily rate-limited, so just keeping our deployer wallet funded with test-SOL for repeated runs was a chore. Even worse, the critical state switch from Confirmed to Active needed to happen instantly during the live demo, where a lagging RPC node could stall the whole presentation.

We solved this by making the frontend update instantly the exact moment the wallet returns a successful transaction signature hash. If the node lags, the UI doesn't freeze it falls back gracefully, ensuring the live Solana Explorer link serves as our proof, never our bottleneck.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: we have used it as a core AI engine , which is uses for scanning death certificates-AI Vision and gemini flash lite for fast and accurate responses.

description.title: ElevenLabs
description.body:
ElevenLabs — the person's actual voice, kept alive. This is the emotional core of LastLogin: from a single 60-second recording, ElevenLabs clones a user's voice so their final words can be heard, not just read.

Why: a goodbye in your mother's real voice hits differently than text on a screen. That's the whole product.

Where we use it:

Final messages — the user writes a note, Sarvam translates it to the family's language, and ElevenLabs speaks it back in the user's own cloned voice (legacyMessage.js). ← the centerpiece.
The AI clone companion — guardians can talk with a safety-railed persona of the departed, who replies aloud in that same voice (clone.js).
Voice capture — the cloning happens right on the Messages page from one short reading (elevenlabs.js).

description.title: MongoDB
description.body: we have used it solely to store out user database which are encrypted using DEK  algorithm.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body: When a person passes away, we don't just want to pass down their files; we want to preserve their voice, their language, and their essence. To do this, our platform embraces Open Innovation by integrating external, state-of-the-art AI models from Sarvam AI directly into our ecosystem. Instead of wasting time building expensive language tools from scratch, we plug into Sarvam’s public infrastructure to provide seamless Speech-to-Text (STT) and real-time translation. This allows a grieving loved one to speak naturally in their native language and have a real-time, translated voice chat with an AI persona modeled after the deceased person's memories. By merging public blockchain security with open AI innovation, we are transforming a cold digital vault into a living, breathing legacy.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body: "When a person passes away, their entire life story—from financial accounts to priceless digital memories and photos is often permanently locked behind corporate silos. Our platform changes this through Open Innovation by breaking down these closed walls. Instead of forcing grieving families to fight tech monopolies for access passwords, we built an open, decentralized bridge directly into the public infrastructure of the Solana Blockchain. When a user passes, our backend securely anchors their verified proof-of-death on-chain. This allows their designated Guardian to simply connect a Phantom Wallet and securely unlock their inheritance completely for free. By combining public blockchain technology with human estate planning, we ensure a person's digital accounts and memories are seamlessly passed down to the next generation without a single point of failure

description.title: BlockChain & Web3
description.body: Our platform completely eliminates hackable passwords by using Solana and the Phantom Wallet to protect sensitive recovery keys. When a verified guardian needs to access the vault, they simply connect their wallet and approve a secure sign-in prompt. Because this identity check uses off-chain cryptography, it is 100% free and costs zero gas fees. The exact second the signature is approved, the system confirms their identity and instantly unblurs the secret seed phrases on the screen. This ensures that the keys can never be exposed unless the real guardian approves it with their own wallet

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# 🚑 The Problem DeccanAid Solves

In a medical emergency, the difference between life and death is often measured in minutes. Yet across India, emergency response systems continue to face challenges such as delayed ambulance dispatch, traffic congestion, fragmented communication, lack of hospital visibility, and inefficient resource allocation.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/1cdef346d5ca4a73bd42226b5d907941/cf847e3a-6185-42a1-8f5f-e9a93edacec4.png)

India recorded over **461,000 road accidents and 168,000+ fatalities in a single year**, making road trauma one of the country's most pressing public health challenges. Experts estimate that a significant percentage of these deaths could be prevented through faster emergency response and timely medical intervention during the critical *Golden Hour* — the first hour after a severe injury or medical emergency.

The challenge is even more evident in rapidly growing urban centers like **Hyderabad**, where emergency vehicles often struggle with heavy traffic, delayed dispatch decisions, and limited real-time coordination between ambulances and hospitals. Reports have highlighted emergency response times extending well beyond recommended limits, reducing the chances of successful treatment during critical situations.

## ⚠️ Current Challenges

### Delayed Emergency Assessment

Emergency calls are often manually assessed, resulting in slower prioritization of critical cases such as cardiac arrest, stroke, trauma, and severe accidents.

### Inefficient Ambulance Allocation

The nearest ambulance is not always the most effective choice. Factors such as vehicle availability, traffic conditions, equipment readiness, and hospital destination are rarely optimized together.

### Lack of Hospital Visibility

Patients are frequently transported without real-time awareness of hospital capacity, ICU availability, specialist access, or emergency preparedness.

### Communication Barriers

India's linguistic diversity creates challenges during emergencies, especially when patients and responders speak different languages.

### Fragmented Emergency Ecosystem

Patients, ambulances, hospitals, emergency operators, and family members often operate on disconnected systems, causing delays and information loss.

## 💡 Our Solution: DeccanAid

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/1cdef346d5ca4a73bd42226b5d907941/0f288107-5d69-45e8-a1e0-aaec67281dd9.jpeg)

**DeccanAid** is an AI-powered emergency response platform designed to transform how emergencies are managed from the moment a distress call is received until the patient reaches definitive care.

Using intelligent automation and real-time coordination, DeccanAid creates a connected emergency ecosystem that enables faster, smarter, and more effective emergency response.

### Key Capabilities

#### 🧠 AI-Powered Emergency Triage

Analyzes emergency reports and determines severity, priority level, and required medical resources within seconds.

#### 🚑 Smart Ambulance Dispatch

Identifies and dispatches the most suitable ambulance based on location, availability, emergency type, and route conditions.

#### 🗺️ Real-Time Route Optimization

Uses live traffic intelligence to reduce travel time and improve ambulance arrival speed.

#### 🏥 Intelligent Hospital Matching

Recommends the most appropriate hospital based on medical capabilities, capacity, distance, and patient condition.

#### 🌐 Multilingual Emergency Support

Enables emergency communication across multiple Indian languages, reducing misunderstandings during critical situations.

#### 📡 Live Emergency Coordination

Provides real-time updates to patients, responders, hospitals, and caregivers through a unified platform.

#### 📊 Operational Intelligence Dashboard

Offers emergency operators and healthcare authorities actionable insights into response performance, resource utilization, and system efficiency.

## 🎯 Impact

DeccanAid is designed to reduce response delays, improve emergency decision-making, and strengthen coordination across the healthcare ecosystem.

By combining **Artificial Intelligence**, **real-time location intelligence**, **smart dispatch systems**, and **hospital coordination**, DeccanAid helps ensure that the right ambulance reaches the right patient and transports them to the right hospital at the right time.

### Our Vision

**To make emergency healthcare faster, smarter, and more accessible, ensuring that no life is lost because help arrived too late.**

**Every Second Counts. Every Life Matters.**

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
# Challenges We Ran Into

## 🔌 IoT-to-Cloud Connectivity

One of the biggest challenges we faced was establishing reliable communication between our IoT devices and the cloud-hosted backend.

During local development, the ESP32 devices could easily communicate with our backend using local network endpoints. However, after deploying the application to the cloud, we encountered multiple issues related to:

* Network accessibility and public endpoint configuration
* CORS and API communication restrictions
* Device authentication and request handling
* Intermittent connectivity between the IoT hardware and cloud services
* Data synchronization delays between the device and server

To overcome this, we reconfigured our backend architecture, optimized API communication, implemented proper endpoint management, and extensively tested device-to-server interactions under real-world network conditions until we achieved stable communication.

---

## 📱 Cross-Platform Responsiveness

Another significant challenge was ensuring a consistent user experience across multiple platforms and screen sizes.

Our application needed to work seamlessly on:

* Mobile devices
* Web browsers
* Linux desktops
* Different screen resolutions and aspect ratios

Several UI components initially appeared correctly on one platform but broke or became difficult to use on others. We encountered issues such as:

* Layout overflows
* Inconsistent component scaling
* Navigation inconsistencies
* Responsive dashboard rendering problems
* Device-specific UI behavior

We addressed these challenges by redesigning critical layouts, implementing responsive design principles, testing across multiple devices, and continuously refining the interface to ensure a smooth experience regardless of platform.

---

## ⚡ Real-Time System Integration

Integrating multiple moving components into a single emergency response workflow was also challenging. The system combines:

* IoT accident detection
* Real-time location tracking
* AI-powered emergency analysis
* Ambulance dispatch workflows
* Hospital coordination

Ensuring that data flowed reliably and efficiently between all these components required careful API design, error handling, and extensive end-to-end testing.

---

## 🎯 Key Takeaway

The biggest lesson from this project was that building individual features is often easier than making an entire ecosystem work reliably in real-world conditions. Solving cloud deployment issues, IoT connectivity challenges, and cross-platform responsiveness helped us transform DeccanAid from a prototype into a scalable emergency response platform.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Managing personal health records is a fundamentally broken experience for the average patient, who must constantly navigate a fragmented mess of physical papers, scattered PDFs across disconnected hospital portals, and cryptic lab results that are nearly impossible to track or interpret over time. This lack of centralized data makes it an administrative nightmare whenever someone needs to seek a second opinion or securely share their longitudinal history with a new specialist. JeevaKosh solves these critical pain pains by introducing an all-in-one, security-first personal health ecosystem that consolidates a patient's entire medical history into an intuitive, user-owned repository structured dynamically by hospitals and customizable report subfolders.

Beyond simple storage, the platform actively breathes life into static documents by utilizing an automated AI OCR pipeline to extract unstructured medical text and transform it into an interactive health dashboard, allowing users to effortlessly visualize long-term trends for critical biomarkers like hemoglobin or blood glucose levels. To ensure healthcare remains highly collaborative yet completely seamless, JeevaKosh aggregates demographics, chronic conditions, active medications, allergies, and past surgeries into a unified, portable patient portfolio designed to bridge the communication gap between patients and clinicians safely. Furthermore, to remove the anxiety and accessibility barriers tied to navigating sudden symptoms, the application features a multilingual, voice-first triage assistant that allows users to verbally describe their concerns in their native tongue, instantly delivering plain-language differential diagnostic insights and clear clinical urgency stratification while keeping sensitive personal history isolated and protected under strict multi-tenant security guardrails.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body: One of the primary technical hurdles we faced was shifting away from traditional database queries to support a robust semantic search architecture, specifically when transforming our standard MongoDB Atlas collection into a functional vector database to power the RAG chatbot ecosystem. Setting up the custom vector index directly inside Atlas required meticulous planning around field schemas and dimensions to ensure our high-dimensional embeddings—generated via the Qwen3-Embedding-8B model—could be stored and queried dynamically via our async FastAPI backend. We ran into consistency issues where the background OCR processing workers would mismatch document IDs during structural extraction, which initially broke our RAG pipeline's retrieval context and delivered irrelevant snippets to the LLM. Furthermore, because medical history data like chronic illnesses, surgical operations, allergies, and lab results are inherently deeply nested, unpredictable, and highly varied across different patients, parsing these unstructured OCR text arrays into clean, deterministic JSON objects for the profile collection proved incredibly difficult.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: JeevaKosh stands as a powerful implementation of Google’s open-weights model ecosystem, seamlessly integrating Gemma and MedGemma to build an advanced, localized medical intelligence pipeline. Instead of relying on generic cloud text parsers, the platform utilizes specialized open models to handle complex clinical documents and diagnostic decision support.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body: Healthcare data is inherently unstructured, multi-modal, and deeply interconnected. JeevaKosh relies on MongoDB Atlas as its foundational data layer to handle everything from secure object storage and flexible medical metadata to real-time vector search embeddings.

description.title: Open Innovation

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Counterfeit medicines kill over 1 million people every year globally. In India alone, the WHO estimates that 25% of medicines sold are substandard or falsified. A rural farmer buying a ₹10 paracetamol has no way to know if it's genuine or a sugar pill with a fake label. Existing solutions are either too expensive (NFC tags), too basic (single-layer batch lookup), or inaccessible to non-English speakers.
SafeDose solves this by giving every consumer the power to verify any medicine in seconds using just their phone camera. Our 6-layer verification engine checks batch existence, cryptographic hash integrity, QR clone detection, geographic diversion, expiry validation, and supply chain completeness to generate a trust score from 0 to 100. No app download needed. No special hardware. Just scan and know.
For the 70% of India that doesn't speak English, SafeDose includes a voice AI assistant powered by Sarvam AI that speaks in 10 Indian languages including Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, and Odia. Users can also report counterfeit medicines through voice in their native language.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Challenges We Ran Into

QR Code Detection from Real-World Photos Our QR scanner worked perfectly with clean, screen-displayed QR codes but consistently failed when users uploaded photos of real medicine packaging. The QR codes in photos were often small within large high-resolution images, had poor lighting, or low contrast. We solved this by implementing multi-scale image processing that attempts detection at multiple zoom levels, along with contrast enhancement and inverted color attempts to handle varied lighting conditions.

Web Speech API Inconsistencies on Mobile The browser's Speech Recognition API behaved very differently across devices. On mobile, interim results were being concatenated with final results, causing words to repeat in the transcript (e.g., "दवाईदवाईदवाई एक्सपायर" instead of "दवाई एक्सपायर"). We fixed this by properly separating isFinal results from interim results and only displaying the combined output. Additionally, the microphone needed time to initialize, causing the first word to be cut off. We resolved this by waiting for the onaudiostart event before prompting the user to speak.

Sarvam AI Model Migration (Bulbul v2 to v3) Mid-development, we upgraded from Sarvam AI's Bulbul v2 to v3 for better voice quality. However, v3 had different API parameters. The pitch and loudness parameters from v2 were no longer supported, the speaker voice names changed, and the default sample rate was different. Our TTS calls silently failed until we read the documentation carefully and updated all parameters. We also had to balance audio quality (higher sample rate) against loading speed for a smooth demo experience.

Cryptographic Hash Synchronization Our verification engine uses SHA-256 hashes to validate medicine authenticity. Every time we re-seeded the database for testing, new hashes were generated. But the fallback QR mapping in our scan page still referenced old hashes from previous seed runs, causing hash validation to fail even for genuine medicines. This taught us the importance of keeping all references in sync whenever seed data changes.

Audio Echo When Switching Languages When a user changed the voice language while the AI was still speaking in the previous language, both audio streams would play simultaneously, creating an echo effect. We solved this by fully destroying the previous Audio object (pause, clear source, force release) before creating a new one, and adding a stale-request guard so responses from old fetch calls are discarded if the language changed during the API round-trip.

Multilingual Voice Accessibility Building voice AI that works in 10 Indian languages was challenging beyond just translation. Each language has different script rendering, different speech patterns, and different TTS pronunciation characteristics. We had to test each language individually and ensure the welcome prompts, issue prompts, and success messages sounded natural when spoken by the TTS engine, not just when read as text.

Figma to Responsive Code Translating our designer's Figma mockup for the hero section into responsive, pixel-perfect code required multiple iterations. The layered pill and bottle assets needed absolute positioning with a unified scale variable so we could adjust the entire composition with a single constant during the live demo. We also had to handle overflow visibility so assets could extend beyond their container without being clipped.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: SafeDose integrates Google's Gemini API in two key areas. First, after every medicine verification scan, Gemini generates a natural language AI analysis that summarizes the verification results in plain English, explaining exactly why a medicine passed or failed each layer and providing a risk assessment that consumers can easily understand. Second, we built a Gemini powered chatbot that lives on every page of the app, allowing users to ask questions about any medicine they are viewing, including its uses, side effects, dosage instructions, and potential drug interactions. The chatbot is context aware, meaning if a user is on the results page after scanning a medicine, it automatically knows which medicine they are asking about and provides relevant answers without the user needing to type the medicine name again.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body: SafeDose uses MongoDB as its primary database to store all medicine records, manufacturer profiles, supply chain events, scan logs, counterfeit reports, and pharmacy trust scores. Each medicine entry contains the batch ID, serial number, cryptographic SHA-256 hash, manufacturing and expiry dates, authorized distribution region, and drug interaction data. When a user scans a QR code, our 6 layer verification engine queries MongoDB to check batch existence, compare hashes, count previous scans for clone detection, validate geographic authorization, and verify the supply chain event trail. We use Mongoose as the ODM layer with indexed queries for fast lookups. MongoDB's flexible document model was ideal for our use case because each medicine can have varying numbers of supply chain events, side effects, and interaction warnings without requiring rigid schema migrations.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body: SafeDose uses Sarvam AI's Bulbul v3 text-to-speech model to make medicine verification accessible to the 70% of India that doesn't speak English. When a user scans a medicine and gets a verification result, our backend calls the Sarvam TTS API to convert the verdict message into natural sounding speech in the user's selected language. We support all 10 Indian languages offered by Sarvam including Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, and Odia. Beyond the scan results page, we also built a voice powered counterfeit reporting system where the AI assistant speaks prompts in the user's native language using Sarvam TTS, asks for the pharmacy name and the issue with the medicine, and submits the report, all through voice with no typing needed. This makes SafeDose usable by semi literate and non English speaking consumers in rural India, which is exactly where counterfeit medicines cause the most harm.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body: SafeDose is a perfect fit for the Open Innovation track because it tackles a critical, unsolved public health problem with a novel technical approach that is freely accessible to everyone. Unlike existing pharmaceutical verification solutions that are locked behind expensive B2B contracts and proprietary hardware, SafeDose is built as an open, consumer first platform that anyone with a smartphone can use for free, in their own language, without downloading an app. Our 6 layer verification engine is an original innovation that combines cryptographic hashing, clone detection through scan frequency analysis, geographic diversion tracking, temporal validation, and supply chain integrity checking into a single scan. No existing solution in the market offers this multi layered approach. The platform also innovates on accessibility by integrating Sarvam AI's Bulbul v3 for voice feedback in 10 Indian languages, making pharmaceutical safety technology available to rural and semi literate populations for the first time. Our architecture is designed to be extensible, with open API endpoints that allow manufacturers, pharmacies, and regulators to plug into the verification ecosystem. SafeDose demonstrates that open innovation can directly save lives by putting the power of medicine verification into the hands of the people who need it most.
