financial_calibration.py — post-processes CFO outputs into market-realistic ranges when the LLM drifts (e.g. absurd student CAC)
Non-evaluable handling — low scores, no roadmap/plan for non-startup inputs (prevents hallucinated “venture plans” for invalid input)
This demonstrates that you understand Gen AI’s weakness (hallucination, format drift, over-agreement) and built systems around the models.

6. Streaming UX (Gen AI as a live experience)
The backend exposes POST /api/evaluate/stream (SSE). The UI updates agent cards as each specialist finishes — users see Gen AI working, not wait for a spinner.

That is important for the track because it shows:

Real-time orchestration
User-facing Gen AI transparency
A demo that feels like six agents working in parallel
7. Gen AI outputs that drive action (beyond text)
Gen AI tracks like projects that generate artifacts, not just opinions:

0–100 score + verdict
Per-agent analysis with recommendations and risks
MVP roadmap (3–10 weeks, complexity-aware)
Implementation plan with Cursor-ready tasks and checkboxes
Templates with agent-specific “ideal startup” reference content
The LLM is not the destination — the deliverables are. That aligns with “Gen AI for real workflows.”

dum-biriyani-f1b8.name: Planet Prompt
dum-biriyani-f1b8.tagline: Where every prompt meets the biosphere.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
AI usage has a real environmental cost — every query consumes electricity (carbon), cooling water, and grid-related land — but that cost is **completely invisible** to the people generating it. Developers see token counts and dollar costs in their API dashboards, but nothing about carbon, water, or land footprint. So there's no feedback loop, no accountability, and no incentive to write leaner prompts.

This is becoming a real business problem too: regulations like CSRD (EU) and emerging SEC climate disclosure rules are pushing companies to report Scope 3 emissions — and AI/cloud usage increasingly falls under that umbrella. Most companies have **no idea what their AI usage actually costs the planet**, let alone a way to break it down per team or per query.

## What People Can Use It For

**Individual developers** get visibility into the hidden cost of their experimentation — every prompt they test, every model they call, translated into concrete units (grams of CO₂, ml of water, cm² of land) instead of abstract token counts.

**The Prompt Advisor** turns "I should probably write a tighter prompt" into an automated, one-click action — paste a prompt, get a leaner rewrite, and see exactly how many tokens (and how much carbon/water/land) you saved, side by side.

**Teams and organizations** (with the org features) get an aggregated view across all members — a leaderboard of who's using the most resources, org-wide totals, and trends over time — without anyone having to manually collect numbers from individual dashboards.

**Sustainability/ESG teams** get auto-generated monthly narrative reports that summarize the org's AI footprint in plain language with an actionable tip — exactly the kind of content that otherwise has to be written by hand for sustainability reports.

## How It Makes Things Easier / Safer

- **Makes the invisible visible** — the same way cost dashboards made cloud spend visible and changed engineering behavior, PlanetPrompt does that for environmental impact.
- **Turns abstract numbers into intuition** — "0.3g of CO₂" means nothing to most people; "equivalent to driving an EV 25 meters" or "X smartphone charges" does.
- **Removes manual reporting work** — instead of someone compiling usage stats for an ESG report once a quarter, the data and narrative are generated automatically.
- **Builds in optimization, not just monitoring** — most footprint trackers just show you a number; the Advisor actively helps you reduce it.
- **De-risks future compliance** — orgs that start tracking this now won't be caught scrambling when AI-related emissions reporting becomes a regulatory requirement.

If it's useful, I can tighten this further or adjust the framing depending on whether this is going into a hackathon submission, a README, or a pitch deck — they each tend to want slightly different emphasis (technical vs. business vs. narrative).

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Building on Next.js 16 with stale assumptions

The project runs on Next.js 16, which has enough breaking changes from earlier versions that a lot of standard conventions don't apply anymore — including the AI tooling we used to scaffold parts of the app, whose training data predates these changes. The most visible example: middleware now lives in `proxy.ts` instead of `middleware.ts`, with a different matcher convention for distinguishing static assets from API routes. We hit a few dead ends where generated code assumed the old conventions and silently didn't run (auth wasn't being enforced on protected routes). The fix was to explicitly point any AI-assisted changes at the actual docs shipped in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` rather than relying on memorized APIs, and to add a project note (`AGENTS.md`) flagging this so it gets re-checked on every change.

## The "optimizer" sometimes made things worse

Early on, the Prompt Advisor's optimization step (heuristic rewriting + Gemini fallback) would occasionally return a prompt that was the *same length or longer* than the original — either because the heuristic regex passes didn't actually trim much, or because the LLM rewrite added explanatory framing instead of compressing. This broke the UI in an ugly way: the "Resource Savings" badge would show a **negative percentage**, which looks like the tool is actively making things worse — exactly the opposite of the product's pitch.

We added a safety net in `/api/optimize`: after generating the optimized version, we compare token counts. If the optimized count isn't strictly lower than the original (or the text is identical), we short-circuit and return an "already optimized" response instead — same code path used when the input was already lean. This turned a confusing negative number into a positive, encouraging message ("Great prompt, already optimized!"), which is both more honest and a better UX.

## Avoiding the irony of an inefficient "efficiency tool"

A sustainability tool that calls a full LLM to rewrite *every* prompt — even ones that are already concise — would be burning extra tokens (and therefore extra carbon/water) just to tell someone their prompt is fine. That felt like it undermined the whole premise.

To solve this, we added a lightweight gatekeeper (`gatekeeper/gatekeeper.ts`) that runs a zero-shot classifier (Hugging Face's `facebook/bart-large-mnli`) against the prompt first, with three labels: "needs no optimization," "needs some optimization," and "needs significant optimization." Only prompts classified as needing real optimization get sent to the heavier Gemini rewrite step — anything already lean returns early without the extra API call. It's a small architectural detail, but it kept the tool's own footprint consistent with what it's trying to encourage.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
****Sarvam AI plays two distinct roles in PlanetPrompt, and both of them sit at the heart of the product's most interactive features.
The first role is prompt optimization, handled in app/api/optimize/route.ts. When a user pastes a prompt into the Prompt Advisor and clicks "Analyze & Optimize," the backend sends that prompt to Sarvam's sarvam-30b model with a very specific system instruction: rewrite the prompt to be leaner and more token-efficient while preserving all the original meaning, and output only the rewritten text with no explanations or conversational fluff. The model's response is then compared against the original — token counts are estimated for both, footprint metrics are calculated using the selected model's carbon, water, and land coefficients, and the savings percentage is computed. This means Sarvam is doing the actual semantic compression work, understanding what a prompt is trying to say and finding a shorter way to say it, which is fundamentally harder than a find-and-replace approach and why the heuristic fallback exists for when the API isn't available.
The second role is running the optimized prompt to show the user a real AI response, handled in app/api/run-prompt/route.ts. After the advisor shows the before-and-after comparison, users can click "Run Optimised" or "Run Unoptimised" to actually execute either version and see the output side by side. Both of these calls go to Sarvam's chat completions endpoint with the sarvam-30b model, and the response gets rendered directly in the advisor panel. This makes the comparison concrete — you're not just told that the optimized prompt is shorter, you can verify that it produces an equivalent answer, which is the real proof that compression didn't sacrifice quality.
What makes this architecture interesting is that Sarvam is being used as both the tool that reduces AI usage and the engine that demonstrates the result of that reduction, which fits neatly into PlanetPrompt's broader message that being environmentally efficient and being technically capable aren't in conflict.

description.title: Sustainable Development
description.body:
## Sustainable Development, Concretely

"Sustainable development" usually means meeting present needs (here, using AI tools productively) without compromising future resources (energy, water, land used by data centers) — and PlanetPrompt operationalizes that at the layer where the decision actually happens: the moment someone is about to send a prompt.

### Aligns with established sustainability frameworks

- **SDG 13 (Climate Action)** — direct carbon accounting for AI workloads, the fastest-growing source of compute-driven emissions.
- **SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)** — encourages "consuming" AI compute more efficiently rather than wastefully, the same logic as reducing food waste or energy waste.
- **SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure)** — pushes toward sustainable infrastructure choices by surfacing *which models/regions* are more resource-intensive, so teams can factor that into architecture decisions.

### Measurement enables behavior change

A core principle of sustainable development is that **what gets measured gets managed**. Right now, AI usage is one of the only major categories of corporate resource consumption with *zero* visibility — teams know their cloud spend down to the cent, but have no equivalent for carbon/water/land from AI. PlanetPrompt closes that gap at the individual-decision level, the same way a smart electricity meter changes household behavior simply by making consumption visible in real time.

### Built to scale from individual to systemic impact

Sustainable development isn't just personal virtue — it's about **systems**. A single developer trimming a prompt saves a negligible amount. But:

- The **org/leaderboard features** turn individual habits into measurable organizational metrics, which is what actually drives policy (e.g., "our team must reduce average tokens-per-query by 10% this quarter").
- The **monthly AI-generated reports** feed directly into ESG/CSRD-style sustainability reporting, which is increasingly *required*, not optional — so the tool helps organizations meet emerging regulatory sustainability obligations rather than just "feel good" about it.

### The tool practices what it preaches

This is the part we're proudest of: most sustainability tools have a footprint problem of their own (dashboards that poll constantly, AI features that call expensive models for trivial tasks). The **gatekeeper classifier** ensures the optimizer itself doesn't burn extra carbon/water optimizing prompts that don't need it — so the tool's own resource consumption stays proportional to the value it delivers. That's a small-scale example of a bigger sustainable-development idea: efficiency has to be designed into the system itself, not bolted on as an afterthought.

### The bigger picture

AI adoption is accelerating faster than the infrastructure to power it sustainably. Tools like PlanetPrompt don't solve the energy problem on their own — but they shift the *incentive structure* so that "use AI efficiently" becomes a visible, trackable, and rewarded behavior, for individuals and for the organizations that will increasingly be held accountable for it.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/06f177561dbe4fefad3d60503c283052/d3d299fb-56d5-4de7-9daa-ede1dcaebbc8.jpeg)

Parallel Earth DAO solves the problem of understanding and testing decentralized governance systems before they affect real communities, economies, or organizations. Today, most DAO and governance platforms only allow voting and treasury management, but they do not help people visualize the long-term societal consequences of those decisions.

Our platform creates a live AI-powered governance simulation where users can experiment with proposals, economic policies, treasury allocation, crisis management, and governance structures inside a dynamic digital civilization. Instead of relying only on charts or spreadsheets, users can actually see how governance decisions impact participation, inequality, infrastructure growth, economic stability, and societal health in real time.

The platform also makes decentralized governance more transparent and accessible through AI-powered policy explanations, blockchain-backed proposal verification, and wallet-based participation using MetaMask. By combining AI, Web3, and procedural simulation, Parallel Earth DAO helps researchers, DAO communities, students, and future digital governments better understand how decentralized societies may evolve and how governance decisions can shape entire ecosystems over time.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges we faced was integrating multiple advanced systems, AI governance agents, procedural 3D rendering, MetaMask/Web3 functionality, and real-time simulation, into a single stable platform. The 3D civilization system was the biggest headache, especially while importing and optimizing large evolving city assets and handling real-time rendering performance. We used Draco Loader compression techniques to optimize heavy 3D models and improve loading efficiency inside the browser.

During deployment, we also encountered hydration mismatches and strict Content Security Policy issues that caused parts of the UI and blockchain integrations to break in production. We solved this by restructuring unstable client-side components, optimizing rendering behavior, and carefully adjusting deployment security policies to support modern Web3 and AI systems safely.

Another challenge was making the governance simulation feel meaningful rather than cosmetic, so we connected proposal outcomes directly to treasury behavior, participation levels, inequality metrics, and even the evolution or collapse of the procedural civilization itself.

description.title: BlockChain & Web3
description.body:
Parallel Earth DAO fits into both Blockchain and Web3 because it models a decentralized governance ecosystem where users interact through wallet-based participation, transparent proposal systems, DAO economics, and blockchain-backed verification instead of centralized control. MetaMask integration and cryptographic proposal anchoring ensure governance actions are verifiable and tamper-proof using Ethereum-compatible Web3 infrastructure.

At the same time, the platform pushes Web3 beyond simple transactions by combining AI governance councils, real-time treasury and participation analytics, and an evolving procedural civilization that visually reacts to governance outcomes — creating a simulation of how future AI-assisted decentralized digital societies could operate.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
ExoCompute bridges the gap between expensive AI demand and wasted consumer supply by eliminating the friction of entry.

By running AI inference models natively inside a standard web browser (using WebGPU and WebAssembly), ExoCompute allows any user to monetize their idle laptop instantly just by opening a web link. It provides developers with a hyper-local, low-cost decentralized inference network, and gives everyday consumers a frictionless path to passive income.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. The SharedArrayBuffer Crash

Hurdle: Multi-threaded WebAssembly (WASM) execution silently failed because modern browsers block SharedArrayBuffer by default to prevent side-channel attacks.

Fix: We configured our Node.js server to globally inject strict cross-origin isolation headers (COOP/COEP), allowing the WebGPU and WASM pipelines to fire up securely.

2. "Thundering Herd" Task Duplication

Hurdle: Because our Orchestrator broadcasts tasks to all nodes simultaneously for speed, multiple laptops were computing the same task, causing wallets to double-count earnings.

Fix: We built a "First-Response-Wins" architecture. The server maps incoming webhooks to unique UUIDs in an active Set. The first node to return the calculation gets paid, and subsequent redundant results are silently dropped.

3. Network Bandwidth Choking

Hurdle: Our 20MB edge AI model kept re-downloading every time a worker browser tab refreshed, which would have killed our local network on the demo floor.

Fix: We explicitly forced env.useBrowserCache = true in Transformers.js. This utilized the browser's native Cache API to store the quantized model locally, dropping subsequent load times to milliseconds with zero network payload.

4. Wiring Pre-Built UI to a Vibe-Coded Backend

Hurdle: Merging our manually crafted static UI screens with the rapidly generated backend engine caused WebSocket routing and asset conflicts.

Fix: We avoided heavy bundlers like Vite or Webpack entirely. By mapping Express to serve the static folder directly and exclusively using vanilla JS ES Modules via CDN, we kept the architecture completely flat and conflict-free.

description.title: Vultr
description.body:
To make ExoCompute a truly viable product, our central orchestration engine required an ultra-reliable, low-latency environment. While the actual AI inference happens on decentralized edge browsers, the backbone routing those tasks must never go down. We deployed our Node.js and Socket.io Master Orchestrator directly onto a Vultr Cloud Compute instance.

Here is exactly how Vultr powered our architecture:

High-Frequency WebSocket Hub: The core of ExoCompute relies on maintaining hundreds of simultaneous WebSocket connections with consumer browsers while instantly broadcasting AI task matrices. Vultr’s high-performance compute environment provided the CPU stability and ultra-low latency network required to handle the "Thundering Herd" of micro-telemetry data without dropping a single node connection.

Production Webhook Gateway: Relying on temporary local tunnels (like ngrok) is a massive point of failure for Twilio WhatsApp webhooks. We utilized our Vultr instance to establish a permanent, secure, and dedicated ingress gateway (via an Nginx reverse proxy). This guaranteed that when a judge sends a WhatsApp prompt, the webhook is ingested, parsed, and distributed by Vultr in milliseconds.

Proximity to the Database: By deploying our Vultr instance strategically, we minimized the network hop latency between our WebSocket orchestrator and our MongoDB Atlas cluster, ensuring that our real-time reputation scoring and routing algorithms could execute flawlessly on the fly.

Vultr provided the exact high-speed, reliable cloud backbone necessary to orchestrate our decentralized mesh network.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body:
MongoDB Atlas serves as the strategic orchestrator and absolute source of truth for ExoCompute’s decentralized peer-to-peer network. While the raw AI inference happens via WebGPU inside the edge browsers, MongoDB is the "brain" responsible for keeping the chaotic mesh network secure, efficient, and reliable.

Here is exactly how we utilized MongoDB's architecture for this track:

Reputation-Based Task Routing: To prevent bad actors and slow machines from bottlenecking the system, we store the historical confidence and reputation scores of every connected consumer PC in MongoDB. We utilize Aggregation Pipelines to instantly query the active node pool, sorting them by latency and reputation, to intelligently route complex AI tasks to the most reliable machines.

Flexible Document Model for Edge Hardware: Our network's hardware is completely unpredictable—ranging from M2 MacBooks to standard Windows desktops. MongoDB’s schema-less document model allows us to seamlessly ingest these highly disparate hardware profiles, connection states, and dynamically changing node capabilities without being locked into rigid SQL constraints.

High-Velocity Telemetry & Payouts: Every time a node finishes a matrix calculation, it fires back telemetry (execution duration, tokens-per-second, and micro-transaction earnings). MongoDB handles these high-throughput write operations flawlessly, allowing us to dynamically adjust a node's reputation score in real-time based on its actual, verifiable performance history.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body:
ExoCompute embodies the spirit of Open Innovation by fundamentally rethinking how global computational infrastructure is sourced, distributed, and monetized. We aren't just solving a specific industry problem; we are proposing a radical new paradigm for decentralized edge computing.

Here is why ExoCompute belongs in the Open Innovation track:

Democratizing AI Infrastructure: We are challenging the monopoly of centralized cloud giants. By creating a peer-to-peer marketplace, we enable indie developers and startups to access hyper-local, low-cost AI inference, while everyday consumers can finally monetize the 70-80% of their laptop's computational power that currently goes to waste.

The "Zero-Friction" Breakthrough: Previous attempts at decentralized compute networks failed to reach the masses because they required complex Docker containers, CLI knowledge, and specialized mining hardware. Our true innovation is our frictionless architecture: by executing complex AI models natively inside a standard web browser using WebGPU and WebAssembly, we reduced the barrier to entry to a single URL click.

Universal Applicability: ExoCompute is an industry-agnostic infrastructure layer. While our MVP demonstrates AI inference triggered seamlessly via WhatsApp, the underlying browser-based mesh network can be adapted to process anything from medical image rendering to climate data parsing.

By turning any consumer device with a web browser into a secure, sandboxed inference node, ExoCompute represents an open-ended, scalable shift in the future of global computing.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
Here is exactly how ExoCompute pushes the boundaries of the AI/ML track:

Decentralized Edge Inference: We shifted the heavy lifting of machine learning away from expensive, centralized GPU data centers directly to the edge. By crowdsourcing idle consumer laptops, we proved that distributed ad-hoc networks can handle low-latency AI inference tasks seamlessly.

Web-Native ML Execution: We successfully engineered a pipeline that downloads, caches, and executes quantized machine learning models (such as DistilBERT) natively inside standard web browsers. By leveraging Transformers.js and the WebGPU API, our worker nodes execute complex tensor math using their local graphics hardware, requiring zero external server compute.

Democratizing AI Deployment: Currently, deploying ML features at scale requires massive venture funding just to cover AWS or Azure compute costs. ExoCompute slashes the cost of AI inference by up to 50% by tapping into the 70% of consumer hardware that sits idle daily. We lower the financial barrier to entry, allowing indie developers to integrate AI seamlessly.

Privacy-First Pipeline Potential: Because the ML inference happens completely within an isolated browser sandbox on the edge, ExoCompute lays the groundwork for highly secure, privacy-preserving AI applications where sensitive data never has to be transmitted to a centralized server for processing.

ExoCompute isn't just an AI application; it is the decentralized engine that will power the next generation of affordable, scalable machine learning.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Electric vehicle batteries are often retired even though they still retain a significant amount of usable capacity. Today, there is no simple and reliable way to determine whether a battery is suitable for a second-life application, what it should be used for, or how to connect available batteries with real-world energy needs.

VoltLife solves this by using battery health data and AI-driven analysis to assess retired batteries, estimate their remaining useful life, assign a deployment grade, and recommend the most suitable second-life applications. Instead of sending batteries directly to recycling or disposal, organizations can make informed decisions about reuse, extending battery life and reducing waste.

The platform helps battery owners, energy developers, businesses, and communities identify the right battery for the right application, making second-life battery deployment more accessible, efficient, and practical.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/924c9648cd3049108c80d8f7174337fa/7a769d9c-f7d3-43a7-884f-f6a75e4549c3.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/924c9648cd3049108c80d8f7174337fa/3a25de6b-a6e0-47a5-b03e-36a91b060892.png)

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges we faced was bridging the gap between battery health assessment and real-world deployment decisions. While battery metrics such as State of Health (SOH), Remaining Useful Life (RUL), and battery chemistry can be calculated, translating those values into practical second-life recommendations required extensive research into battery reuse applications and deployment criteria.

Another challenge was designing a platform that remained simple for users while integrating multiple components, including AI-powered analysis, battery grading, recommendation systems, and inventory discovery. We spent significant time refining the workflow to ensure that users could move seamlessly from battery assessment to deployment recommendations without needing deep technical knowledge.

We also encountered challenges with backend deployment, database connectivity, and integrating different services within a limited hackathon timeline. These issues were addressed through iterative testing, architecture simplification, and focusing on delivering a reliable end-to-end solution that demonstrates the core value of intelligent second-life battery deployment.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
VoltLife leverages Google's Gemini through a custom Volt AI layer to make second-life battery deployment more accessible and intelligent. Instead of requiring users to understand complex battery specifications, Volt AI allows them to describe their energy needs in natural language, such as backup power, community energy storage, or renewable energy applications.

Gemini helps interpret user requirements, extract key deployment parameters, and generate structured recommendations that can be matched with suitable battery assets. This enables a more intuitive user experience, bridging the gap between technical battery data and real-world deployment decisions.

By combining battery health assessment data with Gemini-powered requirement analysis, VoltLife helps users identify the right second-life battery solutions faster and with greater confidence.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/924c9648cd3049108c80d8f7174337fa/6eb5adf0-887d-4df5-8688-646f994190b6.png)

description.title: Sustainable Development
description.body:
VoltLife supports sustainable development by helping retired EV batteries find a productive second life instead of being prematurely discarded. Many EV batteries still retain **70–80% of their original capacity** when they are removed from vehicles, making them suitable for energy storage and backup power applications.

The project aligns with **SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy)** by enabling access to more affordable energy storage solutions. 

It also supports **SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)** by promoting the reuse of battery resources through a circular economy approach rather than a linear use-and-dispose model.

Additionally, VoltLife contributes to **SDG 13 (Climate Action)** by extending battery lifecycles and reducing the need for new battery production, which helps lower resource consumption and environmental impact.

By combining AI-powered battery assessment with intelligent deployment recommendations, VoltLife transforms retired batteries into valuable energy assets, creating both economic and environmental benefits.

flowstate-2e0b.name: FlowState
flowstate-2e0b.tagline: FlowState — catching the moment a mind wanders, fr

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Ever read a whole page and realized you absorbed nothing? Your eyes kept moving, but your brain had checked out. This "zoning out" happens constantly while studying, in online classes, and on long drives — and the problem is you almost never notice it in the moment. There's no outside signal of what's happening inside your head, so the lapse just silently costs you: wasted study hours, missed lecture content, or — behind the wheel — your life.

FlowState fixes the "you don't know you've drifted" problem. It reads your brain activity from a forehead EEG sensor, turns it into a live focus score, and alerts you the instant your attention drops — so you can catch the lapse and refocus while it's happening, not after.

What people can use it for:

Studying & self-learning — get nudged the moment you start reading without comprehending, and see exactly when you focused or faded during a session.
Online classes — give students and instructors real visibility into engagement, which webcams can't capture (you can stare blankly at a screen and look perfectly "present").
Late-night & long-haul driving 🚗 — drowsy, zoned-out driving is a leading cause of fatal crashes, and drivers rarely realize they're drifting until it's too late. The same detection that nudges a student could wake a drifting driver and save a life.
Any high-stakes focus job — pilots, machinery operators, security/monitoring roles, surgeons in long procedures — anywhere one lapse in attention is dangerous.
Focus & ADHD training — biofeedback that helps people learn to recognize and rebuild their own attention.
Why it's different: most attention trackers use a webcam and only see your gaze — easily fooled by a blank stare. FlowState measures a physiological signal of engagement directly, which is much harder to fake. We're honest that it's a relative, personalized proxy, not a medical device — but it makes an invisible mental state visible in real time, which is the thing no one else does.

Studying is just the use case we built and demo today. The core capability — detecting the exact moment a human brain stops paying attention — generalizes to almost any task where staying focused matters. From there, the only limit is imagination.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Pulling a real brain signal out of a wall of noise. A single dry electrode on the forehead picks up way more 50 Hz powerline hum than actual microvolt-level EEG — raw, the brain signal is basically buried. I built a cleanup chain: a 50 Hz notch filter plus its 100 Hz harmonic, then a 1–40 Hz bandpass, all using zero-phase filtfilt so the wave peaks don't shift in time. We wrote a separate analyze_csv.py tool that prints band power before vs. after filtering — it confirmed the 50 Hz peak drops by orders of magnitude and real theta/alpha/beta survive underneath.

2. A random crash under load: OpenBLAS error: Memory allocation still failed after 10 retries. This one was brutal because it was intermittent. The cause: NumPy/SciPy's BLAS backend allocates a memory pool per thread, and we were calling it from two threads at once (the Flask server + a background compute loop), exhausting the pool. The fix was non-obvious — pin BLAS/OpenMP to a single thread by setting OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 (and OMP/MKL) before NumPy is ever imported. Our FFT windows are tiny, so single-threaded costs us nothing, and the crash disappeared.

3. Real-time updates without freezing the dashboard. Reading the sensor, filtering, running FFTs, and scoring 20 times a second can easily block the web server. We split it into background threads (one reads the data source, one runs the analysis loop) and push results to the browser over Server-Sent Events, downsampling the waveform for display so the stream stays light. The UI now updates smoothly at 20 Hz while the heavy math runs out of the way.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: FlowState uses Google Gemini (gemini-2.5-flash) as an AI Focus Coach. After each session we feed Gemini the real EEG-derived stats (avg focus, zone-outs, focus trend, band mix) inside a grounded system prompt that forbids inventing numbers, then let the user chat with it for personalized, actionable advice on why they lost focus and how to improve. Gemini is what turns raw brainwave data into coaching a human can act on — with a graceful offline fallback so the demo never breaks.

description.title: IoT and Embedded System
description.body: FlowState is a wearable brain-computer interface: a BioAmp EXG Pill sensor + Arduino UNO R4 that samples forehead EEG on A0 at a precise 500 Hz (jitter-free micros() timing, 14-bit ADC) and streams it live over serial. It's a classic embedded IoT architecture — a constrained MCU doing rock-solid real-time biosignal acquisition at the edge, feeding a host that filters, analyzes, and reacts. A real physical-sensor-to-decision pipeline, not a simulation.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Every year, thousands of Indian students relocate to new cities for college and choose PGs or hostels based on fake reviews, broker promises, and misleading listings. There is no reliable, verified system to assess accommodation safety. Students end up facing food poisoning, water contamination, security threats, poor sanitation, and structural hazards — with no way to warn others.
SafeStay fixes this by letting only verified college students report real safety issues. Every report is verified by 3 AI models before it affects any score. A dynamic SafeStay Safety Index (SSI) is computed per accommodation and displayed on an interactive map — giving students honest, AI-verified safety intelligence before they commit to a place.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Our biggest challenge was building a reliable AI verification pipeline under time pressure. We initially used 2 models (Mistral + Groq) but one would occasionally fail under free-tier rate limits, killing the entire pipeline. We switched to Promise.allSettled with a 2-of-3 consensus system across Mistral Pixtral 12B, Groq Llama 3.3 70B, and Gemini Flash — so even if one model fails, the verdict still goes through.
The second challenge was team environment setup. MongoDB Atlas was only connecting successfully on one team member's machine — others were getting connection refused errors due to IP whitelist restrictions on the Atlas cluster. We fixed this by whitelisting 0.0.0.0/0 for development and sharing a single Atlas URI across the team.
Cloudinary API keys were also causing silent failures — image uploads were returning 401s without clear error messages. We traced it to mismatched environment variable names across team members' .env files and standardised them with a shared .env.example.
Permission issues on shared routes and middleware were blocking team members from testing their own features — admin and owner middleware was rejecting valid tokens due to role field mismatches in the JWT payload. We fixed this by aligning the token signing payload across all auth routes and documenting the exact shape expected by each middleware.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: Gemini Flash is the third model in our AI verification pipeline. It runs in parallel with Mistral and Groq via Promise.allSettled. A 2-of-3 consensus is required for a VERIFIED verdict. Gemini acts as the tiebreaker when Mistral and Groq disagree, making the pipeline more robust and reducing false positives.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body: MongoDB Atlas stores all users, reports, accommodations, OTPs, and verification results. The SSI computation uses aggregation pipelines across reports with time decay, severity weights, and resolution status. The CounterReport schema enables owner dispute tracking. TTL indexes auto-expire OTPs. GeoJSON location data powers the map markers endpoint.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body: Sarvam AI powers real-time translation for safety report summaries and SSI explanations into Telugu and Hindi, making the platform accessible to students who are more comfortable in their regional language. The language toggle is persistent across sessions.

description.title: Sustainable Development
description.body: SafeStay creates measurable social impact by giving India's 35+ million college students access to community-verified, AI-moderated safety data about their accommodation options. The platform incentivises owners to fix issues through a public trust score, creating a feedback loop that improves living conditions over time. It is built to scale beyond student housing to any rental market in India. This directly addresses SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities), SDG 3 (Good Health and Wellbeing) and SDG 9 Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure: SafeStay introduces a novel multi-model AI verification pipeline (Mistral Pixtral 12B + Groq Llama 3.3 70B + Gemini Flash).

gurukul-7f73.name: GURUKUL
gurukul-7f73.tagline: New Age of Education Begins Here

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
**The Problem**
Modern classrooms are failing to keep students engaged:

- Visualisation gap — Subjects like chemistry and biology require 3D intuition (molecular structures, cell anatomy, reaction mechanisms), but are taught on flat 2D screens. Smart boards help, but they don't solve the core problem.
- Attention problem — Traditional instruction struggles to hold student attention. Passive learning leads to poor retention.
- No personalisation — Every student learns at the same pace with the same material, regardless of individual strengths or gaps.
- No incentive loop — There is little motivation for students to engage with the material beyond exam pressure.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Adaptive profiling without over-fitting to a single bad session
Averaging raw scores per topic meant one bad round could trash a student's profile. We solved this with Exponential Moving Average (α = 0.25) — recent results influence the profile but don't overwrite it.

2. Topic key drift across Gemini sessions
Gemini generates slightly different topic strings each run ("covalent bonding" vs "covalent bonds"). We added a second Gemini call (resolve_topics) that deduplicates new topics against existing profile keys before merging — scoped by subject to prevent cross-domain false merges (e.g. "chemistry|diffusion" won't collapse into "biology|osmosis").

3. Accessible VR on low-end hardware
High-fidelity VR is expensive. We used A-Frame WebVR — it runs in any modern mobile browser with a cardboard headset. No app install, no dedicated hardware required.

4. Real-time multiplayer avatars in VR
Synchronising player positions and animations across clients required combining Networked-AFrame for scene state and EasyRTC for WebRTC peer connections, with a lightweight Node.js signalling server.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
- We used Gemini API in generating quizzes, profiling students, powering our AI assistants. 
- We also used Gemini CLI in building and exploring the technologies used in the project.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body:
- We used MongoDB in maintaining profiles of individual students to provide key insights in profile section.
- We used MongoDB to store the students performance and also used the records to generate quizzes

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
Gurukul is built around Generative AI and machine learning as first-class citizens, not add-ons:

1. Generative content at runtime — Gemini Flash 2.5 generates a completely fresh set of 10 diagnostic quiz questions on every session, ensuring no two rounds are identical and content always matches the curriculum.
2. ML-driven student modelling — Every answer feeds a per-student, per-topic skill model updated via Exponential Moving Average. This is an online learning algorithm that continuously refines its estimate of a student's mastery without requiring retraining or manual intervention.
3. LLM-powered deduplication — A second Gemini call canonicalises topic labels across sessions, acting as a lightweight semantic matching layer to prevent profile fragmentation — a practical application of LLM reasoning beyond content generation.
4. Conversational AI for doubt resolution — The in-app Gemini chatbot provides context-aware, subject-specific answers in real time, reducing the dependency on a teacher being physically present.

Every AI call serves a concrete educational purpose: generate, assess, deduplicate, or explain. The result is a platform that gets measurably smarter about each student the more they use it.

lifesync-a8ac.name: lifesync
lifesync-a8ac.tagline: every seconds counts. Sync with live donors

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
LifeSync is an AI-powered blood donation platform that connects hospitals with verified donors in seconds — in their own language.
People can use it to:
🏥 Hospitals — post emergency blood requests instantly and get matched with nearest available donors automatically
🩸 Donors — register once and receive voice alerts in their mother tongue when blood is needed nearby
👨‍👩‍👧 Patients — get blood faster because donors respond quicker when alerted in Telugu, Hindi or their native language
What makes it easier and safer:
Existing apps send English text notifications — donors in rural areas miss them. LifeSync sends Sarvam AI powered voice calls in 11 Indian languages — Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Bengali, Marathi, Malayalam, Gujarati, Punjabi, Odia and English.
Result — faster donor response, fewer lives lost, no language barrier.
Built for every Indian — not just English speaking India.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Our biggest challenge was integrating Sarvam AI for multilingual voice alerts under time pressure.
The venue WiFi blocked external APIs completely — Sarvam's DNS couldn't be resolved. We discovered this at 1am with no solution in sight.
We switched to mobile hotspot, but then faced a second issue — the default Sarvam speaker "meera" was not recognized by the API, causing all 11 language generations to fail.
We debugged the error, identified the correct speaker name "vidya", fixed it, and successfully generated voice alert audio files in all 11 Indian languages within 30 minutes.
Third challenge — connecting frontend to Flask backend across different ports caused CORS errors. We resolved this by configuring Flask-CORS to accept requests from both localhost ports.
We also integrated Twilio for real phone calls to donors and successfully received a live call during testing.
The team worked through the night — sleeping only 1.5 hours — to deliver a working product with Sarvam voice alerts, Flask backend, AI donor matching and Twilio integration.
Every obstacle made the final demo stronger.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
LifeSync fits the GenAI track through two core AI integrations:
1. Sarvam AI — Generative Voice Alerts
We use Sarvam's state-of-the-art Indian language text-to-speech model (bulbul:v2) to generate natural sounding voice alerts in 11 Indian languages in real time. Given an emergency message as text input, Sarvam's generative model produces human-like audio output in Telugu, Hindi, Tamil and 8 other languages — making blood donation alerts accessible to every Indian regardless of language.
2. AI Donor Matching
Our matching algorithm uses intelligent filtering — analyzing blood type compatibility and geographic proximity to surface the top 3 nearest matching donors instantly from our database.
Together these GenAI capabilities transform a traditionally manual, English-only process into an automated, multilingual, voice-first emergency response system.
LifeSync demonstrates how Generative AI — specifically Indian language voice generation — can solve real healthcare problems at scale across diverse linguistic communities in India.

oice-440c.name: OICE
oice-440c.tagline: The Missing Layer Between Ideas and Execution.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
The Problem It Solves

Innovation often fails not because of a lack of ideas, but because of a lack of coordination, trust, and incentives. Today, founders, researchers, students, and communities rely on disconnected tools such as GitHub, Notion, Discord, Jira, and spreadsheets to manage contributors and track progress. These tools help organize work, but they do not solve the fundamental challenge of ensuring contributors are rewarded fairly and transparently for their contributions.

For early-stage projects, it is difficult to:

* Attract and coordinate contributors.
* Define clear milestones and ownership.
* Ensure funds are distributed fairly.
* Track who contributed what.
* Build trust between project owners and contributors.

As a result, many promising ideas never progress beyond the planning stage, while contributors often hesitate to participate because compensation and recognition are uncertain.

How OICE Solves This

OICE (Open Innovation Contribution Escrow) creates a trustless innovation coordination layer where projects, contributors, milestones, and funding are managed in a single platform.

Project owners can:

* Create innovation projects.
* Define milestones and contribution bounties.
* Lock funds into blockchain-backed escrow.
* Review and approve submitted work.
* Automatically distribute rewards upon completion.

Contributors can:

* Discover projects aligned with their skills.
* Claim tasks and submit deliverables.
* Build a verifiable contribution history.
* Receive transparent, guaranteed rewards.

Why This Matters

By combining open collaboration with escrow-backed incentives, OICE makes it significantly easier and safer to coordinate innovation across distributed teams. Instead of relying on trust, manual payments, and fragmented tools, participants operate within a transparent system where expectations, contributions, and rewards are clearly defined.

Potential use cases include:

* Startup product development
* Open-source software funding
* Research and academic collaboration
* Hackathons and innovation challenges
* DAO and community-driven initiatives
* Student project coordination
* Public-good and social impact projects

OICE enables anyone to transform an idea into a coordinated, funded, and executable project while ensuring contributors are fairly rewarded for the value they create.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Challenges We Ran Into

1. Designing Fair Contribution Verification

One of the biggest challenges was determining how project owners could verify contributions without making the approval process overly complex. Contributors may submit many different types of work, including research documents, designs, code, and smart contracts. This made it difficult to create a universal validation system.

To address this, we introduced milestone based submissions where deliverables are attached directly to specific project checkpoints. This provides a structured review process while remaining flexible enough to support different contribution types.

2. Escrow and Reward Distribution Logic

Implementing escrow backed rewards introduced several edge cases. We needed to ensure that funds remained secure while still allowing project owners to approve work and distribute rewards efficiently. Managing milestone approvals, partial project completion, and reward allocation required careful smart contract design to prevent funds from becoming locked or distributed incorrectly.

We solved this by separating project management logic from fund custody logic and implementing clear approval workflows before any reward distribution can occur.

3. AI Generated Project Planning

A key feature of OICE is its AI copilot, which helps transform vague ideas into actionable project plans. Early versions frequently generated unrealistic milestones, duplicate tasks, or plans that were too generic to be useful.

We improved results through iterative prompt engineering, structured output schemas, and validation layers that force the AI to produce measurable milestones, realistic timelines, and contributor friendly task breakdowns.

4. Coordinating Complex Project State

Projects can move through multiple stages including creation, funding, milestone approval, contribution submission, review, and reward distribution. Keeping frontend state synchronized with backend data while maintaining a responsive user experience proved challenging.

We addressed this by introducing a clearer state management architecture, strict validation rules, and predictable status transitions throughout the platform.

5. Building a Unified Experience

Many existing collaboration tools solve only part of the problem. Combining project management, contributor coordination, AI planning, and blockchain escrow into a single cohesive experience required significant iteration on both architecture and user experience.

We overcame this by continuously refining the workflow and focusing on a simple principle: every feature should help move an idea one step closer to execution.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
OICE uses Gemini as an intelligent project copilot that transforms vague ideas into structured, executable innovation projects.

When a user submits an idea, Gemini analyzes the concept and generates a complete project framework, including milestones, deliverables, timelines, risks, contributor roles, and success criteria. This helps founders and innovators move from an unstructured idea to an actionable roadmap within minutes.

Gemini is also used to:

* Analyze project proposals and identify potential risks and gaps.
* Generate milestone based execution plans.
* Recommend contributor roles and responsibilities.
* Evaluate contribution submissions against project objectives.
* Provide contextual guidance throughout the project lifecycle.
* Help project owners coordinate complex innovation efforts with less manual planning.

Without Gemini, project owners would need to manually define project structures, milestones, and contribution requirements. By embedding Gemini directly into the workflow, OICE significantly reduces planning overhead and enables users to launch and manage collaborative innovation projects faster and more effectively.

Gemini serves as the intelligence layer of OICE, helping transform ideas into organized, fundable, and executable projects.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body:
MongoDB serves as the primary data layer powering OICE's innovation ecosystem. The platform manages highly connected and rapidly evolving data, including projects, milestones, contributors, submissions, reward pools, escrow transactions, AI generated plans, and project activity.

Using MongoDB enables OICE to efficiently store and query complex project structures while maintaining the flexibility needed for projects at different stages of development. As ideas evolve into active collaborations, project requirements, milestones, contributor roles, and submissions can change dynamically without requiring rigid database schemas.

MongoDB is used to:

* Store projects, milestones, and contribution workflows.
* Manage contributor profiles and contribution histories.
* Track submission reviews and approval states.
* Persist AI generated project plans and analyses.
* Maintain project activity feeds and collaboration records.
* Support real time updates across the platform.

The flexibility and scalability of MongoDB make it well suited for an open innovation platform where every project may have unique structures, workflows, and collaboration patterns. MongoDB enables OICE to provide a seamless experience while supporting the complex relationships between ideas, contributors, funding, and execution.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body:
How OICE Fits the Open Innovation Track

OICE is built specifically to enable open innovation by making it easier for people around the world to collaborate on ideas, contribute meaningful work, and be rewarded transparently for their contributions.

Traditional innovation efforts are often limited by organizational boundaries, fragmented tools, unclear ownership, and a lack of trust between project creators and contributors. OICE addresses these challenges by providing a platform where anyone can launch an idea, define milestones, attract contributors, and fund development through escrow backed reward pools.

Contributors can discover projects, submit work, build a verifiable contribution history, and receive rewards when their contributions are approved. Project owners can coordinate distributed teams, manage milestones, and ensure accountability throughout the project lifecycle.

By combining AI powered project planning, collaborative execution, and transparent reward distribution, OICE lowers the barriers to innovation and enables communities, startups, researchers, students, and builders to work together on solving real world problems.

At its core, OICE transforms innovation from a closed organizational process into an open, global, and incentive aligned ecosystem where great ideas can attract talent, funding, and execution regardless of who creates them.

description.title: BlockChain & Web3
description.body:
OICE (Open Innovation Contribution Escrow) uses blockchain to solve one of the biggest challenges in collaborative innovation: trust.

Projects can create innovation bounties, define milestones, and lock reward funds in an on-chain escrow. Contributors submit work, project owners review deliverables, and approved contributions automatically trigger transparent reward distribution through smart contracts.

By moving contribution tracking, approvals, and payments onto the blockchain, OICE provides:

Transparent and auditable contribution history
Trustless escrow for bounty and milestone payments
Verifiable ownership and attribution of work
Reduced disputes through immutable records
Global participation without relying on centralized intermediaries

The platform combines AI-assisted project planning with decentralized coordination, enabling innovators, builders, designers, and researchers to collaborate and get rewarded fairly for their contributions.

OICE demonstrates a practical Web3 use case where blockchain is not just a payment layer but the foundation for transparent innovation management and contributor incentive alignment.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Applying for government documents in India often involves several common roadblocks for everyday citizens:

- Information Fragmentation: Guidelines, document requirements, and fee structures are scattered across multiple outdated portals.
- Complex Guidelines: Official rulebooks contain legal jargon that is difficult to interpret.
- Unexpected Rejections: Scans are often rejected due to minor mistakes (e.g. upload resolution, expiration states, or wrong document type), resulting in lost appointments and processing delays.
- Vague Timelines: Estimated durations listed on government portals do not reflect real-world waiting times at local centers.

CivicPilot solves this by bringing all instructions into a unified, digital notebook. It uses Google Gemini AI to analyze questions and check documents, and stores user progress and citizen feedback securely on MongoDB. This ensures that you always know what to prepare, where to apply, and what to expect.

CivicPilot is an intelligent, user-friendly digital handbook and checklist planner designed to help citizens understand and complete complex Indian government application processes. Getting documents like passports, driving licenses, or business permits in India can be confusing due to multiple departments, hidden fees, specific document rules, and long wait times. CivicPilot simplifies this by converting complex bureaucratic processes into clear, step-by-step roadmaps, auditing your documents using AI, tracking expiration dates, and hosting a community forum for real-time tips and compliance Q&As.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1.Offline Syncing Conflicts
Hurdle: Merging offline progress (localStorage) with cloud database records without overwriting newer data.
Resolution: Developed a client-side union merge algorithm that combines local and remote completed checklist steps, pushed to MongoDB using a debounced 1-second delay.

2. PII (Personal Data) Storage Risk
Hurdle: Uploaded government documents (Aadhaar/PAN) could leak if stored permanently on the server.
Resolution: Configured an Express controller to read uploads into a temporary buffer, send them to Gemini, and trigger an immediate file deletion (fs.unlinkSync) inside a finally block.

3. Analytics Performance Bottleneck
Hurdle: Slow response times when fetching and sorting document expiration dates in JavaScript.
Resolution: Moved calculations to a MongoDB Aggregation Pipeline using $unwind, $cond, and date casting, reducing API payload sizes and response times by 90%.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body: SkillSeekho addresses a critical gap in India's informal skill economy. Millions of skilled individuals possess valuable expertise but remain undiscoverable due to literacy barriers, lack of digital access, and absence of trust mechanisms. By combining voice-first onboarding, hyperlocal discovery, community verification, and seamless payments, SkillSeekho enables skilled professionals to earn from their expertise while helping learners find trusted local mentors and trainers.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body: One of the biggest challenges was implementing accurate voice-based onboarding. Since SkillSeekho is designed for users who may not be comfortable with typing, we had to ensure that speech-to-text conversion worked reliably across different accents and speaking styles. Another challenge was structuring unorganized voice input into meaningful profile information such as skill category, experience, and service description. We addressed this by integrating AI-powered transcription and processing pipelines that convert natural speech into structured, user-friendly listings.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body: Sarvam AI enables voice-first accessibility by converting speech into text in real time. This allows skilled professionals who may not be literate to onboard themselves using voice commands, while users searching for local skilled workers can also interact with the platform through speech instead of typing. The technology makes the platform inclusive, accessible, and easy to use for India's large non-English-speaking and digitally underserved population.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body: SkillSeekho aligns with the Open Innovation track by addressing a fundamental gap in India's informal skill economy. Millions of skilled individuals possess valuable expertise but lack digital visibility, trust mechanisms, and accessible ways to connect with potential learners or customers. By creating a voice-native, community-verified platform that enables discovery, booking, and payments, SkillSeekho brings traditionally offline talent into the digital economy. The solution combines AI, hyperlocal networking, trust-based verification, and accessibility to empower underserved communities, making it a scalable innovation with social and economic impact across multiple sectors.

courtsaarthi-6e72.name: CourtSaarthi
courtsaarthi-6e72.tagline: Legal AI you can actually trust.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
India's solo practitioners and small law firms deal with massive amounts of paperwork every day, but most legal AI tools are designed for large firms. They are expensive, English-focused, and often produce answers without showing where the information came from. In legal work, even a single incorrect fact can damage a case, making many AI tools difficult to trust.

**CourtSaarthi** is built specifically for lawyers and focuses on one thing above all else: trust.

1. Lawyers can upload FIRs, complaints, court orders, charge sheets, agreements, and other legal documents. The system quickly extracts key facts, parties, dates, legal sections, witnesses, and important events, while showing exactly where the information came from in the original document. Every extracted fact is linked back to its source so lawyers can verify it instantly.
 
2. The platform also assists with drafting legal notices, bail applications, replies, affidavits, and other legal documents. Instead of inventing information, it uses only the facts available in the uploaded case file and leaves important legal decisions and missing details for the lawyer to review and complete.
 
3. CourtSaarthi automatically organizes case information into a structured workspace. Case summaries, timelines, documents, parties, hearing dates, and important deadlines are generated and stored only after the lawyer confirms them.
 
4. To improve communication with clients, the platform can generate case updates in simple language and convert them into audio in the client's preferred language, including Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, and other Indian languages.
 
5. By helping lawyers read documents faster, organize cases efficiently, draft documents with confidence, and communicate clearly with clients, CourtSaarthi reduces repetitive work while ensuring that every AI-generated output remains transparent, verifiable, and trustworthy.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of our biggest challenges was making citations truly trustworthy. Since CourtSaarthi relies on source-backed facts, we found that LLMs often paraphrase text while presenting it as a quote. To solve this, we built a "propose and verify" workflow where the AI suggests a quote and our Python layer confirms that it actually exists in the source document before displaying it. We also implemented whitespace-tolerant matching to handle formatting differences and OCR inconsistencies.

Another challenge was the drafting module. Early drafts were incomplete because the drafter was using a short summary instead of the full document text. Once we connected it to the complete extracted case content, the generated drafts became far more detailed and accurate.

We also encountered issues with Sarvam AI's text-to-speech integration. The API was returning errors due to an outdated voice configuration and incorrect request format. Updating the configuration and payload structure resolved the issue, enabling multilingual voice updates for clients.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
Sarvam AI plays a key role in making CourtSaarthi accessible and multilingual.

**1. Document Digitization (OCR)**
Lawyers often upload scanned FIRs, complaints, court orders, and other legal documents. Sarvam's document intelligence extracts the text from these files so our analysis pipeline can process them. For clean digital PDFs, we use a pdfplumber fallback, while Sarvam handles more complex scanned and image-based documents.

**2. Translation**
Once a case update is generated, Sarvam translates it into the client's preferred language, such as Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, and other Indian languages. This helps lawyers communicate case updates more effectively to clients.

**3. Text-to-Speech**
Sarvam converts the translated update into spoken audio, allowing clients to receive voice-based case updates in their own language.

**Why Sarvam Matters**

CourtSaarthi is designed for Indian lawyers and clients who communicate in many different regional languages. While most legal AI tools are English-focused, Sarvam's support for Indian languages enables us to bridge that gap. By combining document understanding, translation, and speech generation, CourtSaarthi makes legal information more accessible and easier for clients to understand.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
- OCR / document digitization — Sarvam AI extracts text from uploaded scanned legal documents.
- Document analysis & extraction — Llama 3.3 70B (via Groq) reads the digitized text and extracts key facts, parties, dates, and applicable sections, each tied to a source quote.
- Section mapping — Llama 3.3 70B (via Groq) infers applicable offences from the facts of the case, separate from sections explicitly named in the document.
- Document drafting — Llama 3.3 70B (via Groq) generates court-ready documents (bail applications, legal notices, replies, affidavits) from the case's facts, in proper legal format.
- Translation — Sarvam AI translates client updates into Indian languages (Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, and more).
- Text-to-speech — Sarvam AI generates spoken client updates in the client's own language.

lock-shield-fb63.name: Lock Shield
lock-shield-fb63.tagline: Detect. Defend. Protect. Before break-In Happens

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
**DESCRIPTION**
LockShield is an AI-powered smart security system designed to detect, defend, and protect before a break-in occurs.

Unlike traditional CCTV systems that only record incidents after they happen, LockShield proactively identifies suspicious activity through vibration pattern analysis and responds based on the detected threat level.

The system continuously monitors door disturbances using a vibration sensor connected to an ESP32 microcontroller. When abnormal vibration patterns are detected, an ESP32-CAM captures real-time images of the area as visual evidence.

The captured images are securely processed and analyzed using Google Gemini AI, which generates contextual insights about the situation. Based on the vibration intensity and AI analysis, the system classifies the event into different threat levels and immediately notifies the owner through Telegram alerts containing the threat level, captured evidence, and AI-generated assessment.

For low-level threats, LockShield provides early warnings and situational awareness. For high-risk intrusion attempts, the system automatically activates protective measures including door locking, buzzer alerts, and high-priority emergency notifications, helping prevent unauthorized access before a break-in can occur.

**HOW LOCKSHIELD WORKS**
Vibration patterns near the door are continuously monitored.
Suspicious disturbances are classified into multiple threat levels.
ESP32-CAM captures real-time images as evidence.
Images are analyzed using Google Gemini AI.
The system generates a threat assessment based on sensor data and AI insights.
Telegram alerts are sent to the owner with evidence and risk level.
For high-risk threats, the system automatically:
Locks the door
Activates a buzzer
Sends emergency notifications

**KEY FEATURES**
• Multi-Level Threat Detection using vibration pattern analysis
• ESP32 & ESP32-CAM Based Architecture
• Real-Time Image Capture and evidence collection
• AI-Powered Scene Analysis using Google Gemini
• Instant Telegram Alerts with threat assessment and evidence
• Automatic Door Locking during high-risk intrusion attempts
• Audible Alarm Activation for intrusion deterrence
• Low-Cost, Scalable, and Smart-Home Ready Design

**IMPACT**
LockShield transforms passive surveillance into proactive protection by detecting threats early, analyzing risks using AI, collecting evidence in real time, and taking immediate defensive action before unauthorized entry occurs.

**WHY LOCKSHIELD?**
Most security systems react after a break-in. LockShield acts before one happens.
By combining IoT, Computer Vision, Artificial Intelligence, and Real-Time Threat Response, LockShield provides an intelligent security solution that not only monitors intrusions but actively works to prevent them.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
**Challenges I Ran Into**
**1. ESP32-CAM Integration**

Integrating the ESP32-CAM with the main ESP32 controller was challenging due to communication and image transfer issues. Initially, image capture and transmission were inconsistent.

Solution:
We optimized the communication flow between the ESP32 and ESP32-CAM, verified pin configurations, and tested image transmission step-by-step until reliable image capture and transfer were achieved.

**2. Gemini API Integration**

Connecting the project with Gemini AI required proper API configuration and secure handling of API keys. During development, we encountered issues with API setup and response handling.

Solution:
We validated API requests, corrected authentication issues, and implemented proper backend integration using Python and Flask to ensure successful image analysis and response generation.

**3. ESP32 Overheating and Stability**

During continuous testing, the ESP32 experienced overheating and occasional instability due to prolonged operation and repeated communication requests.

Solution:
We optimized the execution flow, reduced unnecessary processing, introduced controlled delays where required, and improved power management to maintain stable operation throughout testing.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
LockShield leverages **Google Gemini AI** to transform captured images into actionable security insights.

When suspicious activity is detected, images captured by the ESP32-CAM are analyzed using Gemini AI to understand the scene, assess the threat level, and generate contextual descriptions. These AI-powered insights are then included in real-time Telegram alerts sent to the user.

By combining **computer vision, multimodal AI analysis, and IoT-based security**, Gemini enables LockShield to provide intelligent threat assessment rather than just raw image notifications.

description.title: IoT and Embedded System
description.body:
LockShield fits into the **IoT and Embedded Systems** track by combining **ESP32**, **ESP32-CAM**, vibration sensors, and real-time communication to create an intelligent security solution.

The system uses embedded hardware to detect suspicious door disturbances, capture evidence, classify threat levels, and trigger automated responses such as door locking and buzzer alerts. It further integrates **Gemini AI** and **Telegram notifications** to provide real-time threat assessment and remote monitoring.

By combining **embedded systems, IoT connectivity, AI-powered analysis, and automated protection**, LockShield demonstrates a practical and scalable smart security solution.
