description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Modern voice assistants (such as Google Assistant or Siri) are designed primarily for monolingual English users. For bilingual users—particularly in regions like India—conversations naturally blend languages into Hinglish (mixed Hindi and English). Standard assistants frequently misinterpret these commands, fail to handle regional pronunciations, or mangle text dictation during translations.

Furthermore, traditional assistants are heavily cloud-reliant, streaming voice logs to remote servers (compromising privacy) and are restricted only to applications that expose official APIs or shortcuts.

Jago solves these problems by providing a production-grade, bilingual AI voice assistant for Android with the following features:

Hinglish-Native Translation & Command Matching: Incorporates a custom semantic and fuzzy parsing pipeline. It uses token-level Levenshtein distance matching to correct STT transcriptions and translates bilingual inputs natively.
Smart Message Protection Heuristics: When you dictate a message (e.g., "Rishabh ko WhatsApp karo aur bolo mai aa raha hu"), Jago translates the command intent to locate the contact and open WhatsApp, but isolates and preserves the Hindi message body verbatim instead of converting it to English.
Privacy-First Offline Wake Word: Runs a three-stage on-device ONNX Runtime pipeline (melspectrogram.onnx 
→
→ embedding_model.onnx 
→
→ jaag_ruut.onnx) inside an Android Foreground Service. It features silence energy-gating and rolling buffers to detect "Jaagrut" entirely offline, consuming zero cloud APIs and protecting user privacy.
Multimodal UI Automation (Visual Agent): Uses Android's Accessibility Service APIs to control third-party apps like WhatsApp and Spotify. It clicks, taps, scrolls, and types automatically, making it possible to control apps that don't have public APIs, serving as a powerful utility for hands-free operations or users with motor/visual impairments.
Automated Research Syncing: Links mobile voice commands to backend orchestration tools (like n8n), letting users automatically schedule, download, and review PDF research summaries natively.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Android's Lack of JNDI for MongoDB Atlas Connection
Standard Java MongoDB drivers rely on JNDI (javax.naming.directory.InitialDirContext) to resolve mongodb+srv:// URIs. However, the Android SDK does not support JNDI, resulting in an immediate NoClassDefFoundError crash upon connection.

How we solved it: We built a custom DNS resolver from scratch using Google’s secure DNS-over-HTTPS JSON API. Jago queries SRV records to find replica set host ports and TXT records for connection parameters, dynamically compiling them into a standard mongodb:// URI at runtime to connect natively.
2. Layout Shifts & Flaky Click Nodes in Accessibility Automation
Modern Android apps often use custom views or load dynamic content (e.g., promotional banners, account switchers), causing standard Accessibility node clicks to fail or target the wrong elements.

How we solved it: We implemented a two-tier click resolver. If the standard accessibility action click fails, Jago retrieves the physical bounds of the element on screen and dispatches an absolute coordinate tap gesture. We also created application-specific heuristics (e.g., for WhatsApp, filtering out QR codes and account-switching buttons to ensure it only clicks the user's name/profile card).
3. Message Body Distortion in Language Translators
Translating Hinglish to English via machine translation typically translates the entire query, which ruins the body of messaging commands (e.g., converting a message to a relative into broken English instead of keeping it in Hindi).

How we solved it: We developed a translation pre-processor that detects messaging triggers, splits the string into command routing ("Send message") and message body, translates only the command structure, and leaves the actual text payload intact.

description.title: Best Hack Built using n8n
description.body:
Jago isn't just a voice assistant; it acts as a mobile trigger and receiver for automated backend workflows orchestrated by n8n.

Voice-Triggered Workflows: The JagrutExecutionEngine parses specific command intents and dispatches webhook requests (TRIGGER_N8N_WORKFLOW) to your n8n cloud server (https://lazydracko.app.n8n.cloud). This bridges mobile speech and complex API workflows.
Daily Research Syncing: The research reporting module utilizes n8n to schedule, crawl, and compile daily research on topics defined by the user. n8n fetches the data, compiles it, and broadcasts it back to the app via ResearchReceiver as Base64 PDFs, showing a complete closed-loop integration of mobile clients with n8n automation.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
Gemini acts as the "orchestration brain" of Jago, transforming raw, unstructured voice commands into precise system instructions:

The Multimodal Intent Compiler (JagrutExecutionEngine): Whenever a voice command misses the local fuzzy match cache, it is passed to Gemini 3.5 Flash. Gemini compiles the raw natural language (or Hinglish) into a structured JSON execution schema.
Dynamic Action Dispatching: Gemini analyzes the request and maps it to one of four low-level system actions:
NATIVE_INTENT: Opening specific Android settings, launching system apps, or dialing contacts.
REFLECTIVE_CALL: Dynamically executing whitelisted Java reflection calls on Android system services (like adjusting volume or toggling DND).
SHELL_COMMAND: Safely running terminal commands within the application's secure sandbox.
AUTOMATION_SEQUENCE: Triggering multi-step Accessibility macros (e.g. driving Spotify search or WhatsApp profile changes).
Conversational Fallback: If the query is conversational rather than action-oriented, Gemini generates natural, context-aware responses.

description.title: ElevenLabs
description.body:
ElevenLabs elevates Jago's user experience from a basic utility to a premium, lifelike product:

High-Fidelity English Speech: For English voice outputs, Jago leverages ElevenLabs TTS (using the Rachel voice profile) to generate incredibly natural, highly expressive, and human-like voice responses, completely bypassing the robotic default Android System TTS.
Smart Hybrid TTS Routing (JagoTTS): Jago implements a resilient, multi-tiered voice adapter. If the device goes offline or the network latency is high, Jago dynamically falls back to ElevenLabs' native English profiles, then to Sarvam's English (en-IN) voices, and finally to the local Android system voice. This ensures that premium voice synthesis is used whenever possible, without compromising app responsiveness.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body:
Jago utilizes MongoDB Atlas not just as a standard document store, but as a central sync hub and a semantic vector search database for voice macros:

DNS-over-HTTPS connection workaround: The official Java MongoDB driver relies on JNDI (javax.naming.directory.InitialDirContext) to resolve mongodb+srv:// connection strings. Since the Android SDK does not support JNDI, attempting to connect to MongoDB Atlas directly causes an immediate crash (NoClassDefFoundError). Jago solves this by integrating a custom DNS resolver that queries Google's secure DNS-over-HTTPS API. It fetches SRV records (for host and ports) and TXT records (for replicaSet details) and dynamically reconstructs a standard mongodb:// URI at runtime, enabling seamless native connections to MongoDB Atlas directly from the Android app.

Macro Database Syncing: Android Accessibility macros (which let the voice assistant perform multi-step visual UI sequences on third-party apps) are saved to MongoDB Atlas. This allows macros recorded on one device to be instantly synchronized and shared across a network of devices.

MongoDB Atlas Vector Search: Jago employs Atlas Vector Search (using the $vectorSearch aggregation pipeline) to match voice commands to saved accessibility macros. When a user speaks a command, the app generates a vector embedding and queries MongoDB. Using a cosine similarity threshold of 
≥
0.82
≥0.82, it retrieves the most semantically similar macro, meaning the user can trigger a macro using different natural language variations instead of memorizing exact macro names.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
Jago is a showcase of building AI tailored for India, leveraging Sarvam AI’s suite to solve the "Hinglish" and regional language barrier:

Bilingual Speech-to-Text (STT): Uses the SarvamSTTAdapter to upload audio multipart streams, enabling highly accurate transcription of Hinglish (Hindi + English mixed) queries that standard Google STT fails to parse.
Indic-Language Chat Fallback: Employs the sarvam-30b model as the primary bilingual conversational fallback, ensuring natural, culturally contextual conversations.
Hybrid Text-to-Speech (TTS): Uses Sarvam's localized Hindi TTS voices (like "meera") to read output back to the user, providing a warm, native-sounding assistant.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body:
The Open Innovation track is looking for projects that break boundaries, solve real-world problems creatively, and exhibit high engineering depth. Jago fits this theme by merging Accessibility, Bilingual NLP, Edge AI, and Cloud Automation into a unified mobile agent:

Democratizing App Automation Without Public APIs: Historically, automating mobile applications has required developers to expose official APIs or shortcuts. Jago utilizes Android's Accessibility Service in a novel way to interact with any third-party app (like Spotify and WhatsApp) exactly like a human user would (by traversing layouts, executing fallback gesture taps, and recording customizable visual macros). This enables automation across the entire Android ecosystem, regardless of whether developer APIs exist.

Breaking the Language & Accessibility Barrier for Hinglish Users: Standard voice assistants are built with an English-first bias, leaving millions of bilingual users struggle to control their devices. Jago’s custom translation pipeline with message protection heuristics ensures that Hinglish commands are routed correctly while preserving Hindi dictation verbatim. This makes natural voice control accessible to non-native English speakers, elderly users, or individuals with motor and visual impairments.

Privacy-First Hybrid Edge Architecture: By running a multi-stage ONNX Runtime pipeline on-device for wake word detection, Jago ensures that the microphone stream is processed locally, keeping the user's data completely private. Only when a command is verified does the app call cloud endpoints (like Gemini or Sarvam) for parsing, creating a highly optimized, battery-efficient, and secure architecture.

Unlocking Desktop/Enterprise Cloud Capabilities on Mobile: By bypassing Android's lack of JNDI support using a custom DNS-over-HTTPS SRV/TXT resolver, Jago bridges MongoDB Atlas and Vector Search directly with Android. This shows how complex, vector-embedded cloud infrastructure can be bridged with lightweight mobile clients, opening up new possibilities for mobile AI application development.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
The problem CoWorkX solves
Short version (for submission): Running AI agents today means paying for expensive cloud GPUs and sending your data to Google, OpenAI, or AWS — while millions of capable personal GPUs sit idle. CoWorkX flips this: it lets anyone rent out their idle GPU as an AI worker node, runs the AI locally on that hardware (no cloud, no data leaving the machine), and lets users get real tasks done autonomously — cheaper, private, and decentralized.

Detailed version:

Today there are three painful gaps:

AI compute is centralized and expensive. To run AI agents at scale you rent cloud GPUs from a handful of providers. It's costly, and you're locked into their pricing and availability — meanwhile countless gaming laptops and personal machines with capable GPUs sit idle most of the day.

Privacy is sacrificed by default. Using cloud AI means your prompts, screenshots, and task data are sent to a third-party model provider. For sensitive or personal tasks, that's a non-starter.

AI agents aren't accessible to everyone. Setting up an autonomous browser agent is technical, English-centric, and tied to paid API keys most people don't have.

CoWorkX addresses all three:

Idle GPUs become a marketplace. Anyone runs a one-click worker node and earns credits when their machine completes tasks — turning dead hardware into a productive, peer-to-peer compute network (DePIN).
The AI runs locally on the worker's GPU via Ollama/LLaVA — no cloud inference, no internet needed for the model, and no task data ever leaves the host machine. Privacy by architecture.
Anyone can use it, in their own language. Voice input in Telugu/Hindi/English (Sarvam AI) means a user just speaks a task; the autonomous agent does the rest and even narrates its progress back.
Trust without a middleman. A token economy + cryptographic proof-of-execution settle payment between requester and host and prove the work was actually done.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Containerized AI agent couldn't reach the host services. The browser agent runs inside Docker, but it needs to call the local AI (Ollama) and the coordinator. localhost inside a container points to the container itself. We fixed this by routing through host.docker.internal and binding Ollama to 0.0.0.0:11434 so the container could reach the host GPU service.

2. The live "stream" showed the wrong thing. Our agent runs headless inside Docker, so there was no visible window for FFmpeg to capture — the stream showed the host desktop instead of the agent. We re-architected it so the agent posts its own per-step screenshots to the coordinator, which relays them to the browser canvas — so users see the agent's actual pages, synced with the step log.

3. Small local models couldn't follow the agent loop. Cloud models were rate-limited (and the goal was local AI anyway), but tiny vision models like moondream looped forever and never finished tasks. We added an anti-loop safety net: when the model repeats an action, the agent reads the page itself and completes the task with a real answer — guaranteeing every run finishes while still proving GPU inference.

4. Making it truly decentralized across two laptops. Getting a second machine to join over the network meant solving stale machine registrations, a daemon that got stuck "busy" and stopped polling, broken copied virtual environments, a Docker SDK incompatibility with newer requests, and Windows cp1252 crashes on emoji logs. We fixed each: dedup/most-recent machine selection, a finally block to always free the daemon, fresh per-machine venvs, pinning requests<2.32, and forcing UTF-8 subprocess output.

5. Real-time updates without page refresh. Tasks run on a remote machine but must appear live on the user's screen. We used Socket.io rooms so each task's steps, status, and screenshots stream to the right browser in real time.

6. Voice for a multilingual audience. Hyderabad users mix Telugu, Hindi, and English. We integrated Sarvam AI's codemix speech-to-text for task input and Hindi text-to-speech for step narration, with fail-silent fallbacks so the demo never crashes if the API hiccups.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body:
It's a genuinely novel combination. Most projects pick one lane — an AI agent, or a Web3 app, or a voice tool. CoWorkX fuses several: a vision AI agent loop + a peer-to-peer GPU marketplace + local privacy-preserving inference + proof-of-execution + Telugu/Hindi voice. That cross-domain originality is the heart of Open Innovation.

It tackles a real, open-ended problem creatively. Instead of accepting that AI compute must come from expensive centralized clouds, it asks "what if the millions of idle personal GPUs were the cloud?" — and builds a working answer. Open Innovation is about fresh approaches to problems no single track defines, and this reframes the entire economics of AI compute.

It's inclusive and accessible by design. Voice input in regional Indian languages means people who can't type English commands can still command an AI workforce. Open Innovation values impact for real, diverse users — not just developers.

It's a platform, not a single feature. CoWorkX is extensible: today browser automation and code-fixing, tomorrow any task type, any model, any machine. It opens a new category rather than improving an existing one — which is precisely what "open innovation" means.

One line for the form:

CoWorkX fits Open Innovation because it's an original, cross-disciplinary platform — merging decentralized GPU sharing, autonomous local AI agents, a token economy, and multilingual voice — to rethink how AI work is done, owned, and paid for, rather than iterating on any existing product category.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
India has 25L+ registered EVs (growing 49% YoY) but only ~29,000 public chargers — a ratio of 1 charger per 215 EVs nationally (1:400 in Hyderabad). At current deployment rates, India will miss its charging infrastructure targets by 87% (6.1 lakh stations short).

The real issue isn't just the count — it's placement. Most chargers sit at standalone highway hubs, forcing EV owners to make a separate trip and wait ~45 minutes just to charge.

How ChargeHive Solves It

ChargeHive installs smart AC/DC chargers at places people already park — malls, offices, hotels — turning parking time into charging time.

Arrive at a destination you were already visiting
Scan QR → UPI Autopay → session starts in under 30 seconds
Return to a fully charged car — zero extra trip, zero extra time
It's a two-sided platform: EV owners get effortless, certified-safe charging (BIS/CEA hardware, OCPP 2.0 security, IK10 enclosures, 4-hour SLA) at 71–77% lower cost than petrol, while venues (malls, hotels, offices) earn new recurring revenue from idle parking space — with ChargeHive absorbing 50% of CAPEX. It also directly supports India's clean energy and sustainability goals (UN SDG 7, 11, 13).

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
### The problem it solves

Digital fraud often starts with something small: a message, a link, a UPI ID, a call, or a screenshot that looks real enough to trust. Most people do not have a quick way to check it before they reply, pay, or share personal information.

**Sanket gives people a simple safety step before taking action.**

Users can send suspicious messages, links, phone numbers, UPI IDs, screenshots, or voice notes on WhatsApp and get a clear risk check with practical next steps. It helps them understand whether something looks like a scam, what warning signs were found, and what they should do next.

It can be used to:

* Check suspicious payment requests, job offers, delivery/KYC messages, refund claims, and investment promises.
* Verify links, UPI IDs, phone numbers, and screenshots before trusting them.
* Get help in Indian languages through text or voice.
* Understand what to do after a scam, including reporting and recovery steps.
* Build community memory so repeated scam identifiers can be flagged faster for others.

Sanket makes scam checking easier by bringing fraud detection, explanation, and recovery guidance into the place where many scams already happen: WhatsApp.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
### Challenges I ran into

One of the biggest challenges was making Sanket reliable in messy real-world situations, not just clean demo inputs. Scam reports can come as screenshots, forwarded WhatsApp messages, voice notes, broken links, UPI IDs, phone numbers, or code-mixed Indian languages. The same scam can also look different depending on who reports it.

A major hurdle was **extracting scam identifiers accurately**. Early versions depended too much on the model output, which sometimes missed UPI IDs, mixed up phone numbers, or treated official helplines as suspicious. I fixed this by adding deterministic cleanup after the AI step: regex-based extraction, identifier normalization, masking, whitelisting for official contacts, and separate handling for UPI IDs, URLs, phone numbers, Telegram handles, and bank details.

Another challenge was **multilingual voice and text support**. Users do not always write in one language, and many messages are romanized, like Hindi or Malayalam typed in English letters. Voice notes added another layer because audio formats from WhatsApp are not always consistent. I handled this by using Sarvam for speech-to-text, translation, language detection, and text-to-speech, with fallbacks so the bot can still respond even if one service fails.

The **agentic call flow** was one of the hardest parts. Sanket is not only a text bot; it also supports voice interaction through an agentic calling setup. The challenge was making sure the voice agent did not confidently act on a misheard UPI ID, phone number, or link. To solve this, I added a read-back confirmation step: the agent repeats the detected identifier and asks the user to confirm before giving a verdict. I also connected the call flow back into the main fraud-checking system so a voice conversation can still use the same scam memory, risk checks, and recovery guidance as WhatsApp chat.

Webhook reliability was another important issue. WhatsApp requires fast responses, but scam analysis can take time because it may involve media download, OCR/STT, database lookup, web search, VirusTotal, Reddit signals, and final reasoning. I solved this by acknowledging the webhook quickly, then processing the message asynchronously and sending the final result back to the user once the analysis is complete.

I also had to deal with **external service failures and cost control**. The system depends on multiple APIs, and any one of them can be unavailable or rate-limited. I added graceful degradation: if one provider is missing or fails, Sanket falls back to another method, a simpler heuristic, or a safer partial response instead of breaking completely. I also added rate limits around the public demo endpoint to reduce abuse.

Another hurdle was building a useful **community memory** without exposing sensitive data. Sanket needs to remember repeated scam identifiers, but users may send personal information inside screenshots or messages. I handled this by normalizing and masking identifiers for public display, hashing reporters, and separating fraud signals from raw user details. This made the system safer while still allowing repeated scammers to be flagged faster.

The final challenge was keeping the architecture maintainable. The live bot, migration orchestrator, Python workers, fraud memory, and voice system all had overlapping responsibilities. I treated the live WhatsApp bot as the production path and kept the newer orchestrator/worker setup as a migration layer until it can fully match the live features. This helped avoid breaking the working product while still moving toward a cleaner long-term architecture.

description.title: ElevenLabs
description.body:
Sanket uses ElevenLabs to make fraud checking available through natural voice conversations, not only text.

The ElevenLabs agent lets users call and speak to Sanket when typing is difficult, slow, or unsafe in the moment. A user can explain a suspicious call, message, UPI ID, link, or payment request in their own words, and the voice agent guides them through the check.

The key part is safety. The agent does not blindly trust what it hears. When it detects a sensitive identifier like a phone number, UPI ID, or link, it reads it back and asks the user to confirm before running the final scam check. This reduces errors from misheard audio and makes the flow more reliable for real fraud situations.

The voice agent connects back to the same Sanket fraud-intelligence pipeline used on WhatsApp, including scam-memory lookup, risk analysis, and recovery guidance. This makes ElevenLabs a practical access layer for the project: users can verify scams, understand risk, and get next steps through a phone-like conversation.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body:
Sanket uses MongoDB as the main memory and intelligence layer behind the fraud-checking system.

Every report submitted through WhatsApp is stored with normalized scam identifiers such as UPI IDs, phone numbers, links, bank details, Telegram handles, and fraud patterns. MongoDB helps Sanket quickly check whether the same identifier has been reported before, how many people reported it, what type of scam it was linked to, and how confident the system should be.

MongoDB also supports the community memory of the project. Instead of treating every scam report as a new case, Sanket can connect repeated reports and detect recurring fraud campaigns. This makes the system more useful over time as more people use it.

The project also uses MongoDB Atlas Vector Search for similarity matching. Scam messages are converted into embeddings, allowing Sanket to find related scams even when the wording, language, or format is different. This is important because fraudsters often change small details while keeping the same underlying pattern.

Overall, MongoDB is used for storing reports, managing scammer intelligence, tracking conversations, supporting fast lookups, and powering the fraud-memory system that makes Sanket improve with real-world usage.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
Sanket fits the **Sarvam.ai** track because Sarvam is used to make the fraud-checking experience truly accessible for Indian users across language, speech, and text.

Many scam victims do not describe fraud in clean English. They may send a WhatsApp voice note, a screenshot, a forwarded message, or a code-mixed sentence like Hindi, Malayalam, Tamil, or Kannada written in English letters. Sarvam helps Sanket handle this naturally.

The project uses Sarvam for **speech-to-text**, **speech translation**, **text translation**, **language identification**, and **text-to-speech**. When a user sends a voice note, Sanket can transcribe it, detect the language, translate it for scam analysis, and then reply back in the user’s language. This makes the system useful for people who are more comfortable speaking than typing.

Sarvam also helps Sanket support Indian-language scam reports instead of forcing users into English. This is important because many real scams happen through regional-language calls, WhatsApp messages, delivery alerts, KYC warnings, job offers, loan traps, and UPI payment requests.

By combining Sarvam’s language and voice capabilities with Sanket’s fraud-intelligence pipeline, the project makes scam checking easier, faster, and more inclusive for real users in India. It allows people to report and understand suspicious messages, links, UPI IDs, phone numbers, screenshots, and voice notes in the language they actually use.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
Sanket fits the **Gen AI & ML** track because it uses AI as the core decision layer, not just as a chat interface.

The system analyzes suspicious WhatsApp messages, screenshots, links, UPI IDs, phone numbers, and voice notes to identify scam risk and explain why something may be unsafe. It combines LLM-based reasoning with deterministic entity extraction, multilingual speech-to-text, translation, text-to-speech, web intelligence, VirusTotal checks, and fraud-memory search.

A key part of the project is its AI-powered scam memory. Reports are converted into embeddings so Sanket can find similar scam patterns even when the wording, language, or format is different. This helps detect repeated fraud campaigns instead of treating every report as isolated.

The project also includes an agentic call flow, where users can speak to the assistant. The voice agent can understand the user, extract suspicious identifiers, confirm them through read-back, and then run the same fraud-checking pipeline used by the WhatsApp bot. This makes scam checking accessible to people who may not be comfortable typing or reading long responses.

Overall, Sanket uses Gen AI and ML to make fraud detection faster, multilingual, explainable, and practical for real-world users.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
When production breaks at 2 AM, an outage, a payment system double charging, a security breach, or a botched release, the hard part usually isn't the technical fix. **It's the conversation.** Talking a stressed VP off a ledge, calming an angry customer, running an incident bridge, and giving a clear status update *while the clock is running* is a skill, and almost nobody gets to practice it before it counts.

Teams drill the *mechanics* of incidents (runbooks, postmortems, on call rotations), but they rehearse the *communication* for the first time live, in front of the people who matter most. A runbook doesn't prepare you for a CTO asking "how long until it's fixed?" when you don't know yet. That gap is where incidents spiral: panic, vague answers, lost trust, and bad escalation calls.

**Redline is a flight simulator for crisis communication.** It drops you into a realistic, high pressure incident and an AI plays the other side of the call, an angry customer, a confused stakeholder, or an outage commander pushing for timelines. You respond **out loud, by voice, in real time**. The AI escalates when you fumble and calms down when you handle it well, so you feel the actual pressure of the moment instead of reading about it.

## What you can use it for

- **Onboarding and training**: Get new engineers and support staff reps handling incidents *before* a real SEV 1, in a space where mistakes are free.
- **Realistic, repeatable practice**: 25+ authored scenarios across production outages, payment failures, security breaches, broken releases, latency spikes, and support escalations, each at three difficulty tiers (warmup → production like → redline). The same incident plays completely differently as the pressure ramps up.
- **Practice *any* incident**: Describe a scenario in plain English ("Kafka cluster dropping messages during Black Friday") and Redline authors a brand new drill on the spot: the persona, the stakes, the facts they're hiding, the objectives, and the severity model.
- **Objective coaching**: After each drill you get a debrief that scores not just *what* you said but *how* you handled it across five dimensions: clarity, de escalation, information gathering, escalation judgment, and status communication, with concrete rewrite suggestions for your weakest turns.

## Why it makes things safer

Incident response is one of the few high stakes skills people are expected to perform well without ever rehearsing under realistic conditions. Redline turns crisis communication into something you can **practice deliberately, measure, and improve**, so when a real incident hits, the conversation is muscle memory instead of a first attempt. Better communication under pressure means faster resolution, calmer stakeholders, and fewer incidents that get worse because of how they were handled.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
The hardest problem was **latency**. Our pipeline runs mic → Saaras v3 STT → LLM reasoning → scenario state update → Bulbul v3 TTS → playback, and even small delays killed the sense of urgency. The whole point of Redline is that the conversation feels *live*, and a two second pause breaks the pressure instantly. We fixed it by **streaming both STT and TTS over WebSockets** instead of waiting on full request to response cycles. Audio starts transcribing as you speak and the persona starts talking back before the full reply is generated. That's what made the call feel real time instead of laggy.

The second hurdle was making the AI **feel like a real stakeholder under pressure, not a polite chatbot**. Early versions were too helpful, but real incidents involve people who interrupt, demand ETAs, and panic. We solved it with a **structured scenario engine**. Every incident carries hidden facts the persona knows but won't volunteer, escalation triggers, and severity progression rules. So instead of following a script, each persona reacts to *how* you handle them, withholding information when you're vague, escalating when you stall, and calming down when you take control.

We also wanted Redline to **remember how someone performs across sessions**. We wanted to track where they hesitate, escalate late, or go quiet under pressure. We used **PostgreSQL** to store transcript embeddings and behavioral patterns, turning each drill into data that sharpens future coaching, and hosted it on **Vultr**.

But the real challenge underneath all of these was **balancing technical realism with emotional realism**. We weren't just building a simulator. We were building *pressure*. Getting the AI to feel genuinely stressful while still being useful to learn from was the breakthrough that made Redline work.

description.title: Vultr
description.body:
Redline's production stack runs on a Vultr VPS, fronted by nginx, with the full app deployed via Docker Compose and shipped through GitHub Actions CI/CD:

Host — Vultr: production VPS running the full Dockerized stack (FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, Postgres)
Reverse proxy — nginx: routes traffic to the right container and terminates TLS
CI/CD — GitHub Actions: builds and tests on every push, then redeploys the containers to the Vultr box automatically

Redline ships from a single git push GitHub Actions builds and tests the stack, then deploys it via Docker Compose behind nginx on a Vultr VPS, taking the project from commit to live in minutes.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
## The Problem WaterSafe Solves

Millions of people consume contaminated drinking water every day without realizing it because current water testing methods are delayed, expensive, and reactive. In many communities, contamination is only discovered after people start falling sick.

Traditional water monitoring systems mainly operate at municipal or laboratory level:
- Water samples are manually collected and tested
- Results can take **2–3 days**
- Household and community-level monitoring is almost nonexistent
- Sudden pipeline leaks, sewage mixing, or filtration failures often go undetected in real time

This creates a dangerous gap where schools, apartments, hostels, rural communities, and public water systems continue supplying unsafe water before authorities can respond.

---

## What People Can Use WaterSafe For

WaterSafe acts as a **real-time early-warning system for drinking water safety**.

It can be used in:
- Schools & colleges
- Apartment complexes
- Hostels & hospitals
- Rural water systems
- Community water tanks
- Public drinking water infrastructure

The system continuously monitors water quality using multiple sensors and Edge AI anomaly detection.

---

## How WaterSafe Makes Existing Systems Safer & Easier

### ✅ Real-Time Detection
Detects abnormal water conditions within seconds instead of waiting days for lab testing.

### ✅ Continuous Monitoring
Works 24/7 automatically without manual sample collection.

### ✅ Early Warning Alerts
Instantly alerts users through OLED/buzzer/SMS when contamination is suspected.

### ✅ Offline-First Operation
Works even without internet connectivity, making it suitable for rural and underserved areas.

### ✅ Affordable Deployment
Provides low-cost decentralized monitoring compared to expensive industrial systems.

### ✅ Reduced False Alarms
Uses a TinyML Autoencoder + Context Engine to distinguish real contamination from noise, bubbles, or sensor drift.

### ✅ Preventive Safety
Helps stop exposure before contamination spreads to hundreds of people in shared water systems.

---

## Core Impact

WaterSafe transforms water safety from:
> **Reactive testing after illness**
to
> **Proactive real-time monitoring before harm occurs**

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
When requesting concept extraction from the Gemini API, the model would occasionally include conversational preamble (e.g., "Here is your JSON knowledge graph:") or wrap the output in Markdown code blocks (⁠```json ... ```⁠). This completely broke standard ⁠JSON.parse()⁠ methods on the backend, resulting in application crashes and preventing the 3D graph from population

How We Got Over It-
We implemented a multi-layered defensive parsing pipeline inside ⁠/lib/gemini.ts⁠:  
1. System-Level Constraints- We explicitly engineered the prompt to demand ONLY valid JSON with no preamble.  
2. String Sanitization- We implemented a regex cleanup mechanism using ⁠.replace(/^```json/g, "").trim()⁠ to strip away potential Markdown formatting wrappers before parsing.

also 

In the initial builds, the AI was tasked with assigning 3D coordinates for extracted concepts. However, because LLMs lack inherent spatial awareness, Gemini generated clusters of nodes that sat directly on top of each other within a tight coordinate bounds (originally ⁠[-5, 5]⁠). In the frontend, this made the React Three Fiber knowledge universe look like a cluttered, unreadable ball of text.

How We Got Over It:
We moved spatial logic out of the AI's hands and engineered a dynamic mathematical dispersion layer directly inside our backend processing engine. We modified ⁠/lib/gemini.ts⁠ to assign coordinates programmatically by scaling a randomized distribution vector across a much wider ⁠[-8, 8]⁠ coordinate field

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Accessing reliable, timely, and understandable healthcare in a country with over 1.4 billion people and immense linguistic diversity is a massive challenge. Millions face barriers ranging from language constraints and fragmented medical records to delayed emergency responses and lack of actionable health guidance. 
**AROGYA RAKSHAA** solves these critical pain points by providing a unified, AI-driven healthcare ecosystem designed for accessibility and speed at scale.
### 1. Breaking the Language Barrier
Most medical information is available only in English, leaving a vast majority of the population underserved. Arogya Raksha solves this by providing **native support for 8 Indian languages** (including Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, Bengali, etc.), ensuring users can check symptoms, interact with AI doctors, and navigate health services in the language they understand best.
### 2. Fragmented Emergency Response & Crisis Management
During emergencies, every second counts, but fragmented communication often causes fatal delays. 
* Our **Crisis Command Center** and **Ambulance Responder App** provide an end-to-end emergency pipeline. 
* The **Emergency ID & QR Code** system automatically transmits a patient's complete medical profile and vital history to hospitals during SOS situations, ensuring doctors are prepared before the patient even arrives.
### 3. Lack of Immediate Medical Guidance
Instead of relying on inaccurate internet searches, users have access to our **AI Doctor & Symptom Checker**. Powered by Groq and advanced LLMs (Llama 3.3 70B & Vision models), it analyzes symptoms intelligently, reads medical documents/images, and provides preliminary guidance—reducing panic and directing users to appropriate care.
### 4. Difficulty in Finding Resources
Locating nearby facilities or understanding medications can be confusing. The platform aggregates a massive database of over **250,000 medicines** and **200,000 hospitals**. Users can:
* Use the **Medicine Intelligence** module to understand drug details, side effects, and alternatives.
* Use the **Hospital Discovery & Map** features for real-time geolocation of nearby medical facilities.
By combining an intelligent AI agent (MediBot), real-time WebSockets, and a robust data layer, **AROGYA RAKSHAA** democratizes healthcare access, turning a fragmented system into a cohesive, user-centric lifeline.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Building a production-grade healthcare ecosystem with 20+ pages, 17 API routes, and 10+ AI features in just 24 hours was incredibly demanding. Here are the major challenges we overcame:
### 1. Scaling the Data Layer
One of our biggest hurdles was handling massive datasets efficiently. We seeded over **250,000 medicines** and **200,000 hospital records**. Ensuring lightning-fast search and retrieval for the Hospital Discovery and Medicine Intelligence modules required rigorous database optimization in Supabase (PostgreSQL) and implementing Redis caching to prevent API timeouts.
### 2. Ensuring AI Medical Accuracy & Safety
Using LLMs in healthcare is risky due to hallucinations. Integrating Groq (Llama 3.3 70B & Llama 4 Scout Vision) for the **AI Doctor & Symptom Checker** required extensive prompt engineering and context boundary setting. We had to ensure the AI explicitly clarified it was an assistant (not a replacement for doctors) while still providing highly accurate, actionable symptom analysis and clinical pathways.
### 3. Implementing True Multilingual Support
To make the app accessible to 1.4 billion people, we implemented support for **8 Indian regional languages**. Dynamically translating medical terminology accurately without losing the nuance of symptoms, and maintaining UI consistency across varying text lengths, was a significant technical and design challenge.
### 4. Real-time Emergency Infrastructure
The **Crisis Command Center** and **Ambulance Responder App** required rock-solid real-time communication. Implementing Socket.io for live SOS alerts, location tracking via Leaflet maps, and WebRTC for video consultations simultaneously led to complex state management issues on the frontend that we had to meticulously debug.
### 5. Multi-Service Orchestration
Integrating a myriad of third-party services—Clerk (Auth), Supabase (DB), Redis (Caching), Cloudinary (Media), Razorpay (Payments), Firebase (Push Notifications), and Resend (Emails)—into a cohesive flow without bottlenecking the Next.js frontend or Express backend required careful architectural planning and robust error handling.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
### Advanced Integration of Sarvam AI in AROGYA RAKSHAA
To make AROGYA RAKSHAA truly accessible to 1.4 billion people—especially in rural areas with low English literacy—we didn't just stop at a web UI. We deeply integrated **Sarvam AI's advanced Indic language models** to create a seamless, voice-first, multilingual healthcare ecosystem. 
We utilized two primary Sarvam AI models at the core of our application:
#### 1. Context-Aware Medical Translation (Mayura:v1)
Standard translation APIs often fail at complex medical terminology, potentially causing dangerous misunderstandings. We integrated Sarvam's `mayura:v1` model to power our dynamic translation engine. 
* **How we used it:** When our Groq/Llama-based AI Doctor generates complex clinical pathways, symptom analysis, or medicine instructions in English, we pipe that output through the Sarvam Translate API.
* **The Result:** We deliver contextually accurate medical translations in **8 Indian languages** (Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Marathi, Bengali, Bhojpuri, and English), ensuring users read medical advice in their native dialects.
#### 2. Native-Sounding Healthcare Voice Assistant (Bulbul:v1)
To help visually impaired users, elderly patients, or users who prefer listening over reading, we built a Text-to-Speech (TTS) engine using Sarvam's `bulbul:v1` model.
* **How we used it:** We dynamically convert the translated medical text (generated via Mayura) into high-fidelity audio streams. We specifically configured the `meera` speaker profile, optimized the sample rate (22050Hz), and tuned loudness/pace parameters for clear, reassuring medical guidance.
* **The Result:** AROGYA RAKSHAA literally "speaks" to the user. Whether it is reading out SOS crisis instructions or explaining the side effects of a medicine, the Sarvam TTS integration makes our platform highly inclusive and empathetic.
**Summary of Impact:** By chaining Llama 3.3 for reasoning, Sarvam `mayura:v1` for translation, and Sarvam `bulbul:v1` for voice, we built a fully autonomous, voice-enabled, vernacular healthcare assistant that can hold intelligent medical conversations in local Indian languages.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
### How AROGYA RAKSHAA fits the Gen AI & ML Track

AROGYA RAKSHAA is not just a healthcare dashboard; its core value proposition is entirely driven by advanced Generative AI and Machine Learning models. We have deeply integrated Gen AI to transform raw medical data into actionable, accessible, and personalized healthcare intelligence. 

Here is how our project pushes the boundaries of Gen AI & ML:

#### 1. Agentic AI Ecosystem (MediBot)
Instead of a simple RAG chatbot, we built a fully autonomous **Tool-Calling AI Agent (MediBot)** powered by **Llama 3.3 70B** (via Groq). MediBot doesn't just answer questions; it acts on behalf of the user. It can autonomously trigger 8 different internal tools to:
* Search the 250k+ medicine database.
* Book hospital appointments.
* Analyze medical images.
* Provide real-time navigation guidance to the nearest health facilities.

#### 2. Multi-Modal Vision AI for Diagnostics
We integrated **Llama 4 Scout Vision** to give our AI "eyes." Users can upload complex medical documents, prescription slips, or images of physical symptoms. The Vision ML model parses the visual data, extracts the medical context, and translates it into plain language, effectively acting as an instant, preliminary radiologist/pharmacist.

#### 3. AI-Driven Clinical Pathways & Symptom Checking
Our **AI Doctor Symptom Checker** utilizes generative models to conduct dynamic triage. By processing natural language descriptions of user symptoms, the LLM maps them against medical literature to generate probability-based differential diagnoses. It then generates personalized, step-by-step clinical pathways (e.g., "Take this immediate action," "Consult a specialist within 24 hours").

#### 4. Real-Time Multilingual NLP
To serve 1.4 billion people, we utilized Natural Language Processing (NLP) to break language barriers. Generative AI dynamically translates complex medical jargon into highly accurate, localized dialects across **8 Indian languages** (Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, etc.), ensuring AI-driven medical intelligence is not restricted to English speakers.

#### Summary for Judges:
AROGYA RAKSHAA utilizes **Large Language Models for reasoning (Llama 3.3), Vision Models for perception (Llama 4 Scout), and Agentic frameworks for execution**. We moved beyond basic GenAI wrappers to build a deterministic, safe, and robust AI orchestration layer tailored specifically for critical healthcare scenarios.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Drug discovery is broken for small teams.

Running computational screening today requires either a $40,000/year Schrödinger license or weeks of setup with tools like AutoDock that demand deep expertise. A PhD student with a promising molecule idea has no fast, accessible way to know if it's worth pursuing before committing to expensive wet lab experiments.

Molecule Ai solves the access problem.

It takes any molecule, a name, a SMILES string, or a hand-drawn structure, and returns a complete drug viability profile in under 10 seconds. Binding affinity predicted from a model trained on 5,752 real ChEMBL experimental measurements. ADMET safety across absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity. Lipinski oral bioavailability check. Synthesis accessibility score. 3D structure with pharmacophore highlights showing exactly which atoms drive binding.

Before Molecule AI, a researcher with 50 candidate molecules would spend weeks and thousands of dollars running wet lab assays on all of them. Now they filter to the top 5 in minutes, only those go to the lab.

The VS Code extension takes this further: researchers writing screening scripts get inline druggability scores directly in their editor, so they make go/no-go decisions while writing code, not after running it.

description.title: Challenges we ran into

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body: Molecule AI uses machine learning to predict how strongly a molecule will bind to a protein target, trained on real experimental data from ChEMBL so the predictions are grounded in actual lab results. On the generative AI side, a LLaMA 3.3 70B model running on Groq reads the molecular analysis and writes a plain English explanation of why a molecule is likely to succeed or fail as a drug, making the results accessible to researchers who aren't computational chemists. The ML handles the numbers and the LLM handles the interpretation, so the two work together rather than independently.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Problem Statement
Despite significant advancements in artificial intelligence, most robotic systems still rely on rigid programming, predefined motion sequences, and human supervision. These systems can detect objects or perform repetitive actions, but they lack the ability to autonomously reason about their environment and make intelligent decisions before acting.
This limitation creates challenges in industries, laboratories, warehouses, educational environments, and assistive applications where robots must operate safely and adapt to changing conditions.
Our project addresses this gap by introducing an Agentic AI-based robotic manipulation system that bridges perception, decision-making, and physical action. Instead of executing fixed instructions, the system observes its environment, identifies objects, plans actions, validates safety constraints, and performs intelligent manipulation autonomously.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Challenges Faced
Real-Time AI on Embedded Hardware
Running object detection efficiently on Raspberry Pi required balancing accuracy and performance.
Solution: Optimized the vision pipeline and adopted lightweight inference strategies suitable for edge computing.
Coordinating Multiple Autonomous Agents
Maintaining reliable communication between perception, planning, safety, and execution layers was complex.
Solution: Designed standardized communication contracts between agents and implemented a hierarchical control framework.
Safety During Physical Manipulation
Direct execution of generated actions could damage hardware or produce unstable behavior.
Solution: Developed a dedicated Safety Agent that validates every movement before execution and blocks unsafe actions.
Hardware-Software Synchronization
Integrating camera streams, robotic motion, and AI decision-making in real time required extensive testing.
Solution: Built independent modules first and performed staged integration to ensure reliability.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
SportsIQ is an AI-powered platform that helps players learn, coaches train, umpires make better decisions, and organizers manage sports competitions efficiently. 

Our platform helps players improve their skills, assists officials in making fair decisions, provides coaches with performance insights. We are starting with cricket and building a solution that can be expanded to multiple sports in the future.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
. Designing a Unified Sports Platform

The biggest challenge was integrating multiple modules—AI Learning, AI Referee, AI Coach, Match Highlights, and Analytics—into a single platform while maintaining a simple and intuitive user experience.

2. AI-Based Rule Detection

Creating an AI Referee system capable of analyzing video footage and identifying fouls, offsides, no-balls, wides, and other rule violations required studying sport-specific rules and designing a scalable AI workflow.

3. Multi-Sport Scalability

Different sports have different rules, movements, and evaluation criteria. Designing an architecture that can support multiple sports without rebuilding the system from scratch was a significant challenge.

4. Video Processing and Analysis

Sports videos are large and computationally expensive to process. Managing video uploads, frame extraction, event detection, and efficient storage while maintaining acceptable performance was challenging.

5. Real-Time Feedback Generation

The AI Coach feature needed to provide actionable feedback rather than generic suggestions. Designing a system that converts match events into understandable coaching insights was complex.

6. Learning Path Personalization

Building personalized learning recommendations for players of different skill levels required designing flexible content categorization and recommendation mechanisms.

description.title: Gemini
description.body: SportsIQ fits into the Generative AI and Machine Learning track because AI is the core technology powering the platform rather than being an additional feature. The project uses Machine Learning and Computer Vision to analyze sports videos, detect player movements, identify match events, and assist in rule violation detection through the AI Referee system. These models help process visual data and generate objective insights from match footage. Generative AI is integrated using Google's Gemini model, which acts as the intelligence layer of the platform. Gemini analyzes the outputs generated by the ML systems and transforms them into personalized coaching feedback, training recommendations, performance reports, and interactive learning assistance. For example, after a match analysis, Gemini can explain a player's strengths and weaknesses in natural language, suggest specific drills for improvement, answer sports-related questions, and create customized learning paths based on the athlete's skill level. By combining Machine Learning for video understanding and Gemini for human-like reasoning, explanation, and content generation, SportsIQ delivers an intelligent sports ecosystem that provides automated officiating, performance analysis, and personalized coaching, making professional sports guidance accessible to every athlete.

description.title: The problem it solves

It continuously analyzes prompts, URLs, files, and IP addresses to detect potential threats before they reach the AI model. Using AI-driven threat detection, risk scoring, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, and real-time security recommendations, AEGIS AI helps organizations prevent data leakage, block malicious activities, and ensure safe AI adoption.
Impact

One-Line Closing
"AEGIS AI secures AI before AI processes the request." 🛡️🤖

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges we faced during development was integrating multiple APIs and managing API keys securely across the application. During testing, we encountered authentication failures, invalid key errors, and rate-limit issues, which caused disruptions in the threat analysis workflow. Another major hurdle was establishing reliable communication between the frontend and backend, where incorrect endpoint configurations and data handling inconsistencies led to failed requests and delayed responses.

To overcome these issues, we implemented proper environment variable management for API keys, improved error handling and validation mechanisms, and thoroughly tested API integrations using debugging tools. On the backend side, we standardized request/response formats, optimized API routing, and performed extensive end-to-end testing to ensure smooth communication between all components. These improvements significantly increased the stability, security, and reliability of the platform.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body: I use Sarwan AI by submitting a prompt, URL, file, or IP address through the dashboard. The platform automatically analyzes the input for security threats, generates a risk score, maps findings to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, and provides mitigation recommendations. This helps me detect and prevent cyber threats before they reach the AI system.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Data centers waste massive energy on cooling systems that run on fixed schedules, ignoring actual server load or conditions.

Our system fixes this, the RL agent continuously monitors real-time conditions and adjusts cooling dynamically, so you're never over-cooling or under-cooling.

For operators, it removes manual tuning. For sustainability teams, it directly improves PUE and WUE without hardware changes. For engineers, the safety layer ensures automation never puts hardware at risk.

It makes cooling autonomous, efficient, and safe, all at once.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Two datasets, incompatible feature spaces

Air and liquid cooling data had completely different columns — merging them would've broken the model. Built separate model families with a routing layer in the Digital Twin instead of forcing a unified model.
Reward variance was massive

Early training episodes collapsed entirely (reward hit -3.2 = 1-step termination). Diagnosed the instability, tuned early termination conditions, and reshaped the reward function in the Gymnasium environment until training stabilized.
Thermal stability model refused to converge

R²=0.30 even after 600 estimators and heavy tuning. The feature set simply didn't carry enough signal. Acknowledged it as a known limitation — the Safety Filter compensates by enforcing hard thermal bounds regardless.

description.title: Sustainable Development
description.body:
Data centers consume massive amounts of energy and water, yet most cooling systems are still reactive and single-metric. Our project tackles this directly — we built an AI-powered cooling optimization system that uses a Reinforcement Learning agent (SAC) to jointly minimize both PUE and WUE in real time, which is something existing solutions don't do.

By training on a physics-based digital twin, we ensure the system is safe and deployable in actual infrastructure — not just a simulation experiment. The impact is quantifiable: lower energy waste, reduced water consumption, and a smaller carbon footprint per compute unit, at scale.

This is why it fits the sustainable development track — we're not just optimizing a server room, we're building infrastructure that respects resource boundaries.

hybrid-ai-voice-assistant-with-offline-s.name: Hybrid AI Voice Assistant — Works Offline Too

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
The problem it solves
Today's voice assistants — Alexa, Google Home, Siri — only work when the internet works. The moment your Wi-Fi drops (still common across much of India), they can't even switch off a light. They're also expensive (₹4,000+) and send everything you say to the cloud, raising real privacy concerns. And the people who could benefit most — elders, non-English speakers, and homes with weak connectivity — are often the ones left out.
TecnoVoice fixes this. It's a hybrid assistant that stays useful with or without the internet: when connected, it answers questions intelligently in your own language; when offline, it still controls your home appliances instantly and locally.
What people can use it for

🏠 Smart home control — turn lights, fans and appliances on/off by voice, even during an internet outage.
🗣️ Speak in your own language — Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Gujarati and more, including mixed speech, so non-English speakers and elders aren't excluded.
🏥 Hands-free help — useful in hospitals and for people with limited mobility who can't reach switches.
🏫 Learning & everyday Q&A — ask general-knowledge questions; great for students and curious minds.
🌾 Rural & low-connectivity homes — works where cloud-only assistants simply fail.

How it makes things easier and safer

✅ Reliable — core controls never depend on the internet, so there's no single point of failure.
🔐 Private — offline commands never leave your home; the cloud is used only when you choose to ask something.
💸 Affordable — roughly half the cost of commercial assistants (₹1,800–2,200).
♿ Accessible — voice-first design helps elders, the visually impaired, and anyone who finds apps or switches hard to use.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Yeh field hackathon submission ka common part hai — isme bataana hota hai ki banate waqt kya-kya mushkilein aayi. Maine tumhare actual project ke hisaab se honest aur real-sounding likha hai (markdown ke saath). Copy karke paste kar do 👇

Challenges I ran into
Making offline and online work as one system. The hardest part wasn't either mode on its own — it was getting them to hand off cleanly. Building the "decision layer" that senses connectivity and routes each request to the right brain (cloud AI vs. local control) without the user noticing took a lot of trial and error.
Connecting the AI APIs as first-time builders. Most of us hadn't wired up real APIs before, so getting Sarvam and Gemini keys, building a backend to call them, and parsing the responses was a steep learning curve. We also hit CORS restrictions trying to call Sarvam straight from the browser, which pushed us to route those calls through our own server instead.
Multi-language voice recognition. Real people don't speak in clean, single-language sentences — they mix Hindi and English, like "light band karo please." Getting commands recognised reliably across several Indian languages, without misfiring on similar-sounding words, needed a lot of tuning.
Wi-Fi reliability on the ESP32. Since the whole point is to survive bad connectivity, we had to handle drops and reconnections gracefully so the device falls back to offline mode instead of freezing.
Switching 220V appliances safely. Controlling real mains appliances meant being very careful with the relay wiring and isolation. Getting hardware to switch high voltage reliably — and safely — was nerve-wracking the first few times.
Keeping it affordable. Every component was a balance between capability and cost, because the goal was a device far cheaper than commercial assistants without dropping the features that actually matter.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
TecnoVoice is, at its core, an embedded systems and IoT project. The entire system runs on an ESP32 microcontroller that handles real-time audio capture, on-device processing, and network communication. Voice is captured through an I2S MEMS microphone (INMP441) and played back through an I2S amplifier (MAX98357A) and speaker, while a 0.96" OLED shows live device status — all driven by custom firmware written in embedded C/C++.
What makes it a true IoT device is its control over the physical world: the ESP32 drives GPIO pins connected to a relay module that safely switches real 220V appliances like lights and fans on and off. A dedicated offline voice module (Sasi) performs local command recognition, so this physical control works instantly even with no internet — a key reliability feature for embedded deployment in areas with unstable connectivity.
The system is hybrid by design. When connected, the ESP32 streams voice over Wi-Fi to the cloud for AI-powered responses; when offline, it falls back entirely to embedded, on-device control. This blend of microcontroller firmware, sensor and actuator interfacing, relay-based automation, and networked intelligence places TecnoVoice squarely in the IoT and Embedded Systems domain — a low-cost, battery-powered, privacy-friendly smart-home node built from the silicon up.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body: ResQMesh is an offline-first disaster communication and rescue coordination system designed for situations where cellular networks and internet connectivity are unavailable due to natural disasters such as floods, earthquakes, or cyclones. It enables victims to propagate emergency messages through a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) mesh network, allowing requests for help to travel across nearby devices without relying on communication infrastructure. Once any device regains internet access, the collected messages are synchronized to the backend, where Gemini AI automatically classifies and prioritizes incidents based on severity and category. These incidents are then displayed on a Rescue Coordination Dashboard that provides rescue teams with real-time situational awareness through interactive maps, severity-based prioritization, incident tracking, and resolution workflows, helping responders identify and assist the most critical cases faster and more efficiently.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Offline Communication Constraints: Establishing reliable communication without internet connectivity required designing a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) mesh-based approach where messages could propagate across nearby devices.

Message Synchronization: Ensuring that messages generated offline were not lost and could be synchronized correctly once a device regained internet access.

Incident Prioritization: Raw emergency messages vary significantly in format and urgency, making it challenging to automatically identify critical situations and prioritize rescue efforts.

Real-Time Visualization: Integrating classified incidents with an interactive map and maintaining accurate location-based incident tracking.

Database Integration: Transitioning from hardcoded data to persistent MongoDB storage while supporting incident updates and resolution workflows.

Scalability Considerations: Designing a system that works for the prototype stage while remaining extensible to future technologies such as LoRa gateways, drone relays, and cloud deployment

description.title: Gemini
description.body: Disaster triage requires near-instant responses. The gemini-2.5-flash model is Google's most speed-optimized model, processing and classifying incoming emergency distress messages in under a second.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body:
Offline-First Synchronization (Atlas Device Sync)
The core architecture of ResQMesh relies on local gateway servers storing data fully offline and automatically uploading it when internet breakout occurs. MongoDB Atlas provides native, out-of-the-box syncing mechanisms. Records can be flagged as synced: false locally, and MongoDB Atlas handles merging the changes to the cloud repository seamlessly when a connection is established.

2. Flexible Document Schema (BSON / JSON)
Disaster response data is inherently unstructured and variable:

One message might contain specific GPS coordinate floats.
Another might be a text-only distress note.
A third might be a list of required supplies (food, water, blankets). MongoDB’s document-based model allows us to store these varying payloads within a single incidents collection without the strict column limitations of relational SQL databases (PostgreSQL/MySQL).

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body: ResQMesh addresses a real-world societal challenge that spans multiple domains, including disaster management, emergency response, communication systems, artificial intelligence, and public safety. Rather than solving a problem specific to a single industry, it provides a broadly applicable platform that can be adapted for various disaster scenarios and emergency situations. The project combines innovative use of BLE mesh networking, AI-powered incident prioritization, and rescue coordination to create a resilient communication system for environments where traditional infrastructure fails. Its interdisciplinary nature and potential for large-scale social impact make it well-suited for the Open Innovation category.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Here's the submission answer:

The Problem Orion Solves
Every engineering team reviews pull requests for logic, architecture, and bugs. Nobody reviews them for quality.
Not because they don't care — because it's slow, manual, and always someone else's problem. So broken experiences ship to production every day:

🐌 Pages with 4-second load times that kill conversions
♿ Images without alt text that screen readers can't parse
🔗 Broken links that 404 silently
🔍 Missing meta descriptions that tank SEO rankings
🔒 Missing security headers that leave users exposed

You find out three days later. Sometimes three weeks.

What Orion Does
Orion is an autonomous QA platform that integrates directly into your GitHub workflow. The moment a PR is opened, Orion:

Crawls your staging URL using four specialized AI agents — Discovery, Performance, Hygiene, and Scoring
Posts a score (0–100) as a GitHub status check on the PR — blocking merges below your threshold
Drops a full report in the PR comments — every finding, its severity, and a suggested fix
Leaves inline review comments on the exact files that caused the issues

No CI yaml. No configuration files. No new tools to learn. Just install the GitHub App and every PR gets automatically audited.

Who It's For
UserHow They Use OrionFrontend developersCatch performance regressions before mergeSolo foundersGet QA coverage without hiring a QA engineerOpen source maintainersEnforce quality standards on every contributionStartup engineering teamsShip fast without sacrificing quality

What Makes It Different
Most tools are passive — they sit in a separate dashboard, generate reports nobody reads, and tell you about problems that already shipped.
Orion is active — it lives inside the PR, speaks the language developers already use, and catches issues at the only moment that matters: before the merge.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Challenges I Ran Into
1. The Signature Verification Bug That Broke Everything
The single most painful bug was GitHub webhook signature verification silently failing on every request.
The webhook handler was verifying signatures like this:
typescripthmac.update(JSON.stringify(req.body)).digest("hex")
This looks correct but is completely wrong. GitHub signs the raw request bytes — the exact bytes it sent over the wire. But Express was parsing the body into a JavaScript object first, and JSON.stringify() of that object doesn't match the original bytes — key ordering, whitespace, and encoding all differ.
The result: every single webhook returned 401. Silently. No error in GitHub's delivery logs except a failed response.
The fix was to mount the webhook route with express.raw() before the global express.json() middleware, and sign the raw Buffer directly:
typescript// BEFORE (broken)
app.use(express.json()) // parses body globally
app.use("/api/v1/github/webhook", webhookRoutes)

// AFTER (fixed)
app.use("/api/v1/github/webhook", express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), webhookRoutes)
app.use(express.json()) // everything else
The order of middleware in Express matters more than almost anything else — and this one cost hours.

2. ngrok Forwarding to the Wrong App
The monorepo runs multiple apps simultaneously via Turborepo — the Next.js frontend on port 3000 and the Express API on port 4000. ngrok was tunneling to port 4000, but GitHub's webhook responses were returning Next.js HTML pages.
The cause: ngrok on Windows sometimes can't reach 0.0.0.0:4000 via localhost. The fix was explicitly binding to 127.0.0.1:
bash# Broken
ngrok http --domain=xxx.ngrok-free.dev 4000

# Fixed
ngrok http 127.0.0.1:4000 --domain=xxx.ngrok-free.dev
One flag. Two hours lost.

3. Route Path Mismatch — The Silent 404
The GitHub App webhook URL was set to /api/v1/github/webhook. The Express router was mounted at /api/v1/webhooks. Inside that router, the route was router.post("/github", handler).
The actual path the handler was listening on: /api/v1/webhooks/github.

The path GitHub was posting to: /api/v1/github/webhook.
GitHub was getting 404s but still returning 200 to GitHub (Express's default HTML 404 has a 200 status in some proxy configurations), so the delivery logs showed green checkmarks while nothing actually worked.
The fix was aligning the mount path in app.ts with the webhook URL, and changing the router's internal route from /github to /:
typescriptrouter.post("/", handleGithubWebhook) // not "/github"

4. Repo Not Registered — The Silent Skip
Even after the webhook was working perfectly, the Orion QA Agent check never appeared on PRs. The server logs showed:
[webhook] no staging URL for Mohfazam/FOODZY — skipping run
The installation webhook that should have auto-registered the repo fired before the server was correctly set up, so the repo was never saved to the database. With no staging URL in the DB, the handler silently returned 200 and did nothing.
The fix was manually registering the repo via the API with the correct installationId, owner, repo, and stagingUrl — and then redelivering the pull_request webhook from GitHub's delivery logs.

The Pattern
Every single one of these bugs had the same underlying theme: silent failures. No crash, no error, just a 200 response that masked the real problem. The lesson — always log the event name and action at the very top of a webhook handler, before any logic runs, so you can see exactly what's being received.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
How We Used Gemini
Orion uses the Gemini API as the intelligence layer powering its AI agents.
After crawling the target URL, each page's content, structure, and metadata is passed to Gemini for deep analysis. Gemini is responsible for:

Identifying issues — detecting missing alt text, broken links, SEO gaps, security header violations, and performance anti-patterns from the raw page data
Severity classification — determining whether each finding is critical, high, medium, or low based on its real-world impact
Generating fix suggestions — producing human-readable, actionable fix recommendations for each finding that get posted directly into the GitHub PR as inline review comments
Root cause analysis — synthesizing all findings into a single root cause summary that explains the underlying pattern behind the issues

Rather than using hardcoded rules, Gemini lets Orion understand context — it can tell the difference between an image that's decorative and one that genuinely needs alt text, or identify when a performance issue is structural vs incidental.
Every finding you see in the PR comment and on the dashboard — the title, the detail, the suggested fix — is Gemini's output, formatted and delivered automatically into your GitHub workflow.

skillnow-d913.name: SkillNow
skillnow-d913.tagline: Expert Help, Exactly When You Need It

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Modern learners often face challenges while learning new skills, building projects, preparing for interviews, or solving technical problems. Although search engines, tutorials, forums, and AI assistants provide large amounts of information, users frequently struggle to find solutions that fit their specific context.
Many learners spend hours searching across multiple platforms, repeating the same questions, and trying different approaches without success. AI tools can provide guidance, but they may lack the practical experience, domain expertise, and personalized mentorship needed to fully resolve complex or unique situations.
As a result, learners experience frustration, wasted time, slower learning progress, and difficulty finding the right person who can help them move forward.
SkillNow solves this problem by understanding the learner's goals, challenges, context, and previous attempts, then connecting them with the most relevant human expert for personalized assistance and mentorship.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Challenge 1: Extracting meaningful context from webpages
Most webpages contain large amounts of irrelevant information such as navigation menus, advertisements, and repeated content.
Solution:
We built a browser extension that extracts relevant page content and uses AI to identify the user's actual goal, challenge, technologies involved, and required expertise.

Challenge 2: Converting unstructured content into structured tickets
Raw webpage content is difficult to use for expert matching.
Solution:
We integrated Sarvam AI to automatically generate structured support tickets containing problem summaries, root causes, priority levels, and expert requirements.

Challenge 3: Matching Learners with Relevant Experts
Finding the right expert is often more important than finding any expert.
Solution:
We designed a categorization and matching mechanism that uses the extracted context to identify the most suitable experts based on skills and expertise.
