zeuscont-da5d.name: Zeus-Cont
zeuscont-da5d.tagline: Less Weighing Collaborative Malware Analysis Env.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Analyzing a virus or "malware" is usually a slow, dangerous, and complicated process. Zeus-Cont makes
  it fast, safe, and easy for everyone.

  1. It creates a "Digital Cage" for Viruses
   * The Problem: You can’t just open a suspicious file on your laptop to see what it does—it could steal
     your data or break your computer.
   * Our Solution: We provide a safe, isolated container (a "sandbox"). You can run the virus inside this
     cage, and it can’t escape to hurt your actual computer or the internet.

  2. It Translates "Matrix Code" into Plain English
   * The Problem: Malware generates thousands of lines of confusing technical logs. It takes a human
     hours to read through them all.
   * Our Solution: We use Gemini AI to read all that "boring" data for you. In seconds, it writes a
     simple report explaining exactly what the virus was trying to do.

  3. It’s a "GPS" for Security Training
   * The Problem: Most hacking tools are very intimidating and hard to learn.
   * Our Solution: We integrated a Voice Assistant (using Sarvam AI). It actually talks to you and guides
     you through the app, making advanced security research as easy as following a GPS.

  4. No More Working Alone
   * The Problem: Usually, security experts work in silos. If they find something, they have to take
     screenshots and send emails.
   * Our Solution: Our platform is collaborative. Multiple people can jump into the same session to hunt
     a threat together in real-time, just like a shared Google Doc.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Container Orchestration: Making the backend "talk" to Docker to create and destroy isolated sandboxes on demand.
2. Network Isolation: Building a "fake internet" so malware stays trapped but still tries to execute its code.
3. Real-Time Streaming: Pushing file, network, and process events to the browser instantly without any lag.
4. Noise Reduction: Automatically hiding normal system processes so the analyst only sees the malicious activity.
5. AI Data Management: Condensing thousands of raw log lines so Gemini can generate a smart, human-readable report.
6. Forensic Tooling: Packaging heavy-duty security tools (like Radare2 and Volatility) into a lightweight, fast-loading image.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
The Gemini API is the project's "Intelligence Layer." While the sandbox and C agent collect raw data, Gemini acts as the Senior Malware Researcher who interprets that data.

  Its involvement is broken down into three key roles:

  1. Automated Forensic Synthesis
  The most significant involvement is in the Report Generation Engine. When an analyst finishes a session, the backend sends a massive volume of telemetry logs (Process trees, File changes, Network packets) to
  Gemini. 
   * The Task: Gemini parses thousands of lines of raw logs into a structured, professional ANY.RUN-style Malware Analysis Report.
   * The Value: It saves analysts hours of manual work by identifying the "needle in the haystack"—such as distinguishing a normal system file edit from a malicious persistence attempt.

  2. Contextual Intelligence & IOC Extraction
  Gemini is used to identify and categorize Indicators of Compromise (IOCs). It scans the telemetry to extract:
   * Malicious Hashes: Identifying suspicious files dropped during execution.
   * C2 Infrastructure: Spotting Command & Control domains or IP addresses hidden in network traffic.
   * Threat Scoring: Based on the activity patterns, Gemini calculates a "Threat Score" (0-100), helping the analyst prioritize the risk level of the sample.

  3. MITRE ATT&CK Reasoning
  While the system can detect what happened, Gemini explains why it matters. It analyzes the sequences of events to confirm MITRE techniques. For example, if it sees a process modifying ~/.bashrc, Gemini maps
  this to T1546.004 (Persistence via Unix Shell Configuration), providing the technical rationale for why that specific action is a security risk.

  Technical Implementation Details:
   * Models Used: Optimized for gemini-2.0-flash for high-speed analysis and long context windows (to handle large log files).
   * Prompt Engineering: Uses a high-precision system prompt with explicit rules to ensure reports are professional, monochromatic, and free of AI "hallucinations."
   * Determinism: Set to a very low temperature (0.1) to ensure that the same malware activity always results in the same technical conclusion.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
The Sarvam API serves as the "Voice of Zeus," providing the narrative layer for the platform's onboarding and tactical guidance. While the Gemini API handles the "brain" (logic and reporting), Sarvam provides
  the "voice" (audio and communication).

  Its specific involvement includes:

  1. Indic-Specific Tactical Assistance
  The project uses Sarvam’s Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities (specifically the bulbul:v3 model) to provide a localized, natural-sounding audio guide. 
   * The Persona: It powers the "Zeus Tactical Assistant," which speaks to the analyst in high-fidelity Indian dialects/accents.
   * The Goal: This makes the platform more accessible and provides a modern "Mission Control" feel, where the system talks to you while you perform high-stakes analysis.

  2. Interactive Guided Onboarding (Walkthrough)
  The Walkthrough Application is entirely driven by Sarvam. As the user moves through the platform's different zones (Terminal, Telemetry, Intel Column), Sarvam generates real-time audio instructions:
   * It explains complex cybersecurity concepts (like MITRE mapping) through spoken word.
   * It reduces the cognitive load on the analyst, allowing them to keep their eyes on the telemetry feeds while receiving audio cues about the environment.

  3. Real-Time Instruction Proxy
  Technically, the project implements a FastAPI Proxy for Sarvam to ensure security and performance:
   * Security: The API keys are kept on the server side, preventing exposure in the frontend.
   * Speed: It uses Sarvam's low-latency endpoints to ensure that when an analyst clicks "Next" in the walkthrough, the audio response is nearly instantaneous.
   * Hybrid Fallback: The system is designed to check for Sarvam’s availability and fallback to standard Web Speech APIs if the network is disconnected, ensuring the "Assistant" never goes silent.

description.title: CyberSecurity
description.body:
Zeus-Cont is a modular Dynamic Malware Analysis Sandbox designed for high-performance threat research. It maps directly to several critical cybersecurity operations:

   1. Isolated Threat Detonation (Sandboxing): The core of the project is the secure execution of suspicious binaries. By using Docker-based isolation and a custom "Fake Internet" gateway, analysts can observe
      malware behavior in a 100% contained environment, preventing any risk to the host system or external networks.
   2. Advanced Behavioral Telemetry: Unlike static analysis, Zeus-Cont captures real-time system behavior. This includes:
       * Process Tree Visualization: Identifying process hollowing, spawning chains, and stealthy execution patterns.
       * Network Forensics: Monitoring DNS queries and C2 (Command & Control) callbacks to identify malicious infrastructure.
       * File System Auditing: Detecting unauthorized modifications to sensitive system configurations.
   3. Framework Alignment (MITRE ATT&CK): The project integrates a real-time mapping system that translates technical telemetry into standardized tactics (e.g., Discovery, Persistence, Exfiltration). This aligns
      analysis with global industry standards used by SOC (Security Operations Center) teams.
   4. Collaborative Incident Response: By supporting multi-user shared sessions and synchronized terminals, the project facilitates collaborative threat hunting. This mirrors modern "War Room" scenarios where
      multiple researchers must coordinate to dissect a high-priority threat.
   5. AI-Augmented Forensics: Through Gemini AI integration, the platform automates the generation of structured forensic reports. This solves the "Documentation Gap" in cybersecurity, allowing analysts to move
      from detection to mitigation significantly faster.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Aegis solves one of the biggest flaws in modern emergency systems: most safety apps only work when the victim can openly use their phone. In situations like kidnapping, stalking, trafficking, assault, domestic violence, accidents, or disasters, victims often cannot unlock a phone, open an SOS app, or visibly ask for help without increasing danger.

Existing solutions also rely heavily on internet connectivity and usually stop at sending a single alert. They rarely preserve evidence, maintain live tracking, adapt to low battery conditions, or continue trying alternative communication methods when networks fail.

Aegis addresses this by acting as a stealth-first survivability ecosystem disguised as a normal music app. It can be activated covertly through secret phrases, hidden taps, or patterns without revealing any visible SOS activity. Once triggered, it silently captures evidence, tracks movement, assesses threat severity, and continuously attempts to reach help through multiple fallback channels including internet, SMS, mesh networking, LoRa, ultrasonic communication, satellite relay, and offline store-and-forward systems.

By combining stealth, resilience, evidence preservation, multilingual accessibility, and communication redundancy, Aegis increases the chances of rescue even in the most hostile or disconnected environments.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges was building a system that stays completely stealthy while still running critical emergency features in the background. Android aggressively restricts background microphone access, GPS updates, and battery usage, so keeping voice-trigger detection active without making the app look suspicious required careful optimization and permission handling.

Another major hurdle was reliability during poor connectivity. Most emergency systems fail when internet access disappears, so we had to design a fallback communication architecture that could queue distress packets offline, retry automatically, and switch between channels like Firebase and SMS without losing data.

We also faced challenges balancing battery life with live tracking. Continuous GPS and audio recording drained power quickly, especially during long emergencies. To solve this, we implemented an adaptive “Ultra Survival Mode” that reduces update frequency, compresses data, and prioritizes low-cost communication methods when battery levels drop.

Designing the decoy interface was another unique challenge. The app needed to behave convincingly like a real music application while secretly supporting covert triggers and emergency workflows underneath. We solved this by separating the visible UI from the hidden emergency engine running in the background.

Finally, implementing multilingual voice activation across Indian languages introduced speech-recognition accuracy issues due to accents, pronunciation differences, and background noise. We improved reliability by requiring users to train the system with their own spoken trigger phrase during setup instead of relying only on generic recognition models.

description.title: Open Innovation
description.body:
Aegis fits the Open Innovation track because it combines ideas from cybersecurity, emergency response, communication systems, IoT, stealth UX design, and disaster-resilient networking into a single unified safety ecosystem. Instead of solving only one part of the problem, Aegis integrates covert activation, multilingual accessibility, evidence preservation, live tracking, offline recovery, and multi-channel communication redundancy into one platform.

The project also explores innovative fallback communication methods such as mesh networking, LoRa, ultrasonic transmission, DTN, and satellite relay concepts to ensure distress signals can survive even when traditional infrastructure fails. By disguising itself as a normal music app and focusing on survivability in real-world hostile conditions, Aegis rethinks how emergency systems should operate when victims cannot safely ask for help.

Its modular architecture allows future expansion into wearables, official emergency-service integration, and community-based rescue networks, making it a scalable and socially impactful innovation for public safety.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# Echo

## Decision Blind Spot Detector

**Every decision has blind spots. Echo finds them before they become consequences.**

Built for **ZenysLab HackPrix 2026**, Echo helps organizations identify overlooked stakeholders, hidden consequences, and competing interests before implementing policies or major decisions.

---

## The Problem

Many decisions fail because key stakeholders are unintentionally excluded from the process.

Whether it's a government policy, university rule, workplace change, or community initiative, the people most affected are often the least represented.

---

## The Solution

Echo analyzes proposed policies and answers a simple question:

> **Who did we forget?**

It identifies affected stakeholders, detects blind spots, measures fairness, facilitates stakeholder debates, and generates improved policy recommendations.

---

## Features

* **Stakeholder Discovery**
  Identifies affected and overlooked groups.

* **Blind Spot Detection**
  Highlights hidden risks and unintended consequences.

* **Equity Index**
  Scores policy fairness on a scale of 0–100.

* **AI Stakeholder Debate**
  Simulates realistic debates between conflicting stakeholders.

* **Voice-Based Consultation**
  Converts stakeholder perspectives into natural speech.

* **Policy Improvement Draft**
  Generates a more inclusive version of the original policy.

* **Multilingual Input**
  Supports English, Hindi, and Telugu voice submissions.

* **Blockchain Accountability**
  Records analysis results on Solana for transparency.

---

## Tech Stack

### Frontend

* React Native
* Expo
* TypeScript

### Backend

* Node.js
* Express
* MongoDB

### AI & Automation

* Gemini 2.5 Flash
* Sarvam AI
* ElevenLabs
* n8n

### Infrastructure

* Vultr
* Solana Web3.js

---

## How It Works

1. User submits a policy through text or voice.
2. Echo identifies affected stakeholders.
3. Hidden impacts and blind spots are detected.
4. An Equity Index is calculated.
5. Stakeholders debate competing viewpoints.
6. Debate is converted into realistic voice conversations.
7. Echo generates an improved policy draft.
8. Results can be logged on Solana.

---

## Example

**Policy:** All university classes move fully online.

**Echo identifies:**

* Rural students
* Low-income households
* Disabled students
* Faculty members

**Echo generates:**

* Stakeholder Impact Report
* Equity Index
* AI Stakeholder Debate
* Voice Consultation
* Improved Policy Draft

---

## Getting Started

```bash
git clone https://github.com/f4w4z/zenyslab-hackprix-submission.git
cd zenyslab-hackprix-submission

npm install

cd server
npm install
npm run dev

# frontend
npm run web
```

---

## Vision

Echo helps decision makers understand who may be missing from the conversation, enabling more equitable, transparent, and informed decisions before they are implemented.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
MEs often manage finance, inventory, HR, sales, and compliance data across multiple systems, spreadsheets, and documents. This fragmented information makes it difficult to obtain timely insights, automate routine processes, and make informed business decisions.

As a result, organizations face challenges such as:

Limited visibility into financial performance and cash flow
Inefficient inventory and supply chain management
Time-consuming HR operations and employee management
Poor sales forecasting and customer insight generation
Manual compliance tracking and audit preparation
Delayed decision-making due to scattered data

These issues lead to reduced efficiency, increased operational costs, compliance risks, and slower business growth.

Solution: HiveNet

HiveNet is an AI-powered business management platform that addresses these challenges through specialized intelligent agents:

FinBot – Financial analysis, expense tracking, and forecasting
LogBot – Inventory monitoring and supply chain optimization
HRBot – Workforce management and HR process automation
SalesBot – Revenue forecasting and sales intelligence
AuditBot – Compliance monitoring and audit support

By centralizing business data and providing AI-driven insights, HiveNet helps organizations automate operations, improve decision-making, enhance compliance, and drive overall business efficiency.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. Relational Database Design

Designing a unified database structure was challenging because each bot (Finance, HR, Logistics, Sales, and Audit) required different types of data while still needing to share information across modules. Ensuring data consistency, normalization, and efficient relationships between entities required careful schema planning.

2. RAG Pipeline Implementation

Building the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline involved challenges in document ingestion, chunking, embedding generation, vector storage, and retrieval accuracy. Ensuring that responses were based on relevant company documents while minimizing irrelevant context required extensive tuning.

3. Maintaining Common Context Across Bots

Since all bots operate within the same business ecosystem, establishing a shared organizational context was essential. The challenge was enabling each bot to access relevant cross-functional information without creating data duplication or context conflicts.

4. Developing the ISO/Audit Bot

The Audit Bot required interpreting complex ISO standards and compliance documents. Mapping organizational data and uploaded documents against compliance requirements while generating meaningful audit insights and non-conformity detection posed a significant challenge.

5. Cross-Module Integration

Integrating Finance, HR, Logistics, Sales, and Audit functionalities into a single platform while maintaining scalability, performance, and a consistent user experience required careful system architecture and API design.

6. Ensuring Response Accuracy

Providing reliable business insights from both structured database records and unstructured documents was challenging. Considerable effort was spent on improving retrieval quality, prompt engineering, and validation mechanisms to reduce inaccurate responses.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
1. Compliance Document Analysis

Users upload policies, SOPs, audit reports, process documents, or compliance records. Gemini analyzes the content and extracts relevant information related to compliance requirements.

2. ISO Requirement Mapping

AuditBot compares the uploaded organizational documents with ISO clauses and requirements. Gemini identifies whether sufficient evidence exists for each requirement and highlights potential gaps.

Example:

ISO clause requires documented risk management procedures.
Gemini reviews uploaded documents.
AuditBot reports whether evidence is present, partially present, or missing.
3. Gap and Non-Conformity Detection

Gemini analyzes documents to identify:

Missing documentation
Incomplete procedures
Non-conformities
Areas requiring corrective action

This significantly reduces the manual effort normally required during internal audits.

4. Audit Question Answering

Using the RAG pipeline, AuditBot retrieves relevant compliance documents and provides context to Gemini. Gemini then generates accurate responses to audit-related questions.

Example Queries:

"Which ISO 9001 clauses are currently not satisfied?"
"Show evidence for employee training compliance."
"What corrective actions are pending?"
5. Audit Report Generation

Based on the analysis results, Gemini generates:

Compliance summaries
Non-conformity reports
Audit observations
Recommended corrective actions
Technical Flow
User uploads compliance documents.
Documents are processed and stored in the RAG knowledge base.
Relevant sections are retrieved using semantic search.
Retrieved context is sent to Gemini.
Gemini analyzes the evidence against ISO requirements.
AuditBot presents compliance status, gaps, and recommendations.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body: The biggest hurdle was running Firebase Auth alongside Supabase — login lived in Firebase, but profiles, resources, and RLS policies expected Supabase-style UUIDs, so users logged in but data often failed to link. I fixed that with a deterministic UUID mapper (getDeterministicUuid) so every Firebase UID always maps to the same database ID, and I cleared stale Supabase session tokens on app load to stop ghost login states. Messaging was another pain point: without access to auth.users, I couldn’t reliably look users up by email from the client, so I had to work around it via the profiles table and an admin Edge Function for secure user listing. Community discussions needed live updates, so I added Firebase Realtime Database on top of Supabase, which meant managing two backends. Smaller but annoying bugs included password reset URLs arriving in different formats (hash vs query params), PWA install prompts firing too aggressively on SPA routes (fixed with delayed prompts + localStorage dismiss), and landing-page scroll animations breaking on resize until I recalculated layout after the DOM finished painting.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
## The Problem OFFICE-NATOR Solves

---

Meet **Ramesh**. He runs a small textile business in Surat. Every evening he opens Excel to update his inventory — quantities, prices, supplier names. He knows what he wants to do. He just doesn't always know *how* to do it in Excel.

He wants to make the header row bold. He goes to Format → Cells → Font → Bold. Or was it the toolbar? He can't remember. It takes 4 clicks and 30 seconds. He does this every single day.

He wants to freeze the top row so it stays visible while he scrolls. He Googles it. Again. For the third time this month.

**Ramesh is not alone.** He represents hundreds of millions of people across India — shopkeepers, teachers, accountants, government clerks, small business owners — who use Excel daily but never feel fully in control of it.

---

### What OFFICE-NATOR actually changes

**For someone like Ramesh**, instead of hunting through menus:

> *"Pehli row freeze karo"* → done in 1 second.
> *"Header ko bold aur 14 size karo"* → done in 2 seconds.
> *"Column ki width autofit karo"* → done instantly.

He never has to Google a shortcut again. He never has to switch between Hindi thought and English command. He just speaks, like he would to a colleague sitting next to him.

---

### Real tasks it makes faster

**Daily data entry work**
Instead of manually formatting each row after entry, just say *"is row ko currency format mein dikhao"* or *"percentage format lagao"* — the entire formatting pipeline executes in under 2 seconds.

**Report preparation**
Making a monthly report look professional used to mean 20 minutes of formatting — borders, bold headers, alignment, font size. Now: *"header format karo"*, *"borders sab taraf lagao"*, *"center align karo"* — done in under a minute, hands-free.

**Data cleanup**
*"Duplicate rows hatao"*, *"sort A se Z karo"*, *"filter lagao"* — common data hygiene tasks that non-power users typically skip because they don't know where the button is. Now they're one sentence away.

**Avoiding mistakes**
Before OFFICE-NATOR, deleting a row or clearing a range was one accidental click. Now any destructive action requires you to **say "haan" out loud** to confirm. That single confirmation step prevents the most common Excel disaster — accidentally wiping data.

**Working with both hands occupied**
Accountants, data entry operators, and warehouse managers often need to look at physical documents while updating Excel. OFFICE-NATOR lets you keep your eyes on the paper and your voice on the task.

---

### Who specifically benefits

| Person | Their problem | How it helps |
|---|---|---|
| Small business owner | Knows Hindi, struggles with Excel menus | Speaks commands naturally, no English needed |
| Data entry clerk | Repetitive formatting 6 hours a day | Voice shortcuts cut formatting time by 80% |
| Government worker | Uses Excel but never learned shortcuts | 129 operations available by voice |
| Teacher preparing marks sheets | Not tech-savvy, avoids complex features | Simple voice → complex operations |
| Finance professional | Fast-paced work, hands busy | Executes shortcuts without touching keyboard |
| Student learning Excel | Doesn't know where features are hidden | Voice discovers and executes features |

---

### The broader point

**Excel has been around for 40 years. Its power users are a tiny minority.** Most people use 5% of what it can do — not because they don't need the other 95%, but because they never learned it, and the interface doesn't help them find it.

OFFICE-NATOR doesn't just make Excel faster for experts. It makes the full power of Excel accessible to people who never had access to it before — in their own language, in their own words, on their own terms.

That's not a productivity tool. That's a genuinely new kind of access.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Challenges We Ran Into

---

### 1. The LLM kept inventing wrong keyboard shortcuts

This was the first wall we hit and it nearly killed the project.

We started by asking the LLM to generate the keyboard steps for each Excel operation directly. It would confidently return things like `["alt", "h", "w"]` pressed simultaneously for wrap text — which does absolutely nothing in Excel. Or it would return `["ctrl", "shift", "w"]` which doesn't even exist. Every time we tested a new command, something would work for 3 tries and then silently fail on the 4th with a slightly different phrasing.

**The fix:** We stopped asking the LLM to think about keyboard shortcuts at all. We hand-coded 129 Excel operations as deterministic Python functions — every ribbon sequence, every hotkey, every multi-step dialog navigation — verified against real Excel. The LLM's only job now is to read the sentence and say *"that's a `wrap_text`"* or *"that's a `set_font_size` with size=16"*. The actual steps come from the library, not from the model. The LLM classifies. The code executes.

This one architectural change took us from ~40% reliability to near 100%.

---

### 2. Alt+H → W was being pressed simultaneously, not sequentially

Even after building the action library, wrap text still wasn't working. We'd press Alt+H to open the Home ribbon tab, then press W — but nothing happened.

The issue: PyAutoGUI's `hotkey()` function presses all keys *at the same time*. Excel's ribbon navigation requires pressing Alt+H, *releasing it*, then pressing W separately. Pressing Alt+H+W simultaneously is a different shortcut entirely (or nothing at all).

We spent two hours debugging this before we realized it. The visual feedback in Excel was zero — it just silently ignored the input.

**The fix:** We created a new `ribbon` action type in the actuator that presses each key one at a time with an 80ms gap between them. `hotkey` still does simultaneous presses (for Ctrl+B, Ctrl+S etc.), but anything involving ribbon navigation uses the sequential `ribbon` action. Once we split these two action types, everything started working.

---

### 3. The Gemini API key worked, then stopped, then worked again

We spent a full hour thinking our code was broken when actually the Gemini free tier had hit its quota. The API was returning `429` with `limit: 0` — meaning the quota was exhausted at the account level, not per-minute.

The confusing part: we created fresh API keys on new Google accounts and they *also* returned `limit: 0` instantly. Turns out new Google accounts need to visit AI Studio and accept terms of service before the free quota is allocated. The key exists but the quota doesn't until you activate it.

We hit this same wall three times with three different keys before figuring out the pattern.

**The fix:** We switched Groq (Llama 3.3 70B) as the primary provider and kept Gemini as fallback. Groq gives 14,400 free requests per day and responds in under a second. We also built a live provider switcher in the frontend so users can swap between Groq, Gemini, OpenAI, or any custom endpoint without restarting anything. No more single point of failure on one API key.

---

### 4. MongoDB Atlas couldn't connect — but only in Node.js

We built a full auth system with MongoDB Atlas — registration, login, JWT cookies, the works. Tested the connection string in PowerShell DNS: resolved fine. Opened MongoDB Compass: connected fine.

But when Next.js tried to connect, it threw `querySrv ECONNREFUSED _mongodb._tcp.cluster0.vjz9xp3.mongodb.net` every single time.

After an hour of debugging we found the root cause: Node.js on Windows resolves DNS through `127.0.0.1` (the loopback) rather than the system DNS. PowerShell uses Windows DNS which works. Node.js uses a different resolver that was returning connection refused on the SRV record lookup that MongoDB Atlas requires for `+srv` connection strings.

The fix was one line: `dns.setServers(['8.8.8.8', '8.8.4.4'])` at the top of the MongoDB client file, before any connection attempt. This forces Node.js to use Google's public DNS instead of the loopback, and the SRV record resolves immediately.

We documented this in `SETUP_GUIDE.md` because it will catch anyone else who tries to run this on Windows.

---

### 5. The backend can't be deployed — at all

We had the frontend looking great, deployed to Vercel, and then realized: the Python backend literally cannot run in any cloud container.

PyAudio needs a microphone. PyAutoGUI needs a desktop to send keyboard events to. edge-tts needs speakers to play audio through. Vercel, Railway, Render — they're all headless Linux containers. No microphone, no display, no desktop. You can't fake these.

This meant our "deploy and demo" plan fell apart 2 hours before submission prep.

**The fix:** We kept the backend local and used ngrok to expose `localhost:8000` as a public HTTPS URL. The Vercel frontend connects to the ngrok URL via WebSocket. The backend runs on the lap

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
**OFFICE-NATOR** is a multi-model Generative AI pipeline where every stage uses a different AI/ML model working in sequence to translate human intent into machine action.

**The Full GenAI/ML Stack**

- Stage 1 — Speech Understanding (ML) Silero VAD, a lightweight neural network model, continuously analyzes the microphone audio stream in real time to detect when the user starts and stops speaking. This is a classic ML inference task running locally on CPU — no cloud, no API call, pure model inference at 16kHz.

- Stage 2 — Multilingual Speech-to-Text + Translation (GenAI) Sarvam AI's saaras:v3 model transcribes Hindi and Marathi speech and simultaneously translates it to English in a single forward pass. This is a sequence-to-sequence generative model — the same architecture family as Whisper and mT5 — purpose-trained on Indic languages, which no general-purpose STT model handles well.

- Stage 3 — Intent Classification (Large Language Model / GenAI) Groq's Llama 3.3 70B — a 70-billion parameter autoregressive language model — reads the translated English command and generates a structured JSON response identifying which of 129 possible Excel actions the user wants, plus any parameters (font size, column width, cell reference etc.). This is pure generative AI: given natural language input, it produces structured output that drives deterministic execution.

- Stage 4 — Memory-Augmented Context (GenAI + RAG pattern) After each command, the LLM extracts preferences from the interaction ("user prefers Arial font", "user always uses bold headers") and stores them in local JSON. On the next command, these facts are retrieved by keyword similarity and injected into the LLM prompt. This is a lightweight Retrieval-Augmented Generation pattern — the same architecture powering enterprise AI assistants — implemented without a vector database using simple keyword overlap scoring.

- Stage 5 — Neural Text-to-Speech (GenAI) Microsoft Edge's neural TTS voices (Jenny Neural for English, Swara Neural for Hindi) generate natural-sounding audio confirmations and destructive action warnings. These are transformer-based vocoder models streaming audio chunk-by-chunk for low latency.

**What makes this GenAI, not just automation**
Traditional Excel automation (macros, VBA, Power Automate) requires the user to know exact commands in advance and configure them explicitly. OFFICE-NATOR is different:

**Natural language understanding** — "column thoda bada karo" (make the column a bit wider) maps to a specific autofit sequence through LLM reasoning, not pattern matching
**Ambiguity resolution** — when the user says something unclear, the LLM interprets intent in context rather than failing with an error
**Personalization through memory** — the system learns individual habits over time and adapts its behavior, a capability unique to generative AI systems
**Multi-language generalization **— the same model handles variations in phrasing, mixed Hindi-English (Hinglish), and informal speech patterns without explicit programming

**The key architectural insight**
The project deliberately keeps GenAI in the reasoning layer only and uses deterministic code for execution. The LLM never invents keyboard shortcuts — it only picks from 129 pre-verified actions. This is a deliberate design choice that makes the system reliable enough for real work: GenAI for understanding, deterministic code for doing. This is the same principle behind function-calling in GPT-4 and tool-use in Claude — grounding generative outputs in verified, safe actions.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
In today's fast-paced world, many serious health conditions such as heart disease, diabetes, obesity, sleep disorders, and mental health issues often develop silently over time due to unhealthy lifestyle habits, limited health awareness, and a lack of timely intervention. While numerous health applications can track basic health metrics, very few help individuals understand their overall health risks and provide clear, personalized guidance on how to improve their well-being.

PreventAI was developed to bridge this gap. It is an AI-powered preventive healthcare platform that brings together multiple health risk prediction models into a single, user-friendly system. Instead of simply predicting potential health conditions, PreventAI explains the underlying factors contributing to those risks, enabling users to gain meaningful insights into their health.

The platform goes beyond risk assessment by providing personalized workout recommendations, tailored diet plans, health improvement simulations, and structured wellness roadmaps based on an individual's lifestyle and goals. By transforming complex health data into practical and actionable recommendations, PreventAI encourages proactive healthcare, helping users make informed decisions, adopt healthier habits, and reduce the risk of developing chronic diseases in the future.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Building PreventAI involved several technical and design challenges that required careful problem-solving and iterative improvements.

Dataset Integration: Combining multiple healthcare datasets from different sources was challenging because each dataset had different features, formats, and target variables. Significant preprocessing and feature engineering were required to make them suitable for model training.

Data Quality Issues: Several datasets contained missing values, inconsistent labels, imbalanced classes, and categorical features that required cleaning, encoding, and transformation before training reliable machine learning models.

Model Performance Optimization: Achieving good prediction performance across all five health domains required experimenting with different preprocessing techniques, algorithms, and evaluation methods while avoiding overfitting.

Multi-Model Integration: Integrating separate models for heart disease, diabetes, obesity, sleep disorders, and mental health into a single platform required designing a workflow that could generate consistent and meaningful outputs for users.

Explainability and User Trust: A key challenge was ensuring that predictions were not presented as black-box outputs. The system needed to explain why a particular risk was predicted and identify the factors contributing to that prediction.

Personalized Recommendation Generation: Converting model predictions into actionable workout plans, diet recommendations, health insights, and wellness roadmaps required developing additional logic beyond traditional machine learning workflows.

User Experience and Interface Design: Creating a healthcare platform that was both informative and visually appealing required multiple iterations of the website design, dashboard structure, and information presentation.

End-to-End System Integration: Bringing together machine learning models, recommendation engines, simulation logic, report generation, and the web interface into a unified application was one of the most challenging aspects of the project.

Despite these challenges, overcoming them helped transform PreventAI from a collection of individual machine learning models into a comprehensive preventive healthcare platform capable of delivering meaningful and personalized health guidance.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
PreventAI uses Machine Learning + Generative AI together for healthcare prediction and guidance.

ML models analyze user data (age, diet, activity, vitals) to predict disease risks like diabetes, heart disease, etc.
GenAI converts these predictions into simple explanations and personalized health advice, acting like a virtual health assistant.

In short:
ML predicts risk, GenAI explains it and gives lifestyle recommendations.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
This project presents a deep learning-based approach to stock price prediction using a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), specifically an LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) model. The model is trained on historical stock data for companies such as Google and Apple, using features like Open, High, Low, Close, and Volume, with a primary focus on the Open price for time-series forecasting.

A key aspect of the project is the analysis of the lookback window (PAST_DAYS), which defines how many previous days of stock data are used to predict the next value. Experiments were conducted with different window sizes including 30, 60, 90, 120, and 150 days to evaluate their impact on model performance.

The results show that a 30-day lookback window produced the most accurate predictions, while increasing the window size led to reduced performance. This suggests that shorter-term dependencies are more effective for capturing stock market patterns in this dataset, as longer sequences may introduce noise and reduce model focus on recent trends.

Overall, the project demonstrates how LSTM networks can be used for financial time-series forecasting and highlights the importance of selecting an optimal input sequence length for improving predictive accuracy.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the main challenges was understanding how the lookback window (PAST_DAYS) affects model performance. Choosing the right number of past days was not straightforward, and different values like 30, 60, 90, 120, and 150 gave noticeably different results. It took multiple experiments to realize that longer sequences don’t always improve accuracy.

Another challenge was overfitting, since the LSTM model is quite powerful and can easily memorize patterns in the training data. I had to use dropout layers to reduce this issue and make the model generalize better.

A further difficulty was handling time-series data formatting, especially converting raw stock prices into supervised learning sequences. Creating the correct input shape for LSTM (3D structure: samples, timesteps, features) required careful reshaping.

I also faced issues with feature scaling and inverse transformation, because predictions were normalized during training and had to be properly converted back to real stock prices for evaluation and plotting.

Finally, interpreting the results was challenging since stock prices are highly volatile and influenced by external factors not included in the dataset, which limits prediction accuracy.

description.title: Gen AI&ML
description.body:
This project is a deep learning-based stock price prediction system built using an LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) neural network. It analyzes historical stock market data to predict future stock prices based on past trends.

The model is trained on datasets from Google and Apple and uses time-series forecasting techniques, where previous days’ stock prices are used as input to predict the next value. A key part of this project is experimenting with different lookback windows (30, 60, 90, 120, and 150 days) to study how the amount of historical data affects prediction accuracy.

The results show that shorter lookback windows (especially 30 days) perform better, highlighting the importance of recent market trends in financial prediction.

Overall, this project demonstrates the application of deep learning to real-world financial data and explores how sequence length impacts model performance in time-series forecasting.

gov-nexus-ai-add2.name: Gov Nexus AI
gov-nexus-ai-add2.tagline: Ensuring Every Resource Reaches Where It Matters

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Every year, governments, NGOs, and disaster relief agencies manage millions of units of essential resources such as food, medicines, vaccines, sanitation kits, educational materials, and emergency supplies. Despite significant investments, resource distribution remains largely reactive and fragmented.

Many organizations lack real-time visibility into inventory levels across regions, making it difficult to identify shortages before they become critical. Resources are often overstocked in one location while communities in another face urgent shortages. During floods, disease outbreaks, heatwaves, and other emergencies, delayed decision-making and poor coordination can further slow relief efforts and increase human impact.

SmartResource AI addresses these challenges through an AI-powered public resource intelligence platform that predicts future demand, identifies high-risk regions, and recommends optimal resource allocation strategies before shortages occur.

The platform enables governments, NGOs, suppliers, and disaster management authorities to collaborate through a unified system where they can monitor resources, forecast needs, coordinate distribution, and receive real-time alerts.

### What can it be used for?

* Predicting demand for food, medicines, vaccines, drinking water, and relief kits.
* Planning disaster preparedness and emergency resource deployment.
* Detecting shortages, wastage, and inefficient resource utilization.
* Coordinating resource allocation between government departments and NGOs.
* Tracking resource distribution, delivery timelines, and beneficiary coverage.
* Improving transparency and accountability in welfare and relief programs.


By shifting public resource management from reactive decision-making to predictive intelligence, Gov Nexus AI helps ensure that critical supplies reach the right communities at the right time while reducing waste, improving efficiency, and supporting sustainable development goals.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Challenges We Ran Into

One of the biggest challenges was building a system capable of generating reliable demand forecasts from highly diverse and inconsistent data sources. Unlike traditional inventory systems, our platform combines historical resource consumption, demographic information, weather indicators, disaster-related data, and stakeholder requests to predict future demand. Integrating these datasets required significant preprocessing, normalization, and feature engineering to ensure meaningful predictions.

Another major challenge was designing an AI pipeline that could produce actionable recommendations rather than just predictions. Forecasting demand is only one part of the problem; the system also needed to identify shortages, detect overstock situations, assess regional risks, and recommend resource transfers. Balancing prediction accuracy with practical decision-making required multiple iterations of our machine learning workflow.

We also faced challenges while integrating real-time communication services. Using Twilio for automated notifications and alerts required handling message delivery reliability, event triggers, and stakeholder-specific notification logic. Ensuring that critical shortage and emergency alerts reached the right users without overwhelming them with unnecessary notifications was a key design challenge.

Integrating Sarvam AI introduced another layer of complexity. We wanted alerts and recommendations to be understandable by a diverse audience, including government officers, NGO workers, and local coordinators. Generating context-aware summaries and multilingual communications required careful prompt engineering and workflow orchestration to maintain both accuracy and clarity.

Scalability was another hurdle. During disaster scenarios, thousands of simultaneous resource requests and updates may occur. To address this, we designed the architecture around centralized data processing, optimized database queries, and modular services that can scale independently as demand grows.

Finally, one of the most challenging aspects was ensuring that recommendations remained explainable. Public-sector decision-making requires transparency, so we focused on generating AI-driven insights that clearly show why a particular allocation, transfer, or alert was recommended instead of treating the AI model as a black box.

description.title: Gemini
description.body:
Gov Nexus AI utilizes the Gemini API as the intelligence layer powering its conversational assistant for public resource management. The chatbot enables government officials, NGO workers, suppliers, healthcare agencies, and disaster response teams to interact with complex resource data using natural language instead of navigating multiple dashboards and reports.

Through the Gemini-powered assistant, users can ask questions such as:

* "Which districts are expected to face food shortages next month?"
* "Show regions with the highest medicine demand forecast."
* "What resources should be pre-positioned before an approaching cyclone?"
* "Which warehouses currently have excess inventory available for transfer?"
* "Summarize resource distribution performance for the last quarter."

Gemini processes these queries, analyzes the available data, and generates clear, context-aware responses that help stakeholders make informed decisions quickly. The chatbot can also summarize large datasets, explain AI-generated recommendations, and provide actionable insights in a user-friendly format.

In disaster management and public welfare scenarios, decision-makers often need immediate access to information. Instead of manually searching through reports, users can simply converse with the Gemini-powered assistant to obtain forecasts, risk assessments, resource availability information, and operational recommendations.

By integrating Gemini API, Gov Nexus AI transforms complex public resource data into accessible, conversational intelligence, enabling faster decision-making, improved coordination, and more effective resource allocation for sustainable development initiatives.

description.title: ElevenLabs
description.body:
Gov Nexus AI leverages ElevenLabs to power an AI voice agent that enables natural, voice-based interaction with the platform. In public resource management, many stakeholders—including government officers, NGO field workers, healthcare personnel, and disaster response teams—often operate in fast-paced environments where typing reports or navigating dashboards is not practical.

Using ElevenLabs' advanced voice technology, users can communicate with the platform through natural conversations. Field personnel can report shortages, request resources, check inventory status, receive emergency updates, and access AI-generated insights simply by speaking. The voice agent converts complex system interactions into intuitive conversations, reducing response time and improving accessibility.

The ElevenLabs-powered voice agent also delivers critical alerts and recommendations through realistic, human-like speech. During emergencies, users can receive spoken notifications about resource shortages, disaster preparedness actions, delivery updates, and allocation recommendations without needing to constantly monitor a dashboard.

This voice-first approach is especially valuable in disaster response scenarios where rapid communication and hands-free access to information can significantly improve operational efficiency. By integrating ElevenLabs, Gov Nexus AI makes public resource intelligence more accessible, responsive, and user-friendly, ensuring that critical information reaches decision-makers and field workers when they need it most.

description.title: MongoDB
description.body:
Gov Nexus AI relies on MongoDB as the central data platform for managing large volumes of dynamic, real-time, and heterogeneous resource management data. The platform collects and processes information from multiple sources, including resource inventories, NGO requests, government records, disaster indicators, weather data, demographic information, distribution logs, and AI-generated forecasts.

MongoDB's flexible document-based architecture enables us to efficiently store and manage diverse data structures without requiring rigid schemas. This is particularly important because different stakeholders—government agencies, NGOs, suppliers, and relief organizations—generate varying types of data that need to be integrated into a single system.

The platform uses MongoDB to:

* Store resource inventory and warehouse information across multiple regions.
* Manage stakeholder profiles, requests, approvals, and allocation workflows.
* Track resource distribution history and delivery records.
* Store AI-generated demand forecasts, risk assessments, and optimization recommendations.
* Maintain real-time status updates for shortages, emergencies, and resource transfers.
* Support analytics dashboards that provide operational and strategic insights.

MongoDB's scalability and high-performance querying capabilities allow Gov Nexus AI to handle increasing volumes of data during large-scale operations and disaster response scenarios. As resource requests, alerts, and monitoring events grow, MongoDB provides the flexibility and reliability needed to maintain real-time visibility across the entire platform.

By using MongoDB as the backbone of our public resource intelligence system, Gov Nexus AI can efficiently manage complex datasets, support AI-driven decision-making, and deliver a scalable solution for sustainable and transparent resource management.

description.title: Sarvam.ai
description.body:
Gov Nexus AI leverages Sarvam AI's Speech-to-Text (STT) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities to make public resource management more accessible, inclusive, and efficient for diverse stakeholders.

In real-world scenarios, government officers, NGO workers, field coordinators, healthcare staff, and disaster response teams often operate in environments where typing detailed reports or navigating complex dashboards is inconvenient or impractical. Using Sarvam AI's Speech-to-Text technology, users can submit resource requests, shortage reports, inventory updates, and emergency information through natural voice conversations, reducing friction and improving data collection speed.

The platform also utilizes Sarvam AI's Text-to-Speech capabilities to convert AI-generated insights, shortage alerts, allocation recommendations, and emergency notifications into spoken messages. This enables faster communication, especially for field personnel who may be on the move or operating in high-pressure situations.

Additionally, Sarvam AI's multilingual capabilities help bridge language barriers by allowing stakeholders to interact with the system in their preferred language. This is particularly valuable for large-scale public resource management where multiple regions, communities, and organizations are involved.

By integrating Sarvam AI into the workflow, Gov Nexus AI transforms traditional dashboards into a voice-enabled, multilingual public resource intelligence platform, making critical information more accessible and ensuring that resource management decisions can be communicated quickly and effectively during both routine operations and emergency situations.

description.title: Sustainable Development
description.body:
Gov Nexus AI directly addresses one of the core challenges of sustainable development: ensuring that limited public resources are distributed efficiently, equitably, and transparently.

Today, governments, NGOs, healthcare agencies, and disaster management authorities often struggle with resource shortages, overstocking, delayed distribution, and poor coordination. These inefficiencies can lead to food insecurity, reduced access to healthcare supplies, ineffective disaster response, and wastage of valuable public resources.

Our platform uses AI-driven demand forecasting, resource optimization, and stakeholder coordination to ensure that critical resources such as food supplies, medicines, vaccines, educational materials, sanitation kits, and emergency relief equipment reach the communities that need them most.

By reducing waste, improving resource utilization, strengthening disaster preparedness, and increasing transparency in public resource management, Gov Nexus AI contributes directly to multiple United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including:

* **SDG 1 – No Poverty** by improving the delivery of welfare resources and public assistance programs.
* **SDG 2 – Zero Hunger** through better forecasting and distribution of food supplies.
* **SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being** by ensuring timely availability of medicines, vaccines, and healthcare resources.
* **SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities** through proactive disaster preparedness and resilient resource planning.
* **SDG 12 – Responsible Consumption and Production** by minimizing resource wastage and preventing unnecessary stock accumulation.
* **SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions** by improving transparency and accountability in public resource allocation.
* **SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals** by enabling collaboration between governments, NGOs, suppliers, and communities.

Rather than reacting to shortages after they occur, Gov Nexus AI helps organizations make proactive, data-driven decisions that maximize social impact, improve resource accessibility, and support long-term sustainable development.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Challenges Faced During Development

While developing LOOK UP, we faced several challenges that helped us learn more about full-stack web development and API integration. One of the main challenges was understanding how to connect the frontend and backend properly. Since the frontend and backend were being developed separately, we had to ensure that data could be fetched and displayed correctly without breaking the user interface.

Another challenge was integrating multiple space-related APIs into a single platform. Each API provided data in a different format, so we had to understand the responses and process them before sending them to the frontend. Managing different endpoints and ensuring that the correct data was displayed to the user required careful testing and debugging.

Working as a team was also a challenge. Since different members were responsible for different parts of the project, we had to coordinate our work effectively and ensure that all components worked together smoothly. Using tools like VS Code Live Share helped us collaborate, but understanding each other's code and maintaining consistency across the project required continuous communication.

We also faced challenges while setting up the backend environment, installing dependencies, configuring Node.js and Express, managing routes, and resolving errors that occurred during development. Debugging issues such as package installation errors, server crashes, and API response handling took significant time and effort.

Another challenge was making the platform simple and user-friendly. Space-related information can often be technical and difficult to understand, so we focused on presenting the data in a way that is easy for students and general users to explore.

Despite these challenges, the development process helped us improve our skills in web development, API integration, teamwork, debugging, and problem-solving, ultimately leading to the successful creation of LOOK UP.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Problem Statement

Today, a huge amount of space-related information is available through organizations such as NASA and other space agencies. Data about the International Space Station (ISS), Near-Earth Objects (asteroids), space weather conditions, and daily space discoveries are publicly available. However, this information is often spread across multiple websites, dashboards, and technical platforms, making it difficult for students, beginners, and the general public to access and understand.

Most existing platforms present raw scientific data that requires prior knowledge of astronomy or space science. As a result, many people who are interested in space exploration are unable to effectively use this information or stay updated with ongoing developments in the space sector. There is also a lack of a single platform that combines real-time space tracking, educational content, and AI-powered assistance in an easy-to-use interface.

LOOK UP aims to solve this problem by creating a centralized space information platform that brings together multiple space-related services in one place. Users can track the live location of the International Space Station, explore NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day, monitor Near-Earth Objects that pass close to Earth, and stay informed about space weather events that may affect satellites and communication systems. Additionally, an integrated AI assistant helps users understand complex space concepts in simple language, making the platform more educational and engaging.

By transforming scattered and technical space data into a user-friendly experience, LOOK UP helps students, researchers, educators, and space enthusiasts learn about space in a more interactive, accessible, and meaningful way.

argus-9709.name: ARGUS
argus-9709.tagline: Advanced threat detection system for satellite tel

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Space missions conducted by organizations like ISRO and NASA involve extremely high financial and strategic stakes, with satellites costing millions of dollars to design, launch, and maintain. These systems remain vulnerable to two critical risks: undetected system failures and sophisticated cyberattacks. Both can lead to mission degradation or complete failure, resulting in irreversible losses.

Existing infrastructures lack a unified, proactive framework for real-time anomaly detection and response. Additionally, telemetry data and system logs which are crucial for monitoring and post-incident analysis are often mutable, making them susceptible to tampering. This compromises forensic integrity, leaving investigators without a reliable trail to trace the root cause of failures or breaches.

ARGUS addresses these gaps through a 3+1 layered architecture that combines AI-driven detection with blockchain-based auditing. It enables:

Real-time anomaly detection across satellite subsystems using multi-layered AI models
Automated threat response mechanisms to mitigate failures before escalation
Tamper-proof logging using blockchain, ensuring immutable and verifiable telemetry records
Reliable forensic traceability, allowing precise post-incident analysis
By integrating intelligent monitoring with secure, decentralized auditing, ARGUS transforms satellite operations into a more resilient, transparent, and failure-resistant ecosystem saving space agencies millions of dollars.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges was handling the overall system complexity. ARGUS combines multiple technologies, and getting everything to work smoothly together wasn’t straightforward. Blockchain was completely new to us, so figuring out how to use it for secure, tamper-proof logging took a lot of trial and error.

But the worst issue was RESOLVING MERGE CONFLICTS ON GITHUB.

outsurance-9ad4.name: Outsurance
outsurance-9ad4.tagline: Your Health, Your Privacy, No Fine Print.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# The Problem Outsurance Solves

Buying health insurance in India is broken. For the average consumer, navigating the insurance landscape is a frustrating journey through deliberate jargon, hidden clauses, and high-pressure sales tactics. Outsurance re-engineers this experience from the ground up, turning a confusing financial chore into a transparent, secure, and hyper-personalized health strategy.

Here is exactly how Outsurance transforms the process, what people use it for, and how it makes existing tasks significantly easier, safer, and more accurate.

---

## 1. What Can People Use Outsurance For?

Outsurance serves as an autonomous, private digital insurance advisor. Users leverage the platform to:
* **Audit Existing or New Plans:** Evaluate whether a health insurance plan genuinely covers their unique pre-existing conditions (e.g., Diabetes, Hypertension) before buying.
* **Extract Vitals Automatically:** Upload complex medical reports, clinical PDFs, or lab blood tests to immediately extract critical health indicators without manually decoding medical terminology.
* **Run Financial Stress Tests:** Simulate real-world medical emergencies (e.g., *"How much out-of-pocket cost will I pay if I am hospitalized for a heart attack in Mumbai under Plan X?"*).
* **Interact with a Conversational Medical Agent:** Use natural language to query policy nuances, update health parameters on the fly, and ask follow-up questions like, *"What if I develop Asthma next year—how does that change my plan suitability?"*
* **Navigate in Native Languages:** Break down complex financial and medical jargon into over 15+ local Indian languages for family members who are non-native English speakers.

---

## 2. Making Existing Tasks Easier: Frictionless Insurance Discovery

Traditional insurance platforms operate like basic filtering directories. Outsurance replaces manual searching with data-driven automation.

| Traditional Process | The Outsurance Way | How It Makes It Easier |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Manual Data Entry:** Spending 20 minutes manually entering old prescription dates, blood sugar levels, and BP readings. | **Local AI Extraction:** Uploading a lab report triggers a local Small Language Model (SLM) to extract vitals instantly. | **Saves Time & Eliminates Error:** Users don't need to know what "HbA1c" or "Systolic" means; the system inputs the data perfectly in seconds. |
| **Deciphering Fine Print:** Reading 40-page policy PDFs to find waiting periods, co-pays, and disease-specific sub-limits. | **Structured Engine Matching:** Stage 2 & 3 matching algorithms cross-reference extracted health risks against a mapped database of insurance plans. | **Instant Clarification:** Zero scrolling through PDFs. The platform surfaces exact waiting periods and clauses relevant *only* to your conditions. |
| **Opaque Recommendations:** Platforms show a "Best Seller" badge with zero explanation of why that plan fits you. | **Explainable AI (XGBoost + SHAP + Gemma):** Visualizes exactly how metrics like BMI or Age impacted your score, backed by a plain-English explanation. | **Informed Decision Making:** Removes guesswork. Users see exactly *why* a specific plan scored an 8.5/10 versus a 5/10. |

---

## 3. Making Existing Tasks Safer: Privacy & Integrity by Design

The current insurance market carries significant risks regarding data privacy and predatory marketing. Outsurance establishes a secure framework to eliminate these threats.

### 🚫 Stopping Spam & Eliminating Aggregator Leaks
* **The Status Quo:** Entering your phone number on typical insurance aggregator sites instantly results in endless cold calls from aggressive brokers pushing high-commission plans.
* **The Outsurance Safety:** Built with a strict **Zero-Knowledge Design**. Clinical document parsing runs entirely in local memory on the client side. Only 10 anonymous numeric health vitals pass through the Machine Learning pipeline. Your sensitive medical documents never touch a third-party server, keeping your personal contact information secure from broker databases.

### 🧠 Mitigating the "Underwriter Rejection" Trap
* **The Status Quo:** Buying a plan without realizing a pre-existing condition is excluded can lead to claim rejections years later during a medical crisis.
* **The Outsurance Safety:** By running an advanced **4-Stage ML Recommendation Pipeline** (utilizing a custom XGBoost classifier trained on real hospital survey data), the platform calculates an accurate health risk tier (Low to Critical) beforehand. It proactively flags hidden policy traps, exclusions, and co-payment clauses before you pay a single rupee in premiums.

### 🔒 Secure Data Control
* Backed by rigid database **Row-Level Security (RLS)** and stateless JWT tokens, user sessions are completely isolated. For high-security environments, the entire ecosystem is packaged to deploy entirely offline on edge hardware (like a Raspberry Pi kiosk), ensuring sensitive medical queries can happ

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
# Challenges We Ran Into

Building a production-ready, local-first intelligence engine that couples deterministic machine learning pipelines with non-deterministic small language models presented several technical hurdles. Because we chose to deploy on resource-constrained hardware (Raspberry Pi) and enforce absolute client-side data isolation, we could not rely on standard cloud infrastructure solutions. 

Here are the major technical challenges we encountered during development and how we engineered our way around them.

---

### 1. The Small Language Model Context Bloat & Multi-Agent Loop
* **The Hurdle:** Our conversational chatbot (`backend/app/agent.py`) handles complex tasks like tool orchestration, running out-of-pocket stress tests, and comparing plan specifications stored in `plans_db.py`. When we used local `gemma3:1b` via Ollama to evaluate conversational context alongside policy features for multiple plans, the context token count bloated immediately. This caused massive response latency (over 45 seconds per turn) on local hardware and occasionally led the model into an infinite loop of calling the same tool repeatedly.
* **How We Got Over It:** We engineered a **State-Throttled Tool Router**. Instead of passing raw, unstructured policy data or the entire chat history back to the model, we decoupled the execution layers:
  1. We used the local SLM strictly as a lightweight **Intent and Named Entity Recognition (NER) extractor** to pull parameters (e.g., condition names, localized budget ceilings).
  2. We passed these parsed parameters into deterministic, fast Python utility modules (`hospital_network.py` and `stress_test.py`).
  3. The structured responses from these modules were then injected into an optimized, minimal prompt template. This reduced the token payload by **78%**, dropping latency to under 3 seconds on standard local machines.

---

### 2. Feature Asymmetry & Normalization Breakdown in the XGBoost Pipeline
* **The Hurdle:** Stage 1 of our recommendation pipeline relies on a custom XGBoost classification model to assess a user's health risk tier based on real medical vitals (such as HbA1c, systolic blood pressure, and BMI). During testing, we noticed that when users had high qualitative medical risks (e.g., a history of severe kidney stones or a recent major surgical event) but otherwise perfect quantitative vitals (normal blood pressure, low BMI), the XGBoost model completely ignored the qualitative medical history and classified them as "Low Risk." This resulted in dangerous plan mismatches.
* **How We Got Over It:** We introduced **Stage 0: The Dynamic Condition Scorer** (`condition_scorer.py`). Before passing data to the XGBoost matrix, any text-based medical history or parsed clinical report details are processed through a local, aggressively cached risk-weight map (scoring conditions from `0.0` to `5.0`). We engineered a synthetic interaction feature—`metabolic_risk_score`—which cross-multiplies this condition score against quantitative biometric markers. By including this engineered feature in our training dataset, the XGBoost model learned to identify complex interactions, boosting classification accuracy to **85.0%** across all risk tiers.

---

### 3. RAM Swapping & Quantization Bottlenecks on Edge Deployments
* **The Hurdle:** One of our primary objectives was enabling the entire platform to execute entirely offline on a Raspberry Pi. During initial edge runs, launching the FastAPI backend alongside Ollama loading the `gemma3:1b` weights caused immediate memory starvation on the Pi's RAM. The operating system began aggressive memory swapping, which stalled the UI and caused the local AI document-extraction step to crash with out-of-memory (OOM) errors.
* **How We Got Over It:** We resolved this hardware bottleneck through aggressive resource optimizations:
  1. We switched to an aggressively quantized GGUF variant of the model, strictly limiting its execution footprint.
  2. We configured a strict memory-concurrency lock in the backend code, ensuring that the heavy extraction phase, the XGBoost inference matrix, and the chat agent never execute simultaneously in memory.
  3. We built a native **Soft-Fail Engine** that actively monitors hardware overhead. If local system resources cross a critical 92% RAM utilization threshold, the platform cleanly falls back to a high-speed regex-based medical parsing engine and static model matrix, preventing hardware lockups while preserving core platform features.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Key Technical Challenges Overcome

Seamless Google Authentication Integration: Implementing compliant Google One Tap and custom sign-in flows with secure dual-token verification (ID Tokens and Access Tokens) while maintaining a reliable sandbox authentication fallback for development and testing environments required careful OAuth architecture and security handling.

Anti-Cheat & Focus Integrity System: Designing a comprehensive integrity framework featuring timer validation, randomized focus checkpoints, rapid-completion detection, and dynamic Integrity Score calculations to discourage misuse while preserving a frictionless experience for genuine users.

Stress-Adaptive Intelligence (SAGE Engine): Developing an adaptive behavioral system capable of adjusting quest difficulty and workload recommendations based on real-time stress indicators, including automated recovery-mode activation and guided breathing interventions, required sophisticated state management and personalization logic.

Real-Time Analytics & Personalization:  Building advanced personalization systems such as seeded daily quest generation, bottleneck detection, subject health indexing, performance trend analysis, and 30-day growth forecasting demanded accurate backend computation and responsive frontend visualization.

Performance Optimization & Animation Synchronization: Coordinating Framer Motion animations, Web Audio API interactions, real-time UI transitions, and onboarding experiences while maintaining smooth performance across devices required extensive optimization and synchronization efforts.

These challenges collectively shaped a highly polished, production-ready platform that combines intelligent personalization, behavioral science, and robust system design while maintaining an intuitive and engaging user experience.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Problem Statement & Solution Overview

EvolveAura is designed to tackle one of the most significant challenges facing students and young professionals today: declining focus, digital distraction, and inconsistent personal growth.

 Problems Addressed

1. Digital Distraction & Attention Fragmentation
The rise of short-form content platforms has contributed to reduced attention spans, constant task-switching, and difficulty maintaining deep focus during study, work, or skill development.

2. Unsustainable Motivation Systems
Most productivity and digital detox solutions rely on restriction, reminders, or guilt-driven approaches. While these may work temporarily, they often fail to create lasting behavioral change and long-term engagement.

3. Inconsistent Personal Development
Individuals frequently struggle to maintain balanced growth across multiple aspects of life, including academic performance, physical well-being, mental resilience, and creative development. Progress in one area often comes at the expense of another.

4. Limited Self-Awareness
Many users lack clear visibility into their strengths, weaknesses, productivity patterns, stress levels, and personal bottlenecks, making it difficult to identify areas that require improvement.

5. Procrastination, Stress, and Burnout
Without intelligent workload management and recovery mechanisms, users often experience overwhelm, leading to missed goals, declining motivation, and eventual burnout.

6. Low Engagement in Self-Improvement
Traditional self-improvement tools often feel repetitive and uninspiring, causing users to abandon habits before meaningful results can be achieved.

Our Solution

EvolveAura transforms self-improvement into an intelligent, psychology-driven progression system that combines behavioral science, gamification, and adaptive analytics.

The platform helps users replace passive digital consumption with meaningful action through structured quests, personalized growth pathways, real-time performance insights, adaptive recovery systems, and visual progress tracking.

By making personal development engaging, measurable, and rewarding, EvolveAura encourages users to build sustainable discipline, improve focus, develop healthier habits, and achieve balanced growth across academics, wellness, productivity, and creativity.

Mission: To make self-improvement more engaging, rewarding, and sustainable than mindless scrolling, enabling users to unlock their full potential through consistent daily progress.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
## The Problem It Solves

Indian farmers often make critical decisions with limited or delayed information. Crop diseases are usually detected only after significant damage has occurred, irrigation is often based on guesswork rather than actual crop water requirements, and farmers frequently sell produce at local markets without knowing better prices available nearby. This information gap leads to lower yields, unnecessary expenses, water wastage, and reduced profits.

KhetWise solves this by providing farmers with a single AI-powered platform that delivers actionable agricultural intelligence in their preferred language. Farmers can instantly diagnose crop diseases from a photo, monitor crop health using satellite data, receive personalized irrigation recommendations, compare real-time mandi prices, and stay informed about disease outbreaks in nearby regions.

The platform makes farming decisions faster, more accurate, and data-driven while remaining accessible to smallholder farmers through a simple mobile-first experience. By combining AI, satellite monitoring, weather intelligence, and market data, KhetWise helps farmers reduce losses, save resources, and maximize income.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Challenges We Ran Into

### 1. Affordable Real-Time Satellite Monitoring

Obtaining fresh NDVI crop-health data for arbitrary farm locations without relying on expensive commercial APIs was challenging. We solved this by building a lightweight processing layer that computes NDVI from publicly available Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and caches results to minimize API usage and latency.

### 2. Disease Detection Accuracy

General-purpose vision models often struggled with Indian crop varieties, inconsistent lighting conditions, and low-quality smartphone images. To improve reliability, we incorporated crop-specific context such as crop type, growth stage, soil conditions, and region into our AI prompts, significantly improving diagnosis quality.

### 3. Inconsistent Market Price Data

Agricultural market data sources frequently contained missing records, delayed updates, or inconsistent formats across states. We addressed this by creating a normalization layer and implementing multiple fallback sources to ensure users always receive usable market intelligence.

### 4. Multi-Language Voice Input

Support for Indian language speech recognition varies significantly across browsers and devices. We tested multiple locale configurations, implemented language-specific fallbacks, and ensured the application gracefully switches to text-based input when speech recognition is unavailable.

### 5. Performance on Low-End Devices

Many target users rely on entry-level Android phones with limited processing power and unstable network connectivity. To maintain a smooth experience, we optimized rendering performance, parallelized API requests, introduced intelligent caching, and implemented skeleton loading states to reduce perceived wait times.
