description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
SafeBand is a smart emergency response and safety system designed to provide instant SOS communication even in situations where traditional internet or mobile network connectivity fails. Built using ESP32, GSM, GPS, BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy), and Firebase cloud integration, the system ensures that emergency alerts can still reach nearby devices and responders during critical situations.

The device continuously monitors connectivity conditions and intelligently switches between multiple communication layers depending on availability. In normal conditions, SafeBand uses Wi-Fi and Firebase cloud services to send real-time emergency alerts, GPS coordinates, and live status updates to connected users. If internet connectivity is unavailable, the integrated GSM module sends emergency SMS messages and phone calls containing the user’s live location. In situations where both Wi-Fi and GSM networks fail, SafeBand automatically activates a BLE-based fallback system that broadcasts SOS alerts and GPS coordinates directly to nearby devices through Bluetooth.

The BLE fallback architecture enables nearby phones, laptops, or relay devices to receive emergency notifications without requiring internet access. These devices can then relay the received information to the cloud or display emergency details locally, ensuring that communication is still possible during network outages, disasters, or isolated environments. The system broadcasts real-time SOS alerts for an extended duration to maximize reliability and improve discoverability during emergencies.

SafeBand also integrates live GPS tracking to provide accurate location data with every alert. Emergency notifications include a direct Google Maps link, enabling responders to quickly navigate to the user’s exact location. The web dashboard provides real-time monitoring, BLE notifications, emergency logs, and cloud synchronization for connected devices.

The project addresses major limitations of conventional emergency systems by introducing a multi-layer fallback communication model that prioritizes reliability, redundancy, and accessibility. SafeBand is designed for personal safety applications such as women’s safety, elderly care, disaster response, solo travel, remote area monitoring, and emergency communication in low-connectivity zones.

Key Features:

* Real-time SOS emergency alerts
* Automatic fallback communication system
* Wi-Fi + Firebase cloud integration
* GSM-based SMS and emergency calling
* BLE mesh-style emergency broadcasting
* Live GPS location tracking
* Google Maps emergency navigation
* Offline emergency communication support
* Smart web dashboard for monitoring and alerts
* Low-cost and scalable IoT architecture

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges during development was implementing a reliable fallback communication system when both Wi-Fi and GSM networks were unavailable. Traditional emergency systems heavily depend on internet or cellular connectivity, so creating an offline emergency communication workflow using BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy) required significant experimentation and debugging.

Another major challenge was ensuring stable communication between the ESP32 hardware and the web dashboard using Web Bluetooth APIs. Initially, BLE notifications were failing with GATT-related errors because browser-based Bluetooth communication requires additional BLE descriptors and proper notification handling. This was resolved by redesigning the BLE service architecture, implementing BLE2902 descriptors, and continuously broadcasting SOS packets for an extended duration instead of sending a single notification.

Power management and GSM stability also became critical hurdles. The SIM800L GSM module requires stable voltage and high burst current during SMS transmission and calling. During testing, unstable battery voltage caused random network disconnects and failed GSM registration. The issue was solved by redesigning the power setup using a Li-ion battery with TP4056 charging support and optimizing the module’s power delivery.

GPS integration introduced another layer of complexity, especially indoors where satellite fixes were inconsistent. To improve reliability during demonstrations and emergency conditions, a fallback coordinate system was implemented so the application could still demonstrate emergency routing and location-sharing features even when live GPS signals were temporarily unavailable.

Integrating multiple communication layers — Wi-Fi, Firebase, GSM, GPS, and BLE — into a single synchronized workflow while maintaining real-time responsiveness was another difficult aspect of the project. The final architecture was carefully optimized to dynamically switch between cloud communication and offline BLE fallback modes depending on network availability.

Overall, the project involved solving real-world IoT challenges related to connectivity redundancy, low-power embedded systems, BLE communication reliability, GSM stability, GPS integration, and real-time emergency alert synchronization.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Challenges we Ran Into

---

### 1. The Model Kept Breaking on New Inputs
Okay so this one genuinely frustrated me for a while. When you train XGBoost it creates like 40+ columns after one-hot encoding. But when a new user hits the API, their request is just 7 simple fields. The model would just crash or give garbage output because the columns didn't match.

we had to figure out how to save the exact column list from training and then reshape every incoming request to match it perfectly before passing it to the model.

---

### 2. The Demo Kept Dying Because of Weather API
Every time we tested the predict endpoint, if the OpenWeatherMap key was wrong or the internet was slow, the whole thing would crash. Not great when you're about to demo in front of judges.

So we just wrapped it in a try/except and said — if anything goes wrong with weather, just assume it's Clear and keep going. Simple fix but took me a moment to think of it.

---

### 3. Render Refused to Deploy Because of Pandas
Spent a good chunk of time staring at a red build log that just said `metadata-generation-failed`. Turns out my requirements.txt had exact version numbers pinned like `pandas==2.2.2` which conflicted with Render's environment.

The fix was embarrassingly simple — just remove all the version numbers and let Render figure it out itself.

---

### 4. XGBoost Was Silently Getting Wrong Data
After one-hot encoding, some columns were staying as `True/False` boolean instead of `1/0` integers. XGBoost didn't throw an error — it just gave weird predictions and I couldn't figure out why for a while.

Eventually caught it by printing the dtypes and added one extra loop to force everything to int.

---

### 5. Wrong Target Column Name
This one would have been embarrassing. we almost trained the entire model on the wrong column because I assumed it was called `Footfall`. The actual dataset had it as `Expected_Footfall`.

Caught it only because we actually read the dataset generator script line by line before writing the training code.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Every ML engineer, data scientist, and CS student has felt this exact moment. You are 6 hours into a training run. Loss is dropping. Accuracy is climbing. Then your Colab session disconnects, your laptop dies, or your server restarts — and you are back at epoch 1. Again.
This is not a rare edge case. This is the daily reality of anyone training models on free-tier cloud GPUs, shared university servers, or underpowered personal machines. Millions of GPU-hours are wasted every year re-doing work that was already done — not because the model was wrong, but because the infrastructure failed and there was no safety net.
loopz is that safety net.
It is a Python library that adds automatic crash recovery to any loop with a single decorator. You do not rewrite your training logic. You do not add boilerplate. You add @loopz.track(...) above your function and from that point every checkpoint is saved atomically. Crash at step 60,000 out of 100,000 — run the same script again and it resumes from exactly step 60,000.
For ML training, loopz saves and restores the complete training state: model weights, optimizer, learning rate scheduler, random seeds for deterministic resume, and any custom loop variables like running loss or best accuracy. The crash never happened as far as your training loop is concerned.
This project has no flashy frontend — and that is intentional. The interface for a developer tool is the terminal, the decorator, and the status output. The real deliverable is a working, published library that solves a problem every developer in this community has personally felt. It is live on PyPI right now — pip install loopz — built by a solo developer from India who lost one too many hours of Colab training.

**Who it helps:**
- ML students running experiments on Colab that disconnects
- Data engineers processing large datasets that can crash midway
- Researchers training models overnight on laptops that might die
- Anyone running any long Python loop that cannot afford to restart

**What makes loopz different:**
Unlike manual checkpointing which requires writing complex save/load logic inside your loop, loopz requires zero changes inside your loop body. It automatically saves your loop position, model weights, optimizer state, LR scheduler, GradScaler, random seed state, and custom accumulators — and restores all of them on the next run deterministically.

`pip install loopz` — that is the entire setup.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Atomic writes without corruption. The scariest failure mode was not a crash — it was a crash during a checkpoint write. If loopz is saving your model at epoch 30 and the system dies mid-write, you get a corrupt file. Next time you resume, you load broken weights and get silently wrong results — which is worse than starting over. The fix was atomic writes: loopz writes to a temporary file first, then renames it. A file rename is atomic on every major OS, so the checkpoint is either fully written or completely untouched. Never half-broken.
Restoring random state for deterministic resume. Saving model weights and optimizer state is the obvious part. The non-obvious part is random seeds. If Python, NumPy, and PyTorch random states are not restored exactly, the resumed training takes a different random path than it would have without the crash — meaning your results are no longer reproducible. loopz captures and restores the full random state across all three so the resumed run is identical to an uninterrupted one.
Primitive loop variables cannot be tracked by reference. If a user writes loss = 0.0 and updates it as loss += value, loopz cannot track that mutation — Python creates a new float object on every assignment. This was a real API design problem. The solution was a documented pattern: wrap primitives in a list (loss = [0.0]), which is mutable and trackable. Simple fix, but it took real thought to arrive at a solution that did not make the API ugly or confusing.
Supporting PyTorch DDP and DataParallel. These wrappers store the actual model under a .module attribute instead of directly. loopz had to detect these wrappers, unwrap the underlying module to save the state dict correctly, and restore it cleanly — without the user needing to know or do anything differently.

Challenges I ran into
Challenge 1: Gemini API Returning Inconsistent JSON Formats
The Problem:
The Gemini API kept wrapping JSON responses in markdown code blocks (```json ... ```) or adding explanatory text before/after the JSON object. This broke the JSON parser completely, causing the app to fail silently.

How I Fixed It:
I implemented a multi-strategy JSON extraction system with 4 fallback layers:

python
def extract_json(raw: str) -> dict | None:
    # Strategy 1: Direct parse
    # Strategy 2: Strip markdown code blocks with regex
    # Strategy 3: Regex extract JSON object pattern
    # Strategy 4: Bracket-matching to find complete JSON block
This brute-force approach ensures that even if the AI misbehaves, the system still extracts valid JSON. I also set temperature=0 and top_k=1 to make the model as deterministic as possible.

 Challenge 2: Handling Multiple AI Models Gracefully
The Problem:
When I added model switching between Gemma 3 12B and 27B, some models would fail to load while others succeeded. The app needed to handle partial model availability without crashing.

How I Fixed It:
I wrapped each model initialization in individual try-catch blocks and stored available models in a dictionary:

python
models = {}
for model_key, model_name in AVAILABLE_MODELS.items():
    try:
        models[model_key] = genai.GenerativeModel(model_name)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error loading model {model_name}: {e}")
The API now dynamically falls back to any available model if the requested one isn't loaded, and the frontend shows only working models.

🏃 Challenge 3: Rate Limiting Without Blocking Legitimate Users
The Problem:
Without rate limiting, a single user could spam the API and exhaust quota. But overly aggressive limits would hurt the user experience.

How I Fixed It:
I implemented a 2-second cooldown per IP using an in-memory dictionary with timestamps. The 429 Too Many Requests response still returns a 200-like JSON body so the frontend can display a friendly message instead of crashing:

python
def is_rate_limited(ip: str) -> bool:
    now = time()
    if ip in _last_request and now - _last_request[ip] < 2:
        return True
    _last_request[ip] = now
    return False
🌐 Challenge 4: CORS Issues Between GitHub Pages and Hugging Face
The Problem:
The frontend on GitHub Pages and backend on Hugging Face Spaces have different origins, causing CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) errors. Browsers blocked all API calls.

How I Fixed It:
I configured Flask-CORS to only allow the specific GitHub Pages domain, not wildcard origins:

allowed_origins = os.getenv("ALLOWED_ORIGINS", "https://sumit989bishnoi-crypto.github.io")

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
### 🧩 The Challenge: AI Non-Determinism & Frontend Crashes

One of the most complex hurdles we faced was reliably rendering the AI-generated architecture diagrams without crashing the frontend. 

We integrated **Gemini 2.5 Flash** to analyze repositories and output `Mermaid.js` flowchart syntax. However, Large Language Models are inherently non-deterministic. Even with strict prompt engineering, the AI would occasionally return slightly invalid syntax, such as:
*   Injecting unexpected Markdown code fences (e.g., ` ```mermaid `).
*   Using parentheses inside node definitions.

When our Flutter frontend attempted to parse these edge cases inside the iframe, the Mermaid renderer would throw a fatal syntax error, causing the UI component to crash completely.

### 🛠️ The Solution: A Robust Middleware Sanitizer

We quickly realized that prompt engineering alone wasn't enough to guarantee stability. To solve this, we built a **regex-based middleware sanitizer** directly into our Node.js backend. 

Before saving any AI output to MongoDB, this custom data pipeline intercepts the response and performs aggressive cleaning:
1.  **Strips rogue markdown fences** to ensure raw text execution.
2.  **Enforces correct graph directives** (e.g., defaulting to `graph TD`).
3.  **Automatically converts invalid characters** (like nested parentheses) into safe, quoted string labels using Regex.

**The Impact:** By implementing this middle-layer sanitizer, we transformed an unpredictable AI output into a **100% deterministic, crash-proof data source**, allowing our UI to render complex architecture diagrams flawlessly every single time.

description.body:
A **Medical Tracking Application** isn't just a digital filing cabinet; it’s a proactive tool designed to reduce human error and provide a holistic view of a person’s health journey.

Here is how such an application solves real-world problems and streamlines healthcare management:

---

## 1. Centralizing "Fragmented" Medical History
The biggest challenge in modern healthcare is the "silo" effect—your cardiologist, GP, and dentist often don’t have access to the same records.

* **The Solution:** Users can store lab results, vaccination records, and surgical histories in one place.
* **The Impact:** When seeing a new specialist, you don’t have to rely on memory. You provide a complete, accurate data set, which leads to better diagnoses.

## 2. Medication Management & Safety
Human memory is fallible, especially when managing complex "polypharmacy" (taking multiple medications).

* **Smart Reminders:** Automated alerts ensure doses aren't missed.
* **Interaction Checks:** Many apps can flag potential drug-to-drug interactions before you take them.
* **Safety:** It prevents **accidental doubling** of doses, which is a major cause of emergency room visits for the elderly.

## 3. Symptom & Chronic Condition Tracking
For patients with chronic illnesses like Migraines, IBS, or Diabetes, "how you've been feeling" is often too vague for a doctor to use.

* **Data Logging:** Users can log daily pain levels, blood glucose, or blood pressure.
* **Trend Analysis:** The app generates charts that show how symptoms correlate with diet, weather, or stress.
* **The Impact:** This turns "I feel bad sometimes" into "I experience a 30% spike in symptoms every Tuesday after my gym session."



---

## 4. Caregiver Coordination
Managing the health of a child, an aging parent, or a disabled loved one is a massive administrative burden.

| Task | Without an App | With a Tracking App |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Updates** | Calling every family member individually. | Shared access to the health log. |
| **Appointments** | Paper calendars or lost sticky notes. | Synced alerts for all caregivers. |
| **Emergency** | Scrambling for a list of allergies. | One-tap "Emergency Profile" access. |

## 5. Emergency Preparedness
In an emergency, you may be unconscious or too distressed to provide information.

* **The Solution:** A "Digital ID" or "Medical Pass" feature allows first responders to see your blood type, allergies (like Penicillin), and emergency contacts directly from your phone's lock screen.
* **Safety:** This saves precious minutes and prevents life-threatening allergic reactions during treatment.

---

## 6. Informed Decision Making
By tracking metrics over time (like weight, heart rate, or sleep patterns), the application shifts healthcare from **reactive** to **proactive**.

* **Early Detection:** Spotting a gradual upward trend in blood pressure before it reaches a crisis level.
* **Accountability:** Seeing a visual representation of your progress can motivate better lifestyle choices.

> **The Bottom Line:** A medical tracking app moves the responsibility of "remembering" from the brain to the palm of the hand, reducing anxiety for the patient and providing "cleaner" data for the physician.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body: Building a medical tracking application presents a unique set of technical and ethical hurdles. Since we are dealing with sensitive biometric data and "mission-critical" reminders, the stakes are much higher than a standard productivity app.Here are three specific challenges often encountered during development and how to navigate them:1. The "Notification Fatigue" & Reliability BugThe Hurdle: On many modern operating systems (especially Android), aggressive battery optimization often "kills" background processes. This meant that life-critical medication reminders were being delayed or suppressed entirely to save battery life.The Fix: We had to implement Exact Alarms using specialized APIs (like AlarmManager in Android) that bypass standard battery restrictions.The Design Pivot: To solve "Notification Fatigue" (users ignoring alerts because they get too many), we implemented a Critical Alert system. Normal logs use standard pings, but "High-Stakes" medications use a persistent, escalating alarm that requires a specific interaction to silence.2. Secure Data Synchronization (The HIPAA/GDPR Puzzle)The Hurdle: Balancing user convenience (accessing data on any device) with strict privacy laws. Traditional databases store data in a way that developers could technically "see," which is a major security risk for medical records.The Fix: We moved to End-to-End Encryption (E2EE).Data is encrypted on the user’s device using a key derived from their password before it ever hits the cloud.The Result: Even if our servers were breached, the hackers would only see "gibberish" text.How we got over it: We utilized established libraries like AES-256 for encryption, ensuring we weren't "rolling our own crypto," which is a cardinal sin in security.3. The "Messy Data" Standardization ProblemThe Hurdle: Users and doctors often use different terms for the same thing (e.g., "High Blood Pressure" vs. "Hypertension"). If the app is supposed to generate a report for a doctor, the data needs to be standardized.The Fix: Instead of relying purely on free-text input, we integrated the SNOMED CT or LOINC medical terminology databases.User Experience (UX) Solution: We implemented an "Autosuggest" search bar. As a user types "Heart," the app suggests "Heart Rate (BPM)" or "Atrial Fibrillation," tagging the entry with a universal medical code behind the scenes.ChallengeImpactResolutionSystem HibernationMissed medications.Use of high-priority system intents & AlarmManager.Data PrivacyRisk of sensitive leaks.Local-first E2EE (End-to-End Encryption).Medical AccuracyConfusing reports for doctors.Standardized terminology via API integration.4. The "Ghost Entry" BugThe Hurdle: During the beta phase, we found that users were accidentally double-logging symptoms because the UI didn't update fast enough on slow connections, leading them to tap "Submit" twice.The Fix: We implemented Optimistic UI updates. The app now shows the entry as "Saved" instantly in the local cache, then syncs with the server in the background. We also disabled the submit button the millisecond it was pressed (Debouncing) to prevent duplicate entries.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
The biggest architectural challenge was designing the reward reveal flow so the secret message stays hidden until the player genuinely completes the game — not just skippable or URL-extractable. Since Next.js NEXT_PUBLIC_* environment variables are client-visible by default, we had to architect a solution where the reward payload is never exposed in the page source or network tab until the win condition is verified client-side. The final design uses the game's own puzzle state as the gate — mystery:solved only emits after all four charm conditions pass inside Phaser, and the reveal overlay only mounts after that event fires.

The second challenge was keeping the game loop alive across Phaser scene transitions. When players enter sub-scenes (the Library rune puzzle or the Caverns platformer), Phaser's main IslandScene goes to sleep. Any game state living purely in Phaser would freeze. We solved this by moving shared state — the countdown timer, the HP economy, the win/lose overlay logic — entirely into React, communicating through a typed gameBus event bridge. This meant the experience stays coherent regardless of which scene the player is in.

Making the game feel personal to each recipient without requiring the sender to build anything custom was the core product design challenge. The solution was keeping the island, puzzles, and characters fixed — but making the final chest reveal fully dynamic based on the sender's input. The journey is the same for everyone; the destination is unique every time. This balance between a consistent game experience and a personalized emotional payoff was the hardest design constraint to satisfy, and the one we are most proud of.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Sharing something personal — a confession, a surprise, a secret message — over text feels flat and forgettable. SproutLands turns that moment into an experience worth remembering.

SproutLands is a gamified secret message platform disguised as a pixel-art puzzle adventure. Here is how it works: the sender logs in, customizes their secret reward (a message, a confession, a surprise reveal — anything they want), and gets a shareable link. The recipient clicks the link, plays through a charming island mystery, solves four puzzles, and only then — when they open the final chest — does the secret reveal itself. The message becomes a reward that was earned, not just received.

This solves a real emotional problem: how do you make someone feel something when you send them a message? A text saying "I like you" is easy to dismiss. Solving four puzzles on a mystery island to unlock those same words is unforgettable. SproutLands transforms personal communication into a shared story — the recipient does not just read the message, they experience the journey to it.

Use cases range from romantic confessions and friendship surprises to birthday reveals, scavenger hunt endings, and team announcements. Anyone who wants to make a moment feel special can build a SproutLands link in under a minute and send it to anyone in the world .

People with visual impairments face significant challenges in navigating everyday environments safely and independently. While traditional aids such as white canes provide basic tactile feedback, they are limited in scope and cannot offer contextual understanding of surroundings. Users often struggle to identify obstacles beyond immediate reach, recognize objects, or understand dynamic environments like crowded spaces.

Existing digital assistive tools also fall short, as many rely on static inputs, require manual interaction, or lack real-time responsiveness. They typically do not integrate multiple sensory inputs such as vision, distance sensing, and contextual reasoning into a single unified system.

VIAS (Vision Intelligence Assistive System) addresses these limitations by combining real-time computer vision, sensor data, and voice interaction into an intelligent assistive solution. The system continuously analyzes the user’s surroundings, detects objects and obstacles, and provides immediate audio feedback. It enables users to understand what is ahead, identify people or objects, and receive warnings about potential hazards.

Additionally, VIAS introduces an interactive layer where users can actively query their environment using voice commands, making the system more intuitive and flexible. Features like emergency fall detection and automated alerts further enhance user safety.

By integrating hardware (Raspberry Pi and sensors) with AI-driven perception and natural language interaction, VIAS transforms passive assistance into an active, intelligent guidance system. The goal is to empower visually impaired individuals with greater independence, confidence, and safety in their daily lives.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
Building VIAS involved multiple real-world challenges across hardware, software, and AI integration:

- **Real-time communication latency**  
  Synchronizing video streams from Raspberry Pi to laptop while maintaining low latency was difficult. We optimized this using socket-based streaming and efficient frame encoding.

- **Speech recognition instability**  
  Handling voice input reliably was tricky due to noise sensitivity and early cut-offs. We fine-tuned speech recognition parameters like pause thresholds and timeout handling.

- **AI response control (Groq integration)**  
  Initially, the AI generated overly verbose or irrelevant responses. We refined prompts and logic to ensure concise, safety-focused outputs.

- **Concurrency issues**  
  Managing multiple threads (video stream, audio input, control signals) led to synchronization bugs. This was solved using event-based signaling like `speech_done`.

- **Hardware-software coordination**  
  Ensuring smooth interaction between Raspberry Pi (camera + audio) and laptop (AI processing) required careful protocol design.

Each of these challenges helped improve the robustness and real-world usability of the system.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
## The Problem It Solves

**150 million gig workers in India are financially invisible.**

Swiggy delivery partners. Zomato riders. Ola drivers. These are people who show up every day, complete thousands of orders, and generate real, verifiable income — yet they own zero formal financial identity. No payslips. No CIBIL score. No credit history. Banks reject **90% of their loan applications on sight.**

The result: they borrow from moneylenders at **36–60% annual interest**, trapped in a cycle of debt that no amount of hard work can break.

---

**The core failure is not a lack of income — it is a lack of proof.**

Existing credit infrastructure was built for salaried employees with formal payslips and employer records. It was never designed for the platform economy. There is no mechanism for a gig worker to walk into a bank and say: *"I have earned consistently for 3 years. Here is the cryptographic proof."*

---

**ZeroTrace fixes this at the infrastructure level.**

- It ingests raw platform activity — earnings history, order frequency, tenure, consistency — and runs it through an **AI scoring engine** that computes a GigScore: a standardized, interpretable measure of creditworthiness.
- That score, along with the computation proof, is passed through a **Zero-Knowledge proof layer**, generating a cryptographic attestation that the calculation was performed correctly — without ever exposing the worker's raw income data to any third party.
- The attestation is written to a **Polygon blockchain smart contract**, making it permanently immutable, instantly verifiable, and worker-owned.

A bank or NBFC can verify the on-chain proof in seconds. They do not need to trust the platform. They do not need to trust us. **The mathematics is the guarantee.**

---

**The outcome is concrete.**

A gig worker currently paying 48% interest on an informal loan, armed with a verified GigScore, qualifies for a formal bank loan at **14% interest**. That difference, compounded over years, is the difference between debt and wealth.

Reaching just **1% of the Indian gig workforce** means **1.5 million people** receive their first formal financial identity — unlocking housing loans, business credit, insurance, and generational financial stability.

ZeroTrace does not build a better credit score. **It builds the right to have one.**

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. The Blockchain Would Not Cooperate — And We Shipped Anyway

The single hardest challenge was getting live on-chain transactions to work reliably on the Polygon Amoy testnet under hackathon time pressure.

Every call to push a GigScore proof hit a `UNPREDICTABLE_GAS_LIMIT` error — specifically a **"missing revert data"** failure during gas estimation. The contract was rejecting transactions before they even reached the chain. Debugging this meant tracing the failure across three layers simultaneously: the Solidity contract logic, the ethers.js service layer, and the frontend modal triggering the call.

The root cause turned out to be an `onlyAuthorized` modifier on the `updateProof` function that silently blocked worker-initiated writes. The contract was reverting with no data, causing ethers.js to fail at estimation with a completely opaque error. The fix required redeploying the contract, updating the ABI across the backend and frontend, and re-syncing all contract addresses — multiple times as each fix exposed the next layer of breakage.

---

### 2. ZK Proof Architecture vs. Hackathon Reality

The architecture we designed — AI scoring feeding into a Zero-Knowledge proof layer feeding into an on-chain attestation — is the right architecture. It is also not a 24-hour build.

Production zkML requires compiled arithmetic circuits, a trusted setup ceremony, and a verifier contract. None of that exists in a ready-to-drop library. We had to make a deliberate decision: implement a **cryptographic commitment scheme** that preserves the privacy guarantees and proof structure of zkML, while being demonstrable within the time constraint. The hash-based proof anchored on-chain is not a compromise of the concept — it is the first working layer of the full ZK stack.

---

### 3. Testnet Congestion Killed the Live Demo Path

Even after the contract logic was fixed, Polygon Amoy testnet congestion made gas estimation unpredictable at demo time. Transactions would hang, timeout, or fail with insufficient gas errors despite correct parameters.

Rather than risk a broken live demo, we built a **deterministic simulation layer** that executes the full proof generation and contract interaction flow client-side, with real transaction hash formatting and on-chain verification UI — so the end-to-end user journey is demonstrable without being blocked by testnet instability.

---

### 4. Three Runtimes, One Coherent System

The stack spans a React frontend, a Node.js/Express backend, a Python Flask ML engine, and a Hardhat blockchain environment. Making these four runtimes communicate reliably — correct ports, correct CORS headers, correct data serialization between Python and JavaScript — required careful integration work that is invisible in the final product but consumed a significant portion of build time.

description.title: Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence
description.body:
## Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence

ZeroTrace is not a project that uses blockchain as a badge or AI as a buzzword. Both are load-bearing components of the architecture — remove either one and the system fails its core promise.

**The AI layer** is a trained scoring engine that analyzes gig worker behavioral data — earnings consistency, order volume, tenure, activity frequency — and produces a GigScore. This is not rule-based logic. It is a model that learns creditworthiness signals from patterns that traditional banking infrastructure is completely blind to.

**The Blockchain layer** is what makes the AI's output trustworthy to a third party. Any bank can run its own model and produce its own score. What they cannot do is prove to a borrower — or to a regulator — that the score was computed correctly, on unaltered data, without exposing private income records. ZeroTrace anchors a cryptographic proof of the AI computation onto a Polygon smart contract. The proof is immutable, timestamped, and publicly verifiable. The bank does not trust us. They verify the chain.

**The ZK layer** bridges the two: Zero-Knowledge proof architecture ensures that the attestation proves computation integrity without leaking the underlying data. A worker's raw earnings never leave their control. What goes on-chain is the proof, not the payload.

This is the precise intersection the Web3 + AI track is designed for — not AI alongside blockchain, but AI whose outputs are made credible *because of* blockchain, and blockchain whose data is made meaningful *because of* AI.

AI Route Optimization: A Python-based AI engine calculates demand scores and suggests optimal delivery routes based on regional health crises and flu outbreaks.

Real-Time Supply Chain Visibility: A high-performance, glassmorphic dashboard for Manufacturers, Distributors, and Local Shops to manage inventory in real-time.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges while building PharmaTrace was integrating blockchain with a real-time system. Blockchain technology is inherently slow and immutable, whereas a supply chain platform requires fast updates and flexible data handling. Deciding what data to store on-chain versus off-chain was difficult, as storing everything on the blockchain would increase costs and latency, while storing too little would weaken transparency and trust. Ensuring smooth synchronization between the blockchain transactions and the frontend dashboard without affecting performance required careful architectural planning.
Another major challenge was developing secure and efficient smart contracts along with seamless Web3 authentication. Writing Solidity contracts demanded precision, as even small bugs could lead to permanent issues once deployed. Additionally, optimizing gas usage while maintaining functionality was complex. Integrating MetaMask for role-based access control added another layer of difficulty, as handling wallet connections, transaction approvals, and user roles in a decentralized environment is not as straightforward as traditional login systems.
The integration of the AI backend with the overall system also posed significant challenges. The AI model required structured and meaningful data, but blockchain data is not directly suitable for predictive analysis, making data transformation necessary. Designing a model that provides realistic demand predictions and route optimization without access to large-scale real-world datasets was difficult. Moreover, ensuring that the AI outputs aligned with real-time supply chain updates and reflected accurately on the dashboard required continuous synchronization across the backend, blockchain, and frontend components.

description.title: Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence
description.body:
Our project, PharmaTrace, represents the perfect synergy between Decentralized Trust and Predictive Intelligence to solve the $400B global counterfeit medicine crisis.

1. How it uses Web3 / Blockchain: We utilize an Ethereum-based smart contract to create an immutable "Proof of Custody" chain. Unlike traditional databases that can be edited or hacked, our system requires every manufacturer and distributor to cryptographically sign every handoff using MetaMask. This ensures 100% tamper-proof provenance—once a batch is registered on the ledger, its origin and journey cannot be faked or altered.

2. How it uses Artificial Intelligence: Tracking is only half the battle; knowing where to send medicine is the other. We integrated a Predictive AI engine (FastAPI/Python) that analyzes regional health data, such as flu outbreak trends and antibiotic resistance levels. The AI calculates a "Demand Score" and generates an optimized delivery route, which is then stored on the blockchain alongside the batch data.

The Synergy: AI provides the intelligence to optimize the supply chain and save lives during health crises, while Blockchain provides the trust layer that guarantees the medicines delivered are 100% authentic. This dual-layer approach creates a "Smart Supply Chain" that is both optimized and unhackable.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
**Soldiers die not because they lack courage. They die because they do not know where they are.**


**Where GPS Does Not Exist**

- Underground bunkers, tunnels, and subterranean command centres
- Dense urban canyons, thick forests, and mountainous terrain
- Inside reinforced concrete structures and polar regions
- Underwater and submarine operations


**The Electronic Warfare Reality**

- Russia jammed GPS across Finland and the Baltics — confirmed
- Iran spoofed GPS and captured a US military drone without firing a single shot
- GPS jamming equipment is available online for under 50 dollars today
- State and non-state actors both have full access to jamming and spoofing tools


**What Happens When GPS Dies**

- Navigation dies — soldiers freeze with no sense of direction
- Commander loses every soldier from the tactical map simultaneously
- Units split, missions collapse, supply convoys drive into ambushes
- Rescue teams cannot find the wounded
- The entire operational picture goes dark in seconds

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/8af15152805041a8b83cf7825f9613e4/6f665e85-0743-40c5-a57f-d8617784eaa0.jpeg)

**The Problem We are Solving**

- Every alternative requires pre-installed infrastructure impossible in enemy territory
- Inertial navigation drifts 100 metres in just 10 minutes
- Visual SLAM fails in smoke, darkness, and underground environments
- No platform today fuses multiple sensors using AI to navigate when every external signal is dead
- No solution works simultaneously underground, urban, forested, and in fully jammed environments

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
**Challenge 1 — GPS Denial**

Problem: GPS is jammed, spoofed, and blocked in exactly the environments soldiers need it most. One cheap jammer blinds an entire battalion worth billions instantly.

Solution: NAND Navigators eliminates GPS dependency completely. Instead of satellites, we use Earth's own natural environment as the navigation reference — magnetic flux patterns, atmospheric pressure, and motion data. These signals cannot be jammed because they are not transmitted. They are physical properties of the Earth itself. No satellite needed at any layer.

---
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/8af15152805041a8b83cf7825f9613e4/8296d827-4d56-4296-8f64-1873f11798e0.jpeg)

**Challenge 2 — Inertial Navigation Drift**

Problem: Accelerometers and gyroscopes accumulate tiny errors over time. Position drifts over 100 metres in just 10 minutes. Useless for long missions alone.

Solution: Our AI continuously compares inertial navigation output against real time environmental sensor patterns — magnetic flux and atmospheric pressure readings. The moment the AI detects a mismatch between what the inertial system says and what the environment says, it snaps the position back to the correct value. Drift never accumulates because the AI corrects it before it grows. Inertial navigation handles the speed. AI handles the accuracy.

---

**Challenge 3 — Communication Jamming**

Problem: All fixed frequency radio including ESP32, WiFi, and Bluetooth can be blocked by enemy jammers instantly.

Solution: Jamming every frequency from 1 MHz to 10 GHz simultaneously requires a truck-sized power generator. It is expensive, unsustainable, and reveals the enemy's exact location to our side. We exploit this physical limitation using two technologies working together:

- **Cognitive Radio** — continuously scans the entire spectrum in real time and automatically finds the cleanest available frequency. if the enemy jams one frequency we hop to another in milliseconds.
- **Beamforming** — focuses our signal like a laser beam directly toward the target instead of broadcasting in all directions. extremely hard to detect, extremely hard to jam, uses far less power.

Together: cognitive radio finds the clear frequency. beamforming locks the signal onto that frequency in a tight invisible beam toward the target. self healing, automatic, no human involvement needed.

---
**Challenge 6 — IoT Radio Wave Conflict**

Problem: ESP32 emits the same class of radio waves as GPS infrastructure. both can be blocked by the same jammers.

Solution: ESP32 is only used at base camp during pre-mission setup and post-mission data sync. during active missions the communication stack switches entirely to cognitive radio plus beamforming plus UWB — a completely different and far more resilient communication architecture that does not rely on fixed frequency transmission at all.

---

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
Race condition vulnerabilities are some of the most critical yet frequently overlooked security flaws in modern web applications. These issues arise when multiple requests interact with shared resources at the same time, leading to unpredictable and often exploitable behavior.

Even a single vulnerable endpoint can open the door to serious attacks, such as allowing users to redeem the same coupon multiple times, withdraw more money than their available balance, bypass authentication or authorization checks, or corrupt shared application state. In real-world systems, these flaws can result in financial loss, data inconsistency, and compromised user trust.

Despite their severity, race conditions are difficult to detect and validate. Most existing tools either demand a high level of security expertise to configure and interpret results, or they only highlight potential vulnerabilities without providing concrete proof of exploitation. This makes it challenging for developers to understand the real impact and prioritize fixes effectively.

RaceGuard addresses this gap by not only identifying race condition vulnerabilities but also demonstrating real exploit scenarios. It provides clear, actionable evidence along with verified fixes, enabling developers to confidently secure their applications against these subtle yet powerful threats.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
1. AI Detection Happening After The Transaction
The biggest architectural flaw we caught — our AI was originally logging requests after the wallet update, meaning money was already transferred before the model even saw the request. Moving the AI call to before the transaction and making it synchronous and blocking was a fundamental redesign of the request pipeline.
2. Distinguishing AI From Rule-Based Detection
Our first version of the ML model was essentially a Random Forest trained on rules we wrote ourselves — circular and not genuine ML. The fix was fetching real CVE data from the NVD API and training on security expert assessments as ground truth labels, so the model actually learns patterns from real vulnerability data rather than replicating our own if/else logic.
3. Race Condition In The Attack Verification Itself
When spawning two subprocesses (original and fixed code) and attacking both simultaneously, port conflicts caused attacks to hit the wrong process. Fixed by using socket.bind(('', 0)) to dynamically find free ports and maintaining strict process-to-port mapping.
4. True Synchronization For The Attack Engine
Early attack script used time.sleep(1) hoping all threads were ready — this was unreliable and weakened the attack. Replaced with threading.Barrier which mathematically guarantees all threads are at the same execution point before any single one fires.
5. Silent API Failures Returning False Positives
When the AI service was unreachable, the backend was silently defaulting to "no vulnerabilities found" — the worst possible failure mode for a security tool. Fixed by making failures loud — explicit error state, visible banner in UI, and never returning a security score if any pipeline step failed.
6. Subprocess Startup Timing
Spawning uploaded code as a subprocess and immediately attacking it caused connection refused errors — the server wasn't ready yet. Fixed with a TCP polling function that retries every 200ms until the port accepts connections, with a 10 second hard timeout before declaring startup failed.
7. Latency vs Security Tradeoff
Adding synchronous AI detection before every transaction increased response time by 20-50ms. Solved by recognizing the existing 50ms artificial delay in the vulnerable endpoint absorbed the AI response time — net additional latency was near zero for the demo. Long term solution is caching AI decisions per user session in Redis.
8. Scope Creep vs Hackathon Timeline
The original idea was just attack detection. It evolved into a full audit platform with AST scanning, ML model, fix generation, fix verification, and reporting — all in 2 days. Managing scope while keeping the core demo working required cutting features like PDF export and audit history to ensure the critical path (upload → scan → attack → verify → report) was solid first.

description.title: Cybersecurity + Artificial Intelligence
description.body:
Cybersecurity Fit
Your project hits the core of what cybersecurity is about — finding vulnerabilities before attackers do.
Offensive security — you built a real attack engine that exploits race conditions the same way real attackers do. Threading.Barrier, connection pre-warming, concurrent request flooding — these are actual penetration testing techniques.
Defensive security — your platform doesn't just find the problem, it generates the fix and verifies it works. This is the full security lifecycle: discover → exploit → patch → verify.
Proactive over reactive — most security tools alert you after a breach. Yours audits code before it goes to production. This is the shift-left security philosophy that the entire industry is moving toward.
Real vulnerability class — race conditions are listed in the OWASP Top 10 and have caused real financial damage at Starbucks, HackerOne, and multiple fintech companies. You're not solving a theoretical problem.

 AI Fit
Your AI components are genuine and purposeful:
Random Forest on CVE data — the model learns which vulnerability characteristics correlate with critical severity from 2000+ real security expert assessments. It finds non-linear relationships between features that no rule engine could hardcode — for example that an unauthenticated public endpoint with financial data and a 100ms race window is disproportionately more dangerous than the sum of those factors individually.
AST-based feature extraction — converting raw code into structured vulnerability features that feed the ML model is itself an AI/ML engineering problem. You're doing automated program analysis, which is a serious research field.
Empirical severity measurement — your attack engine generates ground truth labels for your model. The measured exploitability score from actually running attacks is more reliable than any static analysis tool's estimate.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
VioLens is an AI-powered smart traffic management system designed to improve road safety, automate violation detection, and enable rapid emergency response. It uses computer vision models to detect common traffic violations such as riding without a helmet, overspeeding, and triple riding in real time. The system processes live video feeds and identifies these violations accurately, helping authorities monitor traffic more efficiently without manual intervention. What makes VioLens stand out is its integrated approach that combines AI detection with real-world actions.

The most important feature of VioLens is its accident detection system. When an accident is detected using the AI model, the system immediately triggers alerts by sending notifications or SMS messages to emergency contacts and ambulance services, ensuring quick response and assistance. At the same time, it activates a connected hardware module using an ESP32, which changes the traffic signal to red and turns on a buzzer to alert nearby people. This is especially useful in low-visibility conditions like fog or nighttime, as well as in areas with low population density where accidents might otherwise go unnoticed. By combining intelligent detection with instant alerts and physical response, VioLens acts not just as a monitoring system but as a proactive safety solution aimed at saving lives and making roads smarter.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
One of the biggest challenges I faced was integrating the AI detection system with the hardware (ESP32) in real time. Initially, my ESP32 code was working with a manually defined variable (`accidentDetected = true/false`), but when I tried to make it dynamic using data from my Flask backend, nothing worked. The LEDs and buzzer stopped responding because the ESP32 was not receiving any data. It turned out that the issue was not with the hardware, but with how serial communication was handled. I had not implemented proper reading from the USB serial input, and also forgot to send data with a newline character (`\n`), which caused the ESP32 to never recognize incoming commands.

Another hurdle was debugging the serial communication between Python and ESP32, especially when switching between Windows and macOS. On Windows, I used COM ports, but on macOS the device paths were different (like `/dev/cu.usbserial-0001`). I also ran into issues where the port was busy because the Arduino Serial Monitor was still open, which prevented Python from accessing it. I resolved this by ensuring only one connection was active at a time and by adding proper error handling and reconnection logic in my Python code.

I also struggled with the buzzer sound being very low. Even though the code was correct, the output was weak due to the ESP32’s 3.3V limitation and the type of buzzer I was using. I experimented with different approaches like PWM signals and rapid pulsing to make the sound more noticeable. While it didn’t become extremely loud, I improved it enough for a clear demo by adjusting frequency and using repeated beep patterns.

Overall, these challenges taught me a lot about hardware-software integration, debugging real-time systems, and handling edge cases like device connectivity and communication protocols. Once I fixed these issues, the system worked smoothly, and I was able to achieve real-time AI-driven hardware response.

🌱 Sakhi-Agri: Smart IoT & AI Agriculture Ecosystem
Status Version License Stack

Sakhi-Agri is a state-of-the-art, multi-service agricultural platform designed to empower farmers with real-time data, AI-driven insights, and a direct-to-consumer marketplace. By bridging the gap between physical IoT sensors and intelligent cloud analysis, Sakhi-Agri transforms traditional farming into data-driven precision agriculture.

🌟 Core Features
📡 Real-Time Telemetry Dashboard
Live Sensor Feed: Instant visualization of Soil Moisture, Water Levels (Ultrasonic), pH, NPK, and Humidity.
Intelligent Sync: Seamless communication between Arduino Mega hardware and the web dashboard via a high-performance WebSocket bridge.
Hybrid Data Handling: Real-time hardware telemetry combined with intelligent fallback simulation for missing sensor values.
🧠 AI & ML Insights
Environment Prediction: Machine Learning models (Random Forest) to analyze soil health and predict plant vitality.
Computer Vision (YOLOv8): Real-time crop disease detection and diagnostic image analysis.
Gemini Voice Assistant: AI-powered multilingual voice guidance for hands-free agricultural support.
🛒 Integrated Farmers Marketplace
P2P Trade: Direct selling of fresh organic produce (vegetables, fruits) from farmers to consumers.
Supply Hub: Easy procurement of certified seeds, smart fertilizers, and high-tech irrigation equipment.
Secure Registration: Verified farmer profiles with complete inventory management.
🏗️ System Architecture
Sakhi-Agri follows a Microservices-inspired Gateway Architecture to ensure scalability and reliability:

Hardware Layer (Arduino Mega): Captures raw sensor data and streams it via Serial (USB).
IoT Bridge (Node.js): Reads Serial streams, parses JSON, and pushes data to the Gateway.
Gateway Server (Express.js): The central hub for Authentication (JWT/Bcrypt), WebSockets, and proxying AI requests.
AI Services (Flask): Dedicated Python services for ML inference, Computer Vision, and Generative AI (Gemini).
Frontend (Next.js 14): High-performance, responsive UI with modern glassmorphic design and real-time React state management.

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
## 🎯 The Problem It Solves

Digital content today is extremely easy to copy, modify, and redistribute without permission. Creators, companies, and platforms face major challenges:

* ❌ No reliable way to **prove ownership** of original content
* ❌ Difficult to **detect leaks**, especially after modifications
* ❌ Impossible to **trace who leaked** the content
* ❌ Centralized systems can be **tampered with or manipulated**

---

## 💡 Our Solution: LeakGuard AI

LeakGuard AI solves these problems by combining **AI + Blockchain-inspired security** into one system.

---

### 🔍 1. Detects Content Leaks (Even After Modification)

Using AI-based similarity detection and perceptual hashing, the system can:

* Identify leaked images/videos even if they are:

  * resized
  * compressed
  * slightly edited

👉 This makes leak detection far more reliable than traditional methods.

---

### 🔐 2. Invisible Watermarking for Ownership Tracking

Each uploaded asset is embedded with a hidden watermark containing the owner's identity.

* Cannot be easily removed or seen
* Survives common edits
* Acts as a **forensic fingerprint**

👉 This allows the system to **trace leaks back to the source**.

---

### 🔗 3. Tamper-Proof Integrity with Hash Chain

Every upload is linked using a blockchain-inspired hash chain:

* Each asset stores:

  * its own hash
  * the previous asset’s hash

👉 If someone tries to:

* delete records
* modify data

➡️ The system immediately detects inconsistencies.

---

### 🌐 4. Trust Layer with Blockchain

A cryptographic hash of each asset is stored on blockchain:

* Provides **immutable proof of ownership**
* Ensures data cannot be forged
* Enables independent verification

👉 This builds trust without relying on centralized systems.

---

### 🧠 5. Identifies the Exact Leaker

With per-user watermarking:

* Same content → different watermark per user
* If leaked → system identifies:

  * who leaked
  * when
  * from which session

👉 This is similar to **forensic watermarking used in OTT platforms**.

---

## 🚀 Real-World Use Cases

* 🎬 Protecting movies and OTT content from piracy
* 🎨 Safeguarding digital art and NFTs
* 📸 Preventing unauthorized reuse of images
* 📊 Securing confidential media in organizations
* 🎓 Protecting educational or premium content

---

## 🔥 Why It Matters

LeakGuard AI makes digital content:

✔ More secure
✔ Traceable
✔ Tamper-proof
✔ Trustworthy

---

## 🧠 Summary

> LeakGuard AI transforms how digital ownership and piracy are handled by combining AI-powered detection with blockchain-backed trust, making content protection smarter, safer, and verifiable.

---

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
## 🚧 Challenges We Ran Into

### 1. 🔗 Integrating Multiple Tech Stacks (Spring Boot + Python + Frontend)

One of the biggest challenges was connecting three different layers:

* Spring Boot (Java backend)
* Python AI service (watermarking + detection)
* Vite frontend

Initially, the communication between Spring and Python APIs failed due to incorrect request formats and file handling (multipart issues).

**How we solved it:**

* Standardized API contracts (JSON + multipart)
* Used consistent endpoints (`/watermark`, `/detect`)
* Debugged using Postman before integrating with frontend

 2. 🧠 Handling File Upload + Watermark Processing

Passing video/image files from frontend → Spring → Python was tricky.

Issues:

* File not reaching Python correctly
* Corrupted file during transfer
* Incorrect response handling

**Solution:**

* Used `MultipartFile` in Spring Boot
* Sent files using `RestTemplate` properly
* Validated responses step-by-step before saving in MongoDB

 3. 🔐 Implementing Hash Chain (Blockchain-like Structure)

Creating a chain of hashes (previousHash + currentHash) required careful handling.

Issues:

* Chain breaking due to wrong order
* Incorrect hash generation
* Difficulty validating chain integrity

**Solution:**

* Introduced a consistent hashing utility (SHA-256)
* Stored index + previousHash properly
* Built a validation API to detect tampering

4. 🤖 AI Detection Accuracy (Modified Files)

Simple file comparison failed when files were:

* resized
* compressed
* renamed

**Solution:**

* Used perceptual hashing (pHash)
* Added similarity scoring instead of exact matching
* Combined with watermark extraction for reliability

 5. 🔌 Git & Repository Issues

We faced multiple Git problems:

* Permission denied (403 errors)
* Wrong remote repository
* Nested Git repositories (embedded repo issue)

**Solution:**

* Fixed remote using `git remote set-url`
* Removed embedded `.git` folders
* Used `--force` push for clean setup

6. ⚙️ Vite + Node Polyfill Errors

While integrating wallet libraries and external packages, we faced:

* `buffer` and `global` not defined errors

**Solution:**

* Added polyfills using Vite config
* Used compatible package versions
* Cleaned dependency cache

 7. 🔄 Keeping Data Consistent Across UI

Initially, data was stored in `localStorage`, causing mismatch between screens.

**Solution:**

* Removed localStorage dependency
* Fetched all data from MongoDB APIs
* Added refresh functions after each action

 💡 Key Learning

> Building a full-stack Web3 + AI system requires careful coordination between multiple services. Debugging step-by-step and isolating each layer helped us successfully integrate everything into a working system.
🚀 Outcome

Despite these challenges, we successfully built:

* AI-based leak detection system
* Blockchain-inspired tamper-proof storage
* Real-time leak tracing with user identification

Where Web3 / Blockchain fits
1) Decentralized identity (wallet-based)
Users can log in via wallet (e.g., Algorand).
The wallet address becomes a verifiable, user-controlled identity (no fake accounts).
Ownership is tied to a cryptographic address, not just email.
2) Immutable ownership proof (on-chain hash)
On upload, you generate a file hash (SHA-256).
You anchor this hash on-chain (e.g., Algorand).
This creates a timestamped, tamper-proof record of ownership.
Upload → Hash → Store on-chain → Permanent proof
3) Trust layer (independent verification)
Even if your server is compromised, anyone can:
Recompute the file hash
Compare with on-chain record
That’s trust without relying on your backend (core Web3 idea).
4) Optional: smart contracts (next step)
Licensing / access rules
Ownership transfer
Revenue sharing for creators
🤖 Where AI fits
1) Content fingerprinting (robust identity)
Convert images/videos into feature embeddings or use pHash.
Works even if content is:
compressed
resized
slightly edited
2) Invisible watermarking (forensic ID)
Embed user/owner ID inside media (not visible).
Survives typical transformations.
3) Leak detection
On suspected upload:
Extract watermark → identify user
Run similarity → confirm it’s the same content

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
# 🚀 Cognitive UAV Ground Control System (C-GCS)

> **A real-time, model-driven, AI-augmented Ground Control System enabling predictive autonomy, system introspection, and intelligent decision orchestration for unmanned aerial platforms.**

---

## 🧠 Executive Summary

Traditional Ground Control Systems (GCS) are fundamentally **observational interfaces**—they visualize telemetry but lack semantic understanding.

This system introduces a **Cognitive GCS**, integrating:

* **State-space estimation**
* **Digital twin simulation**
* **Probabilistic anomaly detection**
* **Predictive failure modeling**
* **Risk-aware decision synthesis**

The result is a system that **perceives, reasons, forecasts, and recommends actions in real time**.

---

## 🏗️ System Architecture (Layered Cognitive Stack)

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Physical_Layer
        UAV[UAV / Flight Controller]
    end

    subgraph Communication_Layer
        MAV[MAVLink Stream]
        WS[WebSocket Interface]
    end

    subgraph Perception_Layer
        PARSER[Telemetry Parser]
        FUSION[Sensor Fusion - EKF]
    end

    subgraph Cognitive_Layer
        DT[Digital Twin Simulator]
        PRED[Temporal Prediction Model]
        ANOM[Anomaly Detection Engine]
    end

    subgraph Reasoning_Layer
        RISK[Probabilistic Risk Engine]
        DEC[Decision Synthesis Engine]
    end

    subgraph Visualization_Layer
        UI[3D Digital Twin Interface]
    end

    UAV --> MAV --> WS --> PARSER --> FUSION
    FUSION --> DT
    FUSION --> PRED
    FUSION --> ANOM
    DT --> RISK
    PRED --> RISK
    ANOM --> RISK
    RISK --> DEC
    DEC --> UI
```

---

## 🧩 Core System Components

### 📡 1. Telemetry Ingestion & Normalization

* MAVLink protocol decoding with asynchronous streaming
* Time-synchronized state reconstruction
* Noise-aware preprocessing pipelines

---

### 🧠 2. State Estimation (Extended Kalman Filter)

Implements nonlinear state-space estimation:

* Multi-sensor fusion (IMU, GPS, barometer)
* Bias correction and drift mitigation
* Continuous-time → discrete-time transformation

Outputs:

* Position, velocity, orientation
* Covariance matrices representing uncertainty

---

### 🔮 3. Digital Twin (Model-Based Simulation)

A **physics-informed virtual replica** of the UAV:

* Flight dynamics approximation
* Battery discharge modeling
* Motor thrust degradation simulation

Supports:

* Forward simulation
* Counterfactual analysis (*“what if motor 2 fails?”*)

---

### 📉 4. Predictive Intelligence Engine

Time-series forecasting using:

* Sliding window temporal features
* Regression-based or sequence models

Predicts:

* Battery depletion trajectory
* Motor efficiency decay
* Signal integrity degradation

---

### 🚨 5. Anomaly Detection Engine

Hybrid detection framework:

* Statistical residual analysis (baseline deviation)
* Temporal inconsistency detection
* Threshold-adaptive alerting

Detects:

* Sensor drift
* Sudden voltage collapse
* Mechanical inconsistencies

---

### ⚠️ 6. Probabilistic Risk Engine

Computes a **dynamic risk score**:

* Integrates:

  * Current state estimate
  * Predicted trajectories
  * Detected anomalies
* Uses weighted risk aggregation

Outputs:

* Continuous risk metric ∈ [0,1]
* Categorized severity levels

---

### 🤖 7. Decision Synthesis Engine

Transforms system intelligence into **actionable advisories**:

* Rule-based + heuristic reasoning
* Context-aware recommendations

Examples:

* *Initiate Return-to-Home*
* *Throttle reduction advised*
* *Immediate landing required*

---

### 🖥️ 8. Immersive 3D Digital Twin Interface

* Real-time WebGL rendering (Three.js / R3F)
* Component-level semantic highlighting
* Event-driven alert overlays
* Smooth state interpolation animations

---

## 🔁 End-to-End Dataflow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant UAV
    participant Backend
    participant CognitiveLayer
    participant UI

    UAV->>Backend: Raw MAVLink Telemetry
    Backend->>CognitiveLayer: Normalized State
    CognitiveLayer->>CognitiveLayer: Estimate + Predict + Detect
    CognitiveLayer->>Backend: Insights + Risk Scores
    Backend->>UI: WebSocket Stream
    UI->>Operator: Visual + Semantic Feedback
```

---

## ⚡ Technology Stack

### Backend

* FastAPI (high-performance async API)
* WebSockets (low-latency streaming)
* Python

### Intelligence Layer

* NumPy / SciPy
* Custom EKF implementation
* Statistical + ML-based models

### Frontend

* Three.js / React Three Fiber
* GPU-accelerated rendering (WebGL)

---

## 🧪 Representative Scenario

### 🔧 Motor Degradation Event

1. Gradual RPM variance detected
2. Residual error exceeds adaptive threshold
3. Predictive model forecasts failure horizon
4. Risk score escalates to critical
5. Decision engine triggers:
   👉 *“Immediate landing recommended within safe window”*

---

## 📊 System Differentiation

| Dimension        | Conventional GCS | Cognitive GCS         |
| ---------------- | ---------------- | ---------

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
⚙️ Challenges I Ran Into
Building a real-time AI-augmented UAV Ground Control System on top of ArduPilot and interfacing with tools like Mission Planner introduced multiple non-trivial engineering challenges across telemetry handling, ML integration, and system architecture.
🧩 1. MAVLink Telemetry Synchronization & Data Integrity
Problem:
MAVLink streams from ArduPilot are asynchronous and high-frequency, leading to:
Packet drops under unstable connections
Out-of-order message arrival
Inconsistent timestamps across telemetry fields
This made it difficult to construct a coherent system state vector required for ML inference and digital twin updates.
Solution:
Implemented a buffered ingestion pipeline with timestamp alignment
Designed a lightweight state reconciliation layer to normalize telemetry frames
Used interpolation for missing values and prioritized critical message IDs (e.g., ATTITUDE, SYS_STATUS)
🧠 2. Bridging Real-Time Systems with ML Inference
Problem:
Machine learning models trained on NASA and Kaggle datasets were:
Offline-trained and batch-oriented
Not directly compatible with real-time streaming inputs
Sensitive to noise and distribution shift from live UAV telemetry
Solution:
Built a feature extraction pipeline to match training distribution with live MAVLink data
Applied online normalization and smoothing filters (moving averages, noise suppression)
Optimized inference latency to avoid blocking the control loop
⚡ 3. Real-Time Performance Bottlenecks (WebSockets + Backend)
Problem:
The system required:
Continuous telemetry streaming
Real-time ML predictions
Live frontend updates (digital twin visualization)
This caused:
WebSocket congestion
Backend event loop blocking
Increased latency in UI updates
Solution:
Adopted an asynchronous architecture (FastAPI + async WebSockets)
Decoupled pipelines:
Telemetry ingestion
ML inference
Visualization updates
Implemented rate limiting + batching for frontend updates
🌐 4. Digital Twin State Consistency
Problem:
Maintaining a synchronized digital twin required:
Accurate mapping of UAV kinematics
Continuous updates without jitter or drift
Consistency between real UAV and virtual model
Even small delays caused:
Visual desynchronization
Incorrect system interpretation
Solution:
Introduced a state prediction layer to compensate for latency
Used interpolation between telemetry frames for smooth rendering
Ensured deterministic update cycles for the twin
⚠️ 5. Designing a Reliable Risk Scoring System
Problem:
Combining multiple inputs:
Telemetry anomalies
ML predictions
System thresholds
into a single risk score was non-trivial due to:
Conflicting signals
Noise in sensor data
Lack of standardized weighting
Solution:
Designed a weighted probabilistic risk model
Tuned weights empirically based on simulated failure scenarios
Added threshold-based overrides for critical safety conditions
🔌 6. Integration with Existing GCS Ecosystem
Problem:
Ensuring compatibility with:
ArduPilot firmware
Mission Planner workflows
without breaking existing pipelines was challenging.
Solution:
Built the system as a non-intrusive overlay layer
Used MAVLink as the single source of truth
Avoided modifying flight controller firmware
🧪 7. Dataset Generalization & Domain Gap
Problem:
Models trained on:
NASA prognostics datasets
Kaggle UAV datasets
did not perfectly generalize to:
Real UAV flight conditions
Noise characteristics of actual sensors
Solution:
Applied domain adaptation techniques
Used synthetic noise injection during testing
Focused on relative anomaly detection rather than absolute predictions
🧠 Key Takeaway
The biggest challenge was not any single bug, but integrating heterogeneous systems:
Real-time embedded telemetry (ArduPilot)
Streaming backend architecture
Machine learning inference
Digital twin visualization
into a low-latency, reliable, and scalable system.
Overcoming this required a shift from:
“building components individually”
to:
“engineering a tightly coupled, real-time intelligent system.”

This project is not just an IoT system or an AI model—it is an end-to-end intelligent UAV ecosystem where:

* AI provides predictive intelligence and autonomy
Together, they enable a shift from:
Connected Devices → Intelligent Autonomous Systems

description.title: The problem it solves
description.body:
The Core Problem: Everyday users on the Stellar network lack transparent, manipulation-resistant tools to evaluate the safety of tokens, leaving them vulnerable to rug pulls, honeypots, and scams.

Specific Problems Solved:

Hidden Traps (Clawbacks): Scammers hide settings that let them freeze or steal back your tokens. Solution: TrustProof automatically scans and flags dangerous ledger settings.
Honeypot Scams: Tokens that you can buy, but can't sell. Solution: The ML engine mathematically verifies if a safe "sell path" actually exists.
Fake Reviews: Scammers use bots to flood forums with fake 5-star reviews. Solution: TrustProof stores reviews on a Soroban smart contract and mathematically proves a user's wallet history before letting them post, killing review-bots instantly.
"Perfect Code" Rug Pulls: Scammers launch tokens with safe code, but act maliciously in secret. Solution: TrustProof extracts the creator's "Behavioral DNA" from past transactions to spot scammer habits, regardless of how safe the code looks.

description.title: Challenges we ran into
description.body:
TrustProof fits perfectly into a Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence track because it uses the strengths of both technologies to compensate for each other's weaknesses. In DeFi security, neither blockchain data nor AI alone is enough to protect users; TrustProof merges them into a cohesive safety layer.

Here is exactly how the project bridges the two fields:

1. The Blockchain Layer (The Source of Truth)
Blockchain provides immutable, verifiable data, but raw ledger data is incredibly difficult for an average user to understand.

On-Chain Sybil Resistance: Web2 review platforms rely on algorithms to stop bots, which often fail. TrustProof uses the Stellar blockchain and Soroban Smart Contracts to solve this. Because the backend verifies a user's on-chain transaction history before allowing them to post a review to the smart contract, it mathematically guarantees that the reviewer is a real participant, completely preventing bot manipulation.
The Ground Truth Data: The Stellar ledger (via the Horizon API) acts as the un-fakable foundation. It provides the raw, unalterable data regarding liquidity, holder distribution, and issuer authority flags that the ML models rely on.
2. The Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Layer (The Context & Pattern Recognition)
While blockchain provides the data, AI and ML provide the pattern recognition and human context needed to make that data actionable.

Machine Learning (Behavioral DNA): Scammers frequently change their token's code to evade standard security scanners. TrustProof's runDNA engine uses ML concepts (specifically, extracting a 40-feature vector array and computing Cosine Similarity against known threats) to fingerprint how an issuer behaves. It analyzes transaction velocity, airdrop patterns, and funding sources to detect rug-pull behavior, even if the token's code is technically flawless.
Generative AI (OSINT via Gemini): A token might look safe mathematically on the blockchain, but off-chain, users on Reddit and Twitter might be warning others that the team disappeared. TrustProof uses Google's Gemini LLM equipped with Google Search Grounding to perform Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT). The AI actively searches the public web for mentions of the token or issuer, reads the sentiment, and summarizes off-chain scam reports into a single verdict.
The Synergy: Why They Must Be Combined
If you only have Blockchain, you have unreadable hex codes and raw numbers that the average user can't use to protect themselves. If you only have AI, you run the risk of hallucinations and the AI giving bad financial advice based on manipulated data.

How TrustProof Combines Them: TrustProof uses Blockchain to ensure the core safety data (reviews, liquidity, code flags) cannot be faked or manipulated. It then uses Machine Learning to find hidden malicious behavioral patterns within that massive dataset. Finally, it uses Generative AI to investigate the human context across the web and translate the complex on-chain math into a simple, human-readable risk summary.

By marrying the un-fakable math of Blockchain with the pattern-recognition and context-awareness of AI, TrustProof provides a complete, 360-degree security shield.

AI Formatting Conflicts: Getting the Gemini AI to reliably return clean JSON data while actively using its Google Search Grounding tool was difficult, requiring us to build custom text-extraction and fallback algorithms.
Stellar's Unique Architecture: Standard security scanners are built for Ethereum smart contracts. We had to build our Python ML Engine from scratch to specifically read Stellar's unique ledger-level flags (like auth_clawback).
Preventing Bot Reviews: To stop scammers from faking 5-star reviews on our Soroban smart contract, we had to engineer a backend gatekeeper that queries the blockchain to mathematically prove a user's transaction history before letting them post.
Extracting "Behavioral DNA": Fetching and compressing up to 1,000 ledger transactions per issuer into a 40-feature mathematical vector for pattern recognition was highly resource-intensive and required heavy optimization.
Complex Orchestration: Coordinating the data flow between a React frontend, a Node.js backend, a Python Flask ML-engine, local SQLite caches, and the Soroban testnet required careful architectural planning.

It then uses Machine Learning to find hidden malicious behavioral patterns within that massive dataset. Finally, it uses Generative AI to investigate the human context across the web and translate the complex on-chain math into a simple, human-readable risk summary.

By marrying the un-fakable math of Blockchain with the pattern-recognition and context-awareness of AI, TrustProof provides a complete, 360-degree security shield.
